'''Aiden Kyle Markram''' (born 4 October 1994) is a South African [[cricket]]er who is the current captain of the [[South Africa national cricket team]] in [[Twenty20 International]] cricket and vice-captain in [[One Day International]] and [[Test cricket]]. Markram attended [[Cornwall Hill College]] briefly before attending [[Pretoria Boys High School]] to take advantage of its superior sporting history and facilities. Markram had captained the South African under-19 cricket team to win the [[2014 Under-19 Cricket World Cup|2014 ICC Under-19 Cricket World Cup]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/icc-under-19-world-cup-2014/content/story/723987.html|title=Aiden Markram leading South Africa U-19|publisher=ESPNcricinfo|date=5 March 2014}}</ref><ref title=Best-player Markram 'not at his best' | work=SuperSport | date=2 March 2014 | access-date=6 March 2014}}</ref> In the 2018 South African Cricket Annual, he was named as one of the five “Cricketers of the Year”.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://cricket.co.za/news/27248/Markram-Ngidi-named-among-SA-Cricket-Annuals-Top-Five |title=Markram, Ngidi named among SA Cricket Annual's Top Five which was formed in 2022, from its inception till his release ahead of the 2025 Auction, winning 2 consecutive titles in 2022 and 2023. Markram was a member of the South African team which won the [[2025 World Test Championship final|2025 ICC World Test Championship final]], the second ICC title the country has won till date, and was the Player of the Match, after scoring 136 (207) in the second innings.

==Domestic and franchise career==
Markram made his [[First-class cricket|first class]] debut for [[Northerns cricket team]] against [[South Western Districts cricket team|South Western Districts]] on 9 October 2014.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/783859.html |title=Sunfoil 3-Day Cup – Pool A: South Western Districts v Northerns at Oudtshoorn, 9–11 October 2014 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=31 October 2014 }}</ref> He was included in the Northerns cricket team squad for the [[2015 Africa T20 Cup]].<ref>[http://www.espncricinfo.com/africa-t20-cup-2015-16/content/squad/910903.html Northerns Squad / Players] – ESPNcricinfo. Retrieved 31 August 2015.</ref> In 2016, Markram was club professional for [[Walkden]] in the [[Bolton Cricket League]].

In May 2017, Markram was named Domestic Newcomer of the Year at [[Cricket South Africa]]'s annual awards.<ref name="awards">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/southafrica/content/story/1097632.html |title=De Kock dominates South Africa's awards |access-date=14 May 2017 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> In August 2017, he was named in [[Nelson Mandela Bay Stars]]' squad for the first season of the [[T20 Global League]].<ref name="T20GL">{{cite web|url=http://www.t20.gl/news/t20-global-league-announces-final-team-squads|title=T20 Global League announces final team squads|access-date=28 August 2017|work=T20 Global League|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170905185645/https://www.t20.gl/news/t20-global-league-announces-final-team-squads|archive-date=5 September 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> However, in October 2017, Cricket South Africa initially postponed the tournament until November 2018, with it being canceled soon after.<ref name="PP">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/southafrica/content/story/1123408.html |title=Cricket South Africa postpones Global T20 league |access-date=10 October 2017 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

In October 2018, Markram was named in [[Paarl Rocks]]' squad for the [[2018 Mzansi Super League|first edition]] of the [[Mzansi Super League]] T20 tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sport24.co.za/Cricket/live-mzansi-super-league-player-draft-20181017 |title=Mzansi Super League - full squad lists |work=Sport24 |access-date=17 October 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.iol.co.za/sport/cricket/domestic/mzansi-super-league-player-draft-the-story-so-far-17521199 |title=Mzansi Super League Player Draft: The story so far |work=Independent Online |access-date=17 October 2018}}</ref>

In March 2019, Markram signed for Hampshire County Cricket Club as their overseas player for the first part of the season.<ref>{{cite news |title=Aiden Markram: South Africa opener to join Hampshire as overseas player |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/47737330 |access-date=31 March 2019}}</ref> Later the same month, Markram scored 127 runs in the final of the [[2018–19 Momentum One Day Cup]], to help Titans win the tournament.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://cricket.co.za/news/29091/Markram-magic-leads-Titans-to-MODC-title |title=Markram magic leads Titans to MODC title |work=Cricket South Africa |access-date=31 March 2019 |archive-date=31 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190331162732/http://cricket.co.za/news/29091/Markram-magic-leads-Titans-to-MODC-title |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://cricket.co.za/news/29088/CSA-congratulates-Titans-on-MODC-triumph |title=CSA congratulates Titans on MODC triumph |work=Cricket South Africa |access-date=31 March 2019 |archive-date=31 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190331162732/http://cricket.co.za/news/29088/CSA-congratulates-Titans-on-MODC-triumph |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In September 2019, Markram was named in the squad for the [[Paarl Rocks]] team for the [[2019 Mzansi Super League]] tournament.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://cricket.co.za/news/31555/MSL-20-announces-its-T20-squads |title=MSL 2.0 announces its T20 squads |work=Cricket South Africa |access-date=4 September 2019 |archive-date=4 September 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190904081427/https://cricket.co.za/news/31555/MSL-20-announces-its-T20-squads |url-status=dead }}</ref> In April 2021, he was named in [[Northerns (cricket team)|Northerns]]' squad, ahead of the 2021–22 cricket season in South Africa.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://cricket.co.za/news/38184/CSA-reveals-Division-One-squads-for-2021-22 |title=CSA reveals Division One squads for 2021/22 |work=Cricket South Africa |access-date=20 April 2021 |archive-date=20 April 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210420104034/http://cricket.co.za/news/38184/CSA-reveals-Division-One-squads-for-2021-22 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On 11 September 2021, Markram was included in the [[Punjab Kings]] squad for the second phase of the [[2021 Indian Premier League]] (IPL) in the UAE.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dawid Malan pulls out, Punjab Kings replace him with Aiden Markram|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/ipl/top-stories/dawid-malan-pulls-out-punjab-kings-replace-him-with-aiden-markram/articleshow/86117041.cms|access-date=11 September 2021|work=The Times of India|date=11 September 2021 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Jonny Bairstow, Chris Woakes, Dawid Malan join Jos Buttler in pulling out of IPL|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-2021-jonny-bairstow-chris-woakes-dawid-malan-jos-buttler-out-of-ipl-1277604|access-date=11 September 2021|work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> In February 2022, he was bought by the [[Sunrisers Hyderabad]] in the [[List of 2022 Indian Premier League personnel changes|auction]] for the [[2022 Indian Premier League]] tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-2022-auction-the-list-of-sold-and-unsold-players-1300689 |title=IPL 2022 auction: The list of sold and unsold players |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=13 February 2022}}</ref>

After successfully leading [[Sunrisers Eastern Cape]] to the first [[SA20 (cricket)|SA20]] championship, Markram was appointed as the captain of [[Sunrisers Hyderabad]] for the 2023 season of the Indian Premier League.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cricket/sunrisers-hyderabad-appoint-aiden-markram-as-captain-ahead-of-ipl-2023-101677131017584.html |title=Sunrisers Hyderabad appoint Aiden Markram as captain ahead of IPL 2023|work=Hindustan Times|access-date=23 February 2023}}</ref>

He decided against being retained by the [[Sunrisers Eastern Cape]] for the [[2026 SA20]] and was bought by [[Durban's Super Giants]] in the auction for R14 million.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Moonda |first1=Firdose |title=Brevis, Markram earn record sums at SA20 2025-26 auction |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/dewald-brevis-aiden-markram-earn-record-sums-at-sa20-2025-26-auction-1502213 |website=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=10 September 2025}}</ref> On 13 September, 2025, he was named captain of the Durban's Super Giants for the 2026 SA20 season.

==International career==
===Early years===
In June 2017, Markram was named in South Africa's [[Test cricket|Test]] squad for their series [[South African cricket team in England in 2017|against England]], but did not play.<ref name="SKTest">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/india-v-korea-2017/content/story/1106145.html |title=Kuhn, Phehlukwayo in South Africa's Test squad |access-date=26 June 2017 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> In August 2017, he was named as [[captain (cricket)|captain]] of the [[South Africa A cricket team]] for their two four-day matches against India A.<ref name="SA4DaySquad">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/india-v-south-korea-2017/content/story/1115339.html |title=Quick turnaround for Markram with A-team captaincy |access-date=6 August 2017|work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

In September 2017, Markram was named in South Africa's Test squad for their series [[Bangladeshi cricket team in South Africa in 2017–18|against Bangladesh]].<ref name="SA-BanTest">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/south-africa-v-bangladesh-2017/content/story/1121546.html |title=Markram set for Test debut against Bangladesh |access-date=22 September 2017 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He made his Test debut for South Africa against Bangladesh on 28 September 2017.<ref name="Test">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1075502.html |title=1st Test, Bangladesh tour of South Africa at Potchefstroom, Sep 28-Oct 2 2017 |access-date=28 September 2017 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

After narrowly missing out on a maiden Test century on debut, Markram completed the feat in the second Test against Bangladesh on 6 October 2017 scoring 143 off 186 balls before being bowled by [[Rubel Hossain]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Markram quickly puts near-miss behind him|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/markram-quickly-puts-near-miss-behind-him-1123176|access-date=2021-07-04|work=ESPNcricinfo|language=en}}</ref>

In October 2017, Markram was added to South Africa's [[One Day International]] (ODI) squad ahead of the third match [[Bangladeshi cricket team in South Africa in 2017–18|against Bangladesh]], replacing [[Hashim Amla]].<ref name="Amla">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/south-africa-v-bangladesh-2017/content/story/1124245.html |title=Amla rested for final ODI; Markram called up |access-date=19 October 2017 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He made his ODI debut for South Africa against [[Bangladesh national cricket team|Bangladesh]] on 22 October 2017, scoring 66 runs as well as taking 2 wickets.<ref name="ODI">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1075506.html |title=3rd ODI, Bangladesh tour of South Africa at East London, Oct 22, 2017 |access-date=22 October 2017 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

In December 2017, Markram scored his second Test hundred and became the first South Africa player to score two centuries in his first three Tests.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/21885837/aiden-markram-record-breaking-start |title=Markram's record-breaking start|access-date=26 December 2017 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

===ODI captaincy===
In February 2018, South Africa's captain [[Faf du Plessis]] was ruled out of the last five ODIs and the [[Twenty20 International]] (T20I) series [[Indian cricket team in South Africa in 2017–18|against India]] due to a finger injury.<ref name="FdP-out">{{cite news |url=http://cricket.co.za/news/23251/Finger-injury-rules-Du-Plessis-out-of-India-ODI-and-T20-Series |title=Finger injury rules Du Plessis out of India ODI and T20 Series |work=Cricket South Africa |access-date=2 February 2018 |archive-date=3 February 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180203005831/http://cricket.co.za/news/23251/Finger-injury-rules-Du-Plessis-out-of-India-ODI-and-T20-Series |url-status=dead }}</ref> Markram was named as South Africa's captain for the remaining ODI fixtures in du Plessis' absence.<ref name="MarkramCapt">{{cite news|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/story/1135446.html |title=Aiden Markram to fill in as South Africa captain |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=3 February 2018}}</ref> He, at the age of 23 years 123 days, is the second youngest player to captain South Africa in ODIs after [[Graeme Smith]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/records/283415.html|title=Records. One-Day Internationals. Individual records (captains, players, umpires). Youngest captains |work=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=1 March 2018}}</ref>

===2018–2019===
On 30 March 2018, Markram scored his career-best score of 152 runs on the first day of the [[Australian cricket team in South Africa in 2017–18|fourth test]] against Australia.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.cricbuzz.com/cricket-news/101345/south-africa-vs-australia-4th-test-day-1-tea-aiden-markram-cricket-report|title=Markram's fourth ton adds to Australia's woes|work=Cricbuzz|access-date=30 March 2018|language=en}}</ref>

In June 2018, Markram was named in South Africa's [[Test cricket|Test]] squad for a two-Test series in Sri Lanka.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/23759192/steyn-returns-test-squad-sri-lanka-tour|title=Steyn returns to Test squad for SL tour|date=11 June 2018|work=ESPNcricinfo|language=en|access-date=11 February 2020}}</ref> Markram averaged just 10 with the bat in this series, his first overseas for South Africa, which showed a vulnerability against [[spin bowling]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/player/600498.html?class=1;series=12318;template=results;type=batting;view=innings|title=Batting records. Test matches  |work=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=11 February 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.news18.com/cricketnext/news/aiden-markram-a-great-start-but-challenges-still-remain-2002019.html|title=Aiden Markram: A Great Start but Challenges Still Remain|date=14 January 2019|website=News18|language=en|access-date=11 February 2020}}</ref>

In August 2018, Markram was named in South Africa's [[Twenty20 International]] (T20I) squad for the one-off match against [[Sri Lanka national cricket team|Sri Lanka]], but he did not play in the fixture.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/805967 |title=Chance for South Africa to finish Sri Lanka tour on a high |work=International Cricket Council |access-date=13 August 2018}}</ref> In March 2019, he was again named in South Africa's T20I squad, this time for the series [[Sri Lankan cricket team in South Africa in 2018–19|against Sri Lanka]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/story/1178250.html |title=Markram, Nortje, Qeshile called up for T20Is against Sri Lanka |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=17 March 2019}}</ref> He made his T20I debut for South Africa against Sri Lanka on 22 March 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1144173.html |title=2nd T20I (N), Sri Lanka tour of South Africa at Centurion, Mar 22, 2019 |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=22 March 2019}}</ref>

In April 2019, Markram was named in [[2019 Cricket World Cup squads#South Africa|South Africa's squad]] for the [[2019 Cricket World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/story/1181308.html |title=Hashim Amla in World Cup squad; Reeza Hendricks, Chris Morris miss out |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=18 April 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/1183187 |title=Amla edges out Hendricks to make South Africa's World Cup squad |work=International Cricket Council |access-date=18 April 2019}}</ref>

In August 2019, Markram was named in South Africa's squad for the three [[Test cricket|Test]] series in India.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/1310933|title=South Africa announces squads for India tour; de Kock to lead the team in T20Is|website=www.icc-cricket.com|language=en|access-date=11 February 2020}}</ref> Markram struggled in the first two matches of this series, bagging a [[Pair (cricket)|pair]] in the second Test, before being ruled out of the third due to a self-inflicted wrist injury.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/27848345/aiden-markram-theunis-de-bruyn-temba-bavuma-south-africa-crossroads|title=Aiden Markram, Theunis de Bruyn, Temba Bavuma and South Africa at a crossroads|date=15 October 2019|work=ESPNcricinfo|language=en|access-date=11 February 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/27863671/aiden-markram-ruled-third-test-self-inflicted-wrist-injury|title=Aiden Markram ruled out of third Test with self-inflicted wrist injury|date=17 October 2019|work=ESPNcricinfo|language=en|access-date=11 February 2020}}</ref> This series raised further questions about Markram's overseas performances, averaging just 10.50 in four away Tests, all in the [[Indian subcontinent|subcontinent]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/27857819/south-africa-act-quickly-arrest-opener-slide|title=Managing Markram: South Africa must act quickly to arrest opener's slide|date=16 October 2019|work=ESPNcricinfo|language=en|access-date=11 February 2020}}</ref>

In December 2019, Markram was named in South Africa's squad for the four-Test home series against England.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/50809358|title=South Africa v England: Proteas name six uncapped players in squad|date=16 December 2019|work=BBC Sport|access-date=11 February 2020|language=en-gb}}</ref> In the first Test, he scored 20 runs in the first innings and 2 in the second as South Africa beat England by 107 runs at [[SuperSport Park|Centurion]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/28372127/zubayr-hamza-strikes-pose-quinton-de-kock-lands-more-telling-blow|title=Zubayr Hamza strikes a pose before Quinton de Kock lands a more telling blow|date=26 December 2019|work=ESPNcricinfo|language=en|access-date=11 February 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/19430/report/1185304/south-africa-vs-england-1st-test-icc-world-test-championship-2019-2021|title=Recent Match Report - South Africa vs England, ICC World Test Championship, 1st Test |work=ESPNcricinfo|language=en|access-date=11 February 2020}}</ref> Markram however missed the remainder of the series after fracturing his finger.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/28380664/finger-fracture-puts-aiden-markram-remainder-england-series|title=Finger fracture puts Aiden Markram out of remainder of England series|date=28 December 2019|work=ESPNcricinfo|language=en|access-date=11 February 2020}}</ref>

===2021–2023===
In January 2021, Markram was named in South Africa's [[Test cricket|Test]] squad for their series [[South African cricket team in Pakistan in 2020–21|against Pakistan]].<ref>{{cite web |title=South Africa announce Test squad for series against Pakistan |url=https://www.geosuper.tv/latest/7624-south-african-announce-test-squad-for-series-against-pakistan |website=Geo}}</ref> In the first test, Markram scored a patient 74 in a losing effort.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1243017.html |title=1st Test, Karachi, Jan 26 - Jan 30 2021, South Africa tour of Pakistan |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=26 January 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Yasir Shah, Nauman Ali hand Pakistan advantage after Aiden Markram, Rassie van der Dussen fifties|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/south-africa-in-pakistan-2020-21-1242968/pakistan-vs-south-africa-1st-test-1243017/match-report|access-date=2021-02-08|work=ESPNcricinfo|language=en}}</ref> In the second test, Markram made his first century in more than two and a half years, and his first in Asia.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Centurion Markram bemoans South Africa's defeat despite having 'started making progress'|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/pak-vs-sa-2nd-test-rawalpindi-aiden-markram-bemoans-south-africa-defeat-despite-progress-1250772|access-date=2021-02-08|work=ESPNcricinfo|language=en}}</ref> Markram finished as the leading run scorer in the series, averaging 56.75, however South Africa lost the series, their first Test series defeat against Pakistan since 2003.<ref>{{Cite web|title=South Africa in Pakistan Test Series, 2020/21 Cricket Team Records & Stats |url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/batting/most_runs_career.html?id=13806&type=series|access-date=2021-02-08|work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Hasan Ali ten-for gives Pakistan first series win over South Africa since 2003|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/south-africa-in-pakistan-2020-21-1242968/pakistan-vs-south-africa-2nd-test-1243018/match-report|access-date=2021-02-08|work=ESPNcricinfo|language=en}}</ref>

In March 2023, he was appointed as the captain of [[South Africa national cricket team|South Africa cricket team]] in T20Is, ahead of their home series [[West Indian cricket team in South Africa in 2022–23|against the West Indies]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aiden Markram ready to fulfill his destiny |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/aiden-markram-ready-to-fulfil-his-destiny-1365167 |access-date=2023-03-26 |work=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref>

====2023 Cricket World Cup====
In October 2023 in a match against Sri Lanka, Markram scored the then fastest century in a men's [[Cricket World Cup]], reaching the milestone in 49 deliveries, a record later broken during the tournament by Australian batter [[Glenn Maxwell]]. He was dismissed soon after for 106 off 54.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Balasuriya |first=Madushka |date=7 Oct 2023 |title=Markram, van der Dussen and de Kock ton up as South Africa trump Sri Lanka in run-fest |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/icc-cricket-world-cup-2023-24-1367856/south-africa-vs-sri-lanka-4th-match-1384395/match-report |website=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

===2024–2025===
====2024 T20 World Cup====
In May 2024, he was named the captain in South Africa's squad for the [[2024 Men's T20 World Cup|2024 ICC Men's T20 World Cup]] tournament.<ref>{{Cite web |title=South Africa Squad for ICC Men's T20I World Cup |url=https://www.scorewaves.com/news-details/south-africa-squad-for-t20-world-cup |access-date=2024-06-11 |website=ScoreWaves |language=en}}</ref> He had a quiet tournament with the bat, but became the first ever Proteas captain to lead the team to the final of an [[Men's T20 World Cup|ICC Men's T20 World Cup]]. South Africa went on to lose the final to [[India national cricket team|India]].

====2025 World Test Championship Final====
He was named as the Player of the Final in the [[2025 World Test Championship final|2025 ICC World Test Championship final]] as South Africa defeated Australia by 5 wickets to win their maiden championship.<ref>{{cite web |access-date=14 June 2025 |title=Markram recounts epic Bavuma stand that turned the WTC25 Final |url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/tournaments/world-test-championship/news/markram-recounts-epic-bavuma-stand-that-turned-the-wtc25-final |work=International Cricket Council}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |access-date=14 June 2025 |title=History made at Lord's as South Africa triumph in WTC25 Final |url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/tournaments/world-test-championship/news/live-south-africa-on-brink-of-wtc25-final-victory-at-lord-s |work=International Cricket Council}}</ref>

===2025–2026===
In August 2025, he was named in the South Africa white ball squads to tour [[Australia national cricket team|Australia]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-07-24 |title=Proteas' big guns picked for Aussie white-ball tour {{!}} cricket.com.au |url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/4322610/south-africa-name-squads-white-ball-t20-odi-australia-tour-top-end-darwin-cairns-mackay-markram-rabada-bavuma |access-date=2026-03-25 |website=www.cricket.com.au |language=en}}</ref>

In September 2025, he was named in the Proteas white ball squads to tour [[England national cricket team|England]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=South Africa tour of England 2025 Squad |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/south-africa-in-england-2025-1448336/south-africa-odi-squad-1500165/series-squads |website=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

In September 2025, he was named captain of the Proteas squad to tour Pakistan, in absence of regular skipper [[Temba Bavuma]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=South Africa tour of Pakistan, 2025 |url=https://www.cricbuzz.com/cricket-series/10895/south-africa-tour-of-pakistan-2025/squads |website=cricbuzz}}</ref>

In November 2025, he was named in the Proteas Test squad [[South African cricket team in India in 2025–26|to tour India]]. In the second and last match, which South Africa won to complete a 2-0 clean sweep, he broke the record for the most catches in a Test match, with 9, surpassing [[Ajinkya Rahane|Rahane]]'s 8 in 2015.<ref>{{cite web |title=Most catches in a match |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/records/most-catches-in-a-match-283561 |access-date=24 November 2025 |website=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> In December 2025, Markram produced a pivotal innings for South Africa in the second ODI against India, keeping the series alive for his team at 1-1 (3). Having previously expressed responsibility for South Africa's shortcomings in the earlier match, Markram responded with a commanding century that restored confidence in the team and provided a solid platform for the team's middle order. His innings was credited with shifting momentum in South Africa's favour, with the match report noting a surge in belief within the squad as Markram set the stage for the team's more aggressive batters. Markram was declared Player of the Match.<ref>{{cite web |last=Moonda |first=Firdose |date=3 December 2025 |title=Belief surges for South Africa as Markram makes amends in style |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ind-vs-sa-belief-surges-for-south-africa-as-markram-makes-amends-in-style-1514270 |access-date=3 December 2025 |website=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> This chase also marked the third time South Africa has successfully chased 350 + runs in ODIs, matching India for the most such chases for any team.<ref>{{cite web |last=BandaruPalli |first=Sampath |date=3 December 2025 |title=Stats – Kohli with back-to-back tons again; SA ace record chase |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/stats-kohli-with-back-to-back-tons-yet-again-and-a-record-third-wicket-stand-1514231 |access-date=3 December 2025 |website=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

===2026–present===
====2026 T20 World Cup====
In January 2026, he was named captain of the South Africa squad to take part in the 2026 edition of the [[Men's T20 World Cup]] in [[India]] and [[Sri Lanka]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Moonda |first=Firdose |date=2 Jan 2026 |title=Rabada to lead strong South Africa pace attack at T20 World Cup |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/t20-world-cup-kagiso-rabada-anrich-nortje-quinton-de-kock-aiden-markram-dewald-brevis-in-south-africa-squad-1517789 |website=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> In the first match against [[Canada national cricket team|Canada]], he led his team to victory with 59 runs off 32 balls.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Miller |first=Andrew |date=9 Feb 2026 |title=Markram, Ngidi help South Africa ease past dogged Canada |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/icc-men-s-t20-world-cup-2025-26-1502138/canada-vs-south-africa-9th-match-group-d-1512727/match-report |website=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> In the third game, he led South Africa's chase with an unbeaten 86 off 44 balls, striking eight fours and four sixes, as his innings powered a seven-wicket win over [[New Zealand national cricket team|New Zealand]] in the [[2026 Men's T20 World Cup|2026 ICC Men's T20 World Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=South Africa's Markram mauls New Zealand in seven-wicket T20 World Cup win |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/2/14/south-africas-markram-mauls-new-zealand-at-t20-world-cup |access-date=2026-02-16 |website=Al Jazeera |language=en}}</ref> In the Super 8 stage of the tournament, he scored 82 not out off 46 balls as his team chased down 177 against the [[West Indies cricket team|West Indies]], securing semi final qualification.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-02-26 |title=T20 World Cup: South Africa stay unbeaten with nine-wicket win over West Indies |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/cricket/articles/cpw01ewydrqo |access-date=2026-03-02 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

'''Muhammad Ahsan Ali Khan'''{{Efn|[[Punjabi language|Punjabi]], {{langx|ur|محمد احسن علی خان}}}} (born December 13, 1990) is an American professional [[cricket]]er.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/54464652 |title=Ali Khan - meet the American international playing in the IPL |work=BBC Sport |access-date=October 12, 2020}}</ref> He has played for the [[United States national cricket team]] since 2016 as a right-arm [[Fast bowling|fast bowler]]. He has also played franchise [[Twenty20 cricket]] in the West Indies, Pakistan, India and the United Arab Emirates.

== Early life ==
Ali Khan was born and raised in [[Attock]], [[Punjab, Pakistan]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Acharya|first=Ayan|title=IPL 2020: USA's Ali Khan says getting picked in the IPL will be dream come true|url=https://sportstar.thehindu.com/cricket/ipl/muhammad-ahsan-ali-khan-usa-cricketer-ipl-auction-interview/article30212204.ece|access-date=September 24, 2020|website=Sportstar|date=December 6, 2019 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=September 12, 2020|title='Next Stop Dubai': USA Cricket's globetrotter Ali Khan sets foot on unique IPL dream|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/sports/ipl-2020/story/ipl-2020-ali-khan-usa-kkr-harry-gurney-1721234-2020-09-12|access-date=September 24, 2020|website=India Today|language=en}}</ref> At the age of 19, his family moved to the United States, settling in [[Ohio]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thecricketer.com/Topics/news/attock_face_united_states_cricket_ali_khan_in_his_own_words.html|title=Ali Khan interview: PSL, IPL, CPL, USA and everything in between | The Cricketer|website=www.thecricketer.com}}</ref> Before becoming a professional cricketer he worked as a sales representative for [[Cricket Wireless]] in [[Dayton, Ohio]].<ref name=resurrection/>

==International career==
Khan made his [[List A cricket|List A]] debut in January 2016, playing for the [[ICC Americas cricket team|ICC Americas]] team in the [[2015–16 Regional Super50]]. On debut against [[Jamaica national cricket team|Jamaica]], he took the wickets of [[Devon Thomas]] and [[Aldane Thomas]], finishing with 2/63 from ten overs.<ref>[http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/951657.html Nagico Super50, Group A: Jamaica v ICC Americas at St Augustine, Jan 9, 2016] – ESPNcricinfo. Retrieved January 13, 2016.</ref> Khan was the only member of the ICC Americas squad to have not previously played for his national team.<ref>Peter Della Penna (October 7, 2015). [http://www.espncricinfo.com/usa/content/story/926905.html "Taylor, Ghous picked in 15-man ICC Americas squad"] – ESPNcricinfo. Retrieved January 13, 2016.</ref> In July 2016 he was one of eleven uncapped players to be named for a USA selection camp ahead of the [[2016 ICC World Cricket League Division Four]] tournament in October.<ref name="camp">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/usa/content/story/1033385.html |title=Eleven uncapped players picked for USA national camp |access-date=July 7, 2016 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref> He made his debut for the U.S. national team against [[Oman national cricket team|Oman]] at the [[2016 ICC World Cricket League Division Four]] tournament in Los Angeles.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/wcl-division-4-2016-17-1062487/bermuda-vs-denmark-1062505/match-report|title=Timil five-for, Taylor century sees USA steamroll Oman|first=Peter|last=Della Penna|publisher=ESPNcricinfo|date=2 November 2016|access-date=6 June 2024}}</ref>

In 2016, Khan suffered a major injury to his left hamstring and had limited game time over the following two years due to this and other leg injuries.<ref name=resurrection>{{cite news|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/the-resurrection-of-ali-khan-1152608|title=The resurrection of Ali Khan|date=17 July 2018|access-date=6 June 2024|first=Peter|last=Della Penna|publisher=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

In August 2018, he was named in the United States' squad for the [[2018–19 ICC World Twenty20 Americas Qualifier]] tournament in [[Morrisville, North Carolina]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.usacricket.org/team-usa-men/team-usa-squad-selected-for-icc-world-t20-americas-qualifier/ |title=Team USA Squad Selected for ICC World T20 Americas' Qualifier |work=USA Cricket |date=August 22, 2018 |access-date=August 22, 2018}}</ref> In October 2018, he was named in the United States' squad for the [[2018 ICC World Cricket League Division Three]] tournament in Oman.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/25015081/hayden-walsh-jr-aaron-jones-usa-squad-wcl-division-three |title=Hayden Walsh Jr, Aaron Jones in USA squad for WCL Division Three |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=October 18, 2018}}</ref>

The [[International Cricket Council]] (ICC) named Khan as one of the five breakout stars in men's cricket in 2018<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/948077 |title=2018 lookback – the breakout stars (men) |work=International Cricket Council |access-date=January 1, 2019}}</ref> and in February 2019 he was named in the United States' [[Twenty20 International]] (T20I) squad for their series [[United States cricket team in the United Arab Emirates in 2018–19|against the United Arab Emirates]], but did not play due to injury concerns.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/26100265/xavier-marshall-recalled-usa-t20i-tour-uae |title=Xavier Marshall recalled for USA's T20I tour of UAE |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=February 28, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.usacricket.org/team-usa-men/team-usa-squad-announced-for-historic-dubai-tour/ |title=Team USA squad announced for historic Dubai tour |work=USA Cricket |date=February 28, 2019 |access-date=February 28, 2019}}</ref> The matches were the first T20I fixtures to be played by the United States cricket team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/1082175 |title=USA name squad for first-ever T20I |work=International Cricket Council |access-date=February 28, 2019}}</ref>

In April 2019, he was named in the United States cricket team's squad for the [[2019 ICC World Cricket League Division Two]] tournament in Namibia.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/media-releases/1173815 |title=All to play for in last ever World Cricket League tournament |work=International Cricket Council |access-date=April 11, 2019}}</ref> In the United States' second match of the tournament, against hosts [[Namibia national cricket team|Namibia]], Khan took his first [[five-wicket haul]] in [[List A cricket]]. He took five wickets for 63 runs from his ten overs, and was named the player of the match.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1174831.html |title=4th match, ICC World Cricket League Division Two at Windhoek, Apr 21 2019 |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=April 22, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/26575995/ali-khan-five-turns-namibia-chase-upside-two-run-thriller-usa |title=Ali Khan five-for turns Namibia chase upside down in two-run thriller for USA |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=April 22, 2019}}</ref> The United States finished in the top four places in the tournament, therefore gaining [[One Day International]] (ODI) status.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/media-releases/1196656 |title=Oman and USA secure ICC Men's Cricket World Cup League 2 places and ODI status |work=International Cricket Council |access-date=April 27, 2019}}</ref> Khan made his ODI debut for the United States on April 27, 2019, against [[Papua New Guinea national cricket team|Papua New Guinea]], in the tournament's third-place playoff.<ref name="ODI">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1174844.html |title=3rd Place Playoff, ICC World Cricket League Division Two at Windhoek, Apr 27 2019 |access-date=April 27, 2019 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref> He was the leading wicket-taker in the tournament, with 17 dismissals in six matches.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/bowling/most_wickets_career.html?class=5;id=12897;type=tournament |title=ICC World Cricket League Division Two, 2019, List A matches, Most wickets |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=April 27, 2019}}</ref>

In June 2019, he was named in a 30-man training squad for the [[United States national cricket team|United States cricket team]], ahead of the [[2018–19 ICC T20 World Cup Americas Qualifier#Regional Finals|Regional Finals]] of the [[2018–19 ICC T20 World Cup Americas Qualifier]] tournament in Bermuda.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/27009108/former-sa-pacer-rusty-theron-named-usa-squad |title=Former SA pacer Rusty Theron named in USA squad |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=June 19, 2019}}</ref> Later the same month, he was selected to play for the Vancouver Knights franchise team in the [[2019 Global T20 Canada]] tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.canadacricket.com/?p=12755 |title=Global T20 draft streamed live |work=Canada Cricket Online |date=June 20, 2019 |access-date=June 20, 2019}}</ref> In August 2019, he was named in the United States' squad for the [[2018–19 ICC T20 World Cup Americas Qualifier#Regional Finals|Regional Finals]] of the [[2018–19 ICC T20 World Cup Americas Qualifier]] tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.usacricket.org/team-usa-men/team-usa-squad-announced-for-icc-t20-world-cup-americas-regional-final/ |title=Team USA Squad Announced for ICC T20 World Cup Americas' Regional Final |work=USA Cricket |date=August 13, 2019 |access-date=August 13, 2019}}</ref>

In October 2021, he was named in the American [[Twenty20 International]] (T20I) squad for the [[2021 ICC Men's T20 World Cup Americas Qualifier]] tournament in Antigua.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.usacricket.org/team-usa-men/team-usa-mens-squad-named-for-t20-world-cup-americas-qualifier-in-antigua/ |title=Team USA Men's Squad Named for T20 World Cup Americas Qualifier in Antigua |work=USA Cricket |date=October 19, 2021 |access-date=October 20, 2021}}</ref> He made his T20I debut on 7 November 2021, for the United States against [[Panama national cricket team|Panama]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1286669.html |title=3rd Match, Coolidge, Nov 7 2021, ICC Men's T20 World Cup Americas Region Qualifier |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=7 November 2021}}</ref>

In April 2023, Khan received a two-match ban from the [[International Cricket Council]] (ICC) for a Level 1 breach of the ICC Code of Conduct, in relation to a send-off of [[Jersey cricket team|Jersey]] batsman [[Elliot Miles]] in the [[2023 Cricket World Cup Qualifier Play-off]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/usa-quick-ali-khan-banned-for-two-matches-after-breach-of-icc-code-1367721|title=Ali Khan banned for two matches after breach of ICC code|publisher=ESPNcricinfo|date=8 April 2023|accessdate=8 April 2023}}</ref>

In January 2026, Khan was named in USA's squad for the [[2026 ICC Men's T20 World Cup|2026 T20 World Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/media-releases/usa-announce-squad-for-icc-men-s-t20-world-cup-2026|title=USA announce squad for ICC Men’s T20 World Cup 2026|work=[[International Cricket Council]]|date=30 January 2026|access-date=2 February 2026}}</ref>

==Franchise career==
On June 3, 2018, he was selected to play for the Winnipeg Hawks in the players' draft for the [[2018 Global T20 Canada|inaugural edition]] of the [[Global T20 Canada]] tournament.<ref name="Squads2">{{cite web|url=https://www.crictracker.com/global-t20-canada-league-full-squads-announced/ |title=Global T20 Canada League – Full Squads announced |work=CricTracker |date=June 4, 2018 |access-date=June 4, 2018}}</ref> In October 2018, he was named in the squad for the [[Khulna Titans]] team, following the draft for the [[2018–19 Bangladesh Premier League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tigercricket.com.bd/2018/10/29/full-players-list-of-the-teams-following-players-draft-of-bpl-t20-2018-19/ |title=Full players list of the teams following Players Draft of BPL T20 2018–19 |work=Bangladesh Cricket Board |access-date=October 29, 2018}}</ref>

During the [[2020 Indian Premier League]], on its 13th Season, he was picked by [[Kolkata Knight Riders]]. He was first American cricketer who was bought in IPL auction but he did not play any IPL match.

On March 15, 2020, he debuted for [[Karachi Kings]] against [[Quetta Gladiators]] and conceded 1/36 in his 3 overs.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/psl-2019-20-2020-21-1211602/karachi-kings-vs-quetta-gladiators-30th-match-1211671/full-scorecard|title=Full Scorecard of Kings vs Gladiators 30th Match 2019/20-2020/21 - Score Report | ESPNcricinfo.com|website=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref><ref>[https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/1970/1970320/1970320.html Ali Khan], CricketArchive. Retrieved September 13, 2020. {{subscription required}}</ref>

During the [[2019 Caribbean Premier League]], Ali Khan was fined for an incident in the match between the [[Trinbago Knight Riders]] and [[St Kitts & Nevis Patriots]], where he was involved in a heated exchange with batsman [[Evin Lewis]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://trinidadexpress.com/sports/local/ali-khan-evin-lewis-lose-big-after-squaring-off-on-field/article_6b949ab2-da38-11e9-99dd-13b5297153c8.html|title=Ali Khan, Evin Lewis lose big $$ after squaring off on field|website=Trinidadexpress.com|date=September 18, 2019 |access-date=April 4, 2022}}</ref> In July 2020, he was named in the [[Trinbago Knight Riders]] squad for the [[2020 Caribbean Premier League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/29417692/nabi,-lamichhane,-dunk-earn-big-cpl-2020-draft |title=Nabi, Lamichhane, Dunk earn big in CPL 2020 draft |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=July 6, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.windiescricket.com/news/teams-selected-hero-cpl-2020/ |title=Teams Selected for Hero CPL 2020 |work=Cricket West Indies |access-date=July 6, 2020}}</ref> He was added to the [[Houston Hurricanes (cricket)|Houston Hurricanes]] for the 2021 Minor League Cricket season.<ref>{{Cite web|last=usacricket|date=September 2, 2020|title=17 of the 24 Squads Confirmed as Inaugural Minor League Cricket Draft is completed|url=https://www.usacricket.org/media-release/17-of-the-24-squads-confirmed-as-inaugural-minor-league-cricket-draft-is-completed/|access-date=September 2, 2020|website=USA Cricket|language=en-US}}</ref>

He played for the [[Los Angeles Knight Riders]] in the inaugural season of the [[Major League Cricket]] in 2023.

In July 2026, He was drafted by [[2026 Canada Super 60|Mississauga Masters]] for the [[2026 Canada Super 60]] season.<ref>{{Cite web | title=Teams announce their squads after 2026 Canada Super60 Draft {{!}} CricTracker | url=https://www.crictracker.com/cricket-news/teams-announce-their-squads-after-2026-canada-super60-draft-5881/ | access-date=2026-10-06 | website=www.crictracker.com}}</ref>

'''Andre Dwayne Russell''' (born 29 April 1988), nicknamed '''Dre Russ''', is a Jamaican former international cricketer who has played international [[cricket]] for the  [[West Indies cricket team|West Indies]] and for [[Jamaica national cricket team|Jamaica]] in domestic cricket as an [[all rounder (cricket)|all-rounder]]. He currently plays in various [[Twenty20|T20]] leagues around the world and periodically represented the [[West Indies cricket team|West Indies]] in [[Twenty20 International|T20is]]. Russell was part of the 2012 and 2016 [[ICC Men's T20 World Cup|ICC World T20]] winning West Indies teams. Russell is considered as one of the greatest cricketers in the [[Twenty20|T20]] format, notable for his powerful hitting, and capability to bowl at speeds consistently above 140 km/h.

==Domestic career==
In 2010 Russell played at Barnards Green Cricket Club in [[Worcestershire]], England, helping them secure promotion from [[Worcestershire Cricket League]] into [[Birmingham League cricket]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.barnardsgreen.com/2010champspics.html | title=Barnards Green Cricket Club – 2010 | publisher=Barnards Green Cricket Club | access-date=16 April 2016}}</ref>

==International career==
A [[fast bowling]] [[all-rounder]], Russell made his [[Test cricket]] debut against [[Sri Lanka national cricket team|Sri Lanka]] in November 2010.<ref name="JO">{{cite news|last=Myers|first=Sanjay|title=Great timing! – Russell cites destiny in journey into WI team|url=http://www.jamaicaobserver.com/sports/Great-timing-Russell-cites-destiny_8121424|access-date=15 November 2010|newspaper=[[Jamaica Observer]]|date=5 November 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101108135354/http://www.jamaicaobserver.com/sports/Great-timing-Russell-cites-destiny_8121424|archive-date=8 November 2010|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="TOIdebut">{{cite news|title=Windies elect to bat in first Sri Lanka Test|url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/top-stories/Windies-elect-to-bat-in-first-Sri-Lanka-Test/articleshow/6928235.cms|access-date=15 November 2010|newspaper=[[The Times of India]]|date=15 November 2010}}</ref> This is the only Test match of his career.

He made his [[One Day International]] (ODI) debut in the [[2011 Cricket World Cup]] match against [[Irish Cricket Team|Ireland]] at [[Mohali]]. After a poor home series against [[Pakistan cricket team|Pakistan]], he made his mark in the ODI series against [[Indian cricket team|India]].{{when|date=May 2019}} After being dropped from the first two ODIs, he scored 92 not out off 64 balls in the 3rd ODI after coming to the crease at 96/7. In the 5th ODI at [[Sabina Park]] in [[Kingston, Jamaica|Kingston]], he was named the [[Player of the Match]] as he took 4/35 (from 8.3 overs) to dismiss India for 251 in 47.1 overs.

He was named in the 'Team of the Tournament' for the 2016 T20 World Cup by the ICC, ESPNcricinfo and Cricbuzz.<ref>{{Cite web|title=ICC names WT20 Teams of the Tournament|url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/icc-world-t20-team-of-the-tournament-india-roy-de-kock-kohli-root-buttler-watson-russell/2016-04-04|access-date=11 July 2021|website=cricket.com.au|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=4 April 2016 |title=ESPNcricinfo's team of the 2016 World T20 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/icc-world-twenty20-2016/content/story/995203.html |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cricbuzz.com/cricket-news/79133/cricbuzz-team-of-the-icc-world-t20-2016|title=Cricbuzz Team of the ICC World T20, 2016|website=Cricbuzz|date=5 April 2016 }}</ref>

In April 2019, he was named in the [[2019 Cricket World Cup squads#West Indies|West Indies' squad]] for the [[2019 Cricket World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/26595791/andre-russell-west-indies-world-cup-squad,-kieron-pollard-misses-out |title=Andre Russell in West Indies World Cup squad, Kieron Pollard misses out |work=ESPNcricinfo |date=24 April 2019 |access-date=24 April 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/1194397 |title=Andre Russell picked in West Indies' World Cup squad |work=International Cricket Council |access-date=24 April 2019}}</ref> In the West Indies match against [[Australia national cricket team|Australia]], Russell became the quickest batsman, in terms of balls faced, to score 1,000 runs in ODIs, facing only 767 deliveries.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.firstpost.com/firstcricket/sports-news/highlights-australia-vs-west-indies-icc-cricket-world-cup-2019-match-full-cricket-score-aaron-finch-and-co-register-15-runs-win-6760861.html |title=Highlights, Australia vs West Indies, ICC Cricket World Cup 2019 Match, Full Cricket Score: Aaron Finch and Co register 15 runs win |work=First Cricket |date=6 June 2019 |access-date=6 June 2019}}</ref> However, on 24 June 2019, Russell was ruled out of the rest of the tournament, due to a knee injury, and was replaced by [[Sunil Ambris]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/27043847/injured-andre-russell-rest-world-cup |title=Injured Andre Russell out of rest of the World Cup |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=24 June 2019}}</ref>

On 9 July 2021, during the first T20I against Australia, Russell scored his maiden T20I half-century. He scored 51 off 28 balls and helped West Indies post 145 before being dismissed by [[Josh Hazlewood]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Obed McCoy takes four wickets after Andre Russell's fifty as West Indies fight back to beat Australia|url=https://www.skysports.com/cricket/news/12040/12352804/obed-mccoy-takes-four-wickets-after-andre-russells-fifty-as-west-indies-fight-back-to-beat-australia|access-date=11 July 2021|website=Sky Sports|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Australia lose 6 for 19 as McCoy, Walsh give West Indies 1–0 lead|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/australia-tour-of-west-indies-2021-1263143/west-indies-vs-australia-1st-t20i-1263156/match-report|access-date=11 July 2021|work=ESPNcricinfo|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Full Scorecard of West Indies vs Australia 1st T20I 2021 – Score Report |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/australia-tour-of-west-indies-2021-1263143/west-indies-vs-australia-1st-t20i-1263156/full-scorecard|access-date=11 July 2021|work=ESPNcricinfo|language=en}}</ref>

In September 2021, Russell was named in the West Indies' squad for the [[2021 ICC Men's T20 World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/t20-world-cup-2021-ravi-rampaul-back-in-west-indies-squad-sunil-narine-left-out-1277122 |title=T20 World Cup: Ravi Rampaul back in West Indies squad; Sunil Narine left out |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=9 September 2021}}</ref>

On 13 December 2023, Russell made a comeback into the [[West Indies Cricket Team|West Indies]] team after a two-year hiatus against [[England national cricket team|England]] in the T20I series at home, getting the man of the match performance in his comeback match.

On 13 February, in the 3rd T20I against  [[Australian national cricket team|Australia]], he scored his highest score in t20i's, 71(29) as he and [[Sherfane Rutherford]] kept the scoreboard ticking and had a partnership of 139 for the sixth wicket.

In May 2024, he was named in the West Indies squad for the [[2024 ICC Men's T20 World Cup]] tournament.<ref>{{Cite web |title=West Indies has announced their Squad for the T20I World Cup |url=https://www.scorewaves.com/news-details/west-indies-cricket-team-west-indies-squad |access-date=7 June 2024 |website=ScoreWaves |language=en}}</ref> On 17 July 2025, he announced his retirement from all forms of international cricket.<ref>{{cite web |access-date=16 July 2025 |title=Andre Russell announces international cricket retirement |url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/andre-russell-set-to-retire-from-international-cricket |work=International Cricket Council}}</ref>

==T20 franchise career==
Russell has played in over 300 T20 matches and appeared for teams in a number of franchise leagues. He was also named in the T20 XI of the years 2016 and 2018 by ESPNcricinfo.<ref>{{Cite web|date=30 December 2016|title=The trump cards of 2016|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/review2016/content/story/1073990.html|access-date=11 July 2021|work=ESPNcricinfo|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=3 January 2019|title=The pick of the pack|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/review2018/content/story/1169902.html|access-date=11 July 2021|work=ESPNcricinfo|language=en}}</ref>

===Indian Premier League===
[[File:Andre Russell (3).jpg|left|thumb|Andre Russell in India in 2015]]
During the [[2012 Indian Premier League]] Players Auction, he was bought by the [[Delhi Daredevils]] for a sum of $450,000.<ref>{{cite web|title=IPL auction 2012|url=http://cricket.yahoo.com/news/ipl-auctions--big-bucks-for-jadeja--no-takers-for-laxman.html|access-date=4 February 2012}}</ref> Ahead of the 2014 season he was bought by [[Kolkata Knight Riders]] and has been seen as a key batsman for the team in the later overs of matches. For his performances in 2015, he was named in the ESPNcricinfo IPL XI for the season.<ref>{{Cite web|title=The IPL 2015 tournament XI|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/the-ipl-2015-tournament-xi-881033|access-date=11 July 2021|work=ESPNcricinfo|date=25 May 2015 |language=en}}</ref> He was on course to win the IPL Super Striker award in 2018, awarded for having the highest strike rate in the tournament, before being pipped by his teammate [[Sunil Narine]]. He eventually won it next year in the 2019 IPL, where he had a record IPL season strike rate{{clarify|date=May 2019}} of over 205, and was also announced as the Player of the Tournament. In an otherwise unsuccessful season, he emerged as both the highest run scorer and the highest wicket taker for his team, while also being the third-highest run-scorer in the tournament. He hit 52 sixes in the tournament; only [[Chris Gayle]] and [[Vaibhav Sooryavanshi]] have hit more sixes in any single season of the IPL.<ref name="IPLT20">{{cite web | url=https://www.iplt20.com/teams/kolkata-knight-riders/squad/177/Andre-Russell/ | title=Andre Russell | publisher=[[IPLT20.com]] | access-date=31 March 2019 | archive-date=13 November 2021 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211113054205/https://www.iplt20.com/teams/kolkata-knight-riders/squad/177/andre-russell | url-status=dead }}</ref> For his performances in the 2019 IPL season, he was named in the ESPNcricinfo IPL XI.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dhoni, Russell, Pandya in ESPNcricinfo's power-packed IPL XI|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/dhoni-russell-pandya-in-espncricinfo-s-power-packed-ipl-xi-1184320|access-date=22 April 2021|work=ESPNcricinfo|date=13 May 2019 |language=en}}</ref>

On 13 April 2021, he took figures of 5/15 off just two overs in a match against [[Mumbai Indians]] during the [[2021 Indian Premier League]]. With the bat, he scored 9 runs off 15 balls as Kolkata lost the game by 10 runs.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Rahul Chahar, Suryakumar Yadav, Trent Boult star as Mumbai Indians pull off unlikely win|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/ipl-2021-1249214/kolkata-knight-riders-vs-mumbai-indians-5th-match-1254062/match-report|access-date=22 April 2021|work=ESPNcricinfo|date=13 April 2021 |language=en}}</ref>

Having played for the Knight Riders from [[IPL 2014]] to [[IPL 2025]], Russell announced his retirement from IPL cricket on 30 November 2025.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.news18.com/cricket/andre-russell-announces-retirement-from-ipl-ws-l-9740387.html |title=Andre Russell Announces Retirement From IPL |work=[[News18]] |date=30 November 2025 |access-date=30 November 2025}}</ref>

===Other T20 leagues===
On 16 August 2016 Russell scored the fastest [[Caribbean Premier League]] century, completing his 100 in 42 balls.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dawntoday.com/andre-russel-makes-record-100-42-balls/|title= Andre Russell makes record 100 in 42 balls|publisher=Dawn Today|date=6 August 2016|access-date=8 August 2016}}</ref> He broke his own CPL record in 2018 with a century in 40 balls.<ref name="Russell's hat-trick and hundred">{{cite web |author=Peter Della Penna |date=11 August 2018 |title=Recent Match Report – Trinbago Knight Riders vs Jamaica Tallawahs, Caribbean Premier League, 3rd Match |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/8623/report/1148649/trinbago-knight-riders-vs-jamaica-tallawahs-3rd-match-caribbean-premier-league-2018 |access-date=31 March 2019 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

In May 2018, he was named as one of the ten marquee players for the [[2018 Global T20 Canada|first edition]] of the [[Global T20 Canada]] cricket tournament.<ref name="marquee1">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/story/1147584.html |title=Steven Smith named as marquee player for Canada T20 tournament |access-date=24 May 2018 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref><ref name="marquee2">{{cite web |url=http://www.sportingnews.com/other-sports/news/steve-smith-australia-cricket-global-t20-canada-ball-scuffing-scandal/1k2lxwrnwsazj1wj8ylmuejdbm |title=Steve Smith named as marquee player for Global T20 Canada |access-date=24 May 2018 |work=Sporting News |archive-date=18 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180618052357/http://www.sportingnews.com/other-sports/news/steve-smith-australia-cricket-global-t20-canada-ball-scuffing-scandal/1k2lxwrnwsazj1wj8ylmuejdbm |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was selected to play for the Vancouver Knights.<ref name="Squads2">{{cite web|url=https://www.crictracker.com/global-t20-canada-league-full-squads-announced/ |title=Global T20 Canada League – Full Squads announced |work=CricTracker |date=4 June 2018 |access-date=4 June 2018}}</ref>

In September 2018, he was named as the Icon Player for Nangarhar's squad in the [[2018–19 Afghanistan Premier League|first edition]] of the [[Afghanistan Premier League]] tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.crictracker.com/afghanistan-premier-league-2018-all-you-need-to-know-from-the-player-draft/ |title=Afghanistan Premier League 2018 – All you need to know from the player draft |work=CricTracker |date=10 September 2018 |access-date=10 September 2018}}</ref> The following month, he was named in the squad for the [[Dhaka Dynamites]] in the [[2018–19 Bangladesh Premier League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tigercricket.com.bd/2018/10/29/full-players-list-of-the-teams-following-players-draft-of-bpl-t20-2018-19/ |title=Full players list of the teams following Players Draft of BPL T20 2018–19 |work=Bangladesh Cricket Board |access-date=29 October 2018}}</ref> In June 2019, he was selected to play for the Vancouver Knights franchise team in the [[2019 Global T20 Canada]] tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.canadacricket.com/?p=12755 |title=Global T20 draft streamed live |work=Canada Cricket Online |date=20 June 2019 |access-date=20 June 2019}}</ref>

In July 2020, he was named in the [[Jamaica Tallawahs]] squad for the [[2020 Caribbean Premier League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/29417692/nabi,-lamichhane,-dunk-earn-big-cpl-2020-draft |title=Nabi, Lamichhane, Dunk earn big in CPL 2020 draft |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=6 July 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.windiescricket.com/news/teams-selected-hero-cpl-2020/ |title=Teams Selected for Hero CPL 2020 |work=Cricket West Indies |access-date=6 July 2020}}</ref> In October 2020, he was drafted by the Colombo Kings for the [[2020 Lanka Premier League|inaugural edition]] of the [[Lanka Premier League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/30148161/lanka-premier-league-2020-chris-gayle-andre-russell-shahid-afridi-big-names-taken-lpl-draft |title=Chris Gayle, Andre Russell and Shahid Afridi among big names taken at LPL draft |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=22 October 2020}}</ref> In April 2021, he was signed by [[Quetta Gladiators]] to play in the rescheduled matches in the [[2021 Pakistan Super League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/psl-2021-replacement-draft-lahore-qalandars-bag-shakib-al-hasan-quetta-gladiators-sign-andre-russell-1261441 |title=Lahore Qalandars bag Shakib Al Hasan, Quetta Gladiators sign Andre Russell |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=28 April 2021}}</ref>

Russell was picked by [[Southern Brave]] for the 2021 edition of [[The Hundred (cricket)|The Hundred]] before he withdrew due to international commitments.<ref>{{cite web |title=Colin de Grandhomme replaces Andre Russell at Southern Brave |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/57839015 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=27 August 2024 |date=14 July 2021}}</ref> In April 2022, he was bought by the [[Manchester Originals]] for the [[2022 The Hundred season|next season of The Hundred]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/60477088 |title=The Hundred 2022: latest squads as Draft picks revealed |work=BBC Sport |access-date=5 April 2022}}</ref>

He plays for the [[Trinbago Knight Riders]] in the 2023 Republic bank [[Caribbean Premier League]]. He garnered a strike rate of 167.05 and contributed 11 wickets over 9 appearances to the Knight Riders making it to the finals.<ref>tkriders.com/players/andre-russell-profile-12047</ref> He was picked by Los Angeles Knight Riders for the inaugural edition of Major League Cricket.

On 3 February 2025, in the 11th edition of the [[Bangladesh Premier League|BPL]], Andre Russell joined Rangpur to play a playoff match. However, neither he nor his team performed well in that match resulting in [[Rangpur Riders]] elimination from the tournament.

==Doping==
According to the Jamaica Anti-Doping Commission (JADCO), in 2016 Russell committed an "[[anti-doping whereabouts]]" violation after missing three doping tests in a 12-month period.<ref name="whereabouts">{{cite web | url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/westindies/content/story/977957.html | title=Andre Russell faces possible ban from cricket for 'anti-doping whereabouts' violation | work=ESPNcricinfo | date=2 March 2016 | access-date=16 April 2016}}</ref> On 31 January 2017, Russell was banned from cricket for one year.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gollapudi |first=Nagraj |date=31 January 2017 |title=Andre Russell banned for one year for doping-code violation |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/andre-russell-banned-for-one-year-for-doping-code-violation-1080431 |access-date=31 January 2017 |work=ESPNcricinfo |publisher=ESPN}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Russell married American model Jassym Lora in 2016; the couple have a daughter.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/life-style/parenting/pregnancy/cricketer-andre-russell-just-made-the-coolest-birth-announcement-and-you-have-to-watch-it/articleshow/71182486.cms|title=Cricketer Andre Russell just made the coolest birth announcement and you have to watch it!|work=[[The Times of India]]|date=18 September 2019 |access-date=20 September 2019}}</ref>

==Outside cricket==
In 2014, Russell began a second career as a recording artist under the name 'Dre Russ', with two singles released in November, one a collaboration with [[Beenie Man]].<ref>Morgan, Simone (2014) "[http://www.jamaicaobserver.com/entertainment/Andre-Russell-bowling-lyrics_17956106 Andre Russell Bowling Lyrics] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190327091050/http://www.jamaicaobserver.com/entertainment/Andre-Russell-bowling-lyrics_17956106 |date=27 March 2019 }}", ''[[Jamaica Observer]]'', 18 November 2014. Retrieved 18 November 2014</ref>

'''Anrich Arno Nortje''' (born 16 November 1993) is a South African [[cricket]]er. He made his international debut for the [[South Africa national cricket team|South Africa cricket team]] in March 2019.<ref name="Bio">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/481979.html |title=Anrich Nortje |access-date=21 September 2016 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> In July 2020, Nortje was named the newcomer of the year at [[Cricket South Africa]]'s annual awards ceremony.<ref>{{cite web |title=Quinton de Kock, Laura Wolvaardt scoop up major CSA awards |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/quinton-de-kock-laura-wolvaardt-scoop-up-major-csa-awards-1226217 |access-date=4 July 2020 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

==Domestic and T20 franchise career==
He was included in [[Eastern Province cricket team|Eastern Province]]'s squad for the [[2016 Africa T20 Cup]].<ref name="Eastern Province">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/squad/1058002.html |title=Eastern Province Squad |access-date=21 September 2016 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> In October 2018, he was named in [[Cape Town Blitz]]'s squad for the [[2018 Mzansi Super League|first edition]] of the [[Mzansi Super League]] T20 tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sport24.co.za/Cricket/live-mzansi-super-league-player-draft-20181017 |title=Mzansi Super League - full squad lists |work=Sport24 |access-date=17 October 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.iol.co.za/sport/cricket/domestic/mzansi-super-league-player-draft-the-story-so-far-17521199 |title=Mzansi Super League Player Draft: The story so far |work=Independent Online |access-date=17 October 2018}}</ref> Midway through the tournament, he was ruled out with an ankle injury.<ref>{{cite web |title=Injured Anrich Nortje leaves his imprint at MSL |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/injured-anrich-nortje-leaves-his-imprint-at-mzansi-super-league-1167451 |access-date=29 November 2018 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> In December 2018, he was bought by the [[Kolkata Knight Riders]] in the [[List of 2019 Indian Premier League personnel changes|player auction]] for the [[2019 Indian Premier League]].<ref>{{cite web |title=IPL 2019 auction: The list of sold and unsold players |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-2019-auction-the-list-of-sold-and-unsold-players-1166896 |access-date=18 December 2018 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/ipl/top-stories/ipl-auction-2019-who-got-whom/articleshow/67144375.cms |title=IPL 2019 Auction: Who got whom |work=The Times of India |access-date=18 December 2018}}</ref> However, in March 2019, he was ruled out of the tournament with a shoulder injury.<ref>{{cite web |title=South Africa quick Anrich Nortje ruled out of IPL |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/south-africa-quicks-anrich-nortje-and-lungi-ngidi-ruled-out-of-ipl-1178529 |access-date=20 March 2019 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

In September 2019, he was named in the squad for the [[Cape Town Blitz]] team for the [[2019 Mzansi Super League]] tournament.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://cricket.co.za/news/31555/MSL-20-announces-its-T20-squads |title=MSL 2.0 announces its T20 squads |work=Cricket South Africa |access-date=4 September 2019 |archive-date=4 September 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190904081427/https://cricket.co.za/news/31555/MSL-20-announces-its-T20-squads |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was released by the Kolkata Knight Riders ahead of the [[List of 2020 Indian Premier League personnel changes|2020 IPL auction]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Where do the eight franchises stand before the 2020 auction? |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/where-do-the-eight-franchises-stand-before-the-2020-auction-1206731 |access-date=15 November 2019 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> In July 2020, he was named in the [[St Lucia Zouks]] squad for the [[2020 Caribbean Premier League]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Mohammad Nabi, Sandeep Lamichhane, Ben Dunk earn big in CPL 2020 draft |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/mohammad-nabi-sandeep-lamichhane-ben-dunk-earn-big-in-cpl-2020-draft-1226284 |access-date=6 July 2020 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.windiescricket.com/news/teams-selected-hero-cpl-2020/ |title=Teams Selected for Hero CPL 2020 |work=Cricket West Indies |access-date=6 July 2020}}</ref> However, Nortje was one of five South African cricketers to miss the tournament, after failing to confirm travel arrangements in due time.<ref>{{cite web |title=Five South Africans to miss CPL after failing to confirm travel arrangements |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/five-south-africans-to-miss-cpl-after-failing-to-confirm-travel-arrangements-1227948 |access-date=28 July 2020 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> In August 2020, Nortje joined the [[Delhi Capitals]] as a replacement for [[Chris Woakes]] in the [[2020 Indian Premier League]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-08-18|title=IPL 2020: Delhi Capitals replace Chris Woakes with Anrich Nortje|url=https://www.crictracker.com/ipl-2020-delhi-capitals-replace-chris-woakes-with-anrich-nortje/|access-date=2020-08-18|website=CricTracker|language=en}}</ref> On 14 October 2020, during the 30th match of the [[2020 Indian Premier League|2020 IPL]], Nortje bowled at the speed of 156.22 km/h (97 mph) to [[Jos Buttler]] of [[Rajasthan Royals]], the fastest delivery to date in the IPL.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-10-15|title=IPL 2020: This bowler delivers the fastest ball in IPL history at 156.22 kmph, breaks Dale Steyn's record. In IPL 2020 He Scored Seven Runs and Picked Up 22 Wickets|url=https://zeenews.india.com/cricket/ipl-2020-this-bowler-delivers-the-fastest-ball-in-ipl-history-at-156-22-kmph-breaks-dale-steyns-record-2317483.html|access-date=2020-10-15|website=Zee News|language=en}}</ref>

In April 2021, he was named in [[Eastern Province (cricket team)|Eastern Province]]'s squad, ahead of the 2021–22 cricket season in South Africa.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://cricket.co.za/news/38184/CSA-reveals-Division-One-squads-for-2021-22 |title=CSA reveals Division One squads for 2021/22 |work=Cricket South Africa |access-date=20 April 2021 |archive-date=20 April 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210420104034/http://cricket.co.za/news/38184/CSA-reveals-Division-One-squads-for-2021-22 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

He was selected for the [[Washington Freedom (cricket)|Washington Freedom]] squad in March 2023, ahead of the inaugural season of [[Major League Cricket]] in USA. In November 2024, he was again picked by [[Kolkata Knight Riders]] for 6.50 crores INR in the [[List of 2025 Indian Premier League personnel changes|2025 player auction]] for the [[2025 Indian Premier League]].

==International career==
In February 2019, he was named in South Africa's [[One Day International]] (ODI) squad for their series [[Sri Lankan cricket team in South Africa in 2018–19|against Sri Lanka]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Fit-again Lungi Ngidi back in South Africa's ODI squad, Hashim Amla left out |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/fit-again-lungi-ngidi-back-in-south-africa-s-odi-squad-hashim-amla-left-out-1175911 |access-date=24 February 2019 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He made his ODI debut for South Africa against [[Sri Lanka national cricket team|Sri Lanka]] on 3 March 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1144167.html |title=1st ODI, Sri Lanka tour of South Africa at Johannesburg, Mar 3 2019 |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=3 March 2019}}</ref> In March 2019, he was named in South Africa's [[Twenty20 International]] (T20I) squad also for the series against Sri Lanka,<ref>{{cite web |title=Aiden Markram, Anrich Nortje, Sinethemba Qeshile called up for T20Is against Sri Lanka |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/aiden-markram-anrich-nortje-sinethemba-qeshile-called-up-for-t20is-against-sri-lanka-1178250 |access-date=17 March 2019 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> but was ruled out of T20I series due to injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/1110673 |title=New-look South Africa seek series win |work=International Cricket Council |access-date=21 March 2019}}</ref>

In April 2019, he was named in [[2019 Cricket World Cup squads#South Africa|South Africa's squad]] for the [[2019 Cricket World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Hashim Amla in World Cup squad; Reeza Hendricks, Chris Morris miss out |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/hashim-amla-in-world-cup-squad-reeza-hendricks-chris-morris-miss-out-1181308 |access-date=18 April 2019 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/1183187 |title=Amla edges out Hendricks to make South Africa's World Cup squad |work=International Cricket Council |access-date=18 April 2019}}</ref> However, on 7 May 2019, he was ruled out of the tournament with a hand injury and was replaced by [[Chris Morris (cricketer)|Chris Morris]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/1212131 |title=Chris Morris replaces Anrich Nortje in South Africa's CWC19 squad |work=International Cricket Council |access-date=7 May 2019}}</ref>

In August 2019, he was named in South Africa's [[Test cricket|Test]] and [[Twenty20 International]] (T20I) squads for their series [[South African cricket team in India in 2019–20|against India]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Nortje, Second and Muthusamy part of South Africa squads to India |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/nortje-second-and-muthusamy-part-of-test-squad-to-india-no-faf-for-t20is-1197305 |access-date=13 August 2019 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He made his T20I debut for South Africa, against [[India national cricket team|India]], on 18 September 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1187005.html |title=2nd T20I (N), South Africa tour of India at Mohali, Sep 18 2019 |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=18 September 2019}}</ref> He made his Test debut for South Africa, also against India, on 10 October 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1187008.html |title=2nd Test, ICC World Test Championship at Pune, Oct 10-14 2019 |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=10 October 2019}}</ref> In January 2020, in the fourth Test [[English cricket team in South Africa in 2019–20|against England]], Nortje took his maiden [[five-wicket haul]] in Test cricket.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cricket.co.za/news/34141/England-outclass-Proteas-after-Nortje-fifer |title=England outclass Proteas after Nortje fifer |work=Cricket South Africa |access-date=26 January 2020}}</ref> In March 2020, he was awarded with a national contract by [[Cricket South Africa]] ahead of the 2020–21 season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Beuran Hendricks earns CSA national contract, Dale Steyn left out 2020}}</ref>

In September 2021, Nortje was named in South Africa's squad for the [[2021 ICC Men's T20 World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/t20-world-cup-south-africa-leave-out-faf-du-plessis-and-imran-tahir-and-chris-morris-1276995 |title=T20 World Cup: South Africa leave out Faf du Plessis, Imran Tahir and Chris Morris |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=9 September 2021}}</ref> In September 2023, he was named in South Africa's squad for the 2023 Cricket World Cup, but was ruled out later due to injury.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-09-21 |title=South Africa face enormous setback as Anrich Nortje ruled out of 2023 World Cup; Proteas make 2 late changes to squad |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cricket/south-africa-face-enormous-setback-as-anrich-nortje-ruled-out-of-2023-world-cup-proteas-make-2-late-changes-to-squad-101695280064059.html |access-date=2023-11-14 |website=Hindustan Times |language=en}}</ref>
