'''Aqib Ilyas Sulehri''' (born 5 September 1992) is a Pakistani-born [[cricket]]er who has played for the [[Oman national cricket team]] since 2015.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.independenturdu.com/node/81991|title='نا تجربہ کار' ٹیموں کے چھپے رستم|date=18 October 2021|website=Independent Urdu}}</ref><ref name="bio">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/940593.html |title=Aqib Ilyas |access-date=15 January 2017 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref> He is a right-handed top-order batsman and also bowls off-spin.

==Personal life==
Ilyas was born on 5 September 1992 in [[Sialkot]], [[Pakistan]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.independenturdu.com/node/82171|title=ٹی 20 ورلڈ کپ: دوسری ٹیموں میں چمکتے پاکستانی ستارے|date=20 October 2021|website=[[Independent Urdu]]}}</ref> He is the younger brother of [[Adnan Ilyas]] who also played international cricket for Oman.<ref name=radley>{{cite news|url=https://www.thenationalnews.com/sport/cricket/2021/10/18/t20-world-cup-aqib-ilyas-making-oman-proud-after-slipping-through-net-in-uae/|title=T20 World Cup: Aqib Ilyas making Oman proud after slipping through net in UAE|newspaper=The National|location=Abu Dhabi|date=18 October 2021|access-date=25 June 2023|first=Paul|last=Radley}}</ref>

His family moved to Oman when Ilyas was six months old. He grew up in [[Muscat]]. In 2010 he moved to [[Dubai]] to attend university, studying civil engineering. He was invited to train with the [[United Arab Emirates national cricket team]], but opted to return to Oman after completing his degree.<ref name=radley/>

In 2021, Ilyas found a tumour on his ankle bone. It was removed via surgery and confirmed as benign, but required a rehabilitation period of 18 months.<ref name=cancer>{{cite news|url=https://www.thenationalnews.com/sport/cricket/2023/06/22/life-first-then-cricket-for-aqib-ilyas-after-recovering-from-bone-cancer-scare/|title='Life first, then cricket' for Aqib Ilyas after recovering from bone cancer scare|newspaper=The National|location=Abu Dhabi|date=22 June 2023|access-date=25 June 2023}}</ref>

==Career==
Ilyas made his [[Twenty20 International]] (T20I) debut for Oman [[Hong Kong cricket team against Oman in the UAE in 2015–16|against Hong Kong]] on 21 November 2015.<ref name="T20I">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/930575.html |title=Hong Kong tour of United Arab Emirates, 1st T20I: Hong Kong v Oman at Abu Dhabi, Nov 21, 2015 |access-date=21 November 2015 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref>

In January 2018, he was named in Oman's squad for the [[2018 ICC World Cricket League Division Two]] tournament.<ref name="OmanWCL2">{{Cite web|url=http://timesofoman.com/article/125576/Sports/Cricket/Cricket-Three-debutants-in-Oman-squad-for-WCL-Division-2-in-Namibia |title=Cricket: Three debutants in Oman squad for WCL Division 2 |access-date=9 January 2018 |work=Times of Oman}}</ref> He made his [[List A cricket|List A]] debut for Oman against [[Canada national cricket team|Canada]] on 8 February 2018.<ref name="LA">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1133931.html |title=3rd match, ICC World Cricket League Division Two at Windhoek, Feb 8 2018 |access-date=8 February 2018 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref>

In August 2018, he was named in Oman's squad for the [[2018 Asia Cup Qualifier]] tournament.<ref name="OmanACQ">{{cite web|url=https://timesofoman.com/article/139366 |title=Cricket: Maqsood to lead Oman at Asia Cup Qualifiers in Malaysia |work=Times of Oman |access-date=6 August 2018}}</ref> He was the leading run-scorer for Oman in the tournament, with 186 runs in five matches.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/averages/batting_bowling_by_team.html?class=15;id=12550;team=37;type=tournament |title=Asia Cup Qualifiers, 2018/19: Oman / Minor cricket (one-day/limited overs) / Batting and bowling averages |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=4 September 2018}}</ref> In October 2018, he was named in Oman's squad for the [[2018 ICC World Cricket League Division Three]] tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://timesofoman.com/article/328633/Sports/Cricket/Maqsood-to-lead-Oman-in-ICC-WCL-Division-3 |title=Cricket: Maqsood to lead Oman in ICC WCL Division 3 |work=Times of Oman |access-date=27 October 2018}}</ref> He scored a century in Oman's match against the [[United States national cricket team|United States]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/story/1165681.html |title=Oman secure promotion with win over USA; Kenya deny Singapore's thrilling charge |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=16 November 2018}}</ref> In December 2018, he was named in Oman's team for the [[2018 ACC Emerging Teams Asia Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/squad/1167676.html |title=Oman Under-23s Squad |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=3 December 2018}}</ref>

In March 2019, he was named in Oman's team for the [[2019 ICC World Cricket League Division Two]] tournament in Namibia.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.omancricket.org/oman-confident-winning-odi-status-finishing-among-top-four-icc-wcl-two/ |title=Oman confident of winning ODI status by finishing among top four in ICC WCL Two |work=Oman Cricket |access-date=27 March 2019}}</ref> Oman finished in the top four places in the tournament, therefore gaining [[One Day International]] (ODI) status.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/media-releases/1196656 |title=Oman and USA secure ICC Men's Cricket World Cup League 2 places and ODI status |work=International Cricket Council |access-date=27 April 2019}}</ref> Ilyas made his ODI debut for Oman on 27 April 2019, against [[Namibia national cricket team|Namibia]], in the tournament's final.<ref name="ODI">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1174845.html |title=Final, ICC World Cricket League Division Two at Windhoek, Apr 27 2019 |access-date=21 November 2015 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref> He was the leading run-scorer for Oman in the tournament, with 168 runs in six matches.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/averages/batting_bowling_by_team.html?class=5;id=12897;team=37;type=tournament |title=ICC World Cricket League Division Two, 2019 - Oman, List A matches: Batting and bowling averages |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=27 April 2019}}</ref>

In September 2019, he was named as the vice-captain of Oman's squad for the [[2019 ICC T20 World Cup Qualifier]] tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://timesofoman.com/article/1925941/Sports/Oman-squad-for-ICC-T20-WC-Qualifier-in-UAE-announced |title=Oman squad for ICC T20 WC Qualifier in UAE announced |work=Times of Oman |access-date=15 September 2019}}</ref> Ahead of the tournament, the [[International Cricket Council]] (ICC) named him as the player to watch in Oman's squad.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/1451570 |title=Team preview: Oman |work=International Cricket Council |access-date=16 October 2019}}</ref> In November 2019, he was named as vice-captain of Oman's squad for the [[2019 ACC Emerging Teams Asia Cup]] in Bangladesh.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.omancricket.org/kaleem-replaces-maqsood-captain-acc-emerging-teams-asia-cup/ |title=Kaleem replaces Maqsood as captain for ACC Emerging Teams' Asia Cup |work=Oman Cricket |access-date=12 November 2019}}</ref>

On 9 February 2020, in the [[2020 Nepal Tri-Nation Series]] match against [[Nepal national cricket team|Nepal]], Ilyas scored an unbeaten 109 runs from 108 balls.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1215125.html |title=28th Match, ICC Men's Cricket World Cup League 2 at Kirtipur, Feb 9 2020 |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=9 February 2020}}</ref> It was the first century by a batsman for Oman in ODI cricket.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cricketeurope.com/DATABASE/ARTICLESTOURNAMENTS/articles/000001/000198.shtml |title=All-round Ilyas takes Oman to top of table |work=Cricket Europe |access-date=9 February 2020 |archive-date=25 May 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200525230737/https://www.cricketeurope.com/DATABASE/ARTICLESTOURNAMENTS/articles/000001/000198.shtml |url-status=dead }}</ref> Two days later, against the [[United States national cricket team|United States]], Ilyas scored his second century in as many matches, with 105 runs.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cricketeurope.com/DATABASE/ARTICLESTOURNAMENTS/articles/000001/000199.shtml |title=Ilyas stars again as Oman beat USA |work=Cricket Europe |access-date=11 February 2020 |archive-date=27 February 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200227190145/https://www.cricketeurope.com/DATABASE/ARTICLESTOURNAMENTS/articles/000001/000199.shtml |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In September 2021, he was named as the vice-captain of Oman's squad for the [[2021 ICC Men's T20 World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/2246807 |title=Oman announce experienced 15-member group for T20 World Cup |work=International Cricket Council |access-date=8 September 2021}}</ref>

In May 2024, Ilyas was named as the captain of Oman's squad for the [[2024 ICC Men's T20 World Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Oman Announces T20 World Cup Squad: Aqib Ilyas Takes Captaincy |url=https://www.scorewaves.com/news-details/oman-cricket-team-icc-mens-t20i-world-cup-squad-for-t20-world-cup |access-date=2024-06-03 |website=ScoreWaves |language=en}}</ref>

'''Azmatullah Omarzai''' ([[Pashto]]: عظمت الله عمرزی born 24 March 2000) is an Afghan [[cricket]]er from [[Nurgal District]] of [[Kunar Province|Kunar]] province in eastern [[Afghanistan]]. Azmatullah started playing cricket when he was 14 years old. He won the [[ICC Men's ODI Cricketer of the Year]] award in 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last=icc |date=2025-01-27 |title=All-rounder named ICC Men's ODI Cricketer of the Year |url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/all-rounder-named-icc-men-s-odi-cricketer-of-the-year |access-date=2025-02-28 |website=www.icc-cricket.com |language=en}}</ref>

He made his international debut for the [[Afghanistan national cricket team|Afghanistan cricket team]] in January 2021.<ref name="Bio">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/819429.html |title=Azmatullah Omarzai |access-date=10 August 2017 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref> He was part of the Afghan team in the [[Cricket World Cup|2023 Cricket World Cup]].

He was awarded the [[ICC Men's ODI Cricketer of the Year]] in the [[2024 ICC Awards]].<ref>{{cite web |title=All-rounder named ICC Men's ODI Cricketer of the Year |url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/all-rounder-named-icc-men-s-odi-cricketer-of-the-year |access-date=27 January 2025 |work=[[International Cricket Council]]}}</ref>

==Domestic career==
He made his [[List A cricket|List A]] debut for [[Mis Ainak Region cricket team|Mis Ainak Region]] in the [[2017 Ghazi Amanullah Khan Regional One Day Tournament]] on 10 August 2017.<ref name="LA">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1115760.html |title=2nd Match, Ghazi Amanullah Khan Regional One Day Tournament at Khost, Aug 10, 2017 |access-date=10 August 2017 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref> He made his [[first-class cricket|first-class]] debut for [[Speen Ghar Tigers|Speen Ghar Region]] in the [[2018 Ahmad Shah Abdali 4-day Tournament]] on 25 March 2018.<ref name="FC">{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1137701.html |title=14th Match, Alokozay Ahmad Shah Abdali 4-day Tournament at Kunar, Mar 25-28 2018 |publisher=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=27 March 2018}}</ref>

In September 2018, he was named in Paktia's squad in the [[2018–19 Afghanistan Premier League|first edition]] of the [[Afghanistan Premier League]] tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.crictracker.com/afghanistan-premier-league-2018-all-you-need-to-know-from-the-player-draft/ |title=Afghanistan Premier League 2018 – All you need to know from the player draft |work=CricTracker |access-date=10 September 2018|date=10 September 2018 }}</ref> He made his [[Twenty20]] debut for Paktia Panthers in the 2018–19 Afghanistan Premier League on 7 October 2018.<ref name="T20">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1160572.html |title=4th Match (D/N), Afghanistan Premier League at Sharjah, Oct 7 2018 |access-date=7 October 2018 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref> In September 2020, he was the joint winner of the player of the tournament award in the [[2020 Shpageeza Cricket League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cricket.af/post/ayobi-kabul-eagles-lift-shpageeza-title-in-a-thrilling-final/english |title=Ayobi Kabul Eagles lift Shpageeza Title in a thrilling Final |work=Afghanistan Cricket Board |access-date=16 September 2020}}</ref>

==International career==
In December 2017, he was named in Afghanistan's squad for the [[2018 Under-19 Cricket World Cup]].<ref name="AfghanistanU19">{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/21701404/mujeeb-zadran-afghanistan-squad-19-world-cup |title=Mujeeb Zadran in Afghanistan squad for Under-19 World Cup |access-date=7 December 2017 |work=ESPN Cricinfo|date=7 December 2017 }}</ref> He was part of Afghanistan's under-23 team in the [[2018 ACC Emerging Teams Asia Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/squad/1167699.html |title=Afghanistan Under-23s Squad |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=3 December 2018}}</ref> In November 2019, he was named in http://www.cricbuzz.com/cricket-news/115511/afghanistan-announce-16-member-squad-for-odi-series-against-ireland |work=Cricbuzz |access-date=2 January 2021}}</ref> He made his ODI debut for tour of United Arab Emirates |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=21 January 2021}}</ref>

In March 2021, the [[Afghanistan Cricket Board]] confirmed that he was pending selection for the T20I matches [[Zimbabwean cricket team against Afghanistan in the UAE in 2020–21|against Zimbabwe]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cricket.af/post/afghanistan-t20i-squad-announced-albeit-visa-issues-for-some-players- |title=Afghanistan T20I squad announced albeit visa issues for Some Players |work=Afghanistan Cricket Board |access-date=14 March 2021}}</ref> once his visa issues had been resolved.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/afg-vs-zim-t20i-series-mujeeb-ur-rahman-gulbadin-naib-wait-on-visa-issue-1254985 |title=Mujeeb Ur Rahman, Gulbadin Naib wait on 'visa issue' ahead of T20I series |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=16 March 2021}}</ref> In February 2022, he was named in Afghanistan's T20I squad for their series [[Afghan cricket team in Bangladesh in 2021–22|against Bangladesh]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cricbuzz.com/cricket-news/121057/nabi-included-in-odi-squad-for-bangladesh-series |title=Nabi included in ODI squad for Bangladesh series |work=CricBuzz |access-date=14 February 2022}}</ref> He made his T20I debut on 3 March 2022, for Afghanistan against [[Bangladesh national cricket team|Bangladesh]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1299832.html |title=1st T20I (D/N), Mirpur, Mar 3 2022, Afghanistan tour of Bangladesh |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=3 March 2022}}</ref>

'''Ben Angus Mayes''' (born 21 November 2007) is an English [[cricket]]er who plays for [[Hampshire County Cricket Club]]. He is a right-handed batsman, a [[wicket-keeper]] and right-arm off spin bowler.

==Career==
Mayes played junior club cricket for [https://lyndhurstashurst.play-cricket.com/home Lyndhurst and Ashurst CC] and [https://tottonandelingcc.co.uk/ Totton and Eling CC] in Hampshire and joined the [[Hampshire County Cricket Club]] talent pathway as an Under 8, making his Hampshire Academy debut in May 2023, at the age of 15 years-old. He was a member of the Hampshire Academy squad that won the Southern Premier League title for the first time, in 2024.<ref name="lewis">{{cite web|url= https://www.hampshirechronicle.co.uk/sport/25345597.hampshire-academys-ben-mayes-signs-first-professional-deal/?callback=in&code=ZTBJZTQWMGITOTHMNS0ZNTDILTGZZDMTMDHLM2M1NDM0N2Y2&state=cd08a6c0db074593a024bef6e256236f|website=Hampshire Chronicle|accessdate=25 August 2025|title= Hampshire Academy's Ben Mayes signs first professional deal|date=28 July 2025}}</ref>

Mayes made his youth international debut against Ireland in September 2024.<ref>{{cite web|website=Hampshire Chronicle|url= https://www.hampshirechronicle.co.uk/sport/24843937.two-hampshire-players-selected-england-mens-u19-squad/|title= Two Hampshire players selected for England Men's U19 squad|accessdate=25 August 2025|date=9 Jan 2025}}</ref> He toured with the [[England national under-19 cricket team]] to South Africa in January 2025 and earned the Player of the Match award in the first Youth ODI.<ref>{{cite web|website=BBC Sounds|accessdate=25 August 2025|url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sounds/play/p0khl83k |title=Solent Sport - 17 year old Ben Mayes on first England Under 19 trip|date=9 January 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|website=Basingstoke Gazette|url= https://www.basingstokegazette.co.uk/sport/25345668.hampshire-cricket-academy-star-ben-mayes-signs-pro-deal/|accessdate=25 August 2025|title= Hampshire Cricket Academy star Ben Mayes signs pro deal|date=28 July 2025

'''Ben Stewart McKinney''' (born 4 October 2004) is an English [[cricket]]er who plays for [[Durham County Cricket Club]] and is a former captain of the [[England under-19 cricket team]]. He is a left-handed batsman and a right-arm off break bowler.

==Early life==
McKinney was a youth team footballer for [[Sunderland F.C.|Sunderland]] before focusing on cricket. McKinney attended [[Seaham High School]] and played for Seaham Harbour Cricket Club, playing age-group cricket for [[Durham County Cricket Club|Durham]] from the under-11 age-group.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.durhamcricket.co.uk/players-and-staff/ben-mckinney|title=Ben McKinney|website=Durham Cricket|accessdate=May 21, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thetimes.com/sport/cricket/article/ben-mckinney-interview-durham-england-sunderland-height-rz2mfldj6|website=The Times|accessdate=28 April 2026|title= Meet 6ft 7in ex-footballer who could become England's tallest batsman|first=John|last=Westerby|date=28 April 2026}}</ref>

==Domestic career==
McKinney made his debut in the [[County Championship]] against [[Sussex County Cricket Club|Sussex]] in April 2023, and made 35 in his first innings.<ref>{{Cite web|title= T20 Blast 2023: Young players to watch|first=Scott|last=Duke-Giles|date=May 19, 2023|accessdate=May 21, 2023|website=The Cricketer|url=
https://www.thecricketer.com/Topics/t20blast/t20_blast_2023_young_players_watch.html}}</ref> He made his [[List A cricket]] debut for Durham on 1 August 2023, against [[Worcestershire County Cricket Club|Worcestershire]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=1 August 2023 |title=Worcestershire defeat Durham despite Liam Trevaskis hat-trick |url=https://www.thecricketer.com/Topics/royal_london_one_day_cup/worcestershire_defeat_durham_despite_liam_trevaskis_hat-trick.html |access-date=1 August 2023 |website=The Cricketer}}</ref> On 4 August 2023 it was announced that McKinney had signed a two-year professional contract with Durham.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thecricketer.com/Topics/countycricket/promising_youngster_ben_mckinney_pens_professional_terms_with_durham.html|website=The Cricketer|first=Joe|last=Turner|date=4 August 2023|accessdate=4 August 2023|title= Promising youngster Ben McKinney pens professional terms with Durham}}</ref> He scored a maiden century for Durham against Kent in the One-Day Cup on 11 August 2024.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.durhamcricket.co.uk/news-and-media/ben-mckinney-scores-maiden-durham-century-with-drissell-and-ackermann-spinning-durham-to-victory-over-kent/ |date=11 August 2024|title=Ben McKinney scores maiden Durham century with Drissell and Ackermann spinning Durham to victory over Kent|accessdate=28 April 2026|website=Durhamcricket.co.uk}}</ref> Later that month, he also scored his maiden first-class century against Notts.<ref>{{cite web|website= bbc.com|title=
County Championship: McKinney & Lees put Durham on top against Notts|accessdate=28 April 2026|date=22 Aug 2024|url= https://www.bbc.com/sport/cricket/articles/cw4yzd0lmkpo

May 1991) is a New Zealand professional cricketer who plays as a right handed [[Batting (cricket)|batter]] and right-arm [[Fast bowling|medium bowler]] for the [[New Zealand national cricket team|New Zealand national team]] and [[Canterbury cricket team|Canterbury]]. {{As of|2026|June}}, he is signed with [[Rawalpindiz]] in the [[Pakistan Super League]]. Having begun his domestic career in 2011 with [[Northern Districts men's cricket team|Northern Districts]] and made his international debut in 2019, Mitchell represented several teams across [[Limited overs cricket|limited-overs]] leagues around the world. Outside of cricket, heas a fitness coach at the [[Waikato Rugby Union]]. His father, [[John Mitchell (rugby union)|John]], is a rugby union coach and former player. == Early life == He was still pursuing his [[bachelor's degree]] in exercise and sports science when he turned up at Northern Districts in 2012 at the age of 20.{{Cite news |title=NZ's structure has nurtured Mitchell on & off pitch |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/cricket/63541567 |access-date=2023-01-28}} He lived in [[Perth]], Western Australia for five of his formative years and he even shared the field with some of the Australian cricketers including the likes of [[Andrew Tye]], [[Marcus Harris (cricketer)|Marcus Harris]] and [[Marcus Stoinis]] especially through the school and grade ranks in Western Australia.{{Cite web |title=Kiwi's Aussie connection has Mitchell feeling right at home |url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/daryl-mitchell-new-zealand-perth-australia-hale-roots-stoinis-world-cup-semi-final/2022-11-07 |access-date=2023-01-28 |website=cricket.com.au |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Old Scarborough friends Mitchell and Stoinis to take field as international foes |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/t20-world-cup-final-old-scarborough-friends-daryl-mitchell-and-marcus-stoinis-turn-international-foes-1288932 |access-date=2023-01-28 |work=ESPNcricinfo}} In March 2009, Daryl Mitchell, Marcus Stoinis and [[Justin Langer]] sat together as team-mates in the changerooms at the [[WACA Ground|WACA]] celebrating a first-grade premiership for [[Scarborough Cricket Club (Australia)|Scarborough]]. During his three years with Hale in school cricket and two years with Scarborough at club cricket, Mitchell also played for the Western Australia Under 19s, Under 23s and for the Australian Centre of Excellence, which was part of a Futures League T20 competition. Following his impressive showing in Australian third grade level competitions, he received a contract from Northern Districts which he gladly accepted and since became a regular in New Zealand domestic circuit. As a teenager, he and his family moved to Western Australia in 2006 when his father John, got the position of head coach of the Western Force rugby union team. == Domestic career == In June 2018, he was awarded a contract with [[Northern Districts men's cricket team|Northern Districts]] for the 2018–19 season.{{cite massive New Zealand win |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=26 March 2021}} === 2021 ICC T20 World Cup === In August 2021, Mitchell was named in New Zealand's squad for the [[2021 ICC Men's T20 World Cup]].{{cite web|url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/cricket/black-caps/126013220/black-caps-announce-twenty20-world-cup-squad-two-debutants-for-leadup-tours-with-stars-absent |title=Black Caps announce Guptill]] during the entirety of the 2021 ICC Men's T20 World Cup although a role he had never done before. He had played in 116 T20 matches prior to the 2021 ICC T20 World Cup where he had never opened the batting in any of those matches.{{Cite web |title=Half a season in the Blast, then blast-off for the lesser-searched Daryl Mitchell |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/t20-world-cup-ind-vs-nz-half-a-season-in-the-blast-then-blast-off-for-the-lesser-searched-daryl-mitchell-1286434 |access-date=2023-01-28 |work=ESPNcricinfo}} He was promoted to open the innings during the 2021 edition of the T20 World Cup by the then head coach [[Gary Stead]]. Prior to the 2021 T20 World Cup, New Zealand coaching staff and management intended to give Mitchell the finishing role in the middle order along with [[Jimmy Neesham]].{{Cite web |title=Taylor left out of T20 World Cup squad; NZ pick Chapman, Todd Astle among 15 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ross-taylor-left-out-of-t20-world-cup-squad-nz-pick-mark-chapman-todd-astle-among-15-1272726 |access-date=2023-01-28 |work=ESPNcricinfo}} However, the plans had to be changed later, courtesy of late arrival of first choice opener [[Tim Seifert]] who joined the [[bio-secure bubble]] pity late due to the latter's involvement with the [[Kolkata Knight Riders]] franchise during the [[2021 Indian Premier League]] and as a result, Daryl Mitchell went onto become an accidental opener of New Zealand cricket.{{Cite web |title=The accidental opener: Daryl Mitchell is relishing his role at the top |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/t20-world-cup-2021-the-accidental-opener-new-zealands-daryl-mitchell-relishing-his-role-at-the-top-1286525 |access-date=2023-01-28 |work=ESPNcricinfo}} In the team's semi-final against England, he opened the batting and scored 72 [[not out]], with New Zealand winning the match by five wickets; Mitchell was awarded the [[Player of the Match awards (cricket)|player of the match]].{{cite web|url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/cricket/black-caps/126945277/daryl-mitchell-stars-as-black-caps-surge-late-to-stun-england-in-t20-world-cup-semifinal |title=Daryl Mitchell stars as Black Caps surge late to stun England in T20 World Cup semifinal |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=10 November 2021 |access-date=10 November 2021}} He ended the 2021 |work=ESPNcricinfo}} === 2022 England test tour === Mitchell maintained a highly successful [[New Zealand cricket team in England in 2022|test tour to England in July 2022]] where he piled up a mammoth runfest aggregating a record 538 runs with a stellar average of 107.60 in the three match test series although New Zealand ended the test tour on a receiving end after being whitewashed by the home team 3–0.{{Cite web |title=Daryl Mitchell proud to have stood tall for New Zealand in 'heavyweight boxing fight' |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/england-vs-nz-3rd-test-daryl-mitchell-proud-to-have-stood-tall-for-new-zealand-in-heavyweight-boxing-fight-1321368 |access-date=2023-01-28 |work=ESPNcricinfo}} Mitchell turned out to be one of the only two bright sparks alongside [[Tom Blundell (cricketer)|Tom Blundell]] for the Kiwis during the one sided test series where he scored three centuries in three successive test matches and he went past [[Martin Donnelly (sportsman)|Martin Donnelly]]'s tally of 462 runs to become the most prolific New Zealand player to have ever scored the most runs in a single test series on English soil against England.{{Cite web |title=Batting records. Test matches. Most runs for New Zealand by a batter in a test series in England |url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/stats/index.html?class=1;filter=advanced;opposition=1;orderby=runs;team=5;template=results;tournament_type=2;type=batting;view=series |access-date=2023-01-28 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}{{Cite web |title=How Black Caps pair changed the course of England test |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/sport/cricket-how-daryl-mitchell-and-tom-blundell-changed-the-course-of-england-test/ZBBATYTJSPN2VGQOPUS4TM35BM/ |access-date=2023-01-28 |website=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |language=en-NZ}} He also became the first New Zealand batsman to score centuries in three consecutive test matches in England and became only the sixth visiting batsman to score centuries in three successive test match appearances in England.{{Cite web |title=Stats - Daryl Mitchell's successive hundreds, and a record pairing with Tom Blundell |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/england-vs-nz-3rd-test-stats-daryl-mitchell-successive-hundreds-and-a-record-pairing-with-tom-blundell-1321356 |access-date=2023-01-28 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}{{Cite web |date=2022-06-24 |title=Mitchell's record-breaking run in ENG |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/visualstories/sports/mitchells-record-breaking-run-in-eng-8061-24-06-2022 |access-date=2023-01-28 |website=www.indiatoday.in |language=en}} He also became the first batter in the world to score hundreds in each match of an away series of three or more tests. During the test series, he along with wicket-keeper batsman Tom Blundell set a new record for New Zealand for being the most successful New Zealand pair in a test series with an aggregate of 611 partnership runs.{{Cite web |title=Mitchell, Blundell and Leach achieve career-best Test rankings |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/icc-test-rankings-eng-vs-nz-daryl-mitchell-tom-blundell-and-jack-leach-achieve-career-best-rankings-1322228 |access-date=2023-01-28 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}{{Cite news |title=Cricket: Daryl Mitchell, Tom Blundell repay selectors' faith as Blackcaps' best in poor England series |language=en |work=[[Newshub]] |url=https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/sport/2022/06/cricket-daryl-mitchell-tom-blundell-repay-selectors-faith-as-blackcaps-best-in-poor-england-series.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230128090217/https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/sport/2022/06/cricket-daryl-mitchell-tom-blundell-repay-selectors-faith-as-blackcaps-best-in-poor-england-series.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=28 January 2023 |access-date=2023-01-28}} His tally of 538 runs in the three-match test series also set a new record for most runs among New Zealand batsmen in a test series.{{Cite web |title=Underplayed to the point of parody, is Daryl Mitchell the uber-Kiwi? |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/england-vs-nz-2nd-test-underplayed-to-the-point-of-parody-is-daryl-mitchell-the-uber-kiwi-1319404 |access-date=2023-01-28 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}{{Cite web |title=Daryl Mitchell unfazed by dip in fortune after posting career-best 190 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/england-vs-new-zealand-2022-daryl-mitchell-unfazed-by-dip-in-fortune-after-posting-career-best-190-1319568 |access-date=2023-01-28 |work=ESPNcricinfo}} Prior to the England test series in July 2022, Mitchell had not played a red ball first-class match in four months and was not in contention for a test spot for the England tour but was included for the first test match of the series at Lord's later as a replacement to [[Henry Nicholls (cricketer)|Henry Nicholls]] whose positive COVID-19 test had played a part in delaying his rehabilitation from a calf injury.{{Cite web |last=reporters |first=Stuff sports |date=2022-05-26 |title=Daryl Mitchell helps case for place in Black Caps for 1st test versus England |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/cricket/black-caps/128775054/daryl-mitchell-helps-case-for-place-in-black-caps-for-1st-test-versus-england |access-date=2023-01-28 |website=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |language=en}} === 2022 ICC T20 World Cup === In September 2022, Mitchell was named in [[2022 ICC Men's T20 World Cup squads|New Zealand's squad]] for the [[2022 ICC Men's T20 World Cup]].{{Cite web |title=New Zealand announce their squad for the T20 World Cup |url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/2797310 |access-date=2023-01-28 |website=www.icc-cricket.com |language=en}}{{cite web |title=Guptill set for record 7th T20 World Cup. Allen & Bracewell included for first time |url=https://www.nzc.nz/news-items/guptill-set-for-record-7th-t20-world-cup-allen-bracewell-included-for-first-time |access-date=2023-01-28 |website=New Zealand Cricket |archive-date=10 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221010225454/https://www.nzc.nz/news-items/guptill-set-for-record-7th-t20-world-cup-allen-bracewell-included-for-first-time |url-status=dead }} === 2023 Cricket World Cup === In September 2023, he was included in New Zealand's 15-member squad for the 50-over World Cup in India. He played a remarkable role in the 2023 Cricket World Cup and almost won the match for New Zealand in the semi final against India by scoring a wonderful 134 off 119 balls.{{Cite web |title=World Cup New Zealand Squad: Check Team New Zealand World Cup Squad 2023. HT Cricket |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cricket/world-cup/team-squad |access-date=2023-11-14 |website=Hindustan Times |language=en}} === 2024 ICC T20 World Cup === In May 2024, he was named in New Zealand's squad for the [[2024 ICC Men's T20 World Cup]] tournament.{{Cite web |title=New Zealand Squad for ICC Men’s World Cup 2024 |url=https://www.scorewaves.com/news-details/new-zealand-squad-icc-mens-world-up-2024-new-zealand-jersey |access-date=2024-06-10 |website=ScoreWaves |language=en}} === 2025–present === On 19 November 2025, he overtook [[Rohit Sharma]] to become the world No. 1 batter in the ICC Men's ODI Rankings. He became the second Kiwi ever to claim the top ranking, 46 years after [[Glenn Turner]] in 1979.{{cite web |date=19 November 2025 |title=Rohit Sharma's No 1 ODI ranking lasts only 22 days as Daryl Mitchell achieves historic first |url=https://www.msn.com/en-in/sports/cricket/rohit-sharma-s-no-1-odi-ranking-lasts-only-22-days-as-daryl-mitchell-achieves-46-year-old-first/ar-AA1QJ1cQ |access-date=22 November 2025 |website=MSN |publisher=Microsoft}} He continued his strong form in New Zealand's [[New Zealand cricket team in India in 2025–26|2026 ODI series against India]], hitting 352 runs, including two consecutive centuries in the second and third matches, and was named the player of the series. New Zealand won the series 2–1, their first ODI series in India.{{Cite news |date=2026-01-15 |title=Daryl Mitchell Stars With Century As New Zealand Script Record Chase vs India, Take ODI Series To Decider |url=https://sports.ndtv.com/india-vs-new-zealand-2026/daryl-mitchell-stars-with-century-as-new-zealand-script-record-chase-vs-india-take-odi-series-to-decider-10751000 |access-date=2026-01-15 |work=NDTV}}{{Cite web |last=Kumar |first=Saurabh |date=2026-01-18 |title=IND vs NZ: Daryl Mitchell boosts No.1 ODI hopes with back-to-back centuries vs India |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/sports/cricket/story/daryl-mitchell-back-to-back-centuries-against-india-new-zealand-3rd-odi-2853834-2026-01-18 |access-date=2026-01-19 |website=India Today |language=en}}{{Cite web |last=Krishnaswamy |first=Karthik |date=18 January 2026 |title=Mitchell, Phillips centuries trump Kohli's as New Zealand win first-ever ODI series in India |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/new-zealand-in-india-2025-26-1490228/india-vs-new-zealand-3rd-odi-1490233/match-report |website=ESPNcricinfo}} == List of International Cricket Centuries == Daryl Mitchell has scored 15 international centuries - 6 in [[Test Cricket]] , and 9 in [[One Day Internationals]]. === Test Cricket Centuries === {| class="wikitable sortable" |- ! '''David Andrew Miller''' (born 10 June 1989) is a South African professional [[cricket]]er. He currently plays for South African national team in [[limited overs cricket]]. He is an aggressive left-handed middle order batsman and an occasional wicket-keeper. He holds the record for the second fastest T20I century among full member ICC teams against full member opposition, tied with [[Rohit Sharma]], achieving the milestone in 35 deliveries.

He plays domestic cricket for the [[Dolphins (South African cricket team)|Dolphins]] and for [[Multan Sultan]]s in Pakistan super League and for the [[Delhi Capitals]] in the [[Indian Premier League]]. He also represents the [[South Africa national cricket team]] in both [[One Day International]] (ODI) and [[Twenty20 International]] cricket. In September 2018, Miller announced that he would no longer be available to play [[first-class cricket]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://cricket.co.za/news/25974/Miller-unavailable-to-play-first-class-cricket |title=Miller unavailable to play first-class cricket |work=Cricket South African |access-date=11 September 2018 |archive-date=11 September 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180911152135/http://cricket.co.za/news/25974/Miller-unavailable-to-play-first-class-cricket |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Domestic career==
Miller made his first-class debut in the Dolphins' final game of the 2007–08 domestic [[SuperSport Series]], scoring a half-century in the first innings in which he batted.

Miller made eight appearances in the one-day [[MTN Domestic Championship]] competition of the same season, though his final match was abandoned after just three overs. Miller scored an average of 13 runs throughout the competition, which saw the Dolphins finish in fifth place in the league.

Miller played two matches in the Pro20 Series Twenty20 competition for the Dolphins, who finished as defeated finalists in the competition.

In May 2018, Miller was named as one of the ten marquee players for the [[2018 Global T20 Canada|first edition]] of the [[Global T20 Canada]] cricket tournament.<ref name="marquee1">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/story/1147584.html |title=Steven Smith named as marquee player for Canada T20 tournament |access-date=24 May 2018 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref><ref name="marquee2">{{cite web |url=http://www.sportingnews.com/other-sports/news/steve-smith-australia-cricket-global-t20-canada-ball-scuffing-scandal/1k2lxwrnwsazj1wj8ylmuejdbm |title=Steve Smith named as marquee player for Global T20 Canada |access-date=24 May 2018 |work=Sporting News |archive-date=18 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180618052357/http://www.sportingnews.com/other-sports/news/steve-smith-australia-cricket-global-t20-canada-ball-scuffing-scandal/1k2lxwrnwsazj1wj8ylmuejdbm |url-status=dead }}</ref> On 3 June 2018, he was selected to play for the Winnipeg Hawks in the players' draft for the inaugural edition of the tournament.<ref name="Squads2">{{cite web|url=https://www.crictracker.com/global-t20-canada-league-full-squads-announced/ |title=Global T20 Canada League – Full Squads announced |work=CricTracker |date=4 June 2018 |access-date=4 June 2018}}</ref>

In October 2018, Miller was named in [[Durban Heat]]'s squad for the [[2018 Mzansi Super League|first edition]] of the [[Mzansi Super League]] T20 tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sport24.co.za/Cricket/live-mzansi-super-league-player-draft-20181017 |title=Mzansi Super League - full squad lists |work=Sport24 |access-date=17 October 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.iol.co.za/sport/cricket/domestic/mzansi-super-league-player-draft-the-story-so-far-17521199 |title=Mzansi Super League Player Draft: The story so far |work=Independent Online |access-date=17 October 2018}}</ref> In September 2019, he was named in the squad for the [[Durban Heat]] team for the [[2019 Mzansi Super League]] tournament.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://cricket.co.za/news/31555/MSL-20-announces-its-T20-squads |title=MSL 2.0 announces its T20 squads |work=Cricket South Africa |access-date=4 September 2019 |archive-date=4 September 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190904081427/https://cricket.co.za/news/31555/MSL-20-announces-its-T20-squads |url-status=dead }}</ref> In April 2021, he was named in [[KwaZulu-Natal (cricket team)|KwaZulu-Natal]]'s squad, ahead of the 2021–22 cricket season in South Africa.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://cricket.co.za/news/38184/CSA-reveals-Division-One-squads-for-2021-22 |title=CSA reveals Division One squads for 2021/22 |work=Cricket South Africa |access-date=20 April 2021 |archive-date=20 April 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210420104034/http://cricket.co.za/news/38184/CSA-reveals-Division-One-squads-for-2021-22 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==T20 franchise cricket==
===Indian Premier League===
In the 2013 IPL auction, [[Kings XI Punjab]] bought Miller for ₨ 6 crore. He went on to play all the matches for his team that season. On 6 May 2013, Miller hit the third fastest hundred in IPL history, scoring 101 [[not out]] off 38 balls in a chase against [[Royal Challengers Bangalore]], at [[Mohali]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|last2=|first2=|last3=|first3=|title=David Miller emulates Gayle to help Punjab annihilate RCB in IPL|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/sports/ipl-6/story/ipl-2013-live-score-kings-xi-punjab-vs-royal-challengers-bangalore-t20-live-161978-2013-05-06|url-status=live|access-date=2021-06-10|website=India Today|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210610105903/https://www.indiatoday.in/sports/ipl-6/story/ipl-2013-live-score-kings-xi-punjab-vs-royal-challengers-bangalore-t20-live-161978-2013-05-06 |archive-date=10 June 2021 }}</ref> The opposing captain [[Virat Kohli]], who dropped a catch when Miller was on 41, said of the innings that it was one of the best innings he had ever seen in the [[Indian Premier League]] history. He was retained by [[Kings XI Punjab]] for [[IPL 7|2014 IPL]] where he played all matches and help his team to reach the finals. It was announced that he will be the captain of the Kings XI Punjab for [[IPL 9|2016 IPL]]. After [[Kings XI Punjab]] lost five of their first six games, he was dropped as the captain and was replaced with [[Murali Vijay]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Miller dropped as Kings XI captain|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/m-vijay-replaces-david-miller-as-kings-xi-punjab-captain-for-rest-of-ipl-2016-1006077|access-date=2021-06-10|work=ESPNcricinfo|language=en}}</ref>

During [[2015 IPL|IPL 2015]], during the match between [[Kolkata Knight Riders]] and [[Kings XI Punjab]] at [[Eden Gardens]] on 9 May 2015, a policeman was left with his left eye blind after the ball hit for a six by struck his eye.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Man blinded in one eye by Miller six|language=en-GB|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/32765150|access-date=2021-06-10}}</ref>

Miller was released by the Kings XI Punjab ahead of the [[List of 2020 Indian Premier League personnel changes|2020 IPL auction]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/28087425/where-do-eight-franchises-stand-2020-auction |title=Where do the eight franchises stand before the 2020 auction?|work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=15 November 2019}}</ref> In the [[List of 2020 Indian Premier League personnel changes|2020 IPL auction]], he was bought by the [[Rajasthan Royals]] ahead of the [[2020 Indian Premier League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/28338426/ipl-auction-analysis-do-eight-teams-their-best-xis-place? |title=IPL auction analysis: Do the eight teams have their best XIs in place? |work=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=20 December 2019}}</ref> In February 2022, he was bought by the [[Gujarat Titans]] in the [[List of 2022 Indian Premier League personnel changes|auction]] for the [[2022 Indian Premier League]] tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-2022-auction-the-list-of-sold-and-unsold-players-1300689 |title=IPL 2022 auction: The list of sold and unsold players |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=13 February 2022}}</ref> He scored 481 runs at average of 68.71 in [[IPL 2022]] for [[Gujarat Titans]] which helped them to win their first title. In the IPL 2025 auction Miller was bought for ₹ 7.5 crores by [[Lucknow Super Giants]].

During IPL 2026, David Miller joined Delhi Capitals.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kumar |first=Saurabh |date=2026-04-09 |title=David Miller hero or villain? Costly call is IPL 2026 Play of the Day in Delhi |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/sports/cricket/story/david-miller-gujarat-titans-edge-delhi-capitals-ipl-2026-thriller-play-of-day-2893502-2026-04-09 |access-date=2026-04-09 |website=India Today |language=en}}</ref>

==International career==
Miller earned his national call up in May 2010 after a series for South Africa A against Bangladesh A, where he ended as the second-highest run-scorer. Miller made his Twenty20 International debut for South Africa on 20 May 2010 against the [[West Indies cricket team|West Indies]] in [[Antigua]]. Miller, called up to replace the injured [[Jacques Kallis]], dispatched the sixth ball of his innings for six and went on to top score as South Africa won by just 1 run.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cricinfo.com/west-indies-v-south-africa-2010/content/story/460451.html |title=David Miller makes an expected mark| publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=22 May 2010}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cricinfo.com/west-indies-v-south-africa-2010/content/story/460397.html |title=South Africa edge home in low-scoring thriller| publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=22 May 2010}}</ref> Two days later, Miller made his ODI debut, also against the West Indies. He put in another good performance, scoring 23 not out and helping South Africa to win.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cricinfo.com/west-indies-v-south-africa-2010/content/current/story/460556.html |title=South Africa continue success with 66-run win| publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=23 May 2010}}</ref> Miller was selected to play in Zimbabwe's tour of South Africa, during which he contributed in both ODI and T20 formats towards a resounding victory by the South Africans. He was then selected for the South African squad to play Pakistan in the U.A.E. during October and November 2010. He played in two ODI series, against West Indies and Pakistan, before being named in South Africa preliminary 2011 World Cup squad.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Rudolph in preliminary South Africa World Cup squad|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/world-cup-2011-four-uncapped-players-in-south-africa-preliminary-squad-492057|access-date=2021-06-10|work=ESPNcricinfo|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=South Africa name uncapped quartet in preliminary 2011 World Cup squad. South Africa cricket team |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2010/dec/14/south-africa-squad-world-cup|access-date=2021-06-10|website=The Guardian}}</ref>

On 15 October 2010, Miller made his maiden ODI fifty against Zimbabwe and South Africa went on to put a massive total of 351.

In the semi-finals of the [[2013 ICC Champions Trophy]], Miller along with [[Rory Kleinveldt]] set the record for the highest 9th wicket partnership in [[ICC Champions Trophy]] history, with 95.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/fow/highest_partnerships_by_wicket.html?id=44;type=trophy|title=Cricket Records. Records. ICC Champions Trophy (ICC KnockOut). Highest partnerships by wicket |work=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=17 June 2017}}</ref>

Miller made his Maiden One Day International century in the 4th ODI [[West Indian cricket team in South Africa in 2014–15|against the West Indies]] on 25 January 2015.<ref name="Debut100">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/south-africa-v-west-indies-2014-15/content/story/823759.html |title=Russell carries WI to one-wicket victory |access-date=25 January 2015 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

In August 2017, Miller was named in a [[List of World XI Twenty20 International cricketers|World XI]] team to play three Twenty20 International matches against Pakistan in the [[2017 Independence Cup (cricket)|2017 Independence Cup]] in [[Lahore]].<ref name="WXI">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/pakistan/content/story/1117616.html |title=Faf du Plessis named captain of World XI to travel to Pakistan |access-date=24 August 2017|work=ESPNcricinfo|date=24 August 2017 }}</ref>

===2015 Cricket World Cup===
Miller was one of South Africa's top performers at the [[2015 Cricket World Cup]] scoring 324 runs at an average of 65 and strike rate of 139 during the tournament.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/icc-cricket-world-cup-2015/engine/records/batting/most_runs_career.html?id%3D6537%3Btype%3Dtournament |title=Cricket Records. ICC Cricket World Cup, 2014/15. Records. Most runs. |access-date=8 July 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150823120058/http://stats.espncricinfo.com/icc-cricket-world-cup-2015/engine/records/batting/most_runs_career.html?id=6537%3Btype%3Dtournament |archive-date=23 August 2015 |df=dmy }}</ref>

Miller scored 49 off 18 balls in the semi-final, although his effort was in vain as New Zealand won the match.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/icc-cricket-world-cup-2014-15-509587/new-zealand-vs-south-africa-1st-semi-final-656491/full-scorecard|title=Full Scorecard of South Africa vs New Zealand 1st Semi-final 2014/15 - Score Report |work=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=16 November 2021}}</ref>

During that World Cup, Miller along with [[JP Duminy]] set the record for the highest 5th wicket partnership in ODI history as well as World Cup history (256*).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/records/252072.html|title=Highest partnerships for each wicket in ODI history|work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

===2017–Onwards===
On [[Bangladeshi cricket team in South Africa in 2017–18#1st ODI|15 October 2017]], Miller played in his 100th ODI and became the third player after [[Rohit Sharma]] and [[Kieron Pollard]] to play 100 ODIs without featuring in a [[Test (cricket)|Test]] match.<ref name="Miller100">{{cite web |url=http://cricket.co.za/news/21555/Miller-set-to-join-100-ODI-club |title=Miller set to join 100 ODI club |access-date=15 October 2017 |work=Cricket South Africa |archive-date=15 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171015201832/http://cricket.co.za/news/21555/Miller-set-to-join-100-ODI-club |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="No test">{{cite web |url=http://www.cricbuzz.com/cricket-news/97800/records-tumble-as-amla-de-kock-lead-sa-prance-in-kimberley |title=Records tumble as Amla, de Kock lead SA prance in Kimberley |access-date=15 October 2017 |work=Cricbuzz|date=15 October 2017 }}</ref> In the 2nd T20I of the same tour, he scored his first century in a T20I and made the then [[List of Twenty20 International records#Fastest 100|fastest century in a T20I]] (35 balls).<ref name="Miller35">{{cite web |url=http://www.sport24.co.za/Cricket/Proteas/666661-its-miller-time-20171029 |title=Miller smashes fastest ever T20 ton |access-date=29 October 2017 |work=Sports24}}</ref> He was also the first player to score a T20I century batting at [[List of Twenty20 International records#Highest individual score (by batting position)|number five]] or lower and is the only player to have done that twice.<ref>{{cite web|first=Gaurav|last=Sundararaman|title=Miller smashes record for fastest T20I ton|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/21210612/david-miller-smashes-record-fastest-t20i-ton|publisher=ESPNcricinfo|date=29 October 2017|access-date=30 October 2017}}</ref> During the match, he became fifth player from South Africa to score 1,000 runs in T20Is.<ref name="Miller1000">{{cite web |url=http://www.indiatoday.in/lite/story/david-miller-david-miller-fastest-100-t20i-south-africa-vs-bangladesh-cricket/1/1077942.html |title=David Miller smashes fastest T20 International hundred |access-date=30 October 2017 |work=India Today}}</ref>

During the [[Pakistani cricket team in South Africa in 2018–19|Pakistan series in February 2019]], regular captain [[Faf du Plessis]] was rested for the last two T20Is of the series,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/1044951 |title=Faf du Plessis rested for last two T20Is against Pakistan |work=International Cricket Council |access-date=2 February 2019}}</ref> with Miller named as captain of South Africa in his place.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Brickhill |first1=Liam |title=Miller to captain SA as Pakistan eye redemption |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/pak-in-sa-2018-19-1144137/south-africa-vs-pakistan-2nd-t20i-1144162/match-preview |website=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=1 March 2024 |date=2 February 2019}}</ref>

In April 2019, Miller was named in [[2019 Cricket World Cup squads#South Africa|South Africa's squad]] for the [[2019 Cricket World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/story/1181308.html |title=Hashim Amla in World Cup squad; Reeza Hendricks, Chris Morris miss out |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=18 April 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/1183187 |title=Amla edges out Hendricks to make South Africa's World Cup squad |work=International Cricket Council |access-date=18 April 2019}}</ref> On 19 June 2019, in the match against [[New Zealand national cricket team|New Zealand]], Miller scored his 3,000th run in ODIs.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.timesandstar.co.uk/sport/national/17717312.kane-williamson-century-leads-new-zealand-to-thrilling-win-over-south-africa/ |title=Kane Williamson century leads New Zealand to thrilling win over South Africa |work=Times and Star |date=19 June 2019 |access-date=20 June 2019}}</ref> In September 2021, Miller was named in South Africa's squad for the [[2021 ICC Men's T20 World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/t20-world-cup-south-africa-leave-out-faf-du-plessis-and-imran-tahir-and-chris-morris-1276995 |title=T20 World Cup: South Africa leave out Faf du Plessis, Imran Tahir and Chris Morris |work=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=9 September 2021}}</ref>
On the South Africa Tour of India in 2022, he was dominating the game against New Team India. For South Africa's tour of England in 2022, David Miller has been selected as New Captain for T20 series. In October 2022, He scored his 2nd T20I Century again India at the [[Dr. Bhupen Hazarika Cricket Stadium, Barsapara|Dr. Bhupen Hazarika Cricket Stadium, Barsapara, Assam]] .

Miller was named in the [[ICC Men's T20I Team of the Year]] in 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/2451961|title= ICC Men's T20I Team of the Year revealed|work=International Cricket Council |access-date=21 January 2022}}</ref> He was selected in South Africa's squad for 2023 Cricket World Cup.<ref>{{Cite web |title=South Africa unveil squad for World Cup 2023 |url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/3671418 |access-date=2023-11-16 |website=www.icc-cricket.com |language=en}}</ref>

===2023 Cricket World Cup===
Miller was one of South Africa's top performers at the [[2023 Cricket World Cup]] scoring 356 runs at an average of 45 and strike rate of 108 during the tournament.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/records/tournament/batting-most-runs-career/icc-cricket-world-cup-2023-24-15338 |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=28 November 2023 |title=ICC Cricket World Cup, 2023/24 batting most runs career Records }}</ref>

Miller scored 101 in the semi-final against Australia in iconic [[Eden Gardens]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/icc-cricket-world-cup-2023-24-1367856/australia-vs-south-africa-2nd-semi-final-1384438/full-scorecard |work=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=28 November 2023 |title=AUS vs SA, ICC Cricket World Cup 2023/24, 2nd Semi-Final at Kolkata, November 16, 2023 - Full Scorecard }}</ref>

=== 2024 T20 World Cup ===
In May 2024, he was named in South Africa's squad for the [[2024 Men's T20 World Cup]] tournament.<ref>{{Cite web |title=South Africa Squad for ICC Men's T20I World Cup |url=https://www.scorewaves.com/news-details/south-africa-squad-for-t20-world-cup |access-date=2024-06-11 |website=ScoreWaves |language=en}}</ref> Miller was one of the key players in getting South Africa to their first World Cup Final, before losing to India in the final.

===Champions Trophy 2025===
In the second semi-final against New Zealand in Lahore, he scored his first century in the Champions Trophy with a 100*(67) albeit in a losing cause as New Zealand won by 50 runs. This century was also the fastest century in the Champions Trophy in terms of balls needed, surpassing a record set by Virender Sehwag and Josh Inglis (77 balls each).<ref>{{Cite web |date=5 March 2025 |title=Fastest ODI hundreds, full list: David Miller breaks Champions Trophy record |url=https://www.wisden.com/series/icc-champions-trophy-2025/cricket-news/fastest-odi-hundreds-full-list-david-miller-breaks-champions-trophy-record |access-date=6 March 2025 |website=Wisden}}</ref>

===2025-Onwards===
In August 2025, he was named in the South Africa T20I team that would tour England for 3 T20 Internationals.

In September 2025, he was named captain of the Proteas T20I squad to tour Pakistan, in the absence of regular skipper Aiden Markram. However, he was forced to withdraw from the squad due to injury.

'''<big>2026 T20 World Cup</big>'''

In January 2026, Miller was selected in South Africa's [[2026 Men's T20 World Cup]] squad. He batted in both super overs against [[Afghanistan national cricket team|Afghanistan]], and scored 16*(4) in the second super over, including 2 sixes, propelling the Proteas to a massive super over score of 23.

In their Super 8 clash against [[India national cricket team|India]], he scored 63 (35), having walked in at 20/3.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/icc-men-s-t20-world-cup-2025-26-1502138/india-vs-south-africa-43rd-match-super-eights-group-1-1512761/match-report|title=All-round SA hammer India in Ahmedabad|website=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=25 May 2026}}</ref>

On 27th September, 2026, during the 2nd ODI against [[Australian cricket team in South Africa in 2026–27 |Australia]], Miller hit a career high 142 runs off 93 balls.

Outside cricket, Miller also plays [[golf]], and considers himself a devout [[Christians|Christian]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Sahi |first=Lokendra Pratap |date=4 May 2016 |title=David Miller: I've been born for something greater than cricket |url=https://www.telegraphindia.com/sports/david-miller-i-ve-been-born-for-something-greater-than-cricket/cid/1340554 |access-date=23 November 2025 |newspaper=[[The Daily Telegraph]]|publisher=ABP Group}}</ref>

He is married to Camilla Harris, and together they have a son.{{Citation needed|date=October 2026}}

'''David Andrew Warner''' (born 27 October 1986) is an Australian former international [[cricket]]er, captain of [[Big Bash League]] team [[Sydney Thunder]] and captain of [[Pakistan Super League]] team [[Karachi Kings]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/psl-2025-david-warner-takes-over-from-shan-masood-as-karachi-kings-captain-1478008 | title=Warner to lead Karachi Kings in PSL 2025 }}</ref> A left-handed [[Batting order (cricket)#Opening batsmen or openers|opening batter]], Warner was the first Australian cricketer in 132 years to be selected for the national team in any format without experience in [[first-class cricket]]. He captained Australia in ODIs and T20Is and served as a vice-captain across formats before his suspension and played his domestic cricket for [[New South Wales Cricket Team]]. Warner was a prominent member of the victorious Australian squad of the [[2015 Cricket World Cup]], the [[2021 T20 World Cup]], where he was the ''Player of the Tournament'', the [[2021–2023 World Test Championship|2021–2023 ICC World Test Championship]], and the [[2023 ICC Cricket World Cup]].  Warner also guided [[Indian Premier League]] team  [[Sunrisers Hyderabad]] to their first and only IPL title,<ref>{{Cite news |date=1 May 2021 |title=IPL 2021: David Warner replaced by Kane Williamson as Sunrisers Hyderabad captain |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/cricket/56956335 |access-date=14 April 2025 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> becoming the third Australian captain after [[Adam Gilchrist]] and [[Shane Warne]] to do so. Warner holds the record of the most international centuries as an opening batsman across all international formats. He also holds the record for most 50+ scores in [[Twenty20|T20 cricket]].<ref>{{Cite web | title=T20 matches {{!}} Batting records {{!}} Most fifties in career {{!}} ESPNcricinfo | url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/records/most-fifties-in-career-283488 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240420023138/https://www.espncricinfo.com/records/most-fifties-in-career-283488 | access-date=2026-09-06 | archive-date=2024-04-20}}</ref>

In January 2017, he became the fourth player to win the [[Allan Border Medal]] more than once and to win the award in consecutive years. On 28 September 2017, he played in his 100th [[One Day International]] (ODI).

In March 2018, following a preliminary investigation into [[2018 Australian ball-tampering scandal|ball tampering by the Australian team]] in the third match of their [[Australian cricket team in South Africa in 2017–18|Test series against South Africa]], Warner was suspended and charged with bringing the game into disrepute.<ref name="cricket.com.au">{{cite web|url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/steve-smith-cameron-bancroft-david-warner-charged-cricket-australia-tampering-renshaw-burns-maxwell/2018-03-28|title=Trio suspended by Cricket Australia|access-date=28 March 2018}}</ref> Following a board meeting later in the month, [[Cricket Australia]] banned Warner from all international and domestic cricket in Australia for one year, and from any leadership positions permanently.<ref name="Ban">{{Cite news|url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/player-sanctions-steve-smith-cameron-bancroft-david-warner-australia-cricket-ball-tampering/2018-03-28|title=Tampering trio learn their fate|work=cricket.com.au|access-date=28 March 2018}}</ref> The ban on leadership positions was lifted on 18 October 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |date=24 October 2024 |title=Warner's leadership ban overturned by Cricket Australia |url=https://www.espn.com.au/cricket/story/_/id/41987465/australia-news-david-warner-leadership-banoverturned-cricket-australia |access-date=25 October 2024 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

In January 2024, Warner played his final Test match for Australia and also announced his retirement from [[One Day International|ODI]] cricket. On 25 June 2024, Warner announced his retirement from international cricket after Australia's exit from the [[2024 ICC Men's T20 World Cup]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=9 July 2024 |title=David Warner retirement: Australian opener calls curtains to international career |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/sports/david-warner-retirement-australian-opener-calls-curtains-to-international-career/articleshow/111594944.cms?from=mdr |access-date=14 April 2025 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}}</ref>

== Early life ==
David Warner was born on 27 October 1986 in [[Paddington, New South Wales|Paddington]], a suburb in eastern Sydney.<ref name="ESPNcricinfo">{{cite web |title=David Warner |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/australia/content/player/219889.html |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=14 February 2019}}</ref> At the age of 13,  he was asked by his coach to switch to right-handed batting because he kept hitting the ball in the air. However his mother, Lorraine Warner (née Orange), encouraged him to return to batting left-handed and he broke the under-16's run-scoring record for the Sydney Coastal Cricket Club.<ref name="Facts about Warner">{{cite web |title=34 Facts about David Warner – The Pocket size dynamo |url=https://www.crictracker.com/34-facts-david-warner/ |website=CricTracker |access-date=15 February 2019 |date=26 October 2015}}</ref> He then made his [[Sydney Grade Cricket|first grade]] debut for the [[Eastern Suburbs Cricket Club|Eastern Suburbs]] club at the age of 15<ref name="Facts about Warner" /> and later toured Sri Lanka with the [[Australia national under-19 cricket team|Australian under-19s]] and earned a rookie contract with the [[New South Wales cricket team|state team]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.smh.com.au/news/sport/cricket/warner-brothers-blockbuster/2009/01/12/1231608617044.html?page=2|title=Warner brothers come up with a blockbuster|last=Pandaram|first=Jamie|date=13 January 2009|access-date=15 July 2009|work=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]]}}</ref> Warner grew up in a housing commission estate in Matraville in Sydney's south-east<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.news.com.au/sport/cricket/insane-detail-of-david-warner-and-familys-9m-home-revealed/news-story/15b0cf5e62b903fe204b803d1e3d39ad |title=Insane detail of David Warner and family's $10m mega-home revealed |website=News.com.au |date=17 December 2023}}</ref> and attended Matraville Public School and [[Randwick Boys High School]].<ref>{{cite web |title=David Warner year 12 report card: Australian cricketer's high school grades |url=https://www.news.com.au/sport/cricket/david-warners-hilarious-high-school-report-card/news-story/1339af7954a20e151123900eb2a84172 |website=www.news.com.au |access-date=15 February 2019}}</ref>

== Domestic career ==
[[File:David Warner batting.jpg|thumb|Warner playing for [[New South Wales cricket team|New South Wales]] in 2011.|left|205x205px]]
On 29 November 2008, Warner hit his first domestic One Day century for New South Wales with a score of 165[[Not out|*]] against [[Tasmania cricket team|Tasmania]] at [[Hurstville Oval]] in Sydney. This innings got him the record of the highest one day score by a Blues player.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.news.com.au/dailytelegraph/story/0,22049,24726020-5001023,00.html|title=David Warner seals NSW Blues win with record knock|work=News.com.au|archive-date=7 February 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090207063657/http://www.news.com.au/dailytelegraph/story/0,22049,24726020-5001023,00.html|access-date=15 February 2019}}</ref> In the reverse fixture at [[Hobart]], he backed it up with a 54-ball 97 to narrowly miss the record for the fastest ever century in Australian domestic cricket.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.news.com.au/heraldsun/story/0,21985,24763519-11088,00.html|title=Opener David Warner just misses Australia's fastest one-day century|work=News.com.au|access-date=9 August 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090207062504/http://www.news.com.au/heraldsun/story/0,21985,24763519-11088,00.html|archive-date=7 February 2009}}</ref>

Warner made his [[First-class cricket|first-class]] debut playing for New South Wales against [[Western Australia]] in the final match of the [[2008–09 Sheffield Shield season]] at the Sydney Cricket Ground on 5–8 March 2009. Batting only once and coming in at number six in the batting order, Warner scored 42 runs off 48 deliveries.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cricinfo.com/australia/engine/match/361256.html|title=Scorecard: New South Wales v Western Australia at the SCG, 5–8|date=March 2009|work=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=15 July 2009}}</ref>

While playing for New South Wales, Warner broke the record for the highest Australian one-day domestic score. His score of 197 came off just 141 balls and included 20 fours and 10 sixes, surpassing [[Jimmy Maher]]'s previous record of 187.<ref>{{cite news|title=David Warner smashes record Australian one-day score|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2013/oct/24/david-warner-smashes-record-australian-one-day-score|newspaper=The Guardian}}</ref>

=== Big Bash League ===
In 2009, Warner set a new record for the fastest half-century scored in the Australian domestic Twenty20 cricket, completing his 50 in 18 balls against Tasmania.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/records/305877.html|title=Records – Twenty20 matches – Batting records – Fastest fifties – ESPNcricinfo|access-date=8 September 2018}}</ref> In the first season of the newly revamped Big Bash League, Warner was named as captain for the [[Sydney Thunder]] and scored 102 [[not out]] from 51 balls in his first match for the team.<ref>{{cite web |title=(N)Big Bash League at Melbourne, Dec 17 2011. Match Summary |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/8044/scorecard/524916/melbourne-stars-vs-sydney-thunder-big-bash-league-2011-12 |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=6 January 2019 |language=en}}</ref> Warner played for [[Sydney Sixers]] in [[2012–13 Big Bash League season|2012–13 season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.in/cricket/story/_/id/22249694/david-warner-signs-sydney-sixers|title=Warner signs with Sydney Sixers|access-date=8 September 2018|date=5 August 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sydneysixers.com.au/news/warner-signs-with-sixers/2012-08-04|title=Warner signs with Sixers|access-date=8 September 2018|archive-date=5 July 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220705190812/https://www.sydneysixers.com.au/news/warner-signs-with-sixers/2012-08-04|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Warner returned to the BBL in 2022 with the Sydney Thunder.<ref>{{cite news |title=Warner to revive Big Bash career at Thunder in BBL{{!}}12 {{!}} cricket.com.au |url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/3318458 |access-date=17 December 2025 |work=www.cricket.com.au |date=21 August 2022 |language=en}}</ref> He was named captain of the Thunder in November 2024.<ref>{{cite news |last1=McGlashan |first1=Andrew |title=David Warner named Sydney Thunder captain |url=https://www.espn.com.au/cricket/story/_/id/42216166/bbl-2024-25-news-david-warner-named-sydney-thunder-captain |access-date=17 December 2025 |work=ESPN.com |date=5 November 2024 |language=en}}</ref> He was named in the Team of the Tournament for [[2024–25 Big Bash League season|BBL14]] after scoring 346 runs.<ref>{{cite news |title=Warner named captain of official BBL{{!}}14 Team of the Tournament {{!}} cricket.com.au |url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/4202465/david-warner-captain-official-bbl14-team-of-the-tournament-players-selections-big-bash-maxwell-stoinis-connolly-owen-behrendorff-david |access-date=17 December 2025 |work=www.cricket.com.au |date=23 January 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

=== Indian Premier League ===
Warner has been one of the most successful overseas batsmen in the [[Indian Premier League]], scoring over 6,000 runs and winning the Orange Cap award for the highest scoring batter in a season three times.<ref>{{Cite web|title=IPL 2019: Warner, Tahir hold Orange and Purple Cap after MI vs CSK final|url=https://sportstar.thehindu.com/cricket/ipl/ipl-2019-top-batsmen-bowlers-orange-cap-purple-cap/article26722073.ece|access-date=19 October 2020|website=Sportstar|date=3 April 2019 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=18 October 2020|title=IPL 2020, SRH vs KKR: David Warner shatters Virat Kohli's record to become the fastest to score 5000 runs in the tournament|url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cricket/ipl-2020-srh-vs-kkr-david-warner-shatters-virat-kohli-s-record-to-become-the-fastest-to-5000-runs-in-the-tournament/story-euewna96VaGs8pvUc7gylN.html|access-date=19 October 2020|website=Hindustan Times|language=en}}</ref>

Warner was signed by [[Delhi Daredevils]] in 2009, playing for the team until 2013.<ref>[http://www.smh.com.au/news/sport/cricket/big-hitting-blues-batsman-hits-the-jackpot/2008/12/17/1229189678907.html Big hitting Blues batsman hits the jackpot] 17 December 2008 – 12:53 pm</ref> Following the [[2014 Indian Premier League|2014 IPL]] auction, however, he moved to [[Sunrisers Hyderabad]] for US$880,000.<ref>{{cite web|title=IPL Auction 2014 Highlights: RCB buys Yuvraj Singh for 17 Crores|url=http://news.biharprabha.com/2014/02/royal-challengers-bangalore-buys-yuvraj-singh-of-17-crores-for-ipl-7/|work=news.biharprabha.com|access-date=12 February 2014}}</ref> In 2015, he was appointed captain of the team and ended the season as the tournament's leading run scorer.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cricbuzz.com/cricket-series/2261/indian-premier-league-2014/points-table|title=Indian Premier League 2014 Points Table|website=Cricbuzz|access-date=8 September 2018}}</ref>

He continued as captain in [[2016 Indian Premier League|2016]],<ref>{{cite news|title=David Warner's 90 guides Sunrisers Hyderabad to season's first win|url=http://www.abplive.in/sports/david-warners-90-guides-sunrisers-hyderabad-to-seasons-first-win-mumbai-indians-ipl-2016-324878|access-date=19 April 2016|work=ABP Live|date=18 April 2016}}</ref> leading the team to its first championship, scoring 69 runs from 38 balls in the final against [[Royal Challengers Bangalore]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.smh.com.au/sport/cricket/david-warner-inspires-sunrisers-to-ipl-glory-20160529-gp6t87.html|title=David Warner inspires Sunrisers to IPL glory|access-date=30 May 2016|last=McCullough|first=Ian|work=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]]|date=29 May 2016}}</ref> Warner finished the season with 848 runs, the second highest in the tournament. In [[2017 Indian Premier League|2017]], Warner scored 126 runs against [[Kolkata Knight Riders]], breaking his previous career highest IPL score of 109 [[not out]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.iplt20.com/match/2017/37|title=David Warner sets new personal IPL highest score|date=30 April 2017|access-date=30 April 2017|publisher=Indian Premier League}}</ref> He finished the season as the leading run scorer, and was awarded the Orange cap for the second time.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.iplt20.com/stats/2017/most-runs|title=IPLT20.com – Indian Premier League Official Website|website=www.iplt20.com|access-date=8 September 2018}}</ref>

After having been named as captain again for the 2018 season,<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.financialexpress.com/sports/ipl/ipl-2018-retained-players-srh-david-warner-shikhar-dhawan-bhuvneshwar-kumar-rashid-khan/1001751/|title=IPL 2018 retained players SRH: David Warner,
