'''Jonathan Marc Bairstow''' (born 26 September 1989) is an English [[cricket]]er who played internationally for [[England cricket team|England]] in all formats as a right-handed [[wicket-keeper-batter]].<ref name="ESPN">{{cite web |title=Jonny Bairstow player profile |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/player/jonny-bairstow-297433 |access-date=12 June 2024 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He represents [[Yorkshire County Cricket Club|Yorkshire]] in domestic cricket and [[London Spirit]] in [[The Hundred (cricket)|The Hundred]].<ref name="JBCA">{{cite web |url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/90/90667/90667.html |title=Jonny Bairstow (profile) |work=CricketArchive |access-date=12 June 2024 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> Bairstow was part of the England team that won the [[2019 Cricket World Cup]].

==Early life==
Jonny Bairstow was born on 26 September 1989 in [[Bradford]], West Yorkshire. His mother, Janet, became the first female vice-president of [[Yorkshire County Cricket Club]] in 2020.<ref name="SFT">{{cite news |url=https://www.yorkshirepost.co.uk/sport/cricket/janet-bairstow-continues-strong-family-tradition-yorkshire-ccc-2521382 |last=Waters |first=Chris |title=Janet Bairstow continues strong family tradition at Yorkshire CCC |work=Yorkshire Post |date=28 March 2020 |access-date=13 June 2024}}</ref> His father was [[David Bairstow]], who played as a [[wicket-keeper]] for both Yorkshire and [[England cricket team|England]]. David died by suicide in 1998 when Jonny was eight years old, but he had taught Jonny how to play cricket and has remained a lasting inspiration.<ref name="WCY">{{cite news |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/wisdenalmanack/content/story/1008133.html |last=Wilde |first=Simon |title=Wisden Cricketers of the Year 2015 |work=Wisden archive |date=2016 |access-date=13 June 2024}}</ref> Jonny has a sister, Rebecca, and their elder half-brother is former [[Derbyshire County Cricket Club|Derbyshire]] player [[Andrew Bairstow]].<ref name="SFT"/><ref name="WCY"/>

Bairstow went to [[St Peter's School, York]], in 2001 and became an all-round athlete. When he was interviewed by ''[[Wisden Cricketers' Almanack]]'' in 2016, he recalled that besides keeping wicket in cricket, he had been a fly-half in [[Rugby union|rugby]], a centre-mid in [[field hockey|hockey]], and a right-back in [[association football|football]]. His cricketing ability was recognised by ''Wisden'' in 2008 when he was chosen as the inaugural winner of their ''Young Schools Cricketer of the Year'' award, after he had scored 654 runs for the school in 2007.<ref name="WCY"/><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cricinfo.com/wisdenalmanack/content/story/345707.html |title=Jonathan Bairstow wins inaugural award |work=Wisden archive Cricketers' Almanack |access-date=12 June 2009}}</ref> In football, Bairstow was a member of the [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United Academy]] for eight years until he was fifteen. When it came to a choice between cricket and football, he felt that he had the ability "to make it professionally" in cricket, but not in football.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.leeds-live.co.uk/sport/leeds-united/england-hero-jonny-bairstow-leeds-24403128 |last=Bloomer |first=Danny |title=England hero Jonny Bairstow on his Leeds United academy background |work=LeedsLive |date=5 July 2022 |access-date=3 September 2022}}</ref>

==Yorkshire==
Aged 18, Bairstow was invited to play Second Eleven cricket for Yorkshire in the [[2008 English cricket season|2008 season]], making six appearances in the [[Second XI Championship]], in which he scored 308 runs at an average of 61.60.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Events/ENG/Second_Eleven_Championship_2008/Yorkshire_Second_XI_Batting.html |title=Second Eleven Championship 2008, Batting and Fielding for Yorkshire Second XI |work=CricketArchive |access-date=12 June 2009 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> He was included in Yorkshire's first-team squad for the final [[County Championship]] match of the season against [[Sussex County Cricket Club|Sussex]], but was not selected for the starting eleven.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.thepress.co.uk/sport/3701409.Durham_could_be_key_for_Tykes/ |title=Durham could be key for Tykes |work=York Press |date=25 September 2008 |access-date=12 June 2009}}</ref> Three weeks later, however, Bairstow signed a two-year contract with Yorkshire.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/bairstow-junior-signs-contract-with-yorkshire-374355 |title=Bairstow junior signs contract with Yorkshire |work=ESPNcricinfo |date=17 October 2008 |access-date=12 June 2024}}</ref>

He began the [[2009 English cricket season|2009 season]] playing for the Second XI. He was awarded his [[county cap|Second XI cap]] and, in early June, he scored 202 [[not out]] against [[Leicestershire County Cricket Club|Leicestershire Second XI]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/210/210847.html |title=Leicestershire Second XI v Yorkshire Second XI |work=CricketArchive |access-date=12 June 2024 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> Bairstow was then picked for the first team in a County Championship match against [[Somerset County Cricket Club|Somerset]] at [[Headingley Cricket Ground|Headingley]]. He replaced the injured [[Michael Vaughan]]<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/yorkshire-batsmen-waste-chances-408555 |last=Ward |first=John |title=Yorkshire batsmen waste chances |work=ESPNcricinfo |date=11 June 2009 |access-date=12 June 2024}}</ref> and, on his [[first-class cricket|first-class]] debut, scored 28 and 82. In Somerset's second innings, Yorkshire's wicket-keeper [[Gerard Brophy]] was injured and Bairstow replaced him, taking four [[caught|catches]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/204/204433.html |title=Yorkshire v Somerset, LV County Championship 2009 (Division 1) |work=CricketArchive |access-date=12 June 2009 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> He played in twelve first-class matches that season, scoring 592 runs at an average of 45.53, completing six half-centuries with a highest score of 84 not out, and taking 21 catches.<ref name="FCBF">{{cite web |url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/90/90667/f_Batting_by_Season.html |title=First-class Batting and Fielding in Each Season by Jonny Bairstow |work=CricketArchive |access-date=12 June 2024 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Bairstow became a Yorkshire first-team regular in the [[2010 English cricket season|2010 season]]. In sixteen first-class appearances, he scored 918 runs at 41.72 with eight fifties and a highest score of 81. He took 29 catches and completed five [[stumped|stumpings]].<ref name="FCBF"/> His potential was recognised by selection for the England Performance Programme squad to tour Australia in 2010–11.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/chris-tremlett-and-monty-panesar-earn-ashes-calls-478475 |first=Andrew |last=McGlashan |title=Tremlett and Panesar earn Ashes calls |work=ESPNcricinfo |date=23 September 2010 |access-date=3 October 2010}}</ref> In addition, he was a member of the [[England Lions cricket team|England Lions team]] which toured the West Indies from January to March 2011. The Lions took part in the [[2010–11 Regional Four Day Competition]] and Bairstow played in three of their seven matches. His best performance was an innings of 85 against [[Combined Campuses and Colleges cricket team|Combined Campuses and Colleges]], sharing a fifth wicket partnership of 134 with [[James Adams (cricketer, born 1980)|Jimmy Adams]].<ref name="FCBF"/>

Bairstow became Yorkshire's first-choice wicket-keeper in the [[2011 English cricket season|2011 season]] and was awarded his [[county cap]].<ref name="JBCA"/> He began the season well and scored 205, his maiden first-class [[century (cricket)|century]], against [[Nottinghamshire County Cricket Club|Nottinghamshire]] at [[Trent Bridge]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/county-cricket-2011/content/story/513904.html |title=Bairstow makes his maiden ton a double |work=ESPNcricinfo |date=5 May 2011 |access-date=18 August 2012}}</ref> Playing in fifteen matches, he scored 1,213 runs in the season at 48.52 with three centuries, and was the only Yorkshire batter to score 1,000 runs. He also took 47 catches.<ref name="FCBF"/>

Bairstow was chosen as the [[Cricket Writers' Club Young Cricketer of the Year]] for 2011. He is the ninth of thirteen Yorkshire players who have won this award; his predecessors included [[Fred Trueman]], [[Geoffrey Boycott]], and Bairstow's team-mate [[Adil Rashid]].<ref name="JBCA"/><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ecb.co.uk/news/domestic/young-cricketer-of-the-year,315972,EN.html |title=Bairstow wins Young Cricketer Award |publisher=England and Wales Cricket Board |date=19 September 2011 |access-date=14 June 2024 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150505011220/http://www.ecb.co.uk/news/domestic/young-cricketer-of-the-year%2C315972%2CEN.html |archive-date=5 May 2015 |df=dmy-all}}</ref>

Yorkshire were in Division One of the County Championship when Bairstow made his debut in 2009. In 2011, they were relegated to Division Two but, with a new team being built under coach [[Jason Gillespie]], they were re-promoted in 2012 as runners-up to [[Derbyshire County Cricket Club|Derbyshire]]. Bairstow played in nine Division Two matches and scored 588 runs with three centuries.<ref>Playfair Cricket Annual 2013, pp. 192–196.</ref> Yorkshire were runners-up to [[Durham County Cricket Club|Durham]] in the 2013 Division One season, Bairstow playing in eight matches. He had a good season as a wicket-keeper, taking 27 catches but was less successful with the bat and scored only one century.<ref>Playfair Cricket Annual 2014, pp. 197–201.</ref> Yorkshire then relived their past glories for the next two seasons winning back-to-back County Championship titles, taking their all-time tally to a record 32. In 2014, Bairstow with 38 catches and four stumpings had a good season as wicket-keeper. He scored 647 runs in his thirteen matches, with a highest score of 161 not out against Sussex at [[County Cricket Ground, Hove|Hove]],<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2014/jun/18/sussex-yorkshire-county-championship-johnny-bairstow |last=Talbot |first=Bruce |title=Yorkshire's Jonny Bairstow outwits Sussex bowlers with unbeaten 161 |work=The Guardian |date=18 June 2014 |access-date=22 June 2024}}</ref> although that was his sole championship century.<ref>Playfair Cricket Annual 2015, pp. 188–193.</ref>

Bairstow had an outstanding season in 2015 as Yorkshire retained the title. He played in only nine championship matches but he scored 1,108 runs at the very high average of 92.33 with five centuries and five half-centuries in his fifteen innings. His highest score was 219 not out against Durham at the [[Riverside Ground]] in [[Chester-le-Street]]. Yorkshire batted first in this match and were struggling at 191/6 when Bairstow was joined by [[Tim Bresnan]]. Batting well into the second day, they added an unbeaten 366 and broke the club record for a seventh wicket partnership, Bresnan scoring 169 not out. Yorkshire went on to win the match by an innings and 47 runs.<ref>Playfair Cricket Annual 2016, pp. 198–204.</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/33306269 |title=County Championship: Bairstow and Bresnan break records |work=BBC Sport |date=29 June 2015 |access-date=22 June 2024}}</ref>
[[File:Revis and Bairstow.jpg|thumb|right|Bairstow captaining Yorkshire CCC in 2025]]
Bairstow's performances in 2015 resulted in him being named as one of the five [[Wisden Cricketers of the Year|''Wisden'' Cricketers of the Year]] in the ''Almanack''{{'}}s 2016 edition. [[Simon Wilde]] in his dedication began by describing Bairstow as a good man in a crisis and pointed out that all five of his 2015 championship centuries "were carved from adversity" because, as in the Durham match, Yorkshire were struggling until Bairstow came in.<ref name="WCY"/>

Having become a regular member of England squads, Bairstow signed a central contract with the national team which has meant him making only occasional appearances for Yorkshire. He played in 88 first-class matches for the club from June 2009 to May 2016, but has appeared in only nine since then until May 2023. In Twenty20, he played in 63 from June 2010 to August 2016, but was then unavailable until June 2021; he has played in five matches between then and May 2023. In Yorkshire's List A matches, he played in 44 from July 2009 to May 2017, but in none since then.<ref name="JBCA"/> In one of his last List A matches for the club, Bairstow scored a career-best 174 from 113 deliveries as Yorkshire defeated Durham by six wickets at Headingley on 3 May 2017. Durham had scored 335/5 and Yorkshire's 339/4 was their highest ever successful run chase in a List A match.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/royal-london-one-day-cup-2017-1068072/yorkshire-vs-durham-north-group-1068454/match-report |title=Bairstow's 174 the star turn in run-fest |work=ESPNcricinfo |date=3 May 2017 |access-date=13 June 2024}}</ref>

In March 2025, Bairstow was named as Yorkshire's red-ball captain.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/articles/cgl0r0ljprxo|title=Bairstow named new Yorkshire red-ball captain|date=27 March 2025 |publisher=BBC Sport|accessdate=27 March 2025}}</ref>

==ODI/T20I==
===Debuts===
On the strength of his performances in 2011, Bairstow was included in the England squads for both [[One Day International|One Day Internationals (ODI)]] and [[Twenty20 International|Twenty20 Internationals (T20I)]].<ref name="debut">{{cite web |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/player/jonny-bairstow-297433/matches |title=Jonny Bairstow Debut/Last Matches |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=1 January 2023}}</ref> In August, he travelled to Dublin with England's ODI squad for a [[English cricket team in Ireland in 2011|match against Ireland]], but did not play.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/14600842 |title=Eoin Morgan named as England captain for Ireland ODI |publisher=BBC Sport |date=20 August 2011 |access-date=20 August 2011}}</ref> He made his ODI debut against [[India national cricket team|India]] on 16 September, and then his T20I debut against [[West Indies cricket team|West Indies]] on 23 September.

Playing as a specialist batter in England's [[Indian cricket team in England in 2011|final ODI against India]], Bairstow scored an unbeaten 41 off just 21 balls to help England reach a [[Duckworth–Lewis–Stern method|Duckworth-Lewis]] adjusted total. His innings included three sixes, the first off just the fifth ball he faced, and he was named [[Player of the Match awards (cricket)|Man of the Match]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/india-tour-of-england-2011-474450/england-vs-india-5th-odi-474481/full-scorecard |title=England v India 2011, 5th ODI |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=14 June 2024}}</ref>

On his T20I debut, Bairstow had competition for the role of wicket-keeper as both [[Jos Buttler]] and [[Craig Kieswetter]] were in the team. Kieswetter "took the gloves", so Bairstow and Buttler played as specialist batters. However, neither of them did bat because Kieswetter and [[Alex Hales]] won the match with an unbeaten first wicket partnership of 128, after West Indies were dismissed for 125.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/west-indies-tour-of-england-2011-525814/england-vs-west-indies-1st-t20i-525816/full-scorecard |title=England v West Indies 2011, 1st ODI |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=14 June 2024}}</ref> There was a second T201 two days later and [[West Indies cricket team|West Indies]] won by 25 runs, the series ending as a 1–1 draw. They scored 113/5 and then dismissed England for 88. Bairstow was England's fifth batter and he was [[bowled]] by [[Garey Mathurin]] for four.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/west-indies-tour-of-england-2011-525814/england-vs-west-indies-2nd-t20i-525817/full-scorecard |title=England v West Indies 2011, 2nd ODI |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=14 June 2024}}</ref>

In 2011–12, Bairstow visited India, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) as part of various England teams. He played for England in five ODIs and one T20I against [[India cricket team|India]] in October. He then joined England Lions in January 2012 for seven matches against [[Bangladesh national cricket team|Bangladesh A]] and five against [[Sri Lanka national cricket team|Sri Lanka A]]. He rejoined England in February 2012 for three T20Is against [[Pakistan national cricket team|Pakistan]] in the UAE.<ref name="FCBA">{{cite web |url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/90/90667/a_Batting_by_Season.html |title=List A Batting and Fielding in Each Season by Jonny Bairstow |work=CricketArchive |access-date=14 June 2024 |url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref name="FCBT">{{cite web |url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/90/90667/tt_Batting_by_Season.html |title=Twenty20 Batting and Fielding in Each Season by Jonny Bairstow |work=CricketArchive |access-date=12 June 2024 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Bairstow completed his first ODI century in a match against West Indies at [[Old Trafford Cricket Ground|Old Trafford]] in September 2017. He opened the innings for England, after West Indies had totalled 204/9, and scored 100 not out as he led England to a seven-wicket victory.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2017/sep/19/england-west-indies-first-odi-old-trafford-match-report-jonny-bairstow |last=Marks |first=Vic |title=Jonny Bairstow century guides England to routine ODI win over West Indies |work=The Guardian |date=19 September 2017 |access-date=16 June 2024}}</ref>

===World Cup tournaments===
[[File:Jonny Bairstow (2).jpg|right|thumb|250px|Jonny Bairstow with fans after the 2019 Cricket World Cup]]
At the end of the 2012 season, Bairstow was included in the England squad for the [[2012 ICC World Twenty20]] in Sri Lanka. He appeared in all five of the matches that the team played but without success, his highest score being 18. England reached the Super 8 (quarter-final) stage where they lost to eventual champions West Indies.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/icc-world-twenty20-2012-13-531597/england-vs-west-indies-14th-match-group-1-533285/full-scorecard |title=West Indies v England, ICC World Twenty20 2012 |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=15 June 2024}}</ref>

He was left out of England's squads for the [[2014 ICC World Twenty20|2014]] and [[2016 ICC World Twenty20]]s, but he played in the [[2021 ICC World Twenty20|2021]] and [[2024 ICC World Twenty20|2024]] editions. He missed the [[2022 ICC World Twenty20|2022]] tournament, which England won, because of a broken leg.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/62770895 |title=Jonny Bairstow: England batter ruled out of third Test and T20 World Cup |work=BBC Sport |date=2 September 2022 |access-date=15 June 2024}}</ref> In May 2024, he was named in England's squad for the [[2024 ICC Men's T20 World Cup]] tournament.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/articles/cne93vemvreo |title=Men's T20 World Cup squads including England, India & Australia |work=BBC Sport |date=26 May 2024 |access-date=13 June 2024}}</ref>

Bairstow also missed the [[2015 Cricket World Cup]] but took part in the [[2019 Cricket World Cup|2019]] and [[2023 Cricket World Cup|2023]] editions. He was a member of England's winning team in 2019, playing in the final against [[New Zealand national cricket team|New Zealand]] at [[Lords cricket ground|Lord's]]. This was a tied match which was decided by means of a [[super over]]. New Zealand batted first and scored 241/8. In reply, England were all out for 241. Bairstow opened the innings with [[Jason Roy]] and was the third man out, having scored 36, at 71/3. The super over was also a tie, 15 apiece, but England won by virtue of having scored more boundaries.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/live/cricket/47484101 |title=Incredible World Cup final |work=BBC Sport |date=14 July 2019 |access-date=15 June 2024}}</ref>

==Test cricket==
===Debut===
Following a successful start to the [[2012 English cricket season|2012 season]], scoring two centuries for Yorkshire, Bairstow was named in the England squad for the first Test match against [[West Indies Cricket Team|West Indies]] at [[Lord's]] in May.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/england-v-west-indies-2012/content/story/564669.html |title=Bairstow gets call after Bopara injury |work=ESPNcricinfo |date=13 May 2012 |access-date=17 May 2012}}</ref> He played in the match, his debut in Test cricket, and was presented with his England cap by close family friend [[Geoffrey Boycott]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/cricket/41523011 |title=Bairstow on his dad and Christmas with Boycott |work=BBC Sport |access-date=1 January 2023}}</ref> England won the three-match series 2–0. [[Matt Prior]] was England's established wicket-keeper so Bairstow was selected as a specialist batter. He played in all three matches but could only score 38 runs in his four innings. [[South Africa national cricket team|South Africa]] toured England from July to September and also played a three-match Test series. Bairstow was left out of the England team for the first two Tests as the selectors tried other options. This series did not go well for England as South Africa were a very strong team. Bairstow continued to play well for Yorkshire and England recalled him for the third Test at Lord's.<ref name="ESA3T">{{cite web |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/south-africa-tour-of-england-2012-534185/england-vs-south-africa-3rd-test-534227/full-scorecard |title=England v South Africa 2012, 3rd Test |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=6 February 2024}}</ref>

South Africa, leading the series 1–0, won the toss and decided to bat first. They reached 262/7 at close of play on the first day and were all out for 309 in the morning session of the second day. England's early batting struggled against the South African attack and they had been reduced to 54/4 when Bairstow, sixth in the order, joined [[Ian Bell]]. They added 124 for the fifth wicket until Bell was dismissed for 58. Bairstow continued with help from Prior, [[Stuart Broad]], and [[Graeme Swann]], taking the score to 264 when he was bowled by [[Morné Morkel]] for 95. England reached 315, a first innings lead of six after facing disaster before Bairstow came in. Bairstow's innings included thirteen boundaries off 196 balls in just over six hours. In the second innings, South Africa scored 351, thanks largely to a century by [[Hashim Amla]]. England, needing 346 to win, were all out on the final day for 294. Bairstow again played well and scored 54 before he was bowled by [[Imran Tahir]] at 134/5. South Africa won the match by 51 runs and the series 2–0.<ref name="ESA3T"/>

''Wisden'' commented that Bairstow's two innings against South Africa "ought to have been a defining moment... but England seemed unsure how to use him". Bairstow had the talent to be a specialist batter in the team but England appeared to view him as their reserve keeper and, therefore, a spare batter.<ref name="WCY"/> Bairstow told ''Wisden'' that he was "more gutted" to get out in the second innings against South Africa than the first. He thought England had a real chance of reaching their target.<ref name="WCY"/>

===First Ashes series===
[[File:Jonny Bairstow batting, 2013 (2).jpg|thumbnail|right|250px|Bairstow batting against Australia in the 1st Test of the 2013 Ashes series at [[Trent Bridge]].]]
Bairstow went to India and New Zealand in the winter of 2012–13, playing in one Test in each country. He was selected for two home Tests against New Zealand in May 2013 and did well by top-scoring with 41 in the first innings of the first Test.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/wisdenalmanack/content/story/755487.html |last=Chevallier |first=Hugh |title=England v New Zealand, 2013 — First Test |work=Wisden archive |date=2014 |access-date=22 June 2024}}</ref> In the second Test, played at Headingley, he scored 64 off 99 balls and shared a fifth-wicket partnership of 124 with his Yorkshire colleague [[Joe Root]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/wisdenalmanack/content/story/755493.html |last=Hamilton |first=Duncan |title=England v New Zealand, 2013 — Second Test |work=Wisden archive |date=2014 |access-date=22 June 2024}}</ref>

In July 2013, Bairstow made his [[The Ashes|Ashes]] debut against [[Australia national cricket team|Australia]]. After scores of 37 and 15 in the first Test at [[Trent Bridge]], he scored 67 off 146 balls in the second Test at [[Lord's]]. England won both matches and went on to a 3–0 series win. In its tour review, ''Wisden'' commented that Bairstow was "impressive mainly in the field".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/wisdenalmanack/content/story/812911.html |last=Haigh |first=Gideon |title=England v Australia, 2013 — Tour Review |work=Wisden archive |date=2014 |access-date=22 June 2024}}</ref>

There was a return series in Australia the following winter and Bairstow was in the squad. He travelled as reserve wicket-keeper to Matt Prior and did not play in any of the first three Tests, all of which England lost. Prior had been in poor form and Bairstow replaced him for the last two matches. This meant he and his father David became the first father/son combination to keep wicket for England in Test cricket. Although Bairstow performed well behind the wicket, he made only 49 runs in his four innings. Australia won both matches and regained the Ashes with a 5–0 series "whitewash".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/wisdenalmanack/content/story/821255.html |last=Dobell |first=George |title=Australia v England, 2013–14 — Tour Review |work=Wisden archive |date=2014 |access-date=22 June 2024}}</ref>

===2015 recall===
Bairstow was left out of the England set-up for the next 18 months until, in recognition of his outstanding season for Yorkshire in 2015, he was recalled to the squad for an ODI against [[New Zealand cricket team in England in 2015|touring New Zealand]]. He scored 83 not out from 60 balls in that match, which England won, and was rewarded with a place in the team for the third Test against Australia at [[Edgbaston Cricket Ground|Edgbaston]]. England won the series 3–2 and ''Wisden'' remarked that, in direct contrast with other England players, Bairstow "looked impressive rather than convincing".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/wisdenalmanack/content/story/1050005.html |last=Llew |first=Jonathan |title=England v Australia, 2015 — Tour Review |work=Wisden archive |date=2016 |access-date=22 June 2024}}</ref> Bairstow scored 5 in his only innings at Edgbaston, but England won the match by 8 wickets to take a 2–1 series lead, and made no unenforced changes to the team for the fourth Test at Trent Bridge. Australia batted first and were dismissed for a mere 60 in just 18 overs, [[Stuart Broad]] taking 8/15. England in reply had made 96/3 when Bairstow came in to join Joe Root. They shared a stand of 173 until Bairstow was out for 74. England's total was 391/9 declared and they bowled Australia out for 253 to take the match by an innings and 78 runs. In its match report, ''Wisden'' said Root and Bairstow "took control" and that Bairstow was "the more obviously busy, urging himself forward and meeting the bowlers head on". Australia won the last Test but England had secured the series at Trent Bridge.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/wisdenalmanack/content/story/1050023.html |last=Booth |first=Lawrence |title=England v Australia, 2015 — 4th Test |work=Wisden archive |date=2016 |access-date=22 June 2024}}</ref>

Bairstow was in the England team which met [[English cricket team against Pakistan in the UAE in 2015–16|Pakistan in the UAE]] in October and November 2015. They lost the three-match series 2–0 but Bairstow played well as a specialist batter, making useful scores of 43, 41 and 79. He was reserve wicket-keeper to [[Jos Buttler]] who struggled to find his form. Ahead of the [[English cricket team in South Africa in 2015–16|2015–16 series in South Africa]], England announced that Bairstow would be their first-choice wicket-keeper in Test cricket.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/south-africa-v-england-2015-16/content/story/952317.html |title=Bairstow ready to wear gloves with pride |work=ESPNcricinfo |date=14 December 2015 |access-date=15 December 2015}}</ref> In the first Test at [[Kingsmead Cricket Ground|Kingsmead]], in [[Durban]], Bairstow scored 41 and a quick-fire 79 to help England win the match by 241 runs. He also took four catches and completed a stumping.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/england-tour-of-south-africa-2015-16-800431/south-africa-vs-england-1st-test-800461/full-scorecard |title=South Africa v England, 2015–16 — 1st Test |work=ESPNcricinfo |date=December 2015 |access-date=22 June 2024}}</ref>

===World record partnership===
The second Test at [[Newlands Cricket Ground|Newlands]], in [[Cape Town]], was a highpoint in Bairstow's career. England batted first and were going well at 223/5 when Bairstow came in to join [[Ben Stokes]]. Together, they shared a world record partnership of 399 for the sixth wicket which ended when Stokes was [[run out]] as they tried to score the 400th run. Stokes, whose innings was especially memorable, had scored 258, the second-fastest double-century in Test history. Bairstow scored 150 not out, his maiden Test century and a defining moment in his life. As ''Wisden'' described it, Bairstow had reached 95 at lunch on the second day to equal his highest Test score, and he then spent 22 balls getting the next five runs. Completing his century was emotional because he looked to the sky and thought about his father, and also his grandfather who had died a few months earlier. His mother Janet and sister Becky were watching him from the stand. ''Wisden'' summarised his innings: "A cricketer sometimes too tense to give his best for England had never batted so serenely, remarkable given the carnage Stokes was inflicting".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/wisdenalmanack/content/story/1066630.html |last=Wilde |first=Simon |title=South Africa v England, 2015–16 — 2nd Test |work=Wisden archive |date=2016 |access-date=22 June 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/35216886 |title=Ben Stokes hits fastest England double century in Tests |work=BBC Sport |date=3 January 2016 |access-date=22 June 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/england-tour-of-south-africa-2015-16-800431/south-africa-vs-england-2nd-test-800463/full-scorecard |title=South Africa v England, 2015–16 — 2nd Test |work=ESPNcricinfo |date=January 2016 |access-date=22 June 2024}}</ref>

===2015–16 to 2021–22===
Bairstow played in most of England's Test matches during the next six years, although he was left out of the team for the winter tours of New Zealand and Sri Lanka in 2019–20.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/27684247/england-drop-jonny-bairstow-call-dom-sibley-zak-crawley-new-zealand-tests |title=England drop Jonny Bairstow, call up Dom Sibley, Zak Crawley for New Zealand Tests |date=23 September 2019 |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=13 February 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/28680063/foakes-jennings-rise-bairstow-moeen-slide-view |title=Foakes and Jennings on the rise, Bairstow and Moeen slide from view |date=11 February 2020 |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=13 February 2020}}</ref> He toured [[English cricket team in Bangladesh in 2016–17|Bangladesh]] and [[English cricket team in India in 2016–17|India in 2016–17]], and [[English cricket team in India in 2020–21|India again in 2020–21]]. He played in a total of seven Tests on the [[English cricket team in Australia in 2017–18|2017–18 tour of Australia]] and [[English cricket team in New Zealand in 2017–18|New Zealand]]. He visited Sri Lanka twice, in [[English cricket team in Sri Lanka in 2018–19|2018–19]] and [[English cricket team in Sri Lanka in 2020–21|2020–21]]; and the West Indies twice, in [[English cricket team in the West Indies in 2018–19|2018–19]] and [[English cricket team in the West Indies in 2021–22|2021–22]].<ref name="FCM">{{cite web |url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/90/90667/First-Class_Matches.html |title=First-class matches played by Jonny Bairstow |work=CricketArchive |access-date=22 June 2024 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Bairstow had a "dream series" in [[Sri Lankan cricket team in England and Ireland in 2016|2016 against Sri Lanka]]. He scored "an imperious century" (140) at Headingley, his county's home ground, having arrived at the crease with England in trouble on 83 for five. There was a similar situation in the third Test at Lord's. England were 84 for four when he came in and he scored 167 not out, taking them to 416. England won the series 2–0, and Bairstow won the Player of the Series award, jointly with [[Kaushal Silva]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/wisdenalmanack/content/story/1108479.html |last=Dobell |first=George |title=England v Sri Lanka, 2016 — Tour Review |work=Wisden archive |date=2017 |access-date=22 June 2024}}</ref>

In the winter of 2021–22, Bairstow went to both Australia, where he played in two Tests; and the West Indies, where he played in three. In the fourth Test against Australia at the [[Sydney Cricket Ground]], he scored 113 in the final innings, England's only century of the series which helped them hold on for a draw. ''Wisden'' commented that, in a disastrous series for England (who lost 4–0), "the batters totalled 17 noughts and one spirited hundred from Jonny Bairstow".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/wisdenalmanack/content/story/1344882.html |last=Haigh |first=Gideon |title=Australia v England, 2021–22 — Tour Review |work=Wisden archive |date=2022 |access-date=22 June 2024}}</ref> In the first Test against the West Indies, Bairstow scored a "pugnacious" 140 to rescue England after they had sunk to 48 for four on the opening day of the series, which West Indies won 1–0.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/wisdenalmanack/content/story/1344882.html |last=Martin |first=Ali |title=West Indies v England, 2021–22 — Tour Review |work=Wisden archive |date=2023 |access-date=22 June 2024}}</ref>

===''Wisden'' Trophy winner in 2022===
In the [[2022 English cricket season|2022 season]], Bairstow played in only six first-class matches which were all Tests: three against New Zealand, one against India, and two against South Africa.<ref name="FCM"/> His statistical record for the season shows that he played eleven innings, twice not out; he scored a total of 681 runs at an average of 75.66; and his highest score was 162 with four centuries and one half-century. He also took twelve catches.<ref name="FCBF"/> ''Wisden'' said that Bairstow's "deconstruction of the usual rules of Test batting" was "stunning".<ref name="WTPY">{{cite web |url=https://www.wisden.com/wisden-cricketers-almanack/the-wisden-trophy-for-the-best-test-performance-of-the-year-the-candidates |title=The Wisden Trophy for the best Test performance of the year: The candidates |publisher=Wisden Cricketers' Almanack |date=13 April 2023 |access-date=23 June 2024}}</ref>

In June, playing in the second Test of the [[New Zealand cricket team in England in 2022|series against New Zealand]] at Trent Bridge, Bairstow hit a match-winning 136 off 92 balls on the fifth day, guiding England to their target of 299.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/new-zealand-in-england-2022-1276891/england-vs-new-zealand-2nd-test-1276902/full-scorecard |title=New Zealand v England 2022, 2nd Test |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=15 June 2022}}</ref> His hundred, completed off 77 balls, was the second-fastest Test century by an English batter.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/cricket/61800089 |title=Brilliant Bairstow leads England to victory-GB |work=BBC Sport |access-date=15 June 2022}}</ref> In the third Test at Headingley, England had slumped to 55 for six in their first innings after New Zealand had scored 329. Bairstow was joined by [[Jamie Overton]] and they added 241 for the seventh wicket, the partnership ending when Overton was out for 97. Bairstow went on to score 162 at better than a run-a-ball and England totalled 360 for a first innings lead. They won the match by seven wickets after Bairstow scored 71 not out in the second innings, sharing an unbeaten fourth wicket partnership of 111 with Joe Root, who scored 86 not out.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/new-zealand-in-england-2022-1276891/england-vs-new-zealand-3rd-test-1276903/match-report |last=Miller |first=Andrew |title=Jonny Bairstow, Joe Root rampage to England's seven-wicket win, and series clean-sweep |work=ESPNcricinfo |date=27 June 2022 |access-date=23 June 2024}}</ref>

England's next Test was the rescheduled fifth match of the previous year's series against India. The match had been postponed because of the disruption caused by the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. India batted first and scored 416. They then reduced England to an overnight 84 for five at the end of the second day. Bairstow again needed to stage a rescue and he did this with an innings of 106 on the third day which saved the [[follow-on]] and took England to 284. India reached 125 for three at the close to lead by 257.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/62017731 |last=Shemilt |first=Stephan |title=Jonny Bairstow ton fails to halt tourists |work=BBC Sport |date=3 July 2022 |access-date=22 June 2024}}</ref> They were all out for 245 on the fourth day, leaving England with a target of 378 to win. With Root and Bairstow together, they reached 259 for three at the close and so needed another 119 on the final day. Root (142 not out) and Bairstow (114 not out) both completed centuries as they reached the target before lunch with an unbroken partnership of 269. The successful run chase was England's highest in Test cricket. Bairstow's century was his second of the match, his fourth in five innings, and his sixth in 2022.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/62031210 |last=Shemilt |first=Stephan |title=Joe Root and Jonny Bairstow complete record chase at Edgbaston |work=BBC Sport |date=5 July 2022 |access-date=22 June 2024}}</ref>

For his performances in the 2022 season, Bairstow received the Professional Cricketers' Association Men's Cricketer of the Year award<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/63134678 |title=Sciver & Bairstow take top PCA awards |work=BBC Sport |access-date=6 October 2022}}</ref> and the Cricket Writers' Club Bob Willis Trophy.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/63134676 |title=Bairstow wins Cricket Writers' Club award |work=BBC Sport |access-date=6 October 2022}}</ref> He was also nominated for the [[ICC Men's Test Cricketer of the Year|2022 Men's Test Cricketer of the Year]] title<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/2990720 |title=Nominees for ICC Men's Test Cricketer of the Year 2022 revealed |work=International Cricket Council |access-date=6 January 2023}}</ref> and was named in the [[ICC Men's Test Team of the Year]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/3032492?sf174602727=1&fbclid=IwAR2t8y3OmbECCZdlJIl-2LlHwq_pBcvzTNBy9I3GEJ2bZw7sIZ0uncoH4gs |title=ICC Men's Test Team of the Year 2022 revealed |work=www.icc-cricket.com |access-date=12 February 2023}}</ref> Bairstow was the inaugural winner of the "Wisden Trophy", launched in April 2023 to recognise the outstanding Test performance of the previous calendar year.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.wisden.com/wisden-cricketers-almanack/jonny-bairstow-named-wisden-trophy-winner-2022#:~:text=Jonny%20Bairstow%20wins%20inaugural%20Wisden%20Trophy%20for%20Edgbaston%20masterclass |last=Ehantharajah |first=Vithushan |title=Jonny Bairstow wins inaugural Wisden Trophy for Edgbaston masterclass |publisher=Wisden Cricketers' Almanack |date=17 April 2023 |access-date=23 June 2024}}</ref> Ten performances were nominated, including three by Bairstow; the others, one each, were by [[Ebadot Hossain]], [[Usman Khawaja]], [[Tom Latham (cricketer)|Tom Latham]], [[Ravindra Jadeja]], [[Prabath Jayasuriya]], [[Marnus Labuschagne]], and [[Harry Brook]]. Bairstow won for his two centuries in the match against India.<ref name="WTPY"/>

In August 2022, Bairstow was playing golf near his home when he fell and, in freak circumstances, broke his left leg in three places. He was out of action for eight months until he made his comeback playing for Yorkshire in May 2023. He returned to Test cricket in June when he played in a match against [[Ireland national cricket team|Ireland]] at Lord's.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/england-vs-ireland-2023-jonny-bairstow-feared-he-d-never-walk-again-after-horrific-leg-injury-1376536 |last=Ehantharajah |first=Vithushan |title=Jonny Bairstow feared he'd 'never walk again' after horrific leg injury |work=ESPNcricinfo |date=17 May 2023 |access-date=23 June 2024}}</ref>

===2023 to present===
Australia toured England that year and Bairstow played in all five Tests. The series was drawn 2–2 and so Australia retained the Ashes. On the final day of the second Test at Lord's, England were chasing a target of 371 and had reached 193 for 5 during the morning session. Bairstow was batting with Ben Stokes and had scored 10 when he faced the final ball of an over from [[Cameron Green]]. It was a short-pitched delivery and Bairstow ducked underneath it, letting it go through to wicket-keeper [[Alex Carey]]. Thinking the ball was dead, Bairstow left his ground and started walking down the pitch to talk to Stokes. Just prior to Bairstow leaving his crease, Carey had underarmed the ball towards the wicket. Bairstow had left his crease when the ball struck the stumps and Carey appealed for a stumping. The decision was left to the VCR umpire who gave Bairstow out. The crowd reacted by booing the Australians and chanting: "Same old Aussies. Always cheating". In fact, they were not cheating because Carey's action complied with [[Laws of Cricket|Law 20.1.2]] in that the fielding team had not "ceased to regard it (the ball) as in play".<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ashes-finds-its-flashpoint-as-jonny-bairstow-stumping-ignites-england-1385390 |last=Roller |first=Matt |title=Ashes finds its flashpoint as Bairstow stumping ignites England |work=ESPNcricinfo |date=2 July 2023 |access-date=23 June 2024}}</ref>

Bairstow's best performance in the series was in the fourth Test at Old Trafford where he scored 99 not out in England's 592. He was left on 99 when the last wicket fell, the third time that has happened in an Ashes Test after Geoff Boycott in 1979 and [[Steve Waugh]] in 1995.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/records/99-not-out-and-199-299-etc-284122 |title=Records for Test Matches – 99 not out (and 199, 299, etc.) |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=23 June 2024}}</ref> With England in a strong position, the match ended in a draw after the final day's play was abandoned due to heavy rain.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/the-ashes-2023-1336037/england-vs-australia-4th-test-1336046/full-scorecard |title=England v Australia 2023, 4th Test |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=23 June 2024}}</ref>

From January to March 2024, Bairstow played in five Tests for [[English cricket team in India in 2023–24|England in India]], a series which India won 4–1. He scored 238 runs in his ten innings with a highest score of 39. The final Test at the [[Himachal Pradesh Cricket Association Stadium]] in [[Dharamshala]] was the [[List of cricketers who have played 100 Tests|100th played]] by both Bairstow and India's [[Ravichandran Ashwin]]. Bairstow also reached 6,000 Test runs in the match.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/tournaments/world-test-championship/news/jonny-bairstow-marks-his-100th-appearance-for-england-in-test-cricket |title=Jonny Bairstow marks his 100th appearance for England in Test cricket |work=International Cricket Council |date=7 March 2024 |access-date=23 June 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news
|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/sports/cricket/story/jonny-bairstow-completes-6000-test-runs-india-vs-england-fifth-test-2511758-2024-03-07/ |title=Jonny Bairstow's record-filled Dharamsala Test |work=IndiaToday |access-date=7 March 2024 |date=23 June 2024}}</ref>

He was dropped for the West Indies tour of England in July 2024, with England men's managing director [[Rob Key]] pointing to his declining form as the reason for his omission.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/eng-vs-wi-1st-test-rob-key-backs-promotion-for-rare-talent-as-jamie-smith-earns-maiden-test-call-up-1441821 |title=Rob Key backs promotion for 'rare talent' as Jamie Smith earns maiden Test call-up |work=ESPNcricinfo |date = 1 July 2024 | access-date=21 July 2024}}</ref>

==Franchises==
Bairstow first played [[Twenty20]] in 2010, for Yorkshire. Since he became an international, he has been in demand by various T20 franchises and has played for [[Peshawar Zalmi]] ([[Pakistan Super League]]; 2015–2016), [[Sunrisers Hyderabad]] ([[Indian Premier League]]; 2019–2021), [[Welsh Fire]] ([[The Hundred (cricket)|The Hundred]]; 2021–2023), [[Punjab Kings]] (Indian Premier League; 2022–2024).

Despite going unsold in the 2025 IPL mega auction, he joined [[Mumbai Indians]] at a price of 5.25 crore (approximately £459,316) as a replacement for [[Will Jacks]] for the IPL 2025 playoffs.<ref>{{cite news |title=Mumbai Indians sign Jonny Bairstow, Richard Gleeson and Charith Asalanka |url=https://www.iplt20.com/news/4219/mumbai-indians-sign-jonny-bairstow-richard-gleeson-and-charith-asalanka |access-date=29 December 2025 |work=iplt20.com |date=20 May 2025}}</ref><ref name="JBCA"/>

In addition to these, Bairstow signed a short-term contract in November 2018 to play for [[Kerala Kings]], alongside [[Eoin Morgan]], in the [[T10 League]] in [[Sharjah]]. In his second (and final) game for the franchise, he scored 84 not out off 24 balls — a record in the format — helping his team to a seven-wicket victory.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/46404495 |title=Jonny Bairstow smashes eight sixes in new T10 record score |work=BBC Sport |date=30 November 2018 |access-date=13 January 2019}}</ref>

==Style and personality==
When Bairstow was chosen as one of the [[Wisden Cricketers of the Year|''Wisden'' Cricketers of the Year]] for 2015, the dedication began by saying he is "a good man for a crisis".<ref name="WCY"/> Bairstow has been hardened by adversity and is inspired by the closeness of a family united by his father's untimely death.<ref name="SFT"/> His mother, Janet, has commented on his work ethic and his determination to succeed.<ref name="SFT"/>

His England batting coach, [[Mark Ramprakash]], says Bairstow is "a proper batter who can play in all formats" and that he excels "in difficult conditions when the ball (is) moving around".<ref name="MRG">{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2024/mar/05/jonny-bairstow-batter-england-100-caps-india-cricket |last=Ramprakash |first=Mark |title=Bairstow is a proper batter but coaching him is tricky because he is so instinctive |work=The Guardian |date=5 March 2024 |access-date=15 June 2024}}</ref> However, Ramprakash adds that while some leading players like [[Alastair Cook]], Ian Bell, or himself are "methodical and organised", Bairstow is not. He is unpredictable in his methods because he is "spontaneous and instinctive", though Ramprakash acknowledges that Bairstow's method is "no less valid" than his own.<ref name="MRG"/> While Bairstow is capable of playing defensively to keep his wicket intact, Ramprakash feels that he is at his best when he can take "the aggressive option" and attack the bowling.<ref name="MRG"/>

==Media==
In 2017, Bairstow published an autobiography titled ''A Clear Blue Sky'', co-written with [[Duncan Hamilton (journalist)|Duncan Hamilton]]. The title recalls the moment when he scored his first Test century at Newlands and looked up to see "a clear blue sky" as he remembered his father.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Bairstow |first1=Jonny |last2=Hamilton |first2=Duncan |title=A Clear Blue Sky |publisher=HarperCollins |location=London |date=2017 |isbn=978-0-00-823268-9}}</ref>

'''Joseph Charles Buttler''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|size=100%|MBE}} (born 8 September 1990) is an English international [[cricket]]er and the former captain of the [[England cricket team]]. He plays for [[Lancashire County Cricket Club|Lancashire]] in domestic cricket and has played in multiple [[Twenty20|T20]] leagues. Widely regarded as England's greatest-ever white-ball cricketer,<ref>{{Cite web | title=Jos Buttler is our greatest ever white-ball cricketer | url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/cricket/2020/09/07/jos-buttleris-greatest-ever-white-ball-cricketer/ | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200908044903/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/cricket/2020/09/07/jos-buttleris-greatest-ever-white-ball-cricketer/ | access-date=2026-09-04 | archive-date=2020-09-08}}</ref> he is known for his innovative and aggressive batting style. He was part of the England team that won the [[2019 Cricket World Cup|2019 ODI World Cup]] and led the team to victory at the [[2022 Men's T20 World Cup|2022 T20 World Cup]].

Buttler made his [[Twenty20 International|T20I]] debut in 2011, his [[One Day International|ODI]] debut in 2012, and his Test debut in 2014. He was the vice-captain and a crucial member of the [[2019 Cricket World Cup squads#England|England team]] that won the [[2019 Cricket World Cup]], and made the [[run out]] during the [[Super Over]] which sealed victory in the [[2019 Cricket World Cup final|final]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/48983890|title=England men win first Cricket World Cup|work=BBC Sport |access-date=15 July 2019|archive-date=15 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190715181544/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/48983890|url-status=live}}</ref> He was appointed captain of England's [[Limited overs cricket|limited-overs]] teams in June 2022.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/cricket/61994862|title=Jos Buttler named England white-ball captain after Eoin Morgan retirement|work=BBC Sport |access-date=30 June 2022}}</ref> He captained England to victory at the [[2022 Men's T20 World Cup|2022 T20 World Cup]], top-scoring for his country at the tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/63613694|title=T20 World Cup: England beat Pakistan to win pulsating final in Melbourne|work=BBC|access-date=13 November 2022|date=13 November 2022}}</ref>

Buttler plays as a right-handed [[Wicket-keeper|wicket-keeper-batsman]] and is England's most-capped T20I player.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/individual/most_matches_career.html?class=3&id=1&type=team|title=England Cricket Team Records & Stats.|work=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=1 November 2021|archive-date=7 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211107074617/https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/individual/most_matches_career.html?class=3;id=1;type=team|url-status=live}}</ref> Along with [[Adil Rashid]], he holds the world record for highest seventh-wicket stand in ODIs: 177 against [[New Zealand national cricket team|New Zealand]] during their [[New Zealand cricket team in England in 2015|2015 tour of England]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/records/252072.html|title=Records. One-Day Internationals. Partnership records. Highest partnerships by wicket.|work=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=28 October 2021|archive-date=28 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211028191143/https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/records/252072.html|url-status=live}}</ref> He is England's highest run-scorer in T20Is,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/batting/most_runs_career.html?class=3&id=1&type=team|title=England Cricket Team Records & Stats.|work=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=1 November 2022|archive-date=7 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211107074708/https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/batting/most_runs_career.html?class=3;id=1;type=team|url-status=live}}</ref> and is one of only two Englishmen to score multiple T20I centuries.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/records/team/batting-most-runs-innings/england-1/twenty20-internationals-3 |title=England T20I Records – High scores |website=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=6 April 2024}}</ref> As a wicket-keeper, he holds the England record for most dismissals in both ODI and T20I formats.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/keeping/most_dismissals_career.html?class=2&id=1&type=team|title=England Cricket Team Records & Stats.|work=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=1 November web|url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/keeping/most_dismissals_career.html?class=3&id=1&type=team|title=England Cricket Team Records & Stats.|work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> In August 2026, Buttler became the highest run-scorer in men's T20 cricket, surpassing Kieron Pollard's previous record.<ref>{{cite the most half-centuries scored by a player in the history of the format.|website=Olympics.com|access-date=6 September 2026}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Born in [[Taunton]], Somerset, on 8 September 1990,<ref name="ESPN308967" /> Buttler was educated at [[King's College, Taunton]], where he displayed his early talent in cricket.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/cricket/2018/08/21/cant-underestimate-feeling-jos-buttlers-maiden-test-century/|title='You can't underestimate that feeling' – Jos Buttler's maiden Test century shows he can be heart of England's team|last=Wigmore|first=Tim|date=21 August 2018|work=The Telegraph|access-date=2 September 2019|language=en-GB|issn=0307-1235|archive-date=2 September 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190902143904/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/cricket/2018/08/21/cant-underestimate-feeling-jos-buttlers-maiden-test-century/|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Domestic career ==
=== Youth ===
Buttler played extensively for Somerset's youth teams, appearing at Under-13, Under-15 and Under-17 level.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/136/136065/Other_matches.html |title=Other matches played by Joseph Buttler (55) |publisher=CricketArchive |access-date=14 May 2010 |archive-date=3 November 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121103043611/http://www.cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/136/136065/Other_matches.html |url-status=dead}}</ref> He made his senior club cricket debut for Cheddar before moving to Glastonbury in the 2006 season, aged just 15, taking three [[Caught|catches]] and 15 [[Run (cricket)|runs]] as wicket-keeper.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/177/177817.html |title=Westbury v Glastonbury |publisher=CricketArchive |date=14 May 2006 |access-date=30 April 2010 |archive-date=3 November 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121103015210/http://www.cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/177/177817.html |url-status=live}}</ref> Later in the same season, he made his first appearance for Somerset Second XI, scoring 71 in the second-innings, and taking six catches in the three-day match against [[Nottinghamshire County Cricket Club|Nottinghamshire]] Second XI.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/86/86407.html |title=Nottinghamshire Second XI v Somerset Second XI |publisher=CricketArchive |date=30 April 2010 |access-date=29 October 2017 |archive-date=14 December 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171214152826/https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/86/86407.html |url-status=live}}</ref> Playing for King's College, he finished the 2006 season with the school's leading [[Batting average (cricket)|batting average]], scoring 447 runs at an average of 49.66.<ref>{{cite book |last=Henderson |first=Douglas |editor1-first=Scyld |editor1-last=Berry |title=Wisden Cricketer's Almanack 2007 |edition=144 |year=2007 |publisher=John Wisden & Co. Ltd. |location=[[Alton, Hampshire]] |isbn=978-1-905625-02-4 |page=1020 |chapter=Schools Cricket, 2006}}</ref> The following season he played regularly for Glastonbury in the [[West of England Premier League]], and for Somerset Under-17s, for whom he scored two centuries; an [[Not out|unbeaten]] 119 during a two-day match against [[Surrey County Cricket Club|Surrey]] Under-17s,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/190/190626.html |title=Surrey Under-17s v Somerset Under-17s |publisher=CricketArchive |date=25 July 2007 |access-date=30 April 2010 |archive-date=3 November 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121103015245/http://www.cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/190/190626.html |url-status=live}}</ref> and 110 against [[Sussex County Cricket Club|Sussex]] Under-17s.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/190/190659.html |title=Sussex Under-17s v Somerset Under-17s |publisher=CricketArchive |date=8 August 2007 |access-date=30 April 2010 |archive-date=3 November 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121103015310/http://www.cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/190/190659.html |url-status=live }}</ref> He once again led the batting averages for King's College, with his 358 runs coming at 51.14.<ref>{{cite book |last=Henderson |first=Douglas |editor1-first=Scyld |editor1-last=Berry |title=Wisden Cricketer's Almanack 2008 |edition=145 |year=2008 |publisher=John Wisden & Co. Ltd. |location=[[Alton, Hampshire]] |isbn=978-1-905625-11-6 |page=967 |chapter=Schools Cricket, 2007}}</ref>

[[File:Jos buttler keeping.jpg|thumb|left|Buttler wicket keeping for [[Somerset County Cricket Club|Somerset]]|alt=A young man with light brown hair is standing on some grass. He is wearing a burgundy, grey and black cricket uniform, large gloves and black trousers covered by black think pads on his lower legs.]]
The highlight of his school career came in April 2008, when he scored 227 [[not out]] during a record-breaking opening [[Partnership (cricket)|stand]] in a 50-over national schools game, adding 340 with [[Alex Barrow]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/cricket/7375597.stm |title=King's duo break schools record |publisher=[[BBC Sport]] |date=30 April 2008 |access-date=1 May 2010}}</ref> He [[Captain (cricket)|captained]] King's during the 2008 season, and improved on his batting totals from the previous two years, scoring 851 runs, over 250 more than any other member of the team.<ref>{{cite book |last=Henderson |first=Douglas |editor1-first=Scyld |editor1-last=Berry |title=Wisden Cricketer's Almanack 2009 |edition=146 |year=2009 |publisher=John Wisden & Co. Ltd. |location=[[Alton, Hampshire]] |isbn=978-1-905625-16-1 |page=903 |chapter=Schools Cricket, 2008}}</ref> His batting average of 94.55 was the sixth highest amongst all school's batsmen reported in ''Wisden'', while his high-score of 227* was the highest score they recorded.<ref>{{cite book |last=Henderson |first=Douglas |editor1-first=Scyld |editor1-last=Berry |title=Wisden Cricketer's Almanack 2009 |edition=146 |year=2009 |publisher=John Wisden & Co. Ltd. |location=[[Alton, Hampshire]] |isbn=978-1-905625-16-1 |page=908 |chapter=Schools Cricket, 2008}}</ref> During that 2008 season, Buttler also played for Somerset Second XI. With captain [[Carl Gazzard]] keeping wicket in the majority of these matches, Buttler played purely as a batsman, although in his final match of the season for the team, he kept wicket and took six catches in the first-innings against [[Worcestershire County Cricket Club|Worcestershire]] Second XI.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/158/158388.html |title=Worcestershire Second XI v Somerset Second XI |publisher=CricketArchive |date=10 September 2008 |access-date=30 April 2010 |archive-date=3 November 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121103015329/http://www.cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/158/158388.html |url-status=live }}</ref> In the previous match, against [[Hampshire County Cricket Club|Hampshire]] Second XI, Buttler had made 140 batting from [[Batting order (cricket)|number four]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/158/158384.html |title=Somerset Second XI v Hampshire Second XI |publisher=CricketArchive |date=3 September 2008 |access-date=30 April 2010 |archive-date=3 November 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121103015358/http://www.cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/158/158384.html |url-status=live}}</ref>

He made his [[First-class cricket|first-class]] debut for Somerset in September 2009, replacing the injured [[Justin Langer]] for the [[County Championship]] match against Lancashire, scoring 30 in his only innings.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.westernmorningnews.co.uk/Horton-ton-cancels-Somerset-s-early-gains/story-11514053-detail/story.html|title=Horton ton cancels out Somerset gains|date=10 September 2009|work=Western Morning News|access-date=15 February 2016}}</ref> He retained his place in the team for the following [[Pro40]] match against Hampshire, making his [[List A cricket|List A]] debut, although he was not required to bat.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/204/204641.html |title=Hampshire v Somerset |publisher=CricketArchive |date=13 September 2009 |access-date=1 May 2010 |archive-date=3 November 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121103020750/http://www.cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/204/204641.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Selected as part of the Somerset squad for the [[2009 Champions League Twenty20]], Buttler made his debut in the 20-over format of the game in Somerset's final match of the league stage, remaining six not out at the close of the innings.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/251/251438.html |title=New South Wales v Somerset |publisher=CricketArchive |date=18 October 2009 |access-date=1 May 2010 |archive-date=22 October 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091022102935/http://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/251/251438.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Buttler again captained King's in 2009, and in the seventeen matches under his leadership they lost only once, and also won the Western School Twenty20 competition.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.somersetcountycc.premiumtv.co.uk/page/News/Newsdetail/0,,11333~2025849,00.html |publisher=[[Somerset County Cricket Club]] |title=JOS BUTTLER LIFTS WISDEN SCHOOL'S CRICKETER OF YEAR |date=15 April 2010 |access-date=3 May 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110725090952/http://www.somersetcountycc.premiumtv.co.uk/page/News/Newsdetail/0%2C%2C11333~2025849%2C00.html |archive-date=25 July 2011 }}</ref> Coupled with his 554 runs for the school at an average of 61.55, and his performances for Somerset, he was named 2010 ''Young Wisden'' Schools Cricketer of the Year.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.wisden.com/default.aspx?id=3 |title=The Young Wisden Schools Cricketer of the Year |work=Wisden |publisher=John Wisden & Co. |access-date=1 May 2010 |archive-date=4 December 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101204005920/http://wisden.com/default.aspx?id=3 |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== First-team opportunity ===
[[File:Jos buttler.JPG|thumb|right|150px|Buttler keeping wicket for [[Somerset County Cricket Club|Somerset]] in the [[ECB40|ECB 40]]|alt=A young man with light brown hair is standing on some grass. He is wearing a burgundy, grey and black cricket uniform, large gloves and black trousers covered by black think pads on his lower legs.]]
When [[Craig Kieswetter]] was called up to the England one-day team in 2010, Buttler was given the chance of a prolonged run in Somerset's first team. [[Brian Rose (cricketer)|Brian Rose]], Somerset's Director of Cricket, chose not to bring in an experienced keeper to deputise, explaining that Kieswetter had been in a similar position three years earlier and that he had good reports of Buttler's ability.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.thisisbristol.co.uk/news/Somerset-hopeful-Buttler-set-profit-Kieswetter-s-England-heroics/article-1862840-detail/article.html |title=Ambitious Buttler ready to stand in for Kieswetter |work=[[The Herald (Plymouth)|The Herald]] |date=22 April 2010 |access-date=1 May 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130505084350/http://www.thisisbristol.co.uk/news/Somerset-hopeful-Buttler-set-profit-Kieswetter-s-England-heroics/article-1862840-detail/article.html |archive-date=5 May 2013}}</ref> In his first match of the 2010 season, Buttler remained 22 not out at the close of Somerset's innings, posting his first runs in List A cricket, and he followed this up with two catches to help Somerset beat [[Glamorgan County Cricket Club|Glamorgan]] in their opening [[ECB40|Clydesdale Bank 40]] fixture.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/262/262613.html |title=Glamorgan v Somerset |publisher=CricketArchive |date=25 April 2010 |access-date=10 May 2010 |archive-date=21 October 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121021204713/http://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/262/262613.html |url-status=live}}</ref>

He made his maiden first-class century in his fourth County Championship match, scoring 144 runs in an innings characterised by "dogged determination and [a] decent range of shots".<ref name="bbc13may10">{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/cricket/counties/8681073.stm |title=Hampshire draw with Somerset as poor start continues |publisher=[[BBC Sport]] |date=13 May 2010 |access-date=14 May 2010}}</ref> In his next match, he scored his debut List A half-century against Sussex. Buttler joined [[James Hildreth]] at the crease with Somerset at 109/4, requiring 183 more runs to win off 129 [[Delivery (cricket)|balls]]. The pair put on a partnership of 158 runs "to turn the game on its head", with Buttler making 69 in 53 balls.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.skysports.com/cricket/match_report/0,19822,11066_85647,00.html |title=Sussex impaled by Sabres |publisher=[[Sky Sports]] |date=15 May 2010 |access-date=18 May 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100517040647/http://www.skysports.com/cricket/match_report/0%2C19822%2C11066_85647%2C00.html |archive-date=17 May 2010 }}</ref> In doing so, they set a new record partnership for the fifth-wicket against Sussex.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Records/England/ListA/Somerset/Partnership_Records/Highest_Partnerships_Somerset_v_Sussex.html |title=Highest Partnerships For Somerset Against Sussex |publisher=CricketArchive |access-date=18 May 2010 |archive-date=3 November 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121103072438/http://www.cricketarchive.com/Archive/Records/England/ListA/Somerset/Partnership_Records/Highest_Partnerships_Somerset_v_Sussex.html |url-status=live }}</ref> His continued good batting form, which also saw him make scores of 52 and 31* in a County Championship match against [[Yorkshire County Cricket Club|Yorkshire]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/262/262674.html |title=Somerset v Yorkshire |publisher=CricketArchive |date=17 May 2010 |access-date=30 June 2010 |archive-date=2 May 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110502060755/http://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/262/262674.html |url-status=live }}</ref> saw him retain his place in the Somerset team upon Kieswetter's return.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/cricket/counties/7742271/Jos-Buttler-follows-Craig-Kieswetters-example-as-Somerset-battle-on.html |title=Jos Buttler follows Craig Kieswetter's example as Somerset battle on |publisher=Telegraph |last=Clutton |first=Graham |date=19 May 2010 |access-date=30 June 2010 |archive-date=24 May 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100524010607/http://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/cricket/counties/7742271/Jos-Buttler-follows-Craig-Kieswetters-example-as-Somerset-battle-on.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

Buttler was named [[Player of the Match awards (cricket)|Man of the Match]] in Somerset's [[2010 Twenty20 Cup|2010 Friends Provident T20]] semi-final victory over Nottinghamshire at the [[Rose Bowl (cricket ground)|Rose Bowl]], reaching a "breathtaking" half-century from 21 balls to score an unbeaten 55 runs in a partnership of 75 with [[Kieron Pollard]].<ref name="ci14aug10">McGlashan, Andrew (14 August 2010) [http://www.espncricinfo.com/fpt20/content/story/472435.html Trescothick and Buttler lead Somerset to the final] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170916100455/http://www.espncricinfo.com/fpt20/content/story/472435.html |date=16 September 2017 }}, ESPNcricinfo. Retrieved 11 November 2017.</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/8053/scorecard/435839/Nottinghamshire-vs-Somerset-2nd-Semi-Final-twenty20-cup-eng/ |title=Nottinghamshire v Somerset |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |date=14 August 2010 |access-date=11 November 2017 |archive-date=11 November 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171111210415/http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/8053/scorecard/435839/Nottinghamshire-vs-Somerset-2nd-Semi-Final-twenty20-cup-eng/ |url-status=live }}</ref> His aggressive batting won him many plaudits and helped Somerset reach the final of the [[2010 Clydesdale Bank 40]] as well as the Twenty20 cup.<ref name="ci4sep10" />
