=== Move to Lancashire ===

At the end of September 2013, Lancashire announced they had signed Buttler.<ref name="ci2oct13" /><ref>{{cite news |date=30 September 2013 |title=Lancashire confirm Buttler signing |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/lancashire-confirm-jos-buttler-signing-675777 |url-status=live |access-date=30 September 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131003143341/http://www.espncricinfo.com/england/content/current/story/675777.html |archive-date=3 October 2013}}</ref> He scored 42 in his first Championship appearance for the county before compiling a "game-changing" innings of 72 on a difficult pitch at [[County Cricket Ground, Northampton|Northampton]]. This showcased Buttler's first-class batting potential and contributed to a record seventh wicket partnership for Lancashire against [[Northamptonshire County Cricket Club|Northants]].<ref name="ci28apr14" /><ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/27183421 Northants v Lancashire: Jos Buttler boosts Red Rose victory hopes] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181219015141/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/27183421 |date=19 December 2018 }}, [[BBC Sport]], 28 April 2014. Retrieved 19 November 2017.</ref><ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/27198784 Northants v Lancashire set up tight finish at Wantage Road], [[BBC Sport]], 29 April 2017. Retrieved 19 November 2017.</ref> He scored his first century for Lancashire (his fourth in first-class cricket) in June against [[Durham County Cricket Club|Durham]]<ref>Hardcastle, Graham (18 June 2014) [http://www.espncricinfo.com/county-cricket-2014/content/story/753571.html Rushworth helps Durham resist Buttler] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201044839/http://www.espncricinfo.com/county-cricket-2014/content/story/753571.html |date=1 December 2017 }}, ESPNcricinfo. Retrieved 22 November 2017.</ref> before equalling the record for the fastest fifty scored in T20 cricket, hitting a half-century in 22 balls against Northants on his way to 58 not out in the [[2014 T20 Blast|2014 NatWest T20 Blast]].<ref>Press Association (20 June 2014) [http://www.espncricinfo.com/county-cricket-2014/content/story/754197.html Buttler's record burns off champions] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201032151/http://www.espncricinfo.com/county-cricket-2014/content/story/754197.html |date=1 December 2017 }}, ESPNcricinfo. Retrieved 22 November 2017.</ref> Lancashire finished runners-up of the T20 competition, losing to [[Warwickshire County Cricket Club|Warwickshire]] in the final.<ref>Dobell, George (23 August 2014) [http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/8053/report/693273/Warwickshire-vs-Lancashire-Final-twenty20-cup-eng Woakes denies Flintoff as Birmingham win Blast] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201045217/http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/8053/report/693273/Warwickshire-vs-Lancashire-Final-twenty20-cup-eng |date=1 December 2017 }}, ESPNcricinfo. Retrieved 22 November 2017.</ref> He played 10 first-class matches for Lancashire during the season and was called into the England Test team as wicket-keeper in July, replacing the injured [[Matt Prior]], although doubts remained about the quality of his wicket-keeping.<ref>Hopps, David (25 July 2014) [http://www.espncricinfo.com/england-v-india-2014/content/story/764055.html Hope springs eternal in Buttler] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201044855/http://www.espncricinfo.com/england-v-india-2014/content/story/764055.html |date=1 December 2017 }}, ESPNcricinfo. Retrieved 22 November 2017.</ref><ref>[https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/136/136065/First-Class_Matches.html First-class matches played by Joe Buttler] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201043632/https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/136/136065/First-Class_Matches.html |date=1 December 2017 }}, CricketArchive. Retrieved 22 November 2017.</ref>

He extended his stay with Lancashire, announcing a new three-year contract on 27 May 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cricket.lancashirecricket.co.uk/news/2016-news/buttler-signs-new-three-year-deal-with-lancashire/|title=Buttler signs new three-year deal with Lancashire|website=Lancashire Cricket Club|access-date=1 November 2021|archive-date=1 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211101144637/https://cricket.lancashirecricket.co.uk/news/2016-news/buttler-signs-new-three-year-deal-with-lancashire/|url-status=live}}</ref>

== England career ==

=== 2008–10: England youth career ===

Buttler's first taste of [[international cricket]] came in July 2008, when he represented England Under-17s in two warm-up matches against [[New Zealand national under-19 cricket team|New Zealand Under-19s]]. Batting at number five, he scored a rapid 77 not out in the 50-over contest, hitting 11 fours and two sixes during the 49 deliveries he faced.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/251/251728.html |title=England Under-17s v New Zealand Under-19s |publisher=CricketArchive |date=21 July 2008 |access-date=3 May 2010 |archive-date=3 November 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121103024256/http://www.cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/251/251728.html |url-status=live }}</ref> He also played in the two-day match between the two teams, scoring 45 in the first-innings as the match was drawn.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/251/251729.html |title=England Under-17s v New Zealand Under-19s |publisher=CricketArchive |date=22 July 2008 |access-date=3 May 2010 |archive-date=3 November 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121103024319/http://www.cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/251/251729.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 2009, Buttler played four matches for England Under-18s, two each against Scotland A and Scotland Development XI. He scored 103 not out in the first of these matches,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/259/259918.html |title=Scotland A v England Under-18s |publisher=CricketArchive |date=26 May 2009 |access-date=1 May 2010 |archive-date=3 November 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121103020651/http://www.cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/259/259918.html |url-status=live }}</ref> and made starts in each of the following matches, reaching double figures on each occasion, but not scoring higher than 28.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/259/259919.html |title=Scotland A v England Under-18s |publisher=CricketArchive |date=27 May 2009 |access-date=15 April 2010 |archive-date=3 November 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121103043625/http://www.cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/259/259919.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/259/259921.html |title=Scotland Development XI v England Under-18s |publisher=CricketArchive |date=29 May 2009 |access-date=15 April 2010 |archive-date=3 November 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121103043639/http://www.cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/259/259921.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/259/259920.html |title=Scotland Development XI v England Under-18s |publisher=CricketArchive |date=29 May 2009 |access-date=15 April 2010 |archive-date=3 November 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121103043657/http://www.cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/259/259920.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Two months later, Buttler made his England Under-19 debut, appearing in the first T20 against [[Bangladesh national under-19 cricket team|Bangladesh Under-19s]]. Playing as a specialist batsman, he scored 33 runs off 17 balls as England won by five wickets.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/247/247628.html |title=England Under-19s v Bangladesh Under-19s |publisher=CricketArchive |date=28 July 2009 |access-date=1 May 2010 |archive-date=3 November 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121103020727/http://www.cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/247/247628.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

During the 2009–10 English winter, Buttler toured with the England Under-19 team. He joined up with the squad in Bangladesh following Somerset's elimination from the Champions League Twenty20 for the seven-match youth [[One Day International]] (ODI) series, playing again as a specialist batsman.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://stats.cricinfo.com/ci/engine/player/308967.html?class=21;filter=advanced;keeper=1;orderby=default;template=results;type=allround |title=Statistics / JC Buttler / Under-19s Youth One-Day Internationals |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=15 May 2010}}</ref> He failed to make a significant impact until the final match when he top-scored for England with 42 runs.<ref>[http://www.espncricinfo.com/bangladesh/content/story/432949.html Mahmudul and Saikat help Bangladesh sign off on high] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171111152944/http://www.espncricinfo.com/bangladesh/content/story/432949.html |date=11 November 2017 }}, ESPNcricinfo, 4 November 1999. Retrieved 11 November 2017.</ref> He remained with the team for the [[2010 Under-19 Cricket World Cup|Under-19 World Cup]], where he played all but one of England's six matches, keeping wicket in three of them. He scored 91 runs in three innings, with a top-score of 78 against [[India national under-19 cricket team|India]] in the fifth-place play-off semi-final. His batting average of 30.33 ranked him fifth on the England team.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Events/NZ/ICC_Under-19_World_Cup_2009-10/England_Under-19s_Batting.html |title=Batting and Fielding for England Under-19s: ICC Under-19 World Cup 2009/10 |publisher=CricketArchive |access-date=1 May 2010 |archive-date=3 November 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121103023334/http://www.cricketarchive.com/Archive/Events/NZ/ICC_Under-19_World_Cup_2009-10/England_Under-19s_Batting.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

2012}}</ref> scoring his maiden limited-overs century against [[Sri Lanka A cricket team|Sri Lanka A]] in January 2012.<ref>[http://www.espncricinfo.com/srilanka/content/story/551248.html Buttler Buttler continued to play regular T20 cricket for England throughout 2012. Against [[South Africa national cricket team|South Africa]] at [[Edgbaston Cricket Ground|Edgbaston]], he joined Somerset teammate Craig Kieswetter with England on 64/3 with only 16 balls remaining. The pair gave "a brutal display of power hitting", raising the final score to 118/5, with Buttler hitting 30 runs from one 32-run over from [[Wayne Parnell]], the second most productive over in International T20 at the time.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/19576600|title=England v South Africa: Jos Buttler stars in crushing Twenty20 win|first=Sam|last=Sheringham|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=12 September 2012|access-date=12 September 2012|archive-date=13 September 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120913001805/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/cricket/19576600|url-status=live}}</ref> The innings established Buttler as a key part of the England one-day team; he had made 10 appearances before the match but reached double figures only once in his six innings, and his performance made him "one of the most talked-about players" in the England team.<ref name="ci16sep12">Hopps, David (16 September 2012) [http://www.espncricinfo.com/icc-world-twenty20-2012/content/story/582499.html Buttler propelled into the spotlight] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171111210716/http://www.espncricinfo.com/icc-world-twenty20-2012/content/story/582499.html |date=11 November 2017 }}, ESPNcricinfo. === 2013–14: Test debut, Champions Trophy and T20 World Cup ===
[[File:Jos Buttler 2014.jpg|thumb|left|Buttler batting against India on Test debut in Southampton (2014).]]
Buttler replaced a rested [[Jonathan Trott]] in the [[English cricket team in India in 2012–13|England ODI squad in India]] in early 2013<ref name="ci18dec12" /> and replaced Craig Kieswetter as the first-choice wicket-keeper halfway through the ODI series.<ref name="ci25jan13">[http://www.espncricinfo.com/india-v-england-2012/content/story/602127.html Buttler admits mixed emotions after ousting friend] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171112190038/http://www.espncricinfo.com/india-v-england-2012/content/story/602127.html |date=12 November 2017 }}, ESPNcricinfo, 25 January 2013. Retrieved 12 November 2017.</ref> This allowed Buttler to break into the England ODI team on a consistent basis, playing regularly throughout the year in both ODI and T20 formats and increasingly as a wicket-keeper, despite some reservations about the quality of his work behind the stumps.<ref name="ci22jan13">Dobell, George (22 January 2013) [http://www.espncricinfo.com/india-v-england-2012/content/story/601767.html England ring for Buttler] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171112191916/http://www.espncricinfo.com/india-v-england-2012/content/story/601767.html |date=12 November 2017 }}, ESPNcricinfo. Retrieved 12 November 2017.</ref><ref name="ci11feb13">Dobell, George (11 February 2013) [http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/story/604503.html Would somebody call the Buttler?] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171112191540/http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/story/604503.html |date=12 November 2017 }}, ESPNcricinfo. Retrieved 12 November 2017.</ref> He scored his maiden half-century for England in a T20 warm-up match at the start of [[English cricket team in New Zealand in 2012–13|England's tour of New Zealand]] followed by his first T20I half-century in the second match of the series.<ref>[http://www.espncricinfo.com/new-zealand-v-england-2013/content/story/603493.html Buttler ready with bat and gloves] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171112191642/http://www.espncricinfo.com/new-zealand-v-england-2013/content/story/603493.html |date=12 November 2017 }}, ESPNcricinfo, 5 February 2013. Retrieved 12 November 2017.</ref><ref>Hopps, David (12 February 2013) [http://www.espncricinfo.com/new-zealand-v-england-2013/content/story/604543.html Brendon McCullum blitz draws New Zealand level] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171112191214/http://www.espncricinfo.com/new-zealand-v-england-2013/content/story/604543.html |date=12 November 2017 }}, ESPNcricinfo. Retrieved 12 November 2017.</ref> After being confirmed as England's first-choice limited-overs wicket-keeper,<ref name="ci25feb13">Dobell, George (25 February 2013) [http://www.espncricinfo.com/england/content/story/606412.html Giles vows to be more "ruthless" as coach] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171112190548/http://www.espncricinfo.com/england/content/story/606412.html |date=12 November 2017 }}, ESPNcricinfo. Retrieved 12 November 2017.</ref> he played in every match in the [[2013 Champions Trophy|2013 ICC Champions Trophy]] in England. For his performances in 2013, he was named in the T20I XI by [[Cricinfo]].<ref>{{cite web |title=AB, Ajmal and Co |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/review2013/content/story/705667.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190716154221/http://www.espncricinfo.com/review2013/content/story/705667.html |archive-date=16 July 2019 |access-date=16 July 2019 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

Buttler played again in the [[2014 World Twenty20|2014 ICC World Twenty20]] in Bangladesh in March and played regular one-day cricket throughout the year. He scored his maiden ODI century against [[Sri Lanka national cricket team|Sri Lanka]] at [[Lord's]] in May, scoring 121 in 61 balls with nine fours and four sixes, the then-fastest century by any England batsman.<ref>{{cite web |title=Records / One-Day Internationals / Batting records / Fastest hundreds |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/records/211608.html |publisher=ESPNcricinfo (ESPN Internet Ventures) |access-date=31 May 2014 |archive-date=7 November 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161107213559/http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/records/211608.html |url-status=live}}</ref> During the fifth ODI of the [[Sri Lankan cricket team in England in 2014|series]] at [[Edgbaston Cricket Ground|Edgbaston]], Buttler was controversially '[[Run out|Mankaded]]' by [[Sachithra Senanayake]], leading to tension between the teams. England captain [[Alastair Cook]] expressed his disappointment, stating: "I've never seen it before in a game. I was pretty disappointed. If he was properly trying to steal the single then I could possibly understand it. But he was half a yard out of his crease.".<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2014/jun/03/england-fury-sri-lanka-mankad-run-out-jos-buttler|title=England fury as Sri Lanka run out Jos Buttler Mankad-style in last ODI|last=Edgbaston|first=Andy Wilson at|date=3 June 2014|work=The Guardian|access-date=31 May 2019|language=en-GB|issn=0261-3077|archive-date=31 May 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190531021105/https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2014/jun/03/england-fury-sri-lanka-mankad-run-out-jos-buttler|url-status=live}}</ref>

After first choice wicket-keeper [[Matt Prior]] stood down after injury on 22 July 2014, Buttler was called up for the England squad for the [[Indian cricket team in England in 2014#3rd Test|third Test against India]]. He made 85 runs from 83 balls in his first Test innings.<ref>{{cite web |title=England vs India, 3rd Investec Test, Southampton, July 27 – 31, 2014 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/india-tour-of-england-2014-667693/england-vs-india-3rd-investec-test-667715/full-scorecard |website=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=27 June 2024}}</ref> He played in the final three Tests of the series before reverting to one-day duty, touring Sri Lanka at the end of the year.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gardner |first1=Alan |title=Buttler's timely intervention reinvigorates England |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/jos-buttler-s-timely-intervention-reinvigorates-england-807921 |website=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=27 June 2024 |date=6 December 2014}}</ref>

=== 2015–17: World Cup, Ashes series, UAE and tour of Bangladesh ===
[[File:Jos Buttler 2017.jpg|thumb|Jos Buttler representing England in a Twenty20 International against South Africa at Taunton in June 2017.]]
After playing for England in the [[Carlton Mid Triangular Series in Australia in 2014–15|Tri-series in Australia]] at the start of the year, Buttler was once again involved with England at an international tournament, playing in the [[2015 Cricket World Cup]] in Australia and New Zealand. He scored an unbeaten 39 in 19 balls against Sri Lanka<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/8039/scorecard/656441/england-vs-sri-lanka-22nd-match-pool-a-icc-cricket-world-cup-2014-15|title=Full Scorecard of England vs Sri Lanka, World Cup, 22nd Match, Pool A – Score Report |work=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=29 May 2019|archive-date=29 June 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190629011423/https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/8039/scorecard/656441/england-vs-sri-lanka-22nd-match-pool-a-icc-cricket-world-cup-2014-15|url-status=live}}</ref> and made 65 against [[Bangladesh national cricket team|Bangladesh]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/8039/scorecard/656463/bangladesh-vs-england-33rd-match-pool-a-icc-cricket-world-cup-2014-15|title=Full Scorecard of Bangladesh vs England, World Cup, 33rd Match, Pool A – Score Report |work=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=29 May 2019|archive-date=28 May 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190528030011/http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/8039/scorecard/656463/bangladesh-vs-england-33rd-match-pool-a-icc-cricket-world-cup-2014-15|url-status=live}}</ref> but ultimately England lost both matches in a disastrous campaign, failing to progress beyond the group stages.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/31792930|title=Cricket World Cup 2015: England knocked out by Bangladesh|date=9 March 2015|access-date=29 May 2019|language=en-GB|archive-date=31 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181031181843/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/31792930|url-status=live}}</ref>

Later in the English winter he was selected in the Test team, as wicket-keeper, for the [[English cricket team in the West Indies in 2014–15|tour of the West Indies]]. He continued in the role throughout the English summer, playing both [[New Zealand cricket team in England in 2015|Tests against New Zealand]] and all five [[Australian cricket team in England and Ireland in 2015|Ashes Tests against Australia]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Statsguru – JC Buttler – Tests – match by match list |url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/player/308967.html?class=1;template=results;type=batting;view=match |website=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=27 June 2024}}</ref>

He continued to play one-day cricket alongside his Test role, making his then highest ODI score of 129 from 77 balls against [[New Zealand national cricket team|New Zealand]].<ref>{{cite news |title=England hit record 408–9 to thrash New Zealand in ODI |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/33065934 |url-status=live |date=9 June 2015|access-date=31 May 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190225045020/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/33065934 |archive-date=25 February 2019 |language=en-GB}}</ref>

After playing in the [[English cricket team against Pakistan in the UAE in 2015–16|first two Tests against Pakistan]] in the [[United Arab Emirates]] during October, Buttler was dropped for the third Test, replaced as wicket-keeper by [[Jonny Bairstow]], and was not selected for any of the Test matches during [[English cricket team in South Africa in 2015–16|England's tour of South Africa]], although he did play again in the one-day fixtures during the tour. In the fourth ODI against Pakistan in [[Dubai]] in November, he scored a 46-ball century, the fastest ODI hundred by an England player.<ref name="BBC34879336">{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/34879336|title=Jos Buttler breaks record as England beat Pakistan to win series|date=20 November 2015|access-date=31 May 2019|language=en-GB|archive-date=30 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201030113233/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/34879336|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/pakistan-v-england-2015-16/content/story/942455.html|title=Buttler's record-breaking ton demolishes Pakistan|date=20 November 2015|work=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=31 May 2019|archive-date=31 May 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190531010426/http://www.espncricinfo.com/pakistan-v-england-2015-16/content/story/942455.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

Buttler again played for England in the [[2016 World Twenty20|2016 ICC World Twenty20]] and was a regular fixture in the limited-overs squad throughout the year. He scored an unbeaten 90 runs against Pakistan as part of an England record score of 444/3, the fastest half-century by an Englishman.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/records/284095.html |title=Fastest 50 in ODIs |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=31 August 2016 |archive-date=24 October 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121024223402/http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/records/284095.html |url-status=live}}</ref> Both records have since been surpassed.

Buttler captained the England team in the [[English cricket team in Bangladesh in 2016–17|ODI series]] against Bangladesh in October 2016 after numerous players, including regular captain [[Eoin Morgan]], declined to tour over raised security concerns following a [[July 2016 Dhaka attack|terrorist attack in Dhaka]] in July.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/cricket/2016/09/09/jos-buttler-to-captain-englands-one-day-team-in-bangladesh-follo/|title=Jos Buttler to captain England in Bangladesh following Eoin Morgan's decision to pull out of tour|last=Hoult|first=Nick|date=9 September 2016|work=The Telegraph|access-date=29 May 2019|language=en-GB|issn=0307-1235|archive-date=29 May 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190529104130/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/cricket/2016/09/09/jos-buttler-to-captain-englands-one-day-team-in-bangladesh-follo/|url-status=live}}</ref> In the second ODI, there was some controversy as Buttler was involved in a heated exchange with numerous Bangladesh players following his dismissal to [[Taskin Ahmed]]. Buttler, aggravated by the opposition's excessive celebrations, turned to confront them, resulting in him being ushered away by the [[Umpire (cricket)|umpires]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/cricket/news/12123/10612206/bangladesh-v-england-tempers-flare-during-and-after-second-odi|title=Bangladesh v England: Tempers flare during and after second ODI|work=Sky Sports |access-date=29 May 2019|archive-date=29 May 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190529104134/https://www.skysports.com/cricket/news/12123/10612206/bangladesh-v-england-tempers-flare-during-and-after-second-odi|url-status=live}}</ref> Following the incident, Buttler was kept away by the [[International Cricket Council]] (ICC) and received one demerit point to his peace record, while Bangladesh captain [[Mashrafe Mortaza]] and [[Sabbir Rahman]] were each fined 20% of their match fees and given a demerit point and their money removed.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/37607649|title=England's Jos Buttler given ICC reprimand as Bangladesh players fined|date=10 October 2016|access-date=29 May 2019|language=en-GB|archive-date=25 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210525085928/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/37607649|url-status=live}}</ref>

Buttler was again reserve wicket-keeper for the Test series against Bangladesh. He returned to the England Test team for the third Test against India in November, playing in the final three Tests of the series. Buttler averaged just under 40 in a horror tour for England resulting in a 4–0 hammering, he top scored in Mumbai with a counter-attacking 76 to drag the visitors to a solid score.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/england-tour-of-india-2016-17-1030195/india-vs-england-4th-test-1034815/full-scorecard|title=Full Scorecard of England vs India 4th Test 2016/17 – Score Report.|work=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=1 November 2021|archive-date=1 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211101144636/https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/england-tour-of-india-2016-17-1030195/india-vs-england-4th-test-1034815/full-scorecard|url-status=live}}</ref> He continued as a regular in the limited-overs team throughout 2016 and 2017, playing again for England in the [[2017 Champions Trophy|2017 ICC Champions Trophy]], but was unable to break back into the Test team and was not selected for the [[2017–18 Ashes series]] in Australia. He was named in the [[ICC Awards|ICC World ODI XI]] in 2016.<ref name="ESPN1073990">{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/review2016/content/story/1073990.html|title=The trump cards of 2016|date=30 December 2016|work=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=16 July 2019|archive-date=16 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190716172819/http://www.espncricinfo.com/review2016/content/story/1073990.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== 2018–2022: Return to Test cricket, World Cup and Ashes series ===
In May 2018, Buttler was recalled into England's Test squad to [[Pakistani cricket team in England in 2018|play Pakistan]] at Lord's later that month.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/44105904|title=England v Pakistan: Jos Buttler & Dominic Bess named in squad for first Test|date=15 May 2018|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=15 May 2018|language=en-GB|archive-date=15 May 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180515144247/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/44105904|url-status=live}}</ref> He had a successful return to Test cricket, scoring two half-centuries and scoring the most runs in the series; he also won the Man of the Match award at [[Headingley Cricket Ground|Headingley]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Dobell |first=George |date=8 June 2018 |title=Success on Test recall 'was a bit of a surprise' – Jos Buttler |work=ESPNcricinfo |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/success-on-test-recall-was-a-bit-of-a-surprise-jos-buttler-1148894 |url-status=live |access-date=24 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180625021808/http://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/23735055/success-test-recall-was-bit-surprise-jos-buttler |archive-date=25 June 2018}}</ref> His unbeaten 80 was the catalyst to put England ahead of the game after first innings.

In the subsequent [[Australian cricket team in England in 2018|ODI series against Australia]] in June 2018, he scored two half-centuries in the first four matches and then, in the fifth and final game of the series, he made 110 not out to take England to a historic series whitewash.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/44595347|title=England v Australia: Jos Buttler century secures 5–0 ODI whitewash|date=24 June 2018|access-date=29 May 2019|language=en-GB|archive-date=4 October 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191004051905/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/44595347|url-status=live}}</ref> In this match, no other English batsman made more than 20 and Buttler was afterwards described as "the best white-ball wicketkeeper batsman in the world".<ref>{{cite web |title=Batting records. One-Day Internationals   |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/player/308967.html?class=2;spanmin2=1+Jun+2018;spanval2=span;template=results;type=batting;view=innings |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=24 June 2018 |archive-date=25 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180625022248/http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/player/308967.html?class=2;spanmin2=1+Jun+2018;spanval2=span;template=results;type=batting;view=innings |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Dobell |first=George |date=24 June 2018 |title=Jos Buttler earns 'best in the world' tag after immense century |work=ESPNcricinfo |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/jos-buttler-earns-best-in-the-world-tag-after-immense-century-1150304 |url-status=live |access-date=24 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180625022845/http://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/23896950/jos-buttler-earns-best-world-tag-immense-century |archive-date=25 June 2018}}</ref> Buttler was named Man of the Match for his 110 not out, and also named Man of the Series for his impressive contributions with both bat and gloves.<ref>{{cite news |title=England hero Jos Buttler: 'Winning games you don't deserve to are the most enjoyable' |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/cricket/2018/06/24/england-hero-jos-buttler-winning-games-dont-deserve-enjoyable/ |website=The Telegraph |date=24 June 2018 |access-date=10 July 2018 |archive-date=13 July 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180713065844/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/cricket/2018/06/24/england-hero-jos-buttler-winning-games-dont-deserve-enjoyable/ |url-status=live |last1=Hoult |first1=Nick }}</ref> Buttler's innings was remarkable, coming in at 27–4, he looked the only settled batsman before the hosts slumped to 114–8. Alongside the tail, he dragged England home in dramatic style. In 2020, [[Wisden Cricketers' Almanack|Wisden]] ranked it Buttler's finest ODI hundred, as well as the best ODI innings of 2018.<ref>{{cite web |date=3 October 2020 |title=Jos Buttler's Nine ODI Centuries, Ranked |url=https://www.wisden.com/cricket-features/jos-buttlers-nine-odi-centuries-ranked |access-date=31 March 2025 |website=Wisden}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last1=Remmington |first1=Billy |url=https://wisden.com/year-in-review/odi-innings-year-no-1-buttlers-masterclass-australia|title=ODI Innings Of The Year: No.1 Buttler Delivers Stunning, Measured Knock|date=23 December 2018|website=Wisden|access-date=17 November 2020|archive-date=8 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201108100846/https://wisden.com/year-in-review/odi-innings-year-no-1-buttlers-masterclass-australia|url-status=live}}</ref> In the T20I match of Australia's tour, Buttler scored the fastest T20I half-century by an English cricketer, in 22 balls.<ref>Dobell, George. (27 June 2018) [http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/18021/report/1119542/england-vs-australia-only-t20i-aus-in-eng-2018 Jos Buttler and Adil Rashid ensure Australia end tour winless] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180628073604/http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/18021/report/1119542/england-vs-australia-only-t20i-aus-in-eng-2018 |date=28 June 2018}}. ESPNcricinfo. Retrieved 3 July 2018</ref>

Buttler replaced [[James Anderson (cricketer)|James Anderson]] as the Test vice-captain on 31 July 2018, thus combining the role in all formats.<ref name="BBC45017582">{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/45017582|title=England v India: Adil Rashid named as hosts' only spinner for first Test|date=31 July 2018|access-date=20 April 2019|language=en-GB|archive-date=27 November 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181127224226/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/45017582|url-status=live}}</ref> He registered his maiden Test century in the third Test of [[Indian cricket team in England in 2018|India's tour of England]] in August 2018, with a score of 106.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/cricket/jos-buttler-century-england-vs-india-test-scorecard-scoreboard-jonathan-liew-a8501911.html|title=Jos Buttler emerges from Test wilderness to savour his century|date=21 August 2018|website=The Independent|access-date=20 April 2019|archive-date=23 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180823183845/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/cricket/jos-buttler-century-england-vs-india-test-scorecard-scoreboard-jonathan-liew-a8501911.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Buttler then retained his place in the Test and one-day squads, being selected to [[English cricket team in Sri Lanka in 2018–19|tour Sri Lanka]] in October and into the following year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ecb.co.uk/england/men/news/854903/england-confirm-test-squad-for-sri-lanka-series|title=England confirm Test squad for Sri Lanka series|date=21 September 2018|website=England and Wales Cricket Board|access-date=1 June 2019|archive-date=24 December 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181224234941/https://www.ecb.co.uk/england/men/news/854903/england-confirm-test-squad-for-sri-lanka-series%20|url-status=live}}</ref> In a low-scoring series, Buttler hit two vital half-centuries as England romped to a 3–0 win. He was commended for nullifying the extremely difficult batting conditions by employing techniques such as using his feet and frequently playing sweep shots.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/46210111|title='Clever Buttler took initiative away'|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=17 November 2020|archive-date=15 November 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181115080741/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/46210111|url-status=live}}</ref>

In February 2019, during the fourth ODI of [[English cricket team in the West Indies in 2018–19|England's tour of the West Indies]], Buttler scored a career-best 150 from 77 deliveries as England reached 418/6.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/18913/scorecard/1158069/west-indies-vs-england-4th-odi-england-tour-of-wi-2018-19|title=Full Scorecard of West Indies vs England 4th ODI 2019 – Score Report |work=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=20 April 2019|archive-date=12 April 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190412011238/http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/18913/scorecard/1158069/west-indies-vs-england-4th-odi-england-tour-of-wi-2018-19|url-status=live}}</ref> During this innings, he hit 12 sixes, at the time the most by any English batsman in an ODI, and went from 51 to 100 in just 15 balls and from 100 to 150 in just 16 deliveries. This was part of an England world record for the most sixes in an ODI, with 24.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.ndtv.com/cricket/england-hit-record-24-sixes-against-the-windies-and-jos-buttler-smashes-half-of-them-watch-2000529|title=England Hit Record 24 Sixes Against The Windies And Jos Buttler Smashes Half Of Them – Watch. Cricket News|last=NDTVSports.com|website=NDTVSports.com|access-date=20 April 2019|archive-date=20 April 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190420033225/https://sports.ndtv.com/cricket/england-hit-record-24-sixes-against-the-windies-and-jos-buttler-smashes-half-of-them-watch-2000529|url-status=live}}</ref> Following the innings, West Indian batsman [[Chris Gayle]] praised Buttler, stating, "He is superb, one of the best strikers [of the ball] in world cricket today.{{nbsp}}... In the second ODI of the five-match [[Pakistani cricket team in England in 2019|series against Pakistan]] in May, Buttler scored an unbeaten 110 from 55 balls, his century coming in only 50 deliveries. ==== 2019 Cricket World Cup ====
In April 2019, he was named as the vice-captain of the [[2019 Cricket World Cup squads#England|England squad]] for the [[2019 Cricket World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Jofra Archer misses World Cup cut but included to play Ireland, Pakistan |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/jofra-archer-misses-initial-world-cup-cut-but-set-for-england-debut-1181187 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190417102319/http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/story/1181187.html |archive-date=17 April 2019 |access-date=17 April 2019 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/1183273 |title=England leave out Jofra Archer from World Cup squad |work=International Cricket Council |access-date=17 April 2019 |archive-date=17 April 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190417102319/https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/1183273 |url-status=live}}</ref> The ICC named Buttler as the key player of England's squad prior to the tournament.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/1227388 |title=Team preview: England |work=International Cricket Council |access-date=28 May 2019 |archive-date=28 May 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190528125728/https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/1227388 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Buttler made a quiet start to the tournament, scoring only 18 runs in the opening match of the tournament against South Africa at [[The Oval]], which ended in a comprehensive 104-run win for England.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/live-scores/cricket/england-v-south-africa/21515/scorecard|title=England vs South Africa. 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190601010729/https://www.skysports.com/live-scores/cricket/england-v-south-africa/21515/scorecard|url-status=live}}</ref> In the next match against Pakistan, he scored 103 from 76 balls (the then-fastest century by an English batsman in a World Cup) and shared a 130-run partnership with [[Joe Root]] for the fourth wicket, despite a shock 14-run defeat.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/48504940|title=Cricket World Cup: Pakistan shock England at Trent Bridge|date=3 June 2019|access-date=3 June 2019|language=en-GB|archive-date=3 June 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190603180237/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/48504940|url-status=live}}</ref> He made 64 in the third match |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/england-s-record-streak-of-300-plus-scores-1187873 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190608221538/http://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/26926622/england-record-streak-300-plus-scores |archive-date=8 June 2019 |access-date=8 June 2019 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> However, he did not keep wicket during Bangladesh's innings after sustaining a minor hip injury while batting, making way for [[Jonny Bairstow]] to assume the role for the match,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://metro.co.uk/2019/06/08/jos-buttler-injury-update-englands-cricket-world-cup-victory-bangladesh-9873952/|title=Jos Buttler injury update after England's World Cup which England won by 106 runs.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/48569905|title=Cricket World Cup: Jason Roy hits 153 as England beat Bangladesh in Cardiff|date=8 June 2019|access-date=8 June 2019|language=en-GB|archive-date=8 June 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190608180122/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/48569905|url-status=live}}</ref>

Buttler scored 59 runs in the [[2019 Cricket World Cup final|final]] against New Zealand and contributed to a crucial 110-run partnership with [[Ben Stokes]] to help tie the match. His innings was particularly crucial and game-changing as he scored at a quicker rate on a difficult pitch where other batsmen including his partner and Man Of the Match Ben Stokes struggled. Towards the end with both teams making 241 from their respective innings, he was selected to bat in the ensuing [[Super Over]] along with Stokes, from which the pair scored 15 runs; Buttler scoring seven with a boundary from the final ball. He completed the [[run out]] of [[Martin Guptill]] on the last ball of New Zealand's over as he attempted a match-winning second run. The throw was from [[Jason Roy]] which was quite wide of the stumps but Buttler's game awareness and compusure made up for it as he completed the run out. His match winning run out was later awarded as the moment of the year in 2020 in BBC Sports awards of 2019. This tied the Super Over and secured England's maiden World Cup title, winning by a superior boundary count.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/48983890|title=England win Cricket World Cup: Ben Stokes stars in dramatic victory over New Zealand|date=14 July 2019|access-date=15 July 2019|language=en-GB|archive-date=15 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190715181544/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/48983890|url-status=live}}</ref>

In July 2019, following England's World Cup success, the ECB named Buttler in the fourteen-man Test squad for the upcoming [[2019 Ashes series|Ashes series]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ecb.co.uk/england/men/news/1294745/england-name-squad-for-first-ashes-test|title=England name squad for first Ashes Test|date=27 July 2019|website=England and Wales Cricket Board|access-date=31 July 2019|archive-date=28 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190728131952/https://www.ecb.co.uk/england/men/news/1294745/england-name-squad-for-first-ashes-test|url-status=live}}</ref>

==== 2021 ====
On 11 December 2020, Buttler was named vice captain for the [[English cricket team in Sri Lanka in 2020–21|tour of Sri Lanka in January 2021]] following [[Ben Stokes]]' resting.<ref>{{cite web |date=11 December 2020 |title=Moeen, Bairstow, Lawrence In Revamped England Test Squad |url=https://www.wisden.com/cricket-news/moeen-bairstow-lawrence-in-revamped-england-test-squad |access-date=31 March 2025 |website=Wisden |language=en-GB}}</ref> He made scores of 30, 55 and 46 not out in [[Galle International Stadium|Galle]] as England won 2–0.<ref>{{cite news|title=England complete win on dramatic day|language=en-GB|publisher=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/55793231|access-date=1 February 2021|archive-date=30 January 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210130185011/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/55793231|url-status=live}}</ref> He retained the wicket-keeping duties for the tour despite his troubled summer and performed impressively, taking 9 catches and executing his first Test stumping.<ref>{{cite news|last=Goodwill|first=Jake|date=26 January 2021|title=Why did Jos Buttler's wicket-keeping look so accomplished in Sri Lanka?|language=en-GB|work=The Telegraph|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/cricket/2021/01/26/did-jos-buttlers-wicket-keeping-look-accomplished-sri-lanka/|access-date=1 February 2021|issn=0307-1235|archive-date=5 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210205222505/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/cricket/2021/01/26/did-jos-buttlers-wicket-keeping-look-accomplished-sri-lanka/|url-status=live}}</ref> It was announced on 21 January that Buttler would be returning home after the first test of the upcoming [[English cricket team in India in 2020–21|series in India]] in line with England's rotation and resting policy.<ref>{{cite web |date=6 March 2021 |title=Did England's Rotation Policy Cost Them The Test Series Against India? In September 2021, Buttler was named in England's squad for the [[2021 Men's T20 World Cup|2021 ICC Men's T20 World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/t20-world-cup-2021-tymal-mills-makes-englands-t20-world-cup-squad-no-return-for-ben-stokes-1276997 |title=Tymal Mills makes England's T20 World Cup squad, no return for Ben Stokes |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=9 September 2021 |archive-date=9 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210909103311/https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/t20-world-cup-2021-tymal-mills-makes-englands-t20-world-cup-squad-no-return-for-ben-stokes-1276997 |url-status=live }}</ref> On 1 November 2021, in England's World Cup match against [[Sri Lanka national cricket team|Sri Lanka]], Buttler scored his first century in T20I cricket, with a 101[[not out|*]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/av/cricket/59123486 |title=T20 World Cup – England v Sri Lanka: Jos Buttler seals first international T20 century with six |work=BBC Sport |access-date=1 November 2021 |archive-date=1 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211101160048/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/av/cricket/59123486 |url-status=live }}</ref> and became the first English men's player to score a century in all three formats of cricket (Tests, ODIs and T20Is).

In November 2021, Buttler was named as the vice-captain of England's squad for the [[2021–22 Ashes series]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jos Buttler commits to Ashes tour as England name squad for Australia |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/the-ashes-2021-22-jos-buttler-commits-to-ashes-tour-as-england-name-squad-for-australia-1282342 |access-date=22 April 2022 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

====2022====
On 17 June 2022, Buttler featured in the first ODI [[English cricket team in the Netherlands in 2022#1st ODI|as part of a three-match series]] against the [[Netherlands national cricket team|Netherlands]]. He scored 162 [[not out]] in 70 balls, his personal ODI high score<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bt.com/sport/news/2022/june/red-hot-england-sizzle-and-post-new-world-record-score-as-jos-buttler-hits-162 |title=Red-hot England sizzle and post new world record score as Jos Buttler hits 162 |work=BT Sport |access-date=17 June 2022}}</ref> and England would score 498 runs, which is the highest [[One Day International|ODI]] score of all time.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cricbuzz.com/cricket-news/122679/stats-england-now-have-top-three-totals-in-odis |title=Stats: England now have top three totals in ODIs |work=CricBuzz |date=17 June 2022 |access-date=17 June 2022}}</ref> During that match Buttler scored 150 runs in 65 balls, the second fastest in the history of ODI cricket, one ball behind [[AB de Villiers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Stats – England smash record for highest-ever total in ODIs |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/neth-vs-eng-2022-1st-odi-stats-england-smash-record-for-highest-ever-total-in-odis-1320404 |access-date=17 June 2022 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

===White-ball captaincy===
Following the retirement of [[Eoin Morgan]], Buttler was appointed as captain of the England ODI and T20I teams on 30 June 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |date=30 June 2022 |title=Jos Buttler replaces Eoin Morgan as England white-ball captain |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2022/jun/30/jos-buttler-replaces-eoin-morgan-as-england-white-ball-captain-cricket |access-date=16 November 2022 |website=The Guardian |language=en}}</ref> His first series as permanent captain was at home to India, with England losing 2–1 in both T20Is and ODIs.<ref>{{Cite web |title=India tour of England, India in England 2022 score, Match schedules, fixtures, points table, results, news |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/india-in-england-2022-1276893 |access-date=16 November 2022 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> This was followed by a drawn ODI series against South Africa and another 2–1 defeat in T20Is,<ref>{{Cite web |title=South Africa tour of England, South Africa in England 2022 score, Match schedules, fixtures, points table, results, news |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/south-africa-in-england-2022-1276896 |access-date=16 November 2022 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> with Buttler making a string of scores between 12 and 29.

====2022 T20 World Cup====
[[File:Jos Buttler with Rishi Sunak in 2023.jpg|thumb|Buttler in a meeting with [[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom]] [[Rishi Sunak]] after England's [[2022 Men's T20 World Cup|2022 T20 World Cup]] victory. He is holding the T20 World Cup trophy in his hand.]]
Buttler's first tournament as captain was the [[2022 Men's T20 World Cup|2022 T20 World Cup]]. After an opening victory against Afghanistan, a surprise defeat against Ireland and a rained-out game against Australia saw England needing to win their remaining two games to qualify for the next round. In the match against New Zealand, Buttler scored 73 off 47 balls, which helped England seal a crucial victory.<ref>{{cite web|title=England move up to second with crucial win|url=http://www.cricbuzz.com/cricket-news/124362/england-move-up-to-second-with-crucial-win|access-date=13 November 2022|work=Cricbuzz|date=November 2022 }}</ref> In the semi-final, he scored 80 not-out as part of a record opening stand of 170 with Alex Hales (86*), seeing England to a 10-wicket victory and a place in the final.<ref>{{cite web|title=England gallop to summit clash with 10-wicket drubbing of India|url=http://www.cricbuzz.com/cricket-news/124474/england-gallop-to-summit-clash-with-10-wicket-drubbing-of-india|access-date=13 November 2022|work=cricbuzz|date=10 November 2022 }}</ref> England won the final against [[2022 Men's T20 World Cup|2022 ICC Men's T20 World Cup]] Pakistan by 5 wickets, with another quickfire score of 26 from 17 balls by Buttler setting them off to a fast start; however, the team was reeling with his dismissal at 45–3, before [[Ben Stokes]] saw the team to victory with one over left. With this Buttler became only the second England captain to win a T20 World Cup, making him a World Cup-winning captain. Buttler's role as a captain was particularly the most important in England's victorious World Cup campaign as he gave all-rounders [[Sam Curran]] and Ben Stokes clarity about their roles and instilled confidence in the youngsters which helped them perform to their potential, and he succeeded both as a captain and as a batsman in the World Cup.<ref>{{cite web|title='Ben Stokes is an incredible player for the big nights'|url=http://www.cricbuzz.com/cricket-news/124498/ben-stokes-is-born-for-these-situations-england-cricket-t20-world-cup-final|access-date=12 November 2022|work=cricbuzz}}</ref>

==== 2024 T20 World Cup ====
In May 2024, he was named the captain in England's squad for the [[2024 Men's T20 World Cup|2024 ICC Men's T20 World Cup]] tournament.<ref>{{Cite web |title=England's Squad for the ICC Men's T20I World Cup 2024 |url=https://www.scorewaves.com/news-details/england-squad-icc-mens-t20i-world-cup-2024 |access-date=11 June 2024 |website=ScoreWaves |language=en}}</ref> England reached the semi-final of the tournament, losing to eventual champions India.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-06-27 |title=T20 World Cup results: England thrashed by India in Guyana semi-final |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/cricket/articles/clwylrqenw0o |access-date=2026-09-30 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

====2025 Champions Trophy====
Buttler resigned the captaincy during the [[2025 Champions Trophy|Champions Trophy 2025]], with England having lost their first two matches in the competition and being unable to qualify for the semi-final stage.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/articles/cg4kk4xypwvo Buttler steps down as England's white-ball captain], [[BBC Sport]], 28 February 2025. Retrieved 28 February 2025.</ref>

== T20 franchise career ==
Buttler has become increasingly involved in playing franchise T20 cricket around the world, and has been described as arguably England's "first ever global Twenty20 superstar".<ref name="ESPN308967" /> On 5 August 2026, Buttler became the all time leading run scorer in T20s, surpassing [[Kieron Pollard]]'s tally of 14,803.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Peter |first1=Mike |title=Buttler breaks T20 runs record in Super Giants win |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/cricket/articles/cn4n1j7ejp1o |access-date=5 August 2026 |date=5 August 2026}}</ref>

=== 2013–14 Big Bash League ===

Buttler's first experience of franchise cricket came in 2013/14 when he played for [[Melbourne Renegades]] in the [[2013–14 Big Bash League season]] in Australia. This coincided with the buildup to the England one-day team playing in Australia at the beginning of 2014 and followed him having been with the England development squad in [[Perth]] for a month prior to the start of the competition.<ref>Hogan, Jesse (16 December 2013) [http://www.smh.com.au/sport/cricket/rising-english-cricket-star-jos-buttler-to-turn-out-for-melbourne-renegades-20131215-2zfbo.html Rising English cricket star Jos Buttler to turn out for Melbourne Renegades] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171202115249/http://www.smh.com.au/sport/cricket/rising-english-cricket-star-jos-buttler-to-turn-out-for-melbourne-renegades-20131215-2zfbo.html |date=2 December 2017 }}, ''[[The Sydney Morning Herald]]''. Retrieved 19 November 2017.</ref> Buttler was initially only expected to play for Melbourne in their first two matches of the competition but this was extended due to the late arrival of Pakistani all-rounder [[Mohammad Hafeez]], who had been called into the [[Pakistan national cricket team|Pakistan]] Test squad. After having scored a "stunning" 61 runs against [[Brisbane Heat]] in his third match,<ref>[http://www.heraldsun.com.au/melbourne-renegades-hold-onto-bighitting-englishman-jos-buttler-for-one-more-game/news-story/582ef43e920877896cca84701c820e9f Melbourne Renegades hold onto big-hitting Englishman Jos Buttler for one more game], ''[[Herald Sun]]'', 31 December 2013. Retrieved 19 November 2014.</ref> Buttler eventually played in five Big Bash matches for Melbourne before leaving to join the England squad.<ref>Hayes, Mark (4 January 2014) [http://www.dailytelegraph.com.au/sport/cricket/glenn-maxwell-cameron-white-guide-melbourne-stars-past-melbourne-renegades/news-story/808a091223d0313cacf430612843f705 Glenn Maxwell, Cameron White guide Melbourne Stars past Melbourne Renegades], ''[[The Daily Telegraph (Sydney)]]''. Retrieved 19 November 2017.</ref><ref>Hogan, Jesse (11 January 2014) [http://www.smh.com.au/sport/cricket/dwayne-bravo-returns-to-melbourne-to-play-for-big-bashs-renegades-20140110-30mnw.html Dwayne Bravo returns to Melbourne to play for Big Bash's Renegades] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171202214839/http://www.smh.com.au/sport/cricket/dwayne-bravo-returns-to-melbourne-to-play-for-big-bashs-renegades-20140110-30mnw.html |date=2 December 2017 }}, ''[[The Sydney Morning Herald]]''. Retrieved 19 November 2017.</ref>

=== 2016 and 2017 Indian Premier League ===

Buttler played for [[Mumbai Indians]] in the 2016 and 2017 [[Indian Premier League]] (IPL) seasons.

=== 2017–18 Bangladesh Premier League ===

Expecting to be left out of the [[2017–18 Ashes series]] in Australia, Buttler signed a two-year contract in August 2017 with [[Comilla Victorians]] to appear in the [[Bangladesh Premier League]] (BPL).<ref>Martin, Ali (11 August 2017) [https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2017/aug/11/jos-buttler-bangladesh-premier-league-ashes-cricket-twenty-20 Jos Buttler signs Bangladesh T20 deal before expected Ashes snub] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170909023502/https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2017/aug/11/jos-buttler-bangladesh-premier-league-ashes-cricket-twenty-20 |date=9 September 2017 }}, ''[[The Guardian]]''. Retrieved 19 November 2017.</ref><ref>[http://www.thedailystar.net/sports/cricket/buttler-set-join-comilla-1447183 Buttler set to join Comilla] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201031114/http://www.thedailystar.net/sports/cricket/buttler-set-join-comilla-1447183 |date=1 December 2017 }}, ''[[The Daily Star (Bangladesh)]]'', 11 August 2017. Retrieved 19 November 2017.</ref> He made his BPL debut in November 2017, scoring 48 runs from 42 balls in his second match for Comilla and recorded his first BPL half-century in his third match.<ref>Manhar Uddin (8 November 2017) [http://www.thedailystar.net/sports/bangladesh-cricket/bangladesh-premier-league-bpl-2017-victorians-outclass-stuttering-vikings-1488028 Victorians outclass stuttering Vikings] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171115131049/http://www.thedailystar.net/sports/bangladesh-cricket/bangladesh-premier-league-bpl-2017-victorians-outclass-stuttering-vikings-1488028 |date=15 November 2017}}, ''[[The Daily Star (Bangladesh)]]''. Retrieved 19 November 2017.</ref>

=== 2017–18 Big Bash League ===
In November 2017, Buttler was signed as an overseas player for [[Sydney Thunder]] for the [[2017–18 Big Bash League season|Big Bash League season 7]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cricbuzz.com/cricket-news/98559/sydney-thunder-sign-jos-buttler-for-forthcoming-bbl-07-season|title=Sydney Thunder sign Jos Buttler for forthcoming BBL season|website=Cricbuzz|date=25 November 2017 |access-date=1 June 2019|archive-date=1 June 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190601193642/https://www.cricbuzz.com/cricket-news/98559/sydney-thunder-sign-jos-buttler-for-forthcoming-bbl-07-season|url-status=live}}</ref> He played in the first six games for Thunder before joining the England squad for the limited-over fixtures of [[English cricket team in Australia in 2017–18|England's tour of Australia]]. He scored 67 and 81 in separate games against [[Hobart Hurricanes]], being named Player of the Match in the first fixture.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/8044/game/1114866/hobart-hurricanes-vs-sydney-thunder-11th-match-big-bash-league-2017-18|title=Sydney Thunder beat Hobart Hurricanes by 57 runs – Hobart Hurricanes vs Sydney Thunder, Big Bash League, 11th Match Match Summary, Report |work=ESPNcricinfo|date=30 December 2017 |access-date=1 June 2019|archive-date=1 June 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190601193641/http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/8044/game/1114866/hobart-hurricanes-vs-sydney-thunder-11th-match-big-bash-league-2017-18|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/8044/report/1114868/sydney-thunder-vs-hobart-hurricanes-13th-match-big-bash-league-2017-18|title=Recent Match Report – Sydney Thunder vs Hobart Hurricanes, Big Bash League, 13th Match |work=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=1 June 2019|archive-date=1 June 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190601193639/http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/8044/report/1114868/sydney-thunder-vs-hobart-hurricanes-13th-match-big-bash-league-2017-18|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== 2018 Indian Premier League ===
In January 2018, Buttler was bought by the [[Rajasthan Royals]] in the [[List of 2018 Indian Premier League personnel changes|2018 IPL auction]] for {{INRConvert|44|m|-3}}.<ref>{{cite web |title=List of sold and unsold players |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-2018-player-auction-list-of-sold-and-unsold-players-1134446 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180128031100/http://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/22218394/ipl-2018-player-auction-list-sold-unsold-players |archive-date=28 January 2018 |access-date=27 January 2018 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> Buttler had a difficult start for the Royals, making a high score of just 29 in his first seven innings. However, on being promoted to open the batting mid-tournament, his performances significantly improved. He subsequently became only the second batsman in IPL history to achieve five scores of fifty or more in consecutive matches.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/match-report/rajasthan-royals-mumbai-indians-ipl-match-report-jos-buttler-sanju-samson-evin-lewis-playoffs/2018-05-14 |title=Buttler equals long-standing IPL record |access-date=29 April 2019 |work=Cricket.com.au |archive-date=19 April 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190419214444/https://www.cricket.com.au/news/match-report/rajasthan-royals-mumbai-indians-ipl-match-report-jos-buttler-sanju-samson-evin-lewis-playoffs/2018-05-14 |url-status=live }}</ref> He made an unbeaten 95 from 60 balls against [[Chennai Super Kings]], his highest score in the season at that time.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/8048/report/1136603/rajasthan-royals-vs-chennai-super-kings-43rd-match-indian-premier-league-2018|title=Recent Match Report – Rajasthan Royals vs Chennai Super Kings, Indian Premier League, 43rd match |work=ESPNcricinfo|date=11 May 2018 |access-date=31 May 2019|archive-date=31 May 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190531014408/http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/8048/report/1136603/rajasthan-royals-vs-chennai-super-kings-43rd-match-indian-premier-league-2018|url-status=live}}</ref>

Buttler again played for Sydney Thunder in the [[2018–19 Big Bash League season|2018–19 Big Bash League]], this time alongside England teammate Joe Root.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/45288760|title=Big Bash: Joe Root and Jos Buttler agree Sydney Thunder stint|date=23 August 2018|access-date=1 June 2019|language=en-GB|archive-date=23 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180923054404/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/45288760|url-status=live}}</ref> The [[England and Wales Cricket Board]] (ECB) allowed Buttler and Root to play the first half of the season, despite a busy international schedule throughout 2019.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/cricket/2018/08/23/ecb-give-joe-root-jos-buttler-green-light-represent-sydney-thunder/|title=ECB give Joe Root and Jos Buttler green light to represent Sydney Thunder in Big Bash despite hectic 2019 schedule|last=Berry|first=Scyld|date=23 August 2018|work=The Telegraph|access-date=1 June 2019|language=en-GB|issn=0307-1235|archive-date=1 June 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190601200201/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/cricket/2018/08/23/ecb-give-joe-root-jos-buttler-green-light-represent-sydney-thunder/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Buttler made his highest BBL score of 89 from 54 deliveries against Hobart Hurricanes, despite a seven-wicket defeat,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.news.com.au/sport/cricket/big-bash/live-hobart-hurricanes-vs-sydney-thunder-at-blundstone-arena/news-story/f7a5d539f0725814ae58d08395c06179|title=Thunder crack in 'disastrous' finish|date=28 December 2018|website=NewsComAu|access-date=1 June 2019|archive-date=1 June 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190601200159/https://www.news.com.au/sport/cricket/big-bash/live-hobart-hurricanes-vs-sydney-thunder-at-blundstone-arena/news-story/f7a5d539f0725814ae58d08395c06179|url-status=live}}</ref> before making 55 in a thrilling one-run win over [[Perth Scorchers]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/46734798|title=Big Bash League: Jos Buttler shines but Joe Root fails again|date=2 January 2019|access-date=1 June 2019|language=en-GB|archive-date=19 August 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190819223810/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/46734798|url-status=live}}</ref> Buttler departed as the tournament's leading run-scorer, with 273 from seven innings, making three half-centuries at an average of 39.00.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/46793136|title=Big Bash League: Joe Root and Jos Buttler end BBL stint with defeat|date=8 January 2019|access-date=1 June 2019|language=en-GB|archive-date=7 February 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190207154813/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/46793136|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== 2020 Indian Premier League ===
Following the rescheduling of the 2020 IPL to the autumn due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], Buttler was retained by the Rajasthan Royals. He started the campaign opening the batting before moving to the middle order to aid the "balance of the team".<ref>{{cite web|title=Jos Buttler prefers opening batting in T20 – but says it was his idea to move down the order in IPL|work=Sky Sports |url=https://www.skysports.com/cricket/news/12173/12129979/jos-buttler-prefers-opening-batting-in-t20-but-says-it-was-his-idea-to-move-down-the-order-in-ipl|access-date=16 April 2021|archive-date=16 April 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210416221445/https://www.skysports.com/cricket/news/12173/12129979/jos-buttler-prefers-opening-batting-in-t20-but-says-it-was-his-idea-to-move-down-the-order-in-ipl|url-status=live}}</ref> He scored 328 runs at an average of 33 with 2 half-centuries, including a match-winning 70* against [[Chennai Super Kings]] in [[Sheikh Zayed Cricket Stadium|Sheikh Zayed Stadium]].

=== 2021 Indian Premier League ===
Buttler started the IPL in batting at 4, scoring a rapid 25 in the opening game, continuing from the previous campaign. However, after [[Ben Stokes]] broke a finger in the team's first match, Buttler was promoted once again to the opening berth.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ben Stokes: England all-rounder to miss rest of Indian Premier League with broken finger|work=Sky Sports |url=https://www.skysports.com/cricket/news/12123/12274618/ben-stokes-england-all-rounder-to-miss-rest-of-indian-premier-league-with-suspected-broken-hand|access-date=16 April 2021|archive-date=16 April 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210416223742/https://www.skysports.com/cricket/news/12123/12274618/ben-stokes-england-all-rounder-to-miss-rest-of-indian-premier-league-with-suspected-broken-hand|url-status=live}}</ref> On 2 May 2021, he scored his maiden IPL and T20 hundred, in 56 balls, against [[Sunrisers Hyderabad]]. His final score was 124 runs in just 64 balls and his contribution enabled Rajasthan Royals to win the game, for which he was named "Man of the Match".<ref>{{cite web|title=Jos' maiden T20 Century against Sunrisers Hyderabad|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/ipl/live-blog/rr-vs-srh-live-ipl-score-today-match-2021-rajasthan-royals-vs-sunrisers-hyderabad-match-28/liveblog/82354213.cms|access-date=2 May 2021|work=Times of India|date=2 May 2021 |archive-date=2 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210502113953/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/ipl/live-blog/rr-vs-srh-live-ipl-score-today-match-2021-rajasthan-royals-vs-sunrisers-hyderabad-match-28/amp_liveblog/82354213.cms|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== 2022 Indian Premier League ===
In November 2021, [[Rajasthan Royals]] retained Jos Buttler for {{INR}}10 crores ahead of the [[List of 2022 Indian Premier League personnel changes|IPL Mega Auction 2022]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.indiatvnews.com/sports/cricket/rr-retention-list-ipl-2022-sanju-samson-jos-buttler-yashasvi-jaiswal-retained-remaining-purse-inr-62-cr-for-ipl-2022-mega-auction-747483|title=Jos Butter retained by Rajasthan Royals for IPL 2022 season|work=India TV News|date=30 November 2021 |access-date=30 November 2021}}</ref> He scored his first century of the season against [[Mumbai Indians]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jos Buttler slams IPL 2022's first Century as Rajasthan Royals beat Mumbai Indians to maintain perfect start|url=https://sports.ndtv.com/ipl-2022/mi-vs-rr-buttler-slams-century-as-rr-beat-mi-to-maintain-perfect-start-2858968|access-date=3 April 2022 |website=NDTVSports.com|language=en}}</ref> He scored his second century of the season against [[Kolkata Knight Riders]], and third against [[Delhi Capitals]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=DC vs RR, IPL Live Score 2022: Sensational Jos Buttler slams third ton of the season : 17.5 : Rajasthan Royals : 182/1 |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/ipl/live-blog/dc-vs-rr-live-score-updates-ipl-2022-delhi-capitals-rajasthan-royals/liveblog/91003590.cms |access-date=22 April 2022 |website=The Times of India |language=en}}</ref> Buttler scored his 4th century of the season against [[Royal Challengers Bengaluru]], which made him the first Overseas player to score 4 Hundreds in a single IPL edition and only the second player in the history of IPL after [[Virat Kohli]] .<ref>{{Cite news |last=Bhattacharya |first=Debayan |date=27 May 2022 |title=Rajasthan Royals' Jos Buttler Slams 4th Century in IPL 2022 |work=India.com |url=https://www.india.com/sports/ipl-2022-rajasthan-royals-jos-buttler-slams-4th-century-of-ongoing-season-5417585/}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Bose |first=Abhimanyu |date=28 May 2022 |title=Jos Buttler Hits 4th Century Of The Season, Equals Virat Kohli's Massive IPL Record |work=NDTV |url=https://sports.ndtv.com/ipl-2022/jos-buttler-hits-4th-century-of-the-season-equals-virat-kohlis-massive-ipl-record-3016397}}</ref> Buttler scored 39 runs in the IPL 2022 final and ended the season with a total of 863 runs, the second highest in IPL history beating [[David Warner (cricketer)|David Warner's]] 848 in [[2016 Indian Premier League|IPL 2016]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Indian Premier League Cricket Team Records & Stats  |url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/batting/most_runs_series.html?id=117&type=trophy |access-date=29 May 2022 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> Buttler secured the 2022 Orange Cap and the awards for most valuable player of the season, most sixes (45) and most fours (83) in the 2022 Edition.<ref>{{Cite news |date=30 May 2022 |title=IPL 2022 award winners: Who won Orange Cap, Purple Cap, Fairplay, other awards |work=Hindustan Times |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cricket/ipl-2022-award-winners-who-won-orange-cap-purple-cap-fairplay-and-other-awards-jos-buttler-umran-malik-yuzvendra-chahal-101653853529740.html}}</ref>

=== The Hundred ===
In April 2022, Buttler was retained by the [[Manchester Super Giants]] for the [[2022 The Hundred season|2022 season]] of [[The Hundred (cricket)|The Hundred]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/60477088 |title=The Hundred 2022: latest squads as Draft picks revealed |work=BBC Sport |access-date=5 April 2022}}</ref>

=== 2022 SA20 League ===
In August 2022, Jos Buttler was drafted by [[Paarl Royals]], a franchise owned by [[Manoj Badale]] for {{US$| 500000}} in the [[2023 SA20|inaugural season]] of the [[SA20]] league. He is the highest-paid drafted player in the league along with [[Liam Livingstone]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jos Buttler drafted by Paarl Royals for SA20 league|url= https://www.crictracker.com/csa-t20-league-2022-jos-buttler-liam-livingstone-in-top-salary-bracket-as-30-overseas-players-signed/|access-date=10 August 2022|work=CricTracker|date= 10 August 2022|language=en}}</ref>

=== 2023 Indian Premier League ===
Buttler was again retained by the Rajasthan Royals for the 2023 season. Buttler had a bittersweet season. He scored 392 runs in 14 game with half centuries. He also scored five ducks in the season, making him the player to be dismissed with most ducks in an IPL season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=ANI |date=20 May 2023 |title=Jos Buttler registers most ducks in single IPL season |url=https://theprint.in/sport/jos-buttler-registers-most-ducks-in-single-ipl-season/1584848/ |access-date=24 January 2025 |website=ThePrint |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== 2024 Indian Premier League ===
In his 100th IPL Match, Buttler hit an unbeaten century in a man of the match performance against the Royal Challengers Bengaluru.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/indian-premier-league-2024-1410320/rajasthan-royals-vs-royal-challengers-bengaluru-19th-match-1422137/full-scorecard|title=RR vs RCB|website=Cricinfo|access-date=17 April 2024}}</ref> Then against the Kolkata Knight Riders he scored another unbeaten century guiding the joint biggest run chase in the history of the IPL.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1426269.html|title=RR vs KKR|website=Cricinfo|access-date=17 April 2024}}</ref>

=== 2025 Indian Premier League ===
Jos Buttler was released by Rajasthan Royals ahead of the IPL 2025 mega auction. On auction day, 24 November 2024, Rajasthan Royals tried to bid back on Jos but he was finally sold to [[Gujarat Titans]] for 15.75 Crore Indian Rupees.<ref>{{Cite news |date=24 November 2024 |title=IPL 2025 Auction: Jos Buttler to join Shubman Gill-led Gujarat Titans |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/sports/ipl-2025-auction-jos-buttler-sold-for-rs-15-75-crore-to-join-shubman-gill-led-gujarat-titans/articleshow/115626035.cms?from=mdr |access-date=24 January 2025 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Buttler is a fan of English team [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=6 November 2014 |title=England cricketer Jos Buttler meets Man City & England's Joe Hart |url=https://m.youtube.com/watch?v=MWIpkWPooUk |website=youtube.com |publisher=[[England and Wales Cricket Board]]}}</ref> On 21 October 2017, Buttler married Louise Webber. His English teammates [[Steven Finn]] and [[Alex Hales]] acted as ushers for the wedding.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/cricket/england-cricketer-jos-buttler-gets-11398671|title=England cricket star quietly gets married as club let news slip|last=Whaling|first=James|date=24 October 2017|website=mirror|access-date=29 May 2019|archive-date=29 May 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190529015136/https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/cricket/england-cricketer-jos-buttler-gets-11398671|url-status=live}}</ref> Their first daughter was born in April 2019, and their second daughter was born in September 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.crictracker.com/england-batsman-jos-buttler-becomes-father-of-a-baby-girl/|title=England batsman Jos Buttler becomes father of a baby girl|date=28 April 2019|website=CricTracker|language=en-US|access-date=29 May 2019|archive-date=29 May 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190529015125/https://www.crictracker.com/england-batsman-jos-buttler-becomes-father-of-a-baby-girl/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://cricketaddictor.com/cricket-news/jos-buttler-blessed-with-a-baby-girl/|title=Jos Buttler Blessed With A Baby Girl|date=5 September 2021|website=Cricket Addictor|language=en-US|access-date=27 June 2022}}</ref> Their third child, a son, was born in May 2024.

Buttler was appointed [[Order of the British Empire|Member of the Order of the British Empire]] (MBE) in the [[2020 New Year Honours]] for services to cricket.<ref>{{Cite web |date=26 February 2020 |title=Ben Stokes, Jos Buttler awarded royal honour at Buckingham Palace |url=https://www.deccanchronicle.com/sports/cricket/260220/ben-stokes-jos-buttler-awarded-royal-honour-at-buckingham-palace.html |access-date=3 April 2022 |website=Deccan Chronicle |language=en}}</ref>
