'''Kane Stuart Williamson''' (born 8 August 1990)<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.cricket.com.au/players/CA:160/kane-williamson | title=Kane Williamson – Biography | website=www.cricket.com.au | access-date=23 June 2024}}</ref> is a New Zealand former international cricketer who [[Captain (cricket)|captained]] the [[New Zealand national cricket team]] in all formats of the game. A right-handed batsman and an occasional [[off spin]] bowler, Williamson is the leading run-scorer for New Zealand in [[Test cricket]] and is widely regarded as one of the world's best contemporary batsmen and one of the greatest New Zealand captains and batsmen of all time. He captained [[New Zealand national cricket team|New Zealand]] to victory in the [[2021 World Test Championship final|2021 ICC World Test Championship final]] and to the finals of the [[2019 Cricket World Cup]] and [[2021 Men's T20 World Cup|2021 T20 World Cup]]. He was also a part of the New Zealand squad to finish as [[2015 Cricket World Cup final|runners-up]] at the [[2015 Cricket World Cup]] and the [[2025 Champions Trophy|2025 ICC Champions Trophy]]. Williamson retired from international cricket on 12 June 2026.

Williamson made his [[first-class cricket]] debut while still a schoolboy at [[Tauranga Boys' College]], in December 2007.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/159/159052/First-Class_Matches.html|title=List of First Class Matches Played by Kane Williamson|publisher=CricketArchive|access-date=7 November 2010}}</ref> He made his U-19 debut against the touring [[India Under-19 cricket team|Indian U-19 team]] the same year and was named captain of the [[New Zealand Under-19 cricket team|New Zealand U-19 team]] for the [[2008 U-19 Cricket World Cup]]. He made his international debut in 2010. Williamson has represented New Zealand at the [[2011 ICC Cricket World Cup|2011]], [[2015 ICC Cricket World Cup|2015]], [[2019 ICC Cricket World Cup|2019]] and [[2023 ICC Cricket World Cup|2023]] editions of the [[Cricket World Cup]] and [[2012 World Twenty20|2012]], [[2014 World Twenty20|2014]], [[2016 World Twenty20|2016]], [[2021 Men's T20 World Cup|2021]], [[2022 Men's T20 World Cup|2022]] and [[2024 Men's T20 World Cup|2024]] editions of the [[Men's T20 World Cup|ICC World Twenty20]]. He made his full-time captaincy debut for New Zealand in the 2016 [[Men's T20 World Cup|ICC World Twenty20]] in [[India]]. He captained New Zealand at the [[2019 Cricket World Cup]], leading the team to the [[2019 Cricket World Cup Final|final]] and winning the [[Cricket World Cup awards#Awards summary|Player of the Tournament award]] in the process. On 31 December 2020, he reached a Test batting rating of 890, surpassing [[Steve Smith (cricketer)|Steve Smith]] and [[Joe Root]] as the number one ranked Test batsmen in the world.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/sport/cricket-kane-williamson-rises-to-number-one-in-world-test-batting-rankings/EPPVZHDNGLJ2MCF6LBAZQU5MVA/|title=Cricket: Kane Williamson rises to number one in world test batting rankings|publisher=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |access-date=13 March 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/media-releases/1960320/|title=Williamson overtakes Smith and Kohli to top position |publisher=ICC|access-date=2 January 2021}}</ref> He was nominated for the Sir Garfield Sobers Award for ICC Male Cricketer of the Decade, and the award for Test cricketer of the decade. [[Ian Chappell]] and [[Martin Crowe]] have ranked Williamson among the top four Test cricket batsmen, along with [[Joe Root]], [[Steve Smith (cricketer)|Steve Smith]], [[Virat Kohli]] of the current era.<ref>{{cite web |title=Test cricket's young Fab Four |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/martin-crowe-test-cricket-s-young-fab-four-774705 |access-date=10 May 2018 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Virat Kohli, Joe Root, Steven Smith, Kane Williamson 'Fab Four' of Tests: Martin Crowe|date=29 August 2014|url=https://indianexpress.com/article/sports/cricket/virat-kohli-joe-root-steven-smith-kane-williamson-fab-four-of-tests-martin-crowe/|publisher=The Indian Express|access-date=13 March 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Big four? What about Warner? |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ian-chappell-big-four-ought-to-be-five-with-warner-in-there-1120679 |access-date=10 May 2018 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

Williamson was the only New Zealander to be named in the ICC Test Team of the Decade (2011–2020).<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/1956753/|title=Kohli named captain of ICC Test Team of the Decade|publisher=ICC|access-date=2 January 2021}}</ref> He won the ICC Spirit of Cricket award in 2018. The late former New Zealand cricketer [[Martin Crowe]] noted that "we're seeing the dawn of probably our greatest ever batsman" in Williamson.<ref>{{cite news|last=Alderson|first=Andrew|title=Crowe: Key to Cup win is fearlessness|url=http://m.nzherald.co.nz/sport/news/article.cfm?c_id=4&objectid=11383165|work=[[The New Zealand Herald]]|date=7 January 2015|access-date=23 April 2017}}</ref> In June 2021, he captained New Zealand to win the inaugural [[World Test Championship|ICC World Test Championship]], the first ICC trophy the team won since winning the [[2000 KnockOut Trophy|2000 ICC KnockOut Trophy]]. In November 2021, he led New Zealand to the [[2021 Men's T20 World Cup final|final]] of the [[2021 Men's T20 World Cup|ICC T20 World Cup]]. He is widely regarded as one of the greatest batsmen of his generation.<ref>{{Cite web |date=28 February 2023 |title=Kane Williamson: New Zealand's greatest ever batsman |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/sport/484966/kane-williamson-new-zealand-s-greatest-ever-batsman |access-date=3 February 2024 |website=[[RNZ]] |language=en-nz}}</ref> Williamson retired from all international cricket on June 12, 2026, with immediate effect, after making 0 and 18 against England at Lords. Speaking on the decision, Williamson said "I've thought about it for a while, but over the last few days it's become clear now is the right time," and "I've always felt a strong drive and hunger for international cricket, and I take pride in knowing I've given it my all in every match I've played for New Zealand. Continuing with anything less wouldn't be right and I feel fortunate to step away on my own terms.<ref name="espncricinfo.com">{{Cite web |date=12 June 2026 |title=Kane Williamson retires from international cricket |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/kane-williamson-retires-from-international-cricket-1540723 |access-date=12 June 2026 |website=[[Cricinfo]] |language=en-nz}}</ref>

==Early life==
Williamson was born on 8 August 1990 in [[Tauranga]], in the [[Bay of Plenty]] region on the [[North Island|North Island of New Zealand]].<ref name=bio>{{cite news|url=http://espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/277906.html|title=Kane Williamson|publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=7 March 2023|archive-date=28 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180828091447/http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/277906.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> His father Brett was a sales representative who had played under-17 and club cricket in New Zealand and his mother Sandra had been a representative [[basketball]] player. He has a twin brother Logan, who is one minute younger than him. The brothers have three older sisters, Anna, Kylie and Sophie. All three were accomplished [[volleyball]] players, and Anna and Sophie were in New Zealand age group teams. Williamson's grandmother [[Joan Williamson-Orr]] served as mayor of [[Taupō District Council|Taupō]]. His first cousin [[Dane Cleaver]] has also played international cricket for New Zealand.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/cricket/300824258/black-caps-vs-sri-lanka-kane-williamson-a-late-arrival-for-first-test-after-grandmothers-death|title=Black Caps vs Sri Lanka: Kane Williamson a late arrival for first test after grandmother's death|publisher=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |first=Richard|last=Knowler|date=7 March 2023|access-date=7 March 2023}}</ref>

Williamson played senior representative cricket at the age of 14 and first-class cricket at 16. He attended [[Tauranga Boys' College]] from 2004 to 2008, where he was head boy in his final year. He was coached by Pacey Depina who described Williamson as having "a thirst to be phenomenal – but not at anyone else's expense."<ref>{{cite news|last1=Cumming|first1=Geoff|title=More than able Kane|url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/sport/news/article.cfm?c_id=4&objectid=11413192|newspaper=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |date=6 March 2015|access-date=7 March 2015}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title = Kane Williamson: 19 facts about the Kiwi superstar|url = http://www.criclife.com/lists/chronicles/kane-williamson-19-facts-about-the-kiwi-superstar-43820|website = CricLife|date = 8 August 2015|access-date = 22 December 2015}}</ref> He reportedly scored 40 centuries before he left school.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.thecricketmonthly.com/story/879501/kane-is-able|title=Kane is able|work=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=29 March 2018|language=en}}</ref>

== Domestic career ==

Williamson made his debut for [[Northern Districts men's cricket team|Northern Districts]] in 2007 at the age of 17, who he has remained with for the duration of his New Zealand domestic career.<ref>{{cite web |title=Kane Williamson Profile – Kane Williamson Cricket Career |url=https://www.news18.com/cricketnext/profile/kane-williamson/4330.html |website=News18 |access-date=4 May 2020 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Kane Williamson Profile – Cricket Player, New Zealand |url=https://sports.ndtv.com/cricket/players/1058-kane-williamson-playerprofile |website=NDTVSports.com |access-date=4 May 2020 |language=en}}</ref>
He scored his first T20 hundred, on 19 September 2014, making 101[[not out|*]] in 49 balls to guide [[Northern Districts men's cricket team|Northern Districts]] to a comfortable win against [[Cape Cobras]] in [[Champions League Twenty20]] 2014.<ref>{{cite web |title=Kane Williamson ton crushes Cobras – Cricket – ESPNcricinfo |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/champions-league-twenty20-2014-15-763543/cape-cobras-vs-northern-districts-3rd-match-group-b-763593/match-report |access-date=28 February 2015 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

=== Indian Premier League ===
In February 2015, a Williamson signed for [[Indian Premier League]] team [[Sunrisers Hyderabad]] (SRH). He played for the team in the [[2016 Indian Premier League|2016 season]], winning the title, and was retained for the [[2017 Indian Premier League|2017]] and [[2018 Indian Premier League|2018 seasons]]. He captained the team in 2018, replacing [[David Warner (cricketer)|David Warner]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://twitter.com/SunRisers/status/979263226746753024|title=SunRisers Hyderabad on Twitter|work=Twitter|access-date=29 March 2018|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.cricbuzz.com/cricket-news/101315/kane-williamson-appointed-sunrisers-hyderabad-cricket-team-captain-for-ipl-2018|title=Kane Williamson appointed SRH captain for IPL 2018|work=Cricbuzz|access-date=29 March 2018|language=en}}</ref> Under Williamson's captaincy, [[Sunrisers Hyderabad]] finished runners-up and he was the season's leading scorer with 735 runs.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.news18.com/cricketnext/news/ipl-2018-kane-williamson-takes-orange-cap-becomes-third-highest-scorer-in-single-season-1761105.html|title=IPL 2018: Kane Williamson Takes Orange Cap, Becomes Third Highest-scorer in Single Season|date=28 May 2018|work=News18|access-date=28 May 2018}}</ref> In IPL 2021, Kane took over the captaincy from [[David Warner (cricketer)|David Warner]] in the middle of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Sportstar|first=Team|title=Williamson replaces Warner as Sunrisers Hyderabad captain in IPL 2021|url=https://sportstar.thehindu.com/cricket/ipl/ipl-news/kane-williamson-replaces-david-warner-as-sunrisers-captain-in-ipl-2021/article34457291.ece|access-date=23 October 2021|website=Sportstar|date=May 2021 |language=en}}</ref> He was retained by the franchise for the [[2022 IPL|2022 edition]] as the captain, but failed to perform, scoring one half-century.<ref>{{Cite web |title=IPLT20.com – Mens Team |url=https://www.iplt20.com/teams/sunrisers-hyderabad/squad-details/440 |access-date=2 June 2022 |website=www.iplt20.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=IPL 2022 retention: Sunrisers Hyderabad retain Kane Williamson; end 7-year association with David Warner |url=https://www.timesnownews.com/sports/cricket/article/ipl-2022-retention-sunrisers-hyderabad-retain-kane-williamson-end-7-year-association-with-david-warner/836445 |access-date=3 April 2022 |website=www.timesnownews.com |date=30 November 2021 |language=en}}</ref> Ahead of the [[IPL 2023|2023 season]], he was bought by the [[Gujarat Titans]], but was injured in the first match of the season.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.indiatvnews.com/sports/cricket/ipl-auction-2023-here-s-entire-list-of-sold-and-unsold-players-2022-12-23-833588 |last=Mehindru |first=Kartik |title=IPL Auction 2023 Full Results: Here's entire list of sold and unsold players |work=India TV News |date=23 December 2022}}</ref> He would go on to play for the Titans for the [[2024 Indian Premier League|2024 season]] before being released and would remain unsold for the [[2025 Indian Premier League|2025 season]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=IPL 2025 Auction {{!}} Players Bought, Top Bids & Team Spending {{!}} IPLT20 |url=https://www.iplt20.com/auction |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250625052309/https://www.iplt20.com/auction |archive-date=25 June 2025 |access-date=25 August 2025 |website=www.iplt20.com |language=en}}</ref>

===The Hundred===

==== Birmingham Phoenix ====
In the [[2021 The Hundred season]], Williamson was drafted for [[Birmingham Phoenix]] but withdrew because of an ongoing elbow injury.

==== London Spirit ====
In [[2025 The Hundred season|The Hundred 2025]], Williamson became the first male to become a direct signing for [[London Spirit]]. He becomes the captain of the Spirit as well as playing for the host county [[Middlesex County Cricket Club|Middlesex]]. He played all 8 games for Spirit, scoring 204 runs as the team won just 3 games, failing to qualify for the playoffs.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Kane Williamson Profile – Cricket Player New Zealand {{!}} Stats, Records, Video |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/cricketers/kane-williamson-277906 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250304030438/https://www.espncricinfo.com/cricketers/kane-williamson-277906 |archive-date=4 March 2025 |access-date=26 August 2025 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref>

=== Other Tournaments ===
Williamson has featured in several T20 franchise leagues around the world.

He played for [[Gloucestershire County Cricket Club|Gloucestershire]] in the [[Friends Life t20]] in 2011 and 2012, scoring 324 runs across 17 matches.

He later represented [[Yorkshire County Cricket Club|Yorkshire]] in the [[NatWest T20 Blast]] in [[2014 T20 Blast|2014]] and [[2016 T20 Blast|2016]], amassing 302 runs in 12 matches at a strike rate of 118.89. He returned to the [[Vitality Blast]] with Yorkshire in [[2018 T20 Blast|2018]] and joined [[Middlesex County Cricket Club|Middlesex]] for the [[2025 T20 Blast|2025]] season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=KANE WILLIAMSON JOINS MIDDLESEX FOR 2025 SEASON |url=https://www.middlesexccc.com/news/2025/02/kane-williamson-joins-middlesex-for-2025-season-2 |access-date=2026-01-24 |website=Middlesex County Cricket Club |language=en}}</ref> As of August 2025, he had made 24 appearances in the competition, scoring 676 runs.

In other T20 leagues, Williamson played for the [[Barbados Tridents]] in the [[2017 Caribbean Premier League]], scoring 172 runs without any half-centuries or centuries.

He featured in the [[2025 SA20|third season of the SA20]] for [[Durban's Super Giants]] in January and February 2025, scoring 233 runs in 8 matches at an average of 46.60 and a strike rate of 118.87.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kane Williamson |url=https://www.sa20.co.za/player/kane-williamson |website=Betway SA20 |access-date=2026-01-24}}</ref> Williamson returned to Durban's Super Giants in the 2026 SA20 season, replacing Taijul Islam.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2025-11-07 |title=Kane Williamson returns to Durban Super Giants for SA20 2026 after T20I retirement |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/news/kane-williamson-returns-to-durban-super-giants-for-sa20-2026-after-t20i-retirement/articleshow/125166097.cms |access-date=2026-02-12 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref> He went on to play 7 matches as the team finished 5th and he scored just 110 runs the whole season.<ref name=":2" />

Williamson has also won two major franchise T20 titles. He was part of the [[Sunrisers Hyderabad]] squad that won the [[2016 Indian Premier League]] title.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kane Williamson Profile |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/cricketers/kane-williamson-277906 |website=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=2026-01-24}}</ref> Most recently, in January 2026, he joined the [[Rajshahi Warriors]] in the [[2025–26 Bangladesh Premier League|12th edition of the Bangladesh Premier League]]. He contributed key performances—including an unbeaten 45* off 38 balls in Qualifier 2 and 24 off 15 balls in the final (adding a partnership with centurion Tanzid Hasan)—to help the team reach and win both playoff matches, defeating Sylhet Titans in Qualifier 2 and Chattogram Royals by 63 runs in the final to secure their maiden BPL title.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fernando, Williamson, Neesham power Rajshahi Warriors into BPL final |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/bangladesh-premier-league-2025-26-1516530/rajshahi-warriors-vs-sylhet-titans-qualifier-2-1516569/match-report |website=ESPNcricinfo |date=2026-01-21 |access-date=2026-01-24}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Tanzid ton, Fernando four-for power Rajshahi Warriors to BPL title |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/bangladesh-premier-league-2025-26-1516530/chattogram-royals-vs-rajshahi-warriors-final-1516570/match-report |website=ESPNcricinfo |date=2026-01-23 |access-date=2026-01-24}}</ref>

==International career==
Williamson was 17, when he led the New Zealand Under-19 team in the World Cup in [[Malaysia]] in 2008. New Zealand reached the semi-final, where they lost to the eventual champions India. On 24 March 2010, Williamson was named in the New Zealand Test squad for the second Test against Australia,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cricinfo.com/nzvaus2010/content/current/story/453236.html|title=Kane Williamson named in New Zealand Test squad|last=Coverdale|first=Brydon|date=24 March 2010|publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=24 March 2010}}</ref> but ultimately he did not play in the match.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cricinfo.com/nzvaus2010/engine/current/match/423790.html|title=Scorecard – 2nd Test: New Zealand v Australia at Hamilton, 27–31 March 2010|publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=6 November 2010}}</ref>

Williamson made his [[One-Day International]] debut against [[India national cricket team|India]] on 10 August 2010. He was dismissed for a 9th ball [[Duck (cricket)|duck]]. In his second match, he was bowled by [[Angelo Mathews]] for a second ball duck. He scored his maiden ODI [[Century (cricket)|century]] against [[Bangladesh national cricket team|Bangladesh]] on 14 October 2010 in [[Dhaka]] and hence became the youngest centurion in New Zealand's cricket history. Due to his performance on the [[New Zealand cricket team in Bangladesh in 2010–11|Bangladesh tour]] where New Zealand suffered a 4–0 whitewash, Williamson was selected in the New Zealand Test squad for the [[New Zealand cricket team in India in 2010–11|tour of India]] that followed.<ref>{{cite web |title=Williamson, Bennett in Test squad |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/new-zealand-in-india-2010-11-kane-williamson-hamish-bennett-in-test-squad-483282 |access-date=7 November 2010 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

Williamson made his [[Test cricket]] debut against [[India national cricket team|India]] at [[Ahmedabad]] on 4 November 2010. In his first innings he scored 131 runs off 299 balls and became the eighth [[List of Test cricket records for New Zealand#Centuries|New Zealand player to score a century on Test debut]].<ref name="TestDebut">{{cite web|title=ESPNcricinfo : New Zealand tour of India (Nov 2010), 1st Test: India v New Zealand at Ahmedabad, Nov 4–8, 2010|url=http://www.cricinfo.com/india-v-new-zealand-2010/engine/current/match/464531.html|publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=6 November 2010}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author=Ravindran, Siddarth |date=7 November 2010 |title=Martin five sparks stunning turnaround |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/new-zealand-tour-of-india-nov-2010-2010-11-464517/india-vs-new-zealand-1st-test-464531/match-report-4 |access-date=7 November 2010 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

=== Rising through the ranks ===
Williamson scored 161* against West Indies in June 2014, his second century of the series and helped secure a rare away Test series victory for his team.  He finished as the leading overall run scorer in the series with 413 runs, and was denied a double century only by rain,<ref name=":1" /> which encouraged skipper [[Brendon McCullum]] to declare in the interest of obtaining a result in the match. He was also reported for a suspect bowling action in April 2014, but was cleared in December 2014.<ref>{{cite news |title=Sachithra Senanayake & Kane Williamson cleared to bowl again |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/30394969 |work=BBC Sport |publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation |date=9 December 2014 |access-date=16 December 2014 }}</ref> He was also named as captain ahead of the ODI and Twenty20 series against [[Pakistan national cricket team|Pakistan]] in December 2014 as McCullum was rested.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cricbuzz.com/cricket-news/67160/kane-williamson-named-as-captain-for-pakistan-series-brendon-mccullum-rested|title=Kane Williamson named as captain for Pakistan series; Brendon McCullum rested|work=Cricbuzz|date=30 November 2014 |access-date=28 February 2015}}</ref>

[[File:Kane Williamson (9773667991).jpg|thumb|234x234px|Williamson batting against [[Sussex County Cricket Club|Sussex]] in 2013]]
Williamson scored 100[[not out|*]] off 69 balls [[New Zealand cricket team in Zimbabwe in 2011–12#3rd ODI|against Zimbabwe]] at [[Bulawayo]], which at the time was the second fastest century by a New Zealander in a [[One-Day International]].<ref>[http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/stats/index.htmlclass=2;filter=advanced;orderby=batting_strike_rate;runsmin1=100;runsval1=runs;team=5;template=results;type=batting;view=innings Statistics / One-Day Internationals / Batting records] ESPNcricinfo Statsguru. Retrieved 29 December 2011</ref> He also established one of the most potent [[Batting order (cricket)#Top order|top-order]] partnership with [[Ross Taylor]], with Williamson himself being the most prolific number-three batsman for the national team since former captain [[Stephen Fleming]]. As a fielder, his position is predominantly at gully.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Mangukiya |first=Manish |date=21 February 2025 |title=Kane Williamson: New Zealand's Cricketing Maestro & Legendary Leader |url=https://www.scoreflood.com/news/kane-williamson-new-zealand-cricketing-maestro-and-legendary-leader/93 |access-date=22 February 2025 |website=ScoreFlood.com}}</ref>

In 2015, he started with 69 and 242[[not out|*]] against [[Sri Lanka national cricket team|Sri Lanka]], with two catches in the field in a man-of-the-match performance.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/new-zealand-v-sri-lanka-2014-15/content/story/817747.html|title=Williamson could be our greatest ever batter – McCullum|work=ESPNcricinfo|date=7 January 2015 |access-date=28 February 2015}}</ref>  On 3 February 2015, he scored the 99th ODI century in the New Zealand's history, against [[Pakistan]]; [[Ross Taylor]] scored the 100th in the same match. He also scored over 700 runs before the [[2015 Cricket World Cup]] in the first two months of the calendar year. On 17 June 2015 he became the fifth-fastest batsmen and fastest New Zealander to score 3,000 runs, getting them in just 78 innings. On 15 November 2015 Williamson and Taylor became the first pair of away batsmen to each score 2nd innings centuries at WACA Ground in [[Perth]].{{citation needed|date=September 2020}}

In December 2015, during the [[Sri Lankan cricket team in New Zealand in 2015–16|second Test against Sri Lanka]], Williamson broke the record for the most Test runs scored in a calendar year by a New Zealander, with 1172 runs.<ref name="2ndTest">{{cite web |date=21 December 2015 |title=Williamson's record ton and NZ's longest unbeaten streak at home |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/williamson-s-record-ton-and-nz-s-longest-unbeaten-streak-at-home-953745 |access-date=21 December 2015 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He also ended 2015 with 2692 runs, the highest total across all forms of international cricket for the year, and third highest total in a single year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/photo.php?fbid=555268464622721&set=o.203262656377121&type=3&theater|title=William Qüensell|website=Facebook.com|access-date=22 August 2018}}</ref>

He was awarded the T20 Player of the Year by NZC for the 2014–15 season.<ref>{{Cite web|url = http://nzcricketmuseum.co.nz/new-zealand-cricket-awards/|title = New Zealand Cricket Awards|date = 4 April 2018|access-date = 21 July 2019|archive-date = 22 July 2019|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20190722000748/http://nzcricketmuseum.co.nz/new-zealand-cricket-awards/|url-status = dead}}</ref>

=== Captaincy ===
In March 2016, Williamson assumed the position of captain of New Zealand across all forms of cricket after the retirement of [[Brendon McCullum]], beginning with the World T20I cup in India. He was named as captain of the 'Team of the Tournament' by ESPNcricinfo and Cricbuzz.<ref>{{Cite web |date=4 April 2016 |title=ESPNcricinfo's team of the 2016 World T20 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/icc-world-twenty20-2016/content/story/995203.html |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cricbuzz.com/cricket-news/79133/cricbuzz-team-of-the-icc-world-t20-2016|title=Cricbuzz Team of the ICC World T20, 2016|website=Cricbuzz|date=5 April 2016 }}</ref> He also picked up NZ player of the year, Test player of the year and the Redpath Cup for top batsman in first class cricket for the second year in a row.<ref>{{Cite web

'''Balapuwaduge Kusal Gimhan Mendis''' (born 2 February 1995) is a professional Sri Lankan [[cricket]]er who plays in all forms of the game and a current captain of the national team.<ref name="Bio">{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/player/kusal-mendis-629074|title=Kusal Mendis|website=[[Cricinfo]]|publisher=[[ESPN Inc.]]|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref> He only played sixteen [[first-class cricket|first-class]] matches before playing for the national team. In November 2017, he was named the [[One Day International]] (ODI) batsman of the year for the 2016–17 season at [[Sri Lanka Cricket]]'s annual awards.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/asela-gunaratne-wins-big-at-slc-s-annual-awards-1125203|last=Balasuriya|first=Madushka|title=Gunaratne wins big at SLC's annual awards|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=1 November 2017|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref>

==Early and domestic career==
In 2013, Mendis was adjudged as the [[Sri Lankan Schoolboy Cricketer of the Year|schoolboy cricketer of the year]] and had captained the national youth and the [[Prince of Wales College, Moratuwa]] teams in his formative years.<ref name="Bio"/><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.smh.com.au/sport/cricket/australia-v-sri-lanka-kusal-mendis-ton-leads-fightback-puts-heat-on-australia-20160728-gqfhyh.html|last=Pierik|first=Jon|title=Australia v Sri Lanka: Kusal Mendis ton leads fightback, puts heat on Australia|access-date=26 November 2022|work=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://archives1.sundayobserver.lk/2018/02/18/sports/observer-mobitel-schoolboy-cricketer-year-2013-kusal-mendis-another-match-winning|title=Cambrian Kusal Mendis Observer-Mobitel Schoolboy Cricketer of the Year|last=Weerawansa|first=Dinesh|work=[[Sunday Observer (Sri Lanka)|Sunday Observer]]|date=18 February 2018|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref>

In March 2018, Mendis was named in Dambulla's squad for the [[2017–18 Super Four Provincial Tournament]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.timesonline.lk/news/cricket-mixed-opinions-on-provincial-tournament/18-1041112|title=Cricket: Mixed opinions on Provincial tournament|work=[[The Sunday Times (Sri Lanka)|Sunday Times]]|date=26 March 2018|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://dailysports.lk/all-you-need-to-know-about-the-sl-super-provincial-tournament/|title=All you need to know about the SL Super Provincial Tournament|publisher=Daily Sports|date=26 March 2018|access-date=27 March 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180327213128/https://dailysports.lk/all-you-need-to-know-about-the-sl-super-provincial-tournament/|archive-date=27 March 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> In the following month, he was also named in Dambulla's squad for the [[2018 Super Provincial One Day Tournament]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.thepapare.com/slc-super-provincial-50-tournament-squads-fixtures/|title=SLC Super Provincial 50 over tournament squads and fixtures|last=Weerasinghe|first=Damith|work=The Papare|date=27 April 2018|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref> In August 2018, Mendis was named to Galle's squad for the 2018 SLC T20 League.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.thepapare.com/slc-t20-league-2018-squads-finalized/|title=SLC T20 League 2018 squads finalized|work=The Papare|date=16 August 2018|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref> He was the leading run-scorer for Galle in the tournament, where he scored 182 runs in six matches.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/averages/batting_bowling_by_team.html?id=12567;team=6179;type=tournament|title=SLC T20 League, 2018 - Galle, Batting and bowling averages|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=30 August 2018|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref> In March 2019, he was named in Galle's squad for the [[2019 Super Provincial One Day Tournament]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thepapare.com/squads-fixtures-announced-for-slc-provincial-50-overs-tournament-2019/|title=Squads, Fixtures announced for SLC Provincial 50 Overs Tournament|work=The Papare|date=19 March 2019|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref>

During the [[2019–20 Premier League Tournament]], Mendis scored 139 against [[Ragama Cricket Club]], where Colombo Cricket Club won the match by an innings and 125 runs.<ref>{{cite web|title=Full Scorecard of Colombo Cricket Club vs Ragama Cricket Club Super Eight 2020 - Score Report|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/plt-tier-a-2019-20-2020-1214518/colombo-cricket-club-vs-ragama-cricket-club-super-eight-1214562/full-scorecard|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref> In 2020, Mendis scored his maiden first-class double-century against [[Nondescripts Cricket Club]] and helped to draw the match.<ref>{{cite web|title=Kusal Mendis hammers 200|url=http://archives1.sundayobserver.lk/2020/08/23/kusal-mendis-hammers-200|date=23 August 2020|access-date=26 November 2022|website=Sunday Observer|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Match drawn - Nondescripts Cricket Club vs Colombo Cricket Club, Premier League Tournament Tier A 2020, Super Eight Match Summary, Report|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/plt-tier-a-2019-20-2020-1214518/colombo-cricket-club-vs-nondescripts-cricket-club-super-eight-1214576/live-cricket-score|access-date=26 November 2022|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.}}</ref> In the final match against [[Chilaw Marians Cricket Club]], Mendis scored another century, with 157 runs, where the match ended in a draw.<ref>{{cite web|title=Match drawn - Chilaw Marians Cricket Club vs Colombo Cricket Club, Premier League Tournament Tier A 2020, Super Eight Match Summary, Report|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/plt-tier-a-2019-20-2020-1214518/chilaw-marians-cricket-club-vs-colombo-cricket-club-super-eight-1214583/live-cricket-score|website=ESPNcricinfo|date=25 August 2020 |publisher=ESPN Inc.|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref>

==Franchise cricket==
In October 2020, Mendis was drafted by the [[Kandy Tuskers]] for the [[2020 Lanka Premier League|inaugural edition]] of the [[Lanka Premier League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/30148161/lanka-premier-league-2020-chris-gayle-andre-russell-shahid-afridi-big-names-taken-lpl-draft|last=Fernando|first=Andrew Fidel|title=Chris Gayle, Andre Russell and Shahid Afridi among big names taken at LPL draft|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=19 October 2020|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref> In November 2021, he was selected to play for the [[Galle Gladiators]] following the players' draft for the [[2021 Lanka Premier League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/kusal-perera-angelo-mathews-miss-out-on-lpl-drafts-1288554|last=Fernando|first=Andrew Fidel|title=Kusal Perera, Angelo Mathews miss out on LPL drafts|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=10 November 2021|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref> In July 2022, he was signed by the [[Galle Gladiators]] for the [[2022 Lanka Premier League|third edition]] of the [[Lanka Premier League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/lpl-2022-draft-kandy-falcons-sign-wanindu-hasaranga-bhanuka-rajapaksa-to-turn-out-for-dambulla-giants-1323338|title=LPL 2022 draft: Kandy Falcons sign Hasaranga; Rajapaksa to turn out for Dambulla Giants|last=Balasuriya|first=Madushka|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=6 July 2022|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref>

On 7 February 2023, Mendis was signed to [[Pretoria Capitals]] in the [[SA20 (cricket)|SA20]] cricket tournament in South Africa. Against [[Paarl Royals]], he scored 80 runs from 41 deliveries hitting 8 boundaries and four sixes, where Capitals won the match by 59 runs and Mendis won the player of the match award.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Full Scorecard of Capitals vs Royals 30th Match 2022/23 - Score Report {{!}} ESPNcricinfo.com |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/sa20-2022-23-1335268/pretoria-capitals-vs-paarl-royals-30th-match-1343970/full-scorecard |access-date=2023-02-08 |website=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

In May 2026, he was signed by [[Colombo Kaps]] as the "Local Icon Player" for the [[2026 Lanka Premier League]].

==International career==
===Debut years (2014–2015)===
In 2014, Mendis was named as the captain for the [[2014 ICC Under-19 Cricket World Cup]]. After strong performances in U-19 career, Mendis became the 132nd Test player for Sri Lanka, after gaining his cap during the second Test of [[Sobers-Tissera Trophy]] [[West Indian cricket team in Sri Lanka in 2015–16|against West Indies]]. He scored 13 runs in the first innings and 39 runs in the second innings.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/west-indies-tour-of-sri-lanka-2015-16-915221/sri-lanka-vs-west-indies-2nd-test-915775/full-scorecard|title=2nd Test Sri Lanka v West Indies|website=[[Cricinfo]]|publisher=[[ESPN Inc.]]|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref> Then in 2016, Mendis was named in the Sri Lanka squad for the [[Sri Lankan cricket team in England and Ireland in 2016|tour of England]]. In the first Test, he got a duck in the first innings, but scored his maiden test half-century with 53 runs in the second innings.

Mendis made his [[One Day International]] (ODI) debut [[Sri Lankan cricket team in England and Ireland in 2016#Ireland|against Ireland]] on 16 June 2016, and scored his maiden ODI fifty.<ref>{{cite web|title=Sri Lanka tour of England and Ireland, 1st ODI: Ireland v Sri Lanka at Dublin (Malahide), Jun 16, 2016|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/sri-lanka-tour-of-england-and-ireland-2016-913581/ireland-vs-sri-lanka-1st-odi-913619/full-scorecard|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=16 June 2015|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref> In the same tour, Mendis made his [[Twenty20 International]] (T20I) debut for Sri Lanka [[Sri Lankan cricket team in England and Ireland in 2016|against England]] on 5 July 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/sri-lanka-tour-of-england-and-ireland-2016-913581/england-vs-sri-lanka-only-t20i-913633/full-scorecard|title=Sri Lanka tour of England and Ireland, Only T20I: England v Sri Lanka at Southampton, Jul 5, 2016|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref>

===Making a mark in the international arena (2016–2018)===
On 28 July 2016, Mendis scored his maiden Test century during the first Test [[Australian cricket team in Sri Lanka in 2016|against Australia]] at the [[Pallekele Cricket Stadium]]. He became the youngest Sri Lankan to score a century against Australia and also the highest score against Australia on home soil.{{Clarify|reason=Was it on Australia's home soil?|date=February 2023}}<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/kusal-mendis-second-youngest-to-score-150-plus-against-australia-1040085|title=Second-youngest to score 150-plus against Australia|last=Seervi|first=Bharath|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=28 July 2016|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref> Sri Lanka won the match by 106 runs, which was only their second Test win against Australia. Mendis won the Man of the Match award for his performance.

In the fifth match of the [[2016–17 Zimbabwe Tri-Series|Tri-series in Zimbabwe]] against the West Indies, Mendis scored match-winning 94 runs and made 94-run partnership with [[Niroshan Dickwella]]. Sri Lanka later posted 330 runs off 50 overs, which was recorded as the highest total by Sri Lanka against the West Indies. Sri Lanka won the match by one run and reached the final, where Mendis won the man of the match award.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/zimbabwe-tri-nation-series-2016-17-1059705/sri-lanka-vs-west-indies-5th-match-1059714/match-report|last=Kishore|first=Shashank|title=Sri Lanka survive Lewis' 148 for thrilling win|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=23 November 2016|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref> In the final against Zimbabwe, Mendis scored another fifty, guiding the team to win the series by 6 wickets. His all-round performances in the series gave him his first Player of the series award.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/tri-nation-zimbabwe-2016-17/content/story/1069191.html|title=Mendis, Tharanga steer Sri Lanka to title|last=Raghavan|first=Sirish|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=27 November 2016|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref>

On the first Test [[Bangladeshi cricket team in Sri Lanka in 2016-17#Tests|against Bangladesh]] at Galle in 2017, Mendis scored his second Test century, just falling short 6 runs for his double hundred.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/sl-v-bdesh-2016-17-1083436/sri-lanka-vs-bangladesh-1st-test-1083444/match-report-1|last=Fernando|first=Andrew Fidel|title=Mendis 166* headlines Sri Lanka dominance|access-date=26 November 2022|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=7 March 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/sl-v-bdesh-2016-17-1083436/sri-lanka-vs-bangladesh-1st-test-1083444/match-report-2|title=Bangladesh begin well in reply to Sri Lanka's 494|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=8 March 2017|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref> On 28 March 2017, in the second ODI [[Bangladeshi cricket team in Sri Lanka in 2017|against Bangladesh]], Mendis scored his maiden ODI century, with 102 runs. However, the match ended with a no result, due to heavy rain.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/sl-v-bdesh-2016-17-1083436/sri-lanka-vs-bangladesh-2nd-odi-1083447/match-report|last=Isam|first=Mohammad|title=Rain thwarts SL's chances after Mendis ton|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=28 March 2017|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref>

On 8 June 2017, against India in [[2017 ICC Champions Trophy|the 2017 ICC Champions Trophy]], Mendis scored a match-winning 89 runs and made a 159-run stand for the second wicket with [[Danushka Gunathilaka]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/alan-gardner-india-s-winning-rhythm-disrupted-by-young-i-papare-i-batting-beat-1102212|last=Gardner|first=Alan|title=India's winning rhythm disrupted by young papare batting beat|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=5 February 2018|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref> In the match, Sri Lanka chased 321 runs scored by India, by recording the highest successful run chase in Champion's Trophy history.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/danushka-gunathilaka-and-kusal-mendis-power-sri-lanka-in-record-chase-1102226|title=Gunathilaka, Mendis power Sri Lanka in record chase|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=9 June 2017|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref> This was Sri Lanka's joint-highest chase, and their first successful 300-plus chase since the 2015 World Cup as well.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/danushka-gunathilaka-announces-his-arrival-1102181|last=Krishnaswamy|first=Karthik|title=Gunathilaka announces his arrival|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=8 June 2017|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref> On 30 June 2017, [[Zimbabwean cricket team in Sri Lanka in 2017|against Zimbabwe]], Mendis passed 1,000 ODI runs, becoming the joint second-fastest with [[Upul Tharanga]] for Sri Lanka to achieve this.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/sl-v-zim-2017-1104471/sri-lanka-vs-zimbabwe-1st-odi-1104478/match-report|last=Fernando|first=Andrew Fidel|title=Mendis, Tharanga fifties propel SL to 316|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=30 June 2017|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref>

During the first Test [[Sri Lankan cricket team in Bangladesh in 2017–18|against Bangladesh in 2018]], Mendis scored his fourth Test hundred on his 23rd birthday. Mendis along with [[Dhananjaya de Silva]] scored a 308-run partnership to the second wicket until De Silva was dismissed for 173 runs. However, Mendis was dismissed for 196 runs, four runs short of his maiden double century.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/sl-in-bdesh-2017-18-1130733/bangladesh-vs-sri-lanka-1st-test-1130744/match-report-2|last=Fernando|first=Andrew Fidel|title=Dhananjaya, Mendis lead strong Sri Lanka reply|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=1 February 2018|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/mendis-and-dhananjaya-battle-adversity-to-keep-sri-lanka-afloat-1135121|last=Isam|first=Mohammad|title=Mendis and Dhananjaya battle adversity to keep Sri Lanka afloat|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=1 February 2018|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/18527/report/1130744/day/3/|last=Fernando|first=Andrew Fidel|title=Sri Lanka pile on the runs and eye big lead|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=2 February 2018|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref> His score of 196, however, made him the second Sri Lankan after [[Kumar Sangakkara]] to get out in the 190s at least twice.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/want-to-give-kusal-mendis-every-opportunity-thilan-samaraweera-1135272|last=Isam|first=Mohammad|title=Want to give Kusal Mendis every opportunity - Samaraweera|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=2 February 2018|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref>

After good performances in Tests against Bangladesh, Mendis was named to the T20I squad for Sri Lanka by replacing injured [[Kusal Perera]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/kusal-mendis-to-replace-injured-kusal-perera-in-t20s-1136417|last=Fernando|first=Andrew Fidel|title=Kusal Mendis to replace injured Kusal Perera in T20s|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=13 February 2018|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref> In the first match, he scored a match-winning knock of 53 from 27 balls. Bangladesh scored 193 in their 20 overs, which was then their highest T20I total. Mendis opened the innings with [[Danushka Gunathilaka]] and they added 53 for the first wicket in just 4.5 overs. Then Mendis scored his first T20I fifty and Sri Lanka won the match by 6 wickets. The chase of 193 is recorded as the highest T20I chase by Sri Lanka as well and Mendis was adjudged man of the match.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/sl-in-bdesh-2017-18-1130733/bangladesh-vs-sri-lanka-1st-t20i-1130746/match-report|last=Isam|first=Mohammad|title=Kusal Mendis, Thisara Perera overpower Bangladesh|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=15 February 2018|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref> In the second T20I, Mendis scored another match-winning half-century and Sri Lanka posted 210 in their 20 overs. This is Sri Lanka's highest T20I score against Bangladesh. Finally, Sri Lanka won the match and series 2-0 and Mendis was awarded with both man of the match and player of the series.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/sl-in-bdesh-2017-18-1130733/bangladesh-vs-sri-lanka-2nd-t20i-1130747/match-report|last=Isam|first=Mohammad|title=Mendis stars in thumping win as SL sweep tour|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=18 February 2018|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/kusal-mendis-has-grabbed-all-opportunities-as-opener-dinesh-chandimal-1137157|last=Fernando|first=Andrew Fidel|title=Mendis has grabbed all opportunities as opener - Chandimal|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=18 February 2018|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref>

In May 2018, he was one of 33 cricketers to be awarded a national contract by [[Sri Lanka Cricket]] ahead of the 2018–19 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/692671|title=Sri Lanka assign 33 national contracts with pay hike|publisher=International Cricket Council|date=22 May 2018|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/sri-lankan-players-to-receive-pay-hike-1147340|last=Fernando|first=Andrew Fidel|title=Sri Lankan players to receive pay hike|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=22 May 2018|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref>

===Ups and downs (2018-2020)===
Mendis was totally out of form during the [[2018 Asia Cup]], where he was dismissed for naught in both games against Bangladesh and Afghanistan. His place in the team was in doubt with poor performances, and he was omitted from the [[English cricket team in Sri Lanka in 2018-19|England tour in Sri Lanka]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/sri-lanka-confirm-angelo-mathews-axe-for-england-odis-1160824|title=Sri Lanka confirm Angelo Mathews axe for England ODIs|website=[[Cricinfo]]|publisher=[[ESPN Inc.]]|date=26 September 2018|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref> But during the ODI series, Mendis was called into the squad for the remainder of the series against England, as a replacement for [[Kusal Perera]], who suffered a quad strain in the second ODI.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/kusal-mendis-called-up-as-replacement-for-kusal-perera-1162497|title=Kusal Mendis called up as replacement for Kusal Perera|last=Fernando|first=Andrew Fidel|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=17 October 2018|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref> In his comeback match, he was again dismissed for naught. In the fourth ODI, he batted in the middle order and scored only 5 runs and England won the series 3–0. In the last match, Mendis batted in the number-4 position. After 24 innings without a fifty, he scored a 30-ball half-century in the match with 6 huge sixes. Sri Lanka won the match by 219 runs in the DLS method.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/kusal-mendis-intensity-the-key-as-sri-lanka-s-hitman-turns-the-corner-1163020|title=Kusal Mendis' intensity the key as Sri Lanka's hitman turns the corner|last=Fernando|first=Andrew Fidel|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=23 October 2018|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref>

During the first Test [[Sri Lankan cricket team in New Zealand in 2018–19|against New Zealand]] in late 2018, Mendis scored his sixth Test century. Mendis along with [[Angelo Mathews]] batted all over the fourth day, which was the fifth time that the Sri Lankan pair had done that in Test history. On the fifth day, they put on an unbeaten double-century partnership which overall lasted for 115 wicketless overs for New Zealanders. With rain interruption, the match ended in a draw.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/sri-lanka-in-nz-2018-19-1153832/new-zealand-vs-sri-lanka-1st-test-1153838/match-report-5|title=Rain completes Mathews and Mendis' epic rescue|last=Fernando|first=Andrew Fidel|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=19 December 2018|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref> The partnership of 246, was also Sri Lanka's highest for any wicket against New Zealand and also Sri Lanka's highest in the second innings of a Test.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/when-i-saw-angie-get-hit-i-thought-there-s-no-way-i-m-getting-out-mendis-1169232|last=Fernando|first=Andrew Fidel|title=When I saw Angie get hit, I thought there's no way I'm getting out - Mendis|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=18 December 2018|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref> It was the first time a Sri Lankan pair had added 200-plus runs in the second innings of a Test outside Asia.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/stats-records-galore-for-mathews-and-mendis-1169218|title=Records galore for Mathews and Mendis|last=Rajesh|first=S.|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=18 December 2018|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref>

In the second Test, Mendis reached 1,000 Test runs in the calendar year 2018. He became only the second player after [[Virat Kohli]] to achieve the feat.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://scroll.in/field/907480/sri-lankas-kusal-mendis-becomes-second-batsman-after-virat-kohli-to-cross-1000-test-runs-in-2018|title=Sri Lanka's Kusal Mendis becomes second batsman after Virat Kohli to cross 1,000 Test runs in 2018|website=[[Scroll.in]]|date=29 December 2018|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref> He finished 2018 as the second-highest run-scorer in Test cricket, with 1,023 runs at an average of 46.50, including three centuries and four fifties.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/batting/most_runs_career.html?class=1;id=2018;type=year|title=Records / 2018 / Test Matches / Most Runs|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref> During the two-match Test series [[Sri Lankan cricket team in South Africa in 2018–19|against South Africa]], Mendis continued his poor form with the bat with scores 0, 12 and 16. However, his fielding efforts at slip improved in each innings. In the second innings of the second test at Port Elizabeth, Mendis scored his 9th test fifty and put on an unbeaten partnership of 163 runs off 213 balls with newcomer [[Oshada Fernando]] to win the match by 8 wickets.<ref name=":0">{{cite news|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/sl-in-sa-2018-19-1144142/south-africa-vs-sri-lanka-2nd-test-1144165/match-report-3|last=Muthu|first=Deivarayan|title=Kusal Mendis, Oshada Fernando lead Sri Lanka to historic series win|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=23 February 2019|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref> Eventually, Sri Lanka won the series 2-0 and Mendis was adjudged man of the match.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/sl-in-sa-2018-19-1144142/south-africa-vs-sri-lanka-2nd-test-1144165/full-scorecard|title=2nd Test, Sri Lanka tour of South Africa at Port Elizabeth, Feb 21-23 2019|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref> It was the first Test series won by Sri Lanka in South Africa and Sri Lanka became the first Asian team to win a test series in South Africa.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/rude-end-to-south-africa-s-seven-series-home-streak-1175844|last=Seervi|first=Bharath|title=Rude end to South Africa's seven series home streak|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=23 February 2019|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref>

In April 2019, he was named in [[2019 Cricket World Cup squads#Sri Lanka|Sri Lanka's squad]] for the [[2019 Cricket World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/lahiru-thirimanne-milinda-siriwardana-jeffrey-vandersay-picked-in-sri-lanka-s-world-cup-squad-1181293|last=Fernando|first=Andrew Fidel|title=Thirimanne, Siriwardana, Vandersay picked in World Cup squad|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=18 April 2019|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/1187360|title=Jeevan Mendis, Siriwardana, Vandersay make comebacks in Sri Lanka World Cup squad|publisher=International Cricket Council|date=18 April 2019|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref> On 1 September 2019, during the first T20I [[New Zealand cricket team in Sri Lanka in 2019|against New Zealand]], he scored a quick 79 runs off 53 balls to set a target of 174.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/new-zealand-in-sri-lanka-2019-1192868/sri-lanka-vs-new-zealand-1st-t20i-1192875/match-report|last=Fernando|first=Andrew Fidel|title=Taylor, de Grandhomme fireworks trump vintage Malinga|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=1 September 2019|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref> However, Sri Lanka lost the match. In the last over of the second T20I, he had a collision with [[Shehan Jayasuriya]] at the boundary line. Jayasuriya was running from long-on, and Mendis from midwicket, in order to intercept an aerial [[Mitchell Santner]], he tripped up by the onrushing Mendis, and was sent crashing into the boundary. Both players picked up knee injuries and rested from the third T20I.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/kusal-mendis-shehan-jayasuriya-uncertain-for-third-t20i-after-on-field-collision-1199616|last=Fernando|first=Andrew Fidel|title=Kusal Mendis, Shehan Jayasuriya uncertain for third T20I after on-field collision|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=4 September 2019|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref>

During the first Test [[Sri Lankan cricket team in Zimbabwe in 2019–20|against Zimbabwe]] on 19 January 2020, Mendis scored his eleventh fifty. He made 80 runs off 163 deliveries in the match and had a strong partnership with eventual double-centurion [[Angelo Mathews]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/sri-lanka-in-zimbabwe-2019-20-1212539/zimbabwe-vs-sri-lanka-1st-test-1212541/match-report-3|last=Fernando|first=Andrew Fidel|title=Angelo Mathews, Kusal Mendis lead Sri Lanka's strong reply|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=21 January 2020|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref> Sri Lanka went on to win the match by 10 wickets.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/sri-lanka-in-zimbabwe-2019-20-1212539/zimbabwe-vs-sri-lanka-1st-test-1212541/match-report|last=Fernando|first=Andrew Fidel|title=Lahiru Kumara breaks through Zimbabwe's resistance to seal victory|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=23 January 2020|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref> In the second Test, Mendis scored his seventh century with an unbeaten 116 in the second innings, with Sri Lanka winning the series 1–0.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/sri-lanka-in-zimbabwe-2019-20-1212539/zimbabwe-vs-sri-lanka-2nd-test-1212542/match-report-5|last=Balasuriya|first=Madushka|title=Kusal Mendis ton helps Sri Lanka secure draw and seal series 1-0|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=31 January 2020|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref>

On 25 February 2020, [[West Indian cricket team in Sri Lanka in 2019–20|against the West Indies]], Mendis scored his second ODI century. Along with [[Avishka Fernando]], they made a 239-run partnership for the third wicket, with Sri Lanka eventually making 345/8. West Indies collapsed in the chase and Sri Lanka won the match by 161 runs.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thepapare.com/west-indies-tour-of-sri-lanka-2020-2nd-odi-match-report-scorecard/|last=Vasudevan|first=Estelle|title=Mendis, Fernando and bowlers give Sri Lanka series win|work=The Papare|date=26 February 2020|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref> This was the biggest win in terms of runs against the West Indies by Sri Lanka in ODIs, with Sri Lanka taking an unassailable lead in the series.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/west-indies-in-sri-lanka-2019-20-1213866/sri-lanka-vs-west-indies-2nd-odi-1213872/match-report|last=Fernando|first=Andrew Fidel|title=Avishka Fernando and Kusal Mendis hit tons as Sri Lanka dominate West Indies|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=26 February 2020|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref>

===International ban (2021)===
On 28 June 2021, [[Sri Lanka Cricket]] (SLC) suspended Mendis, [[Danushka Gunathilaka]] and [[Niroshan Dickwella]] after they breached the team's [[bio-secure bubble]] during Sri Lanka's [[Sri Lankan cricket team in England in 2021|tour of England]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/sri-lanka-s-kusal-mendis-and-niroshan-dickwella-to-be-investigated-after-alleged-bio-bubble-breach-in-england-1268125|last=Fernando|first=Andrew Fidel|title=Bio-bubble breach: Kusal Mendis, Danushka Gunathilaka and Niroshan Dickwella suspended|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=28 June 2021|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref> All ===After the ban (2022–2023)===
On 20 February 2022, Mendis scored a match-winning sixth T20I half-century [[Sri Lankan cricket team in Australia in 2021–22|against Australia]]. His unbeaten 69 runs helped Sri Lanka to win the match by five wickets, with him being named the player of the match.<ref>{{cite web|title=Full Scorecard of Australia vs Sri Lanka 5th T20I 2021/22 - Score Report|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/sri-lanka-in-australia-2021-22-1263459/australia-vs-sri-lanka-5th-t20i-1263475/full-scorecard|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref> On 23 May 2022, he was hospitalized after leaving the field holding his chest minutes before lunch on the first day of the second Test [[Sri Lankan cricket team in Bangladesh in 2022|against Bangladesh]]. The doctors "suspect muscle spasms" as the reason for his discomfort but an ECG test has "come out clear".<ref>{{cite web|last=Vimpany|first=Mike|title=Kusal Mendis 'under observation' in Dhaka hospital after complaining of chest pain|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ban-vs-sl-2nd-test-kusal-mendis-hospitalised-in-dhaka-after-complaining-of-chest-pain-131630|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=29 May 2003|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Breaking: Kusal Mendis Taken Off The Field Due To Massive Chest Pain; Hospitalised: BAN vs SL|url=https://www.india.com/sports/breaking-kusal-mendis-taken-off-the-field-due-to-massive-chest-pain-hospitalised-physio-tells-about-the-condition-5407743/|last=Daud|first=Sunny|website=www.india.com|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref>

In the [[Australian cricket team in Sri Lanka in 2022|Australian Test series]] in July 2022, Sri Lanka suffered a huge defeat, with the match ending in three days.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dimuth Karunaratne hopes 'big first-innings score' can 'build pressure' on Australia|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/sl-vs-aus-2nd-test-2022-dimuth-karunaratne-hopes-big-first-innings-score-can-build-pressure-on-australia-1323521|last=Fernando|first=Andrew Fidel|date=7 July 2022|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref> Mendis scored just 3 and 8 runs in the match. However, on 9 July 2022, in the second Test, Mendis scored 85 runs in a partnership of 152 with [[Dimuth Karunaratne]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Kusal Mendis, Karunaratne lead SL's solid reply after Jayasuriya's six-for|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/australia-in-sri-lanka-2022-1307289/sri-lanka-vs-australia-2nd-test-1307302/match-report|last=McGlashan|first=Andrew|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=11 July 2022|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref> On 1 September 2022, [[2022 Asia Cup|against Bangladesh]] Kusal Mendis scored his 7th T20I half-century. He scored 60 runs while chasing 183 runs. Finally, Sri Lanka won the match and Kusal Mendis won the player of the match award for his performance.<ref>{{cite web|title=Sri Lanka beat Bangladesh Sri Lanka won by 2 wickets (with 4 balls remaining) - Bangladesh vs Sri Lanka, Asia Cup, 5th Match, Group B Match Summary, Report|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/asia-cup-2022-1327237/bangladesh-vs-sri-lanka-5th-match-group-b-1327273/live-cricket-score|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=1 September 2022|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref>

During the [[2022 Asia Cup]], Mendis played as the opener with [[Pathum Nissanka]] and they made match-winning partnerships in the games against Bangladesh, Afghanistan and India.<ref>{{cite web|title=Sri Lanka are discovering new heroes, one match at a time|last=Fernando|first=Andrew Fidel|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/asia-cup-2022-ind-vs-sl-dilshan-madushanka-pathum-nissanka-kusal-mendis-dasun-shanaka-rajapaksa-sri-lanka-heroes-1332898|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=7 September 2022|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref> Against Bangladesh, Mendis made a match-winning knock of 60 runs and Sri Lanka finally chased the target of 183 runs with one wicket.<ref>{{cite web|title=Mendis, Shanaka and Asitha put Sri Lanka in the Super 4s|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/asia-cup-2022-1327237/bangladesh-vs-sri-lanka-5th-match-group-b-1327273/match-report|last=Isam|first=Mohammad|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=1 September 2022|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref> However, Mendis had four clear chances and won by luck.<ref>{{cite web|title=Luck Index - How giving four lives to Mendis cost Bangladesh the game|last=Rajesh|first=S.|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ban-vs-sl-asia-cup-2022-luck-index-how-giving-four-lives-to-kusal-mendis-cost-bangladesh-the-game-1332035|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=1 September 2022|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref> On 6 September 2022 against India, Mendis scored his 8th T20I half-century. He scored 57 runs and put up a strong 97-run partnership with [[Pathum Nissanka]] while chasing 173 runs. Finally, Sri Lanka won the match by 6 wickets.<ref>{{cite web|last=Monga|first=Sidharth|title=Sri Lanka all but through to Asia Cup final, India hanging by a thread|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/asia-cup-2022-1327237/india-vs-sri-lanka-9th-match-super-four-1327277/match-report|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=6 September 2022|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref>

In the first round in [[2022 ICC Men's T20 World Cup|T20I World Cup 2022]], against Netherlands, Mendis scored the 9th T20I half-century and made 79 runs in 44 balls hitting five boundaries and five sixes. Finally, Sri Lanka won the match by 16 runs and qualified for Super 12, where Mendis won the Player of the match award for his performance.<ref>{{cite web|title=9th Match, First Round Group A (D/N), Geelong, October 20, 2022, ICC Men's T20 World Cup (Max O'Dowd 71*, Roelof van der Merwe 0*, Lahiru Kumara 1/28) - RESULT, SL vs NED, 9th Match, First Round Group A, live score, 2022|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/icc-men-s-t20-world-cup-2022-23-1298134/netherlands-vs-sri-lanka-9th-match-first-round-group-a-1298143/live-cricket-score|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=20 October 2022|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref> In the first match in Super 12s in [[2022 ICC Men's T20 World Cup|T20 World Cup 2022]], against Ireland, Mendis scored his 10th T20I half-century and surpassed 1000 T20I runs. Finally, Sri Lanka won the match by 9 wickets and Mendis won the Player of the Match award.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/icc-men-s-t20-world-cup-2022-23-1298134/ireland-vs-sri-lanka-15th-match-group-1-1298149/match-report|last=Fernando|first=Andrew Fidel|title=Spinners, Kusal Mendis star in Sri Lanka's comfortable win|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=23 October 2022|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref>

On 5 January 2023, [[Sri Lankan cricket team in India in 2022–23|against India]], Mendis scored his 11th T20I half-century and eventually Sri Lanka won the match by 16 runs.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Shanaka overcomes Axar to help Sri Lanka keep the series alive |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/sri-lanka-in-india-2022-23-1348629/india-vs-sri-lanka-2nd-t20i-1348641/match-report |access-date=2023-01-07 |website=ESPNcricinfo|date=5 January 2023 }}</ref> In March 2023, in the first test [[Sri Lankan cricket team in New Zealand in 2022–23|against New Zealand]], Mendis scored the fastest half-century and scored 87 off 83 balls. However, in the second test, he was dismissed for a duck in the first innings and scored a half-century in the second innings. On 8 April 2023, in the third T20I match against New Zealand, Mendis scored his 12th T20I fifty in a losing cause.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sri Lanka vs New Zealand Scorecard 2022/23 {{!}} Cricket Scorecard |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/sri-lanka-tour-of-new-zealand-2022-23-1322351/new-zealand-vs-sri-lanka-3rd-t20i-1322364/full-scorecard |access-date=2023-04-08 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref>

On 16 April 2023, in the first test match [[Irish cricket team in Sri Lanka in 2022–23|against Ireland]], Mendis scored his 8th test century and put a 281-run partnership for the second wicket with [[Dimuth Karunaratne]]. Finally, Sri Lanka won the match by an innings and 280 runs.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sri Lanka vs Ireland Scorecard 2023 {{!}} Cricket Scorecard |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/ireland-in-sri-lanka-2023-1363445/sri-lanka-vs-ireland-1st-test-1363447/full-scorecard |access-date=2023-04-18 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref> During the second test match against Ireland, Mendis scored his maiden test double-century. He scored 245 runs from 291 deliveries hitting 18 boundaries and 11 sixes. He also put a 268-run partnership with [[Nishan Madushka]]. Finally, Sri Lanka won the match and the series, and Mendis won Player of the Series award for his performance.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ireland vs Sri Lanka Scorecard 2023 {{!}} Cricket Scorecard |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/ireland-in-sri-lanka-2023-1363445/sri-lanka-vs-ireland-2nd-test-1363448/full-scorecard |access-date=2023-04-28 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref>

===Vice-Captaincy stints (2021/2023)===
Mendis was appointed vice-captain in  April 2021 against Bangladesh ODI series. He was also appointed Vice-captain for the T20 series against England. However, he was dropped from the vice-captain position against India home series in September 2021. In December 2022, he was recalled as a Sri Lanka ODI Vice-captain for the India tour 2023.

During the first [[2023 Cricket World Cup|World Cup match]] against South Africa, Mendis scored his 26th ODI half-century. He scored 76 runs from 42 balls which included four boundaries and eight sixes. His knock went in vain as Sri Lanka lost the match in a huge margin.<ref>{{Cite web |title=SA vs SL, ICC Cricket World Cup 2023/24, 4th Match at Delhi, October 07, 2023 - Full Scorecard |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/icc-cricket-world-cup-2023-24-1367856/south-africa-vs-sri-lanka-4th-match-1384395/full-scorecard |access-date=2023-10-10 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref> On 10 October 2023, against Pakistan, Mendis made his 3rd ODI century and scored 122 runs from 77 deliveries hitting 14 boundaries and 6 sixes. His efforts went in vain against Sri Lanka lost the match.<ref name=":0" />

=== ODI Captaincy (2023) ===
He was appointed as Sri Lanka's captain after regular skipper [[Dasun Shanaka]] was ruled out of the 2023 Cricket World Cup after suffering an injury in the game against Pakistan.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-10-15 |title=World Cup 2023: Sri Lanka announces new captain as Dasun Shanaka gets ruled out of remaining tournament |url=https://crickettimes.com/2023/10/world-cup-2023-sri-lanka-announces-new-captain-as-dasun-shanaka-gets-ruled-out-of-remaining-tournament/?fbclid=IwAR37nvEZGnVRwXMIZJEeigxAI2qIjq8RwYg2mAxMvtFI9Hbfj8dZlIji2ss |access-date=2023-10-16 |website=Cricket Times |language=en-US}}</ref> He scored just 9 runs in his first match as a captain of the Sri Lanka, as they lost to Australia by 5 wickets.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cricket scorecard - Australia vs Sri Lanka, 14th Match, ICC Cricket World Cup 2023 |url=https://www.cricbuzz.com/live-cricket-scorecard/75479/aus-vs-sl-14th-match-icc-cricket-world-cup-2023 |access-date=2023-10-31 |website=Cricbuzz |language=en}}</ref> In the next game against Netherlands, he led his team to a comfortable win.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NED vs SL, ICC Cricket World Cup 2023/24, 19th Match at Lucknow, October 21, 2023 - Full Scorecard |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/icc-cricket-world-cup-2023-24-1367856/netherlands-vs-sri-lanka-19th-match-1384410/full-scorecard |access-date=2023-10-31 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref> He also led Sri Lanka to a famous win against [[England]] which they won by 8 wickets, although he scored only 11 runs.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ENG vs SL, ICC Cricket World Cup 2023/24, 25th Match at Bengaluru, October 26, 2023 - Full Scorecard |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/icc-cricket-world-cup-2023-24-1367856/england-vs-sri-lanka-25th-match-1384416/full-scorecard |access-date=2023-10-31 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref> In the next game against [[Afghanistan]], Sri Lanka faltered big time, as their opponents eased past them with 7 wickets in hand.<ref>{{Cite web |title=AFG vs SL, ICC Cricket World Cup 2023/24, 30th Match at Pune, October 30, 2023 - Full Scorecard |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/icc-cricket-world-cup-2023-24-1367856/afghanistan-vs-sri-lanka-30th-match-1384421/full-scorecard |access-date=2023-10-31 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref>

===Post captaincy (2024–present)===
During T20I series [[Sri Lankan cricket team in Bangladesh in 2023–24|against Bangladesh]], he became highest run scorer in the series scoring 181 runs in three matches with average of 60.33 including two half centuries.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Today's Cricket Match {{!}} Cricket Update {{!}} Cricket News |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/records/series/batting-most-runs-career/sri-lanka-in-bangladesh-t20i-series-2023-24-16069 |access-date=2024-03-15 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref>

In May 2024, he was named in Sri Lanka's squad for the [[2024 ICC Men's T20 World Cup]] tournament.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sri Lanka’s Squad for ICC Men’s T20I World Cup 2024 |url=https://www.scorewaves.com/news-details/sri-lanka-squad-for-icc-t20-world-cup |access-date=2024-06-11 |website=ScoreWaves |language=en}}</ref> In September 2024 in the second test match [[New Zealand cricket team in Sri Lanka in 2024–25|against New Zealand]], Mendis scored his 10th century. He made an unbeaten century partnership with [[Kamindu Mendis]], where Sri Lanka posted a mammoth total of 602 in the first innings. Eventually Sri Lanka won the match by an innings and 154 runs and sealed the series 2–0.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mendises hit powerful centuries to put Sri Lanka in position of dominance|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/sri-lanka-vs-new-zealand-2024-1447091/sri-lanka-vs-new-zealand-2nd-test-1447097/match-report-2 |access-date=2024-09-28 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref>

On 17 October 2024 [[West Indian cricket team in Sri Lanka in 2024–25|against West Indies]] in the third T20I, Mendis made a match winning knock of an unbeaten 68 runs: his fifteenth fifty in T20Is, where he guided Sri Lanka to the victory and clinched the series 2–1. This is the first bilateral T20I series win over West Indies as well. Later, Mendis won the man of the match award for his batting performance.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kusal Mendis and Kusal Perera fifties power SL to series win|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/west-indies-in-sri-lanka-2024-25-1451810/sri-lanka-vs-west-indies-3rd-t20i-1451816/match-report |access-date=2024-09-28 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref>
  
On November 13, 2024, Kusal Mendis hit his highest score in ODIs, 143 off 128, with 17 4s and 2 6s, putting up a 206 run 2nd wicket stand with [[Avishka Fernando]] who also made 100 off 115 with 9 4s and 2 6s, Rain however interrupted the match in the last over leaving Sri Lanka on 324/5 in 49.2 overs, giving New Zealand a target off 221 runs in 27 overs, Sri Lanka did win the match by 45 runs, as New Zealand could only manage 175/9 in their 27 overs

== Controversies ==
=== Car accident ===
In July 2020, Kusal Mendis was involved in a fatal car accident in [[Panadura]], near Colombo. He was driving his [[SUV]] when he struck a 64-year-old man who was riding a [[bicycle]]. Unfortunately, the man succumbed to his injuries.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cricket/sri-lanka-wicketkeeper-batsman-kusal-mendis-arrested-for-causing-fatal-motor-accident-report/story-HlUDVBElAgIMSZPszgdWXK.html|title=Sri Lanka wicketkeeper-batsman Kusal Mendis arrested for causing fatal motor accident: Report|work=[[Hindustan Times]]|date=5 July 2020|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref> Mendis was arrested and taken into custody, and his vehicle was also impounded by the police. But police statement made without mention of whether either Mendis or the victim were under the influence of alcohol.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kusal Mendis arrested after being involved in fatal road accident |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/kusal-mendis-arrested-after-being-involved-in-fatal-road-accident-1226227 |access-date=2025-02-05 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref> A day after the incident, Mendis was released on [[bail]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/kusal-mendis-released-on-bail-day-after-arrest-for-role-in-fatal-road-accident-1226262|last=Fernando|first=Andrew Fidel|title=Kusal Mendis released on bail day after arrest for role in fatal road accident|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN Inc.|date=6 July 2020|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref>

=== Disciplinary issues ===
In July 2021, Mendis, along with [[Danushka Gunathilaka]] and [[Niroshan Dickwella]], was found guilty of breaching the team's [[Bio-secure bubble|bio-secure]] bubble during [[Sri Lankan cricket team in England in 2021|Sri Lanka's tour of England]]. They were sent back home and faced a one-year ban from international cricket and a six-month ban from domestic cricket.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bio-bubble breach: Kusal Mendis, Danushka Gunathilaka and Niroshan Dickwella suspended |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/sri-lanka-s-kusal-mendis-and-niroshan-dickwella-to-be-investigated-after-alleged-bio-bubble-breach-in-england-1268125 |access-date=2025-02-05 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref> The same trio was also penalized for violating curfew regulations by failing to be in their hotel rooms by 10:30 PM. This breach brought disrepute to Sri Lanka Cricket and resulted in a hefty fine of Sri Lanka Rupees 10 million for each player.<ref name="Cricket">{{Cite web |last=Cricket |first=Sri Lanka |date=2021-07-30 |title=Disciplinary Action against Danushka Gunathilaka, Kusal Mendis and Niroshan Dickwella |url=https://srilankacricket.lk/2021/07/disciplinary-action-against-danushka-gunathilaka-kusal-mendis-and-niroshan-dickwella/ |access-date=2025-02-05 |website=Sri Lanka Cricket |language=en-US}}</ref>

In December 2023, Mendis smashed a glass door at the [[Bloomfield Cricket and Athletic Club|Bloomfield Cricket Club]] pavilion after being dismissed for a 'duck' during an inter-club match.<ref name="Cricket"/> In March 2024, during an [[Sri Lankan cricket team in Bangladesh in 2023–24|ODI against Bangladesh]], Mendis, serving as the ODI captain, was fined for verbally abusing the umpires while shaking hands after the match. This incident highlighted concerns over player discipline within the team.<ref>{{Cite web |title=We do not condone such behavior – SLC |url=https://www.sundaytimes.lk/240324/sports/we-do-not-condone-such-behavior-slc-552965.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com |access-date=2025-02-05 |website=Print Edition - The Sunday Times, Sri Lanka}}</ref>{{AI-retrieved source|date=March 2026|checked=no}}

On 12 February 2021, Mendis married his wife in Colombo.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hirunews.lk/english/262432/sl-cricketer-kusal-mendis-gets-married-photos|title=SL cricketer Kusal Medis gets married|work=Hirunews|date=12 February 2021|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref> In June 2022, Mendis' wife gave birth to a baby girl.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dailynews.lk/2022/06/21/sports/281341/kusal-mendis-becomes-father|title=Kusal Mendis becomes a father|work=[[Daily News (Sri Lanka)|Daily News]]|date=21 June 2022|access-date=26 November 2022}}</ref>

web |last1=Smith |first1=Martin |title=Meet Australia's newest Test batsman |url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/marnus-labuschagne-australia-test-squad-queensland-bulls-brisbane-pronounciation-batsman-pakistan/2018-09-11 |publisher=[[Cricket Australia]]|access-date=9 October 2018 |date=11 September 2018}} born 22 June 1994) is an Australian international [[cricket]]er{{Cite web|last1=Ramsey |first1=Michael | url=https://www.smh.com.au/sport/cricket/bolter-labuschagne-impresses-for-australia-on-test-debut-20181009-p508io.html | title=Bolter Labuschagne impresses for Australia on Test debut|work=[[The
