cricket]] and for [[Brisbane Heat]] in the [[Big Bash League]] and is the captain of [[Pakistan Super League]] team [[Hyderabad Kingsmen]]. Labuschagne was once ranked as high as no.1 in the [[ICC Men's Player Rankings#Top 10 Test batsmen|Test batting rankings]]. He was a member of the Australian team that won the [[2023 World Test Championship final|2023 WTC]] and the [[2023 ICC Cricket World Cup|2023 ODI World Cup]]. He represented Queensland at various levels in junior cricket, before making his [[first-class cricket]] debut in 2014. In August 2019, Labuschagne was the first cricketer to become a concussion substitute in a Test match, replacing [[Steve Smith (cricketer)|Steve Smith]].{{cite web|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/1316589 |title=Smith withdrawn from second Test, Labuschagne comes in as concussion replacement, replacing Steve Smith|publisher=[[International Cricket Council]]|date=18 August 2019 |access-date=18 August 2019}} Labuschagne was the leading run-scorer in [[Test cricket|Test matches]] in 2019. He rose to fourth place in the [[ICC Player Rankings]] during the year, a rise of 106 places.[[Australian Associated Press]] (30 December 2019) [https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2019/dec/31/marnus-labuschagne-climbs-106-places-in-iccs-world-test-batting-rankings Marnus Labuschagne climbs 106 places in ICC Test batting rankings], ''[[The Guardian]]''. Retrieved 5 January 2020. In January 2020, Labuschagne was named as the [[ICC Men's Emerging Cricketer of the Year]] by the [[International Cricket Council]] (ICC),{{cite web|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/media-releases/1571932 |title=Stokes wins Sir Garfield Sobers Trophy |publisher=[[International Cricket Council]] |date=15 January 2020 |access-date=15 January 2020}} in February as Australia's Test player of the year,{{cite news |last1=Caffrey |first1=Oliver |title=Marnus Labuschagne wins Test player award |url=https://www.canberratimes.com.au/story/6623952/marnus-labuschagne-wins-test-player-award/ |access-date=9 April 2020 |work=The Canberra Times|date=11 February 2020}}{{cite news |last1=Griffiths |first1=Gareth |title=Marnus Labuschagne: Australia cricket award caps 'special' year |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/51510310 |access-date=9 April 2020 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=16 February 2020}} and in April as one of the five [[Cricketers of the Year]] by ''[[Wisden Cricketers' Almanack]]''.{{cite news |last1=Forsaith |first1=Rob |title=Wisden title an honour: Marnus Labuschagne |url=https://www.canberratimes.com.au/story/6718717/wisden-title-an-honour-marnus-labuschagne/?cs=14238 |access-date=9 April 2020 |work=The Canberra Times|date=9 April 2020}}{{cite news |last1=Hashim |first1=Taha |date=8 April 2020 |title=The summer that made Marnus Labuschagne a Wisden Cricketer of the Year |url=https://www.wisden.com/wisden-cricketers-almanack/the-summer-that-made-marnus-labuschagne-wisden-cricketer-year |access-date=4 April 2025 |work=Wisden Cricketers' Almanack}} ==Early life== Labuschagne was born in [[Klerksdorp]], in [[South Africa]]'s [[North West (South African province)|North West]] province, to South African parents. His family emigrated to Australia in 2004 when he was 10, after his father gained work in the mining industry, and Labuschagne attended school at [[Brisbane State High School]]. He grew up speaking [[Afrikaans]], and only became fluent in English after moving to Australia.Craddock, Robert (27 October 2014) [http://www.dailytelegraph.com.au/sport/cricket/former-south-african-marnus-labuschagne-wellschooled-for-sheffield-shield-debut/story-fni2fnmo-1227104157669?nk=c31059d675cdc6bd0680a0290cb259f3 Former South African Marnus Labuschagne well-schooled for Sheffield Shield debut], ''[[The Daily Telegraph (Sydney)|The Daily Telegraph]]''. Retrieved 1 November 2014. In 2021, he revealed that in November 2010, he worked at [[The Gabba]], [[Brisbane]], as a [[Hot Spot (cricket)|Hot Spot]] [[Thermographic camera|infrared camera]] operator for [[Nine Network|Channel 9]], and witnessed [[Peter Siddle]]'s [[hat-trick]] during the [[2010–11 Ashes series]], on Siddle's 26th birthday.{{Citation|title=Australia's players remember the best Ashes deliveries {{!}} NuPure Top 10| date=27 November 2021 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iz-Whq7ZgPs|language=en|access-date=28 November 2021}} ==Domestic career== A right-handed batsman, Labuschagne played for [[Queensland cricket team|Queensland]] at under-12, under-15, under-17, and under-19 level, and captained the team at the 2012–13 National Championships.[https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/1073/1073270/all_teams.html Teams Marnus Labuschagne played for], CricketArchive. Retrieved 4 January 2020. {{subscription required}}[http://www.redlandcitybulletin.com.au/story/1183924/redland-cricket-stars-in-state-team/ Redland cricket stars in state team], ''Redland City Bulletin'', 13 December 2012. Retrieved 1 November 2014. In [[Brisbane Grade Cricket]], he plays for [[Easts-Redlands District Cricket Club]].[http://www.cricket.com.au/news-list/2014/10/27/new-south-wales-queensland-debutants-rookies-sheffield-shield-round-one Blues, Bulls call on debutants], [[Cricket Australia]], 27 October 2014. Retrieved 1 November 2014. He spent 2013 playing club cricket in England for [[Plymouth Cricket Club|Plymouth]] in the [[Devon Cricket League|Devon Premier League]] and played for Sandwich Town Cricket Club in the [[Kent Cricket League|Kent Premier League]] in 2014, scoring prolifically for both teams.[http://www.devoncricket.co.uk/page.php?Id=3451 Plymouth old boy set for Australian Test debut against Pakistan], Devon Cricket Board. Retrieved 4 January 2020.Harvey, Richard (19 May 2014) [https://www.kentonline.co.uk/kent/sport/sandwich-batsman-marnus-laberchange-smashes-17416/ Shepherd Neame Kent Cricket League Premier Division wrap], ''[[Kent Online]]''. Retrieved 4 January 2020. His 1,049 runs scored for Sandwich Town in the 2014 season set a new Kent Premier League record for runs scored by a batter in a single season, overtaking the previous record of 1,012 set by former-Australia coach [[Justin Langer]] in 1992 whilst representing Dover Cricket Club.{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/59945356|title=Ashes: How Australia's Marnus Labuschagne was made in Plymouth and Sandwich|publisher=BBC Sport|last=Shemilt|first=Stephan|date=12 January 2022|access-date=17 July 2025}} After playing just once for Queensland Academy, Labuschagne made his [[first-class cricket]] debut in the first round of the [[2014–15 Sheffield Shield season]] against [[South Australia cricket team|South Australia]] at the [[Adelaide Oval]]. Opening the batting with [[Joe Burns (cricketer)|Joe Burns]], he scored 83 runs in Queensland's first innings, featuring in a 99-run fourth-wicket [[Partnership (cricket)|partnership]] with [[Nick Stevens (cricketer)|Nick Stevens]].[https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/8043/report/754885/south-australia-vs-queensland-sheffield-shield-2014-15 Stevens ton revives Bulls after Sayers hat-trick], [[CricInfo]], 31 October 2014. Retrieved 4 January 2020. Later in the 2014–15 season, Labuschagne was used as a substitute fielder for the [[Australia national cricket team|Australian national team]] in the second Test against [[Indian cricket team in Australia in 2014–15|India]] at [[the Gabba]], taking a low catch at short leg. Labuschagne made his [[List A cricket|List A]] debut for Queensland in the [[2015–16 Matador BBQs One-Day Cup|2015 One-Day Cup]] in October 2015 and scored his maiden first-class century in the following month, making 112 runs in his eighth Sheffield Shield match. He scored 273 runs at a batting average of 45 in the [[2016–17 Matador BBQs One-Day Cup|2016 One-Day Cup]] and was named player of the tournament. In September 2017, during a [[2017–18 JLT One-Day Cup|2017 One-Day Cup]] match between Queensland and [[Cricket Australia XI]], he became the first fielder to be penalised under the newly introduced [[Laws of cricket|Law]] designed to stop fielders deceiving batsmen. Labuschagne dived to field a ball in the covers, and although he failed to stop the ball he feigned throwing to the wicket-keeper. His team was penalised five runs.{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/8626/report/1118571/western-australia-vs-new-south-wales-3rd-match-jlt-one-day-cup-2017-18 |date=21 August 2017 |access-date=29 September 2017 |title=Labuschagne penalised under new 'fake fielding' rule |publisher=[[CricInfo]]}}{{cite web|last1=Burnett |first1=Adam| url=http://www.cricket.com.au/news/matthew-renshaw-marnus-labuschagne-fake-fielding-video-queensland-jlt-one-day-cup-five-penalty-runs/2017-09-29 |date=21 August 2017 |access-date=29 September 2017 |title=Renshaw endorses new 'fake fielding' rule |publisher=[[Cricket Australia]]}} After being Queensland's leading run-scorer in the [[2017–18 Sheffield Shield season|2017–18 Sheffield Shield]], [[Cricket Australia]] named him in their [[Sheffield Shield]] team of the season.{{cite web|last1=Burnett |first1=Adam |last2=Cameron |first2=Louis |url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/sheffield-shield-team-year-season-17-18-burns-renshaw-bird-tremain-ferguson-doran-labuschagne-wade/2018-03-18 |title=Our Sheffield Shield team of the year |date=18 March 2018 |access-date=18 March 2018 |publisher=[[Cricket Australia]]}} In April 2021, Labuschagne scored 192 in the [[2020–21 Sheffield Shield season]] final against [[New South Wales cricket team|New South Wales]].{{cite web |title=Marnus Labuschagne feasts on New South Wales again to cement Queensland dominance|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/sheffield-shield-2020-21-1233442/queensland-vs-new-south-wales-final-1244521/match-report-2 |website=ESPN CricInfo}} Queensland winning by an innings and 33 runs. In June 2024, Labuschagne was formally announced as Queensland Bulls state captain for both Sheffield Shield and One-Day Cup, having previously filled the role on two occasions in 2023 in One-Day Cup and Sheffield Shield matches against South Australia.{{cite web |title=MARNUS TO LEAD BULLS, New Role For 2024/25|url=https://www.qldcricket.com.au/news/4040265/marnus-to-lead-bulls-new-role-for-2024-25 |website=QLD Cricket |date=18 June 2024 }} In the [[2024–25 Sheffield Shield season]], Labuschagne switched from his part-time legspin to bowling medium pace in the lead-up to the [[Indian cricket team in Australia in 2024–25|Test series against India]].{{Cite web |date=21 November 2024 |title=Marsh 'will definitely' bowl but Marnus' mediums may also get a call |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/bgt-aus-vs-ind-1st-test-mitchell-marsh-will-definitely-bowl-says-pat-cummins-1460599 |access-date=23 November 2024 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}} ===County cricket=== [[File:1 08 Marnus Labuschagne (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|Labuschagne playing for Glamorgan (2023).]] In April 2019, Labuschagne signed for [[Glamorgan County Cricket Club]] for the [[2019 English cricket season]].{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/47772762 |title=Marnus Labuschagne: Glamorgan web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/8204/report/1166987/day/4/undefined|title=Marnus Labuschagne knock keeps Glamorgan unbeaten as match with Sussex is drawn|publisher=[[CricInfo]]|date=30 May an average of 61.89 runs per innings.{{cite web|title=Glamorgan averages 2019|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/teams/glamorgan|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|access-date=3 January 2020}}{{cite web|title=Division Two averages 2019|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|access-date=3 January 2020}} He also took 19 wickets with a bowling average of 38.11.{{cite web|title=Marnus Labuschagne Player Profile|url=https://www.glamorgancricket.com/squad-profile/marnus-labuschagne|publisher=[[Glamorgan County Cricket Club]]|access-date=3 January 2020}} In November deal|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/50395985|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=12 November 2019|access-date=3 January 2020}} In June 2020, Labuschagne's contract was extended for an extra season Australia batsman signs for extra year with Glamorgan], [[BBC Sport]], 19 June 2020. Retrieved 20 June 2020. ==International career== === Tour of UAE against Pakistan 2018–19 === {{Main|Australian cricket team in the United Arab Emirates in 2018–19}} In September 2018, he was named in Australia's [[Test cricket|Test]] squad for their series [[Australian cricket team in the United Arab Emirates in 2018–19|against Pakistan]].{{cite web |last1=Smith|first1=Martin|url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/australia-test-squad-team-pakistan-series-uae-tour-fixture-paine-marsh-maxwell-starc-renshaw-langer/2018-09-11 |title=Maxwell out as Bulls, Finch bolt into Test squad | publisher=[[Cricket Australia]] |date=11 September 2018|access-date=11 September 2018}}{{cite web|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/846802 |title=Australia Test squad for UAE: The newcomers |publisher=[[International Cricket Council]]|date=11 September 2018 |access-date=11 September 2018}} He made his Test debut for Australia against [[Pakistan national cricket team|Pakistan]] on 7 October 2018, scoring a two-ball [[Duck (cricket)|duck]] in his first innings and 13 runs in his second. He also took two wickets on debut.{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1157370.html |title=1st Test, Australia tour of United Arab Emirates at Dubai, Oct 7–11 2018 |publisher=[[CricInfo]] |access-date=7 October 2018}} He had his [[baggy green cap]] presented by [[Michael Hussey]]. In the second Test, he took another five wickets and made scores of 25 and 43, top scoring in Australia's second innings.[https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/18886/scorecard/1157371/australia-vs-pakistan-2nd-test-australia-in-uae-2018-19 2nd Test, Australia tour of United Arab Emirates at Abu Dhabi, Oct 16–19 2018], [[CricInfo]]. Retrieved 9 January 2020. === India and Sri Lanka in Australia 2018–19 === {{Main|Indian cricket team in Australia in 2018–19|Sri Lankan cricket team in Australia in 2018–19}} Marnus was named in the Australian [[One Day International]] squad in December 2018 ahead of the team's tour of India the following year before he was surprisingly added to the Australian Test squad for the fourth Test match [[Indian cricket team in Australia in 2018-19|against the touring Indians]] at the start of the year. He was selected to bat at number three in the batting order, a decision which was "heavily criticised" at the time.McGlashan A (3 January 2019) [https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/25674484/marnus-labuschagne-australia-unlikely-no-3-learns-pujara Labuschagne, Australia's unlikely No. 3, learns from Pujara], [[CricInfo]]. Retrieved 9 January 2020.[https://sports.ndtv.com/cricket/marnus-labuschagne-called-up-as-australia-overhaul-odi-squad-for-india-tour-2149939 Marnus Labuschagne Called Up As Australia Overhaul ODI Squad For India Tour], [[NDTV]], 17 December 2019. Retrieved 9 January 2020. He scored 38 runs in his only innings and was retained in the team for the two Tests against Sri Lanka at the end of the summer.[https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/26419099/marnus-labuschagne-pens-glamorgan-deal-ahead-ashes-push Marnus Labuschagne pens Glamorgan deal ahead of Ashes push], [[CricInfo]], 2 April 2020. Retrieved 9 January 2020. === Ashes in England 2019 === {{Main|2019 Ashes series}} [[File:Marnus Labuschagne Forward Defensive.jpg|thumb|Labuschagne batting for Australia in the 2019 Ashes series]] After showing good early season form for Glamorgan in county cricket,Malcolm, Alex (7 May 2019) [https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/26790969/marnus-labuschagne-sparkles-joe-burns-returns-home Labuschagne sparkles while Burns returns home], [[CricInfo]]. Retrieved 9 January 2020. he was named in Australia's squad for the [[2019 Ashes series]] in England.{{cite web |last1=Ferris|first1=Sam|title=Australia name 17-man Ashes squad |url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/australia-2019-ashes-squad-england-tests-paine-smith-warner-pattinson-wade-marsh-bancroft-neser/2019-07-27 |publisher=[[Cricket Australia]] |date=27 July concussion rules |publisher=[[Cricket Australia]]|date=18 August 2018 |access-date=18 August 2019}} Players substituted in this way are intended to be a "like for like" replacement,{{Cite web|title=Steven Smith, Marnus Labuschagne together at last|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/steven-smith-marnus-labuschagne-together-at-last-1199646|access-date=16 December and intelligent batting".Brettig, Daniel (24 August 2019) [https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/27454649/marnus-labuschagne-sets-example-australia-england Marnus Labuschagne sets the example for Australia – and England], [[CricInfo]]. After England were bowled out for 67 in their first innings, Labuschagne became the fifth batsman in Test history to make two scores in a match higher than the total scored by the opposing team in one of their innings.{{cite web |title=Australia Labuschagne joins elite Test batting club |url=https://www.news24.com/sport/cricket/ashes/australia-labuschagne-joins-elite-test-batting-club-20190824 |website=news24 |access-date=20 October 2021}} === Pakistan and New Zealand in Australia 2019–20 === {{Main|2 = Pakistani cricket team in Australia in 2019–20|3 = New Zealand cricket team in Australia in 2019–20}} Labuschagne retained his place in the Australian team for [[Pakistani cricket team in Australia in 2019–20|the visit of Pakistan]] the following summer, scoring 185, his maiden Test century, at the Gabba.{{Cite web|url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/cricket/australia/cricket-australia-vs-pakistan-first-test-at-the-gabba-marnus-labuschagne-scores-first-century-video/news-story/53aece4e1c06811a88f8d0eb170d403f|title=Cricket Australia vs Pakistan, first Test at the Gabba: Marnus Labuschagne scores first century, video|date=23 November 2019|work=Fox Sports|language=en-AU|access-date=23 November 2019}} He scored another century in the second Test{{Cite web|url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/cricket/australia/cricket-australia-vs-pakistan-second-test-at-adelaide-oval-marnus-labuschagne-continues-his-rise-with-century/news-story/6312a886ca04180585a52612e2dbd646|title=Cricket Australia vs Pakistan, second Test at Adelaide Oval: Marnus Labuschagne continues his rise with century|date=29 November 2019|work=Fox Sports|language=en-AU|access-date=1 December 2019}} before scoring a third in the [[New Zealand cricket team in Australia in 2019-20|first Test against New Zealand]] in December. Having made three consecutive centuries, he made half-centuries in his next two innings before starting 2020 by making his first double-century in the third Test against New Zealand at the [[Sydney Cricket Ground|SCG]], scoring 215 runs.[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/50991733 Australia v New Zealand: Marnus Labuschagne makes 215 for hosts], [[BBC Sport]], 4 January 2020. Retrieved 4 January 2020. He finished 2019 as the year's highest Test match run-scorer, having made 975 of his 1,104 Test runs in the year after his appearance as a concussion substitute in August.[[Australian Associated Press]] (31 December 2019) [https://www.smh.com.au/sport/cricket/labuschagne-up-106-test-rankings-spots-in-2019-20191231-p53nsq.html Labuschagne up 106 Test rankings spots in 2019], ''[[Sydney Morning Herald]]''. Retrieved 9 January 2020.[https://crickettimes.com/2019/12/top-10-batsmen-with-most-test-runs-in-2019/ Top 10 batsmen with most Test runs in 2019], ''The Cricket Times'', 31 December 2019. |title=Usman Khawaja and Marcus Stoinis lose Cricket Australia contracts |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=30 April 2020}} On 16 July 2020, Labuschagne was named in a 26-man preliminary squad of players to begin training ahead of a possible [[Australian cricket team in England in 2020|tour to England]] following the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/29470776/usman-khawaja-marcus-stoinis-expanded-australia-training-squad-possible-england-tour |title=Usman Khawaja and Marcus Stoinis in expanded Australia training squad for possible England tour |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=16 July 2020}}{{cite web|url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/australia-26-player-preliminary-list-training-group-uk-england-tour-odi-t20-covid19/2020-07-16 |title=Aussies name huge 26-player group with eye on UK tour |work=Cricket Australia |access-date=16 July 2020}} On 14 August 2020, [[Cricket Australia]] confirmed that the fixtures would be taking place, with Labuschagne included in the touring party.{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/29658561/riley-meredith,-josh-philippe-daniel-sams-included-australia-tour-england-confirmed |title=Riley Meredith, Josh Philippe and Daniel Sams included as Australia tour to England confirmed |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=14 August 2020}}{{cite web|url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/australia-squad-odi-t20-england-tour-philippe-meredith-sams-maxwell-stoinis-lyon-tye-bubble-covid19/2020-08-14 |title=Uncapped trio make Australia's UK touring party |work=Cricket Australia |access-date=14 August 2020}} === New Zealand in Australia 2020 === {{Main|New Zealand cricket team in Australia in 2019–20}} New Zealand returned to Australia after the Test series, with games scheduled to be held on the 13, 15 and 20 March 2020. The first match was won by Australia, with a winning margin of 71 runs as Labuschagne made 56.{{Cite web|title=Full Scorecard of Australia vs New Zealand 1st ODI 2019 – Score Report |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/new-zealand-in-australia-2019-20-1183522/australia-vs-new-zealand-1st-odi-1183537/full-scorecard|access-date=15 December 2020|work=ESPNcricinfo|language=en}} However, due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the 2nd and 3rd matches were cancelled without a ball being bowled due to travel restrictions.{{Cite web|title=Cricket Coverage – Australia vs New Zealand, New Zealand in Australia, 2nd ODI Match Analysis, Reports |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/new-zealand-in-australia-2019-20-1183522/australia-vs-new-zealand-2nd-odi-1183538/match-news|access-date=15 December 2020|work=ESPNcricinfo|language=en}}{{Cite web|title=Full Scorecard of Australia vs New Zealand 3rd ODI 2019 – Score Report |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/new-zealand-in-australia-2019-20-1183522/australia-vs-new-zealand-3rd-odi-1183539/full-scorecard|access-date=15 December 2020|work=ESPNcricinfo|language=en}}{{Cite web|title=Australia v New Zealand cancelled with travel restrictions in place|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/australia-v-new-zealand-cancelled-with-travel-restrictions-in-place-1219328|access-date=15 December 2020|work=ESPNcricinfo|language=en}} In February 2022, Labuschagne was named in Australia's [[Twenty20 International]] (T20I) squad for their one-off match [[Australian cricket team in Pakistan in 2021–22|against Pakistan]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/story/1302159.html |title=Australia's Test quicks and David Warner rested from Pakistan limited-overs matches |access-date=22 February 2022 |work=ESPNcricinfo}} He made his T20I debut on 5 April 2022, for Australia against [[Pakistan national cricket team|Pakistan]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1288316.html |title=Only T20I (N), Lahore, April 05, 2022 |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=5 April 2022}} === 2021-22 Ashes Series in Australia === {{Main|2021-22 Ashes series}} This series was Labuschagne's first Ashes series at home, in which he played all 5 Test matches, and scored 335 runs with the bat across the series at an average of 41.87.{{cite web|title=Cricket Records in The Ashes, 2021/22|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/records/series/batting-most-runs-career/the-ashes-2021-22-13979|publisher=[[ESPNCricinfo]]}} During the 2nd Test at [[Adelaide Oval]], in Australia's first innings, he scored a 103-run century off a patient 305 balls. In the 2nd innings of the same Test, he scored 51 runs off 96 balls, leading to him being named the [[Player of the Match awards (cricket)|Player Of The Match]].{{cite web|title=Australia vs England, 2nd Test at Adelaide, AUS v ENG, Dec 15 2021 - Full Scorecard|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/england-in-australia-2021-22-1263452/australia-vs-england-2nd-test-1263463/full-scorecard|publisher=[[ESPNCricinfo]]}} === Ashes in England 2023 === {{Main|2023 Ashes series}} Labuschagne scored 328 runs at 32.8 with a century in the 4th Test. This was just his second century scored outside of Australia.{{cite web |url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/cricket/the-ashes/ashes-2023-australia-vs-england-fifth-test-series-player-ratings-pat-cummins-david-warner-video-cricket-news/news-story/ff8bedcbafa1d0ef46b2ee0cfcd72527| title =Khawaja truth Aussies can't deny as Marsh revival stuns; big guns exposed: Series Ratings|website=Fox Sports|date=1 August 2023 }} === 2023 Cricket World Cup === {{Main|2023 Cricket World Cup}} He was selected in Australia's squad for the 2023 World Cup.{{Cite web |title=Australia Squad – ICC Cricket World Cup, 2023 Squad |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/icc-cricket-world-cup-2023-24-1367856/australia-squad-1396545/series-squads |access-date=20 November 2023 |work=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}} He scored a match-winning half century in the [[2023 Cricket World Cup final|World Cup Final]] against India to take his team home.{{Cite web |title=IND vs AUS, ICC Cricket World Cup 2023/24, Final at Ahmedabad, November 19, 2023 – Full Scorecard |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/icc-cricket-world-cup-2023-24-1367856/india-vs-australia-final-1384439/full-scorecard |access-date=20 November 2023 |work=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}} === India in Australia 2024–25 === {{Main|2024-25 Border-Gavaskar Trophy}} Ahead of the first test of the series, there was a lot of speculation about the form of Labuschagne. This intensified following his performance where he batted poorly in both innings.{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/cricket/articles/cvg0yv23w9vo|title='Ruined himself' – the startling decline of Labuschagne|publisher=BBC|access-date=26 November 2024}} To make matters worse, Labuschagne was also criticized for his bowling.{{cite news |url=https://www.footboom1.com/en/news/cricket/2099020-adam-gilchrist-criticizes-australia-for-negative-illegal-tactics-against-india-in-first-test|title=Adam Gilchrist Criticizes Australia for 'Negative, Illegal Tactics' Against India in First Test|publisher=FootBoom|access-date=26 November 2024}} === 2025-26 Ashes Series in Australia === {{Main|2025-26 Ashes series}} Before the beginning of the 2025-26 Ashes series, there was a discussion of whether or not Labuschagne should be a part of the Test team for the series, as his form of the last 6 months had not been up to par. But in the two months coming up the series, Labuschagne found incredible form, scoring two centuries in the [[2025-26 Sheffield Shield season|Sheffield Shield]] of 160 and 159 in October,{{cite web|title=2025-26 Sheffield Shield Batting Records|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/records/tournament/batting-most-runs-innings/sheffield-shield-2025-26-17419|publisher=[[ESPNCricinfo]]}} and 3 more centuries in the [[2025-26 Dean Jones Trophy|Dean Jones Trophy]] of 130, 105, and 101 in September October and November.{{cite web|title=2025-26 Dean Jones Trophy Batting Records|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/records/tournament/batting-most-runs-innings/one-day-cup-australia-2025-26-17420|publisher=[[ESPNCricinfo]]}} Because of the incredible form, he was selected for the series. He played all 5 Test matches, and put up 259 runs with the bat at an average of 28.77, scoring 2 50's.{{cite web|title=2025-26 Ashes Series Batting Records|url= https://www.espncricinfo.com/records/series/batting-most-runs-career/the-ashes-2025-26-16756|publisher=[[ESPNCricinfo]]}} In the 3rd Test in Adelaide, during England's second innings with the bat, he made two spectacular catches to dismiss [[Ollie Pope]] and later [[Will Jacks]], helping Australia to victory in the match and clinching the series.{{cite web|title=Australia vs. England 3rd Test Full Scorecard, Adelaide|url= https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/the-ashes-2025-26-1455609/australia-vs-england-3rd-test-1455613/full-scorecard|publisher=[[ESPNCricinfo]]}} === Australia in Pakistan and Bangladesh 2026 === In 2026, Australia toured Pakistan and he made unremarkable scores. In the first ODI, he was dismissed for a two ball duck, after being trapped and given lbw to [[Arafat Minhas]].{{Cite web |title=PAK vs AUS Cricket Scorecard, 1st ODI at Rawalpindi, May 30, 2026 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/australia-in-pakistan-2026-1535643/pakistan-vs-australia-1st-odi-1535645/full-scorecard |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260604172051/https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/australia-in-pakistan-2026-1535643/pakistan-vs-australia-1st-odi-1535645/full-scorecard |archive-date=2026-06-04 |access-date=2026-06-10 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}} In the second ODI, he made 5 runs off 12 balls, failing to make an impact once again whilst trying to hit the ball hard, but top-edging it straight to a fielder.{{Cite web |access-date=16 June 2026 |title=Pakistan vs Australia, 1st ODI at Rawalpindi, PAK vs AUS, May 30 2026 - Full Scorecard |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/australia-in-pakistan-2026-1535643/pakistan-vs-australia-1st-odi-1535645/full-scorecard |website=ESPN Cricinfo}} In the third ODI, he fell cheaply once more, scoring 19 runs off 31 balls. After touring Pakistan, Australia toured Bangladesh. After just the first ODI, doubts began to arise about his form and statistical analysis revealed that he had averaged 11.64 in his previous 14 ODI innings. It was also shown that in his last 7 innings he had averaged just 4.5, and scored 25 runs. Critics also noticed that his fear of getting out made him afraid to attack bowlers.{{Cite web |last=Cricinfo |first=ESPN |date=10 June 2026 |title=Where to now for Marnus Labuschagne? |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/where-to-now-for-australia-batter-marnus-labuschagne-1540358 }} === Test records === In December 2022, on [[West Indian cricket team in Australia in 2022–23|West Indies tour of Australia]], Labuschagne achieved the 3000 run landmark, and became the joint second-fastest batter to achieve this feat.{{Cite web |date=9 December 2022 |title=Marnus Labuschagne Becomes Joint-Second-Fastest to Complete 3,000 Test Runs |url=https://www.probatsman.com/aus-vs-wi-marnus-labuschagne-becomes-joint-second-fastest-to-complete-3000-test-runs |access-date=9 December 2022 |website=Probatsman}} He took 51 innings to accomplish the landmark, equalling West Indies' batter [[Everton Weekes]].{{Cite web |title=Labuschagne behind only Bradman as fastest to 3,000 |url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/marnus-labuschagne-second-fastest-3000-test-runs-australia-west-indies-second-test-adelaide-bradman/2022-12-09 |access-date=9 December 2022 |website=cricket.com.au |language=en}} === Achievements=== * [[ICC Men's Test Team of the Year]]: 2019, 2021, 2022 * [[Allan Border Medal|Shane Warne Men's Test Player of the Year]]: 2020 * [[ICC Men's Emerging Cricketer of the Year]]: 2019 == Personal life == Labuschagne married his wife, Rebekah, on 26 May 2017. Their first child, a daughter was born on 20 September 2022.{{Cite web|url=http://www.thecricketmonthly.com/story/1214425/how-labuschagne-became-mighty-marnus|title=How Labuschagne became mighty Marnus|work=ESPNcricinfo|language=en|access-date=12 April 2020}} They have a chocolate Labrador named 'Milo' who has been known to make appearances on Labuschagne's Instagram playing backyard cricket.{{citation needed|date=December 2022}} Labuschagne was brought up in a Christian household and committed to the faith aged 17. He has spoken publicly about how his Christian faith provides stability amid the ups and downs of professional cricket.{{cite web |last1=James |first1=Sebastian |title=Big Bash rising star with Bible verses in his shoes |url=https://www.eternitynews.com.au/australia/big-bash-rising-star-with-bible-verses-in-his-shoes/ |work=Eternity News |date=20 December 2017|access-date=17 July 2019 |language=en-AU}} Labuschagne has a strong love for coffee, having completed a barista course at the age of 21. He has been known to take his commercial grade coffee machine away on tour with the Australian Cricket Team. On the tour to Pakistan, he also took 30 kg of coffee beans and 1000L of oat milk for the team.{{Cite web |last=Cummins |first=Pat |date=4 March 2022 |title='This isn't a normal tour': Pat Cummins reflects from Rawalpindi ahead of historic first Pakistan Test |url=https://www.codesports.com.au/cricket/this-isnt-a-normal-tour-pat-cummins-reflects-from-rawalpindi-ahead-of-historic-first-pakistan-test/news-story/d3de2bb40d2a792ad8a3411db92ceb0e}} Away from the field, Labuschagne has been known to hone his batting skills with home-made games in his backyard. In preparation for the 2022 Australian tour of Pakistan, he was seen practising batting on his home balcony in [[Brisbane]] on a rubber mat laden with pieces of taped aluminium and metal sheeting to try to emulate the variable bounce and turn of Pakistani wickets.{{Cite news |date=21 February 2022 |title=How a rubber mat and aluminium sheets are helping Marnus Labuschagne prepare for Pakistan tour |language=en-AU |work=ABC News |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2022-02-21/marnus-labuschagne-prepares-for-australian-pakistan-tour/100849676 |access-date=21 March 2022}} Labuschagne is a '''Michael Gordon Bracewell''' (born 14 February 1991) is a New Zealand [[cricket]]er who plays for [[Wellington cricket team|Wellington]]. He is the nephew of former [[Test cricket|Test]] players [[Brendon Bracewell|Brendon]] and [[John Bracewell]], and the cousin of current international player [[Doug Bracewell]] and comedian [[Melanie Bracewell]]. He attended [[Kavanagh College]] in [[Dunedin]]. He made his international debut for the [[New Zealand national cricket team|New Zealand cricket team]] in March 2022.<ref name="Cricinfo">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/326968.html |title=Michael Bracewell |access-date=30 October 2015 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref>

==Career==
In June 2018, he was awarded a contract with [[Wellington cricket team|Wellington]] for the 2018–19 season.<ref name="con1819">{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/23797021/central-districts-drop-jesse-ryder-contracts-list |title=Central Districts drop Jesse Ryder from contracts list |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=15 June 2018}}</ref> In March 2020, in round six of the [[2019–20 Plunket Shield season]], Bracewell took his maiden [[five-wicket haul]] in first-class cricket.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nzc.nz/match-reports/scorching-firebirds-on-the-up|title=Scorching Firebirds on the up |work=NZ Cricket |access-date=13 March 2020}}</ref>

In June 2020, he was offered a contract by Wellington ahead of the 2020–21 domestic cricket season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/29312525/daryl-mitchell,-jeet-raval-finn-allen-major-domestic-moves |title=Daryl Mitchell, Jeet Raval and Finn Allen among major domestic movers in New Zealand |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=15 June 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/cricket/121831138/auckland-lose-jeet-raval-to-northern-districts-finn-allen-to-wellington-in-domestic-contracts |title=Auckland lose Jeet Raval to Northern Districts, Finn Allen to Wellington in domestic contracts |work=Stuff |access-date=15 June 2020}}</ref> On 8 January 2022, in the [[2021–22 Super Smash (men's cricket)|2021–22 Super Smash]] tournament, Bracewell scored 141 [[not out]] for the Wellington Firebirds against the [[Central Districts cricket team|Central Stags]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/sport/cricket-one-of-the-greatest-t20-knocks-michael-bracewell-smashes-record-books/HBARCXELUQAIY7PZHQAKNJX4CM/ |title=Cricket: 'One of the greatest T20 knocks' - Michael Bracewell smashes record books |work=New Zealand Herald |access-date=8 January 2022}}</ref> It was the highest score in a [[Twenty20]] cricket match in New Zealand.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/cricket/127442027/super-smash-michael-bracewell-smokes-record-score-in-amazing-firebirds-win |title=Super Smash: Michael Bracewell smokes record score in amazing Firebirds win |work=Stuff |access-date=8 January 2022}}</ref>

In March 2022, Bracewell was named in New Zealand's [[One Day International]] (ODI) and [[Twenty20 International]] (T20I) squads for their home series [[Dutch cricket team in New Zealand in 2021–22|against the Netherlands]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/nz-vs-netherlands-2022-michael-bracewell-dane-cleaver-earn-maiden-new-zealand-call-ups-1305746 |title=Michael Bracewell, Dane Cleaver earn maiden New Zealand call-ups for Netherlands series |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=15 March 2022}}</ref> He made his ODI debut on 29 March 2022, for New Zealand against the [[Netherlands national cricket team|Netherlands]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1288987.html |title=1st ODI (D/N), Mount Maunganui, Mar 29 2022, Netherlands tour of New Zealand |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=29 March 2022}}</ref> In May 2022, Bracewell was named in New Zealand's [[Test cricket|Test]] squad for their [[New Zealand cricket team in England in 2022|tour of England]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/eng-vs-nz-2022-michael-bracewell-earns-new-zealand-test-call-up-for-england-tour-kane-williamson-nears-return-1313291 |title=Bracewell earns NZ Test call-up for England tour, Williamson nears return |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=3 May 2022}}</ref> He made his Test debut on 10 June 2022, for New Zealand against [[England cricket team|England]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1276902.html |title=2nd Test, Nottingham, June 10 - 14, 2022, New Zealand tour of England |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=10 June 2022}}</ref>

In July 2022, in the first match of the series [[New Zealand cricket team in Ireland in 2022|against Ireland]], Bracewell scored his first century in ODI cricket.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/new-zealand-in-ireland-2022-1307472/ireland-vs-new-zealand-1st-odi-1303309/match-report |title=Michael Bracewell's 127* helps New Zealand snatch Ireland's dream |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=10 July 2022}}</ref> Bracewell made his T20I debut on 18 July 2022, for New Zealand against [[Ireland cricket team|Ireland]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1303312.html |title=1st T20I, Belfast, July 18, 2022, New Zealand tour of Ireland |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=18 July 2022}}</ref> Two days later, in the next match of the series against Ireland, Bracewell took his first [[List of Twenty20 International cricket hat-tricks|hat-trick in T20I cricket]] in the first over he bowled in an international match.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/cricket/129325729/dane-cleaver-makes-impact-with-bat-as-new-zealand-secure-t20-series-win-over-ireland |title=Dane Cleaver makes impact with bat as New Zealand secure T20 series win over Ireland |work=Stuff |access-date=20 July 2022}}</ref>

In January 2023, Bracewell scored third fastest century for New Zealand in ODI cricket while batting in the first match of the series [[New Zealand cricket team in India in 2022–23|against India]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=19 January 2023 |title=Michael Bracewell Equals MS Dhoni's Rare Feat After Scoring A Century Against India |url=https://www.probatsman.com/ind-vs-nz-michael-bracewell-equals-ms-dhonis-rare-feat-after-scoring-a-century-against-india |access-date=19 January 2023 |website=ProBatsman}}</ref> He also equalled MS Dhoni record of being the only batter to score more than one century while batting at number seven or below.<ref name=":0" />

For [[IPL 2023]], he was signed as a replacement for injured [[Will Jacks]] in the [[Royal Challengers Bangalore]] team.

In May 2024, he was named in New Zealand’s squad for the [[2024 ICC Men's T20 World Cup]] tournament.<ref>{{Cite web |title=New Zealand Squad for ICC Men’s World Cup 2024 |url=https://www.scorewaves.com/news-details/new-zealand-squad-icc-mens-world-up-2024-new-zealand-jersey |access-date=2024-06-10 |website=ScoreWaves |language=en}}</ref>

In February 2025, he was named in New Zealand's squad for the [[2025 Champions Trophy]] in Pakistan.

'''Mohammad Nawaz'''{{efn|[[Urdu]], [[Pashto]]: {{Nastaliq|محمد نواز}}}} ({{IPA|ur|mʊɦəmməd nəwaːz|pron}}; born 21 March 1994) is a Pakistani international [[cricket]]er. In August 2018, he was one of 33 players to be awarded a central contract for the 2018–19 season by the [[Pakistan Cricket Board]] (PCB).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pcb.com.pk/press-release-detail/pcb-central-contracts-2018-19.html |title=PCB Central Contracts 2018–19 |work=Pakistan Cricket Board |date=10 January 2014 |access-date=6 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/24301169/new-central-contracts-guarantee-earnings-boost-pakistan-players |title=New central contracts guarantee earnings boost for Pakistan players |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=6 August 2018}}</ref>

==Early life and family==
Nawaz was born in [[Rawalpindi]], Punjab to a [[Pashtuns|Pashtun]] family, belonging to [[Akbarpura]], a village in [[Nowshera District|Nowshera district]] of [[Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]]. He received his early education from the F.G. Boys School in Rawalpindi.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/cricketers/mohammad-nawaz-348148 | title=Mohammad Nawaz Profile - Cricket Player Pakistan | Stats, Records, Video }}</ref> He is fluent in [[English language|English]], [[Urdu]], [[Pashto]] and [[Punjabi language|Punjabi]].

In 2018, he married Izdihaar, a [[South African people|South African]] diagnostic [[radiographer]] of [[Saudis|Saudi Arabian]] descent.<ref>{{Cite web |last=G. |first=Sandip |date=4 September 2022 |title=Mohammad Nawaz trying to make a name for himself and Pakistan's tribe of left-arm spinners |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/sports/cricket/mohammad-nawaz-trying-to-make-a-name-for-himself-and-pakistans-tribe-of-left-arm-spinners-8129147/ |access-date=5 October 2022 |website=[[Indian Express]] |quote=“Woh Pathan hain, usme dum hain,” references too [...] a boy from Rawalpindi [...] he married a diagnostic radiographer Izdihaar who lives in South Africa of Saudi Arabia descent [...]}}</ref>

==Domestic and T20 franchise career==
Nawaz has played domestic cricket for several regional and departmental teams in Pakistan, including Rawalpindi, National Bank of Pakistan, [[Northern cricket team|Northern]] and [[Baluchistan cricket team|Baluchistan]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Mohammad Nawaz profile - Cricket Player Pakistan |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/cricketers/mohammad-nawaz-348148 |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref> In April 2018 he was named vice-captain of Baluchistan's squad for the [[2018 Pakistan Cup]] and finished the tournament as Baluchistan's leading wicket-taker (nine wickets in four matches).<ref>{{cite web |title=Pakistan Cup one-day tournament to begin in Faisalabad |url=https://www.geo.tv/latest/191967-pakistan-cup-one-day-tournament-to-begin-in-faisalabad |work=Geo TV |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Pakistan Cup 2018, Balochistan: Batting and bowling averages |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/averages/bowling_by_team.html?id=12333;team=852;type=tournament |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref>

In March 2019 he was named in the Federal Areas squad for the [[2019 Pakistan Cup]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Federal Areas aim to complete hat-trick of Pakistan Cup titles |url=https://www.pcb.com.pk/press-release-detail/federal-areas-aim-to-complete-hat-trick-of-pakistan-cup-titles.html |work=Pakistan Cricket Board |date=10 January 2014 |access-date=25 March 2019}}</ref> In January 2021, Nawaz was appointed captain of [[Northern cricket team|Northern]] for the [[2020–21 Pakistan Cup]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Pakistan Cup One-Day Tournament promises action-packed cricket |url=https://www.pcb.com.pk/press-release-detail/pakistan-cup-one-day-tournament-promises-action-packed-cricket.html |website=www.pcb.com.pk |date=10 January 2014}}</ref>

=== Pakistan Super League ===
Nawaz was signed by [[Quetta Gladiators]] for the inaugural [[2016 Pakistan Super League]]. He made an immediate impact in the tournament opener against [[Islamabad United]], taking 4 for 13 and earning the player-of-the-match award.<ref>{{cite web |title=IU v QG, Pakistan Super League 2015/16 – full scorecard |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/pakistan-super-league-2015-16-923069/islamabad-united-vs-quetta-gladiators-1st-match-959175/full-scorecard |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref> He finished the 2016 PSL as one of the tournament's leading wicket-takers (13 wickets) and was retained by Quetta for the 2017 season, where he took 10 wickets in 10 matches as Quetta reached the final.<ref>{{cite web |title=Pakistan Super League, 2015/16 - Most wickets |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/pakistan-super-league-2015-16-923069/stats |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Nerveless Nawaz puts Quetta in PSL final |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/psl-2016-17-1075974/peshawar-zalmi-vs-quetta-gladiators-1st-qualifying-final-1076006/match-report |work=ESPNcricinfo |date=5 March 2017 |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref>

Ahead of the [[2023 Pakistan Super League players draft|2023 PSL Draft]] Nawaz was released by Quetta and later signed by [[Karachi Kings]] as a wild‐card pick.<ref>{{cite web |title=Pakistan Super League squads & drafts 2023 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/pakistan-super-league-2022-23-1332128/series-squads |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref>

=== Other franchise leagues ===
* Balkh Legends ([[Afghanistan Premier League]]): named in the Balkh squad for the inaugural 2018 Afghanistan Premier League.<ref>{{cite web |title=Gayle, Afridi, Russell: icons in Afghanistan Premier League |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/24639625/chris-gayle,-shahid-afridi,-andre-russell-icons-afghanistan-premier-league |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref>  
* [[Edmonton Royals]] (Global T20 Canada): selected for the [[2019 Global T20 Canada]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Global T20 draft streamed live |url=http://www.canadacricket.com/?p=12755 |work=Canada Cricket Online |date=20 June 2019 |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Global T20 Canada 2019 squads |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/global-t20-canada-2019-1203611/squads |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref>  
* [[Cape Town Blitz]] ([[Mzansi Super League]]): named in Cape Town Blitz's squad for the 2019 Mzansi Super League.<ref>{{cite web |title=Cape Town Blitz squad, Mzansi Super League 2019 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/mzansi-super-league-2019-20-1196979/cape-town-blitz-squad-1206004/series-squads |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref>  
* [[Rajshahi Royals]] ([[Bangladesh Premier League]]): signed by Rajshahi Royals for the 2019–20 BPL and played a role in the team's run to the BPL final.<ref>{{cite web |title=Rajshahi Royals squad, BPL 2019/20 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/bpl-2020-2019-20-1207676/rajshahi-royals-squad-1209578/series-squads |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Mohammad Nawaz and Andre Russell fire Rajshahi Royals to BPL title (match report) |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/bpl-2020-2019-20-1207676/khulna-tigers-vs-rajshahi-royals-final-1208112/match-report |work=ESPNcricinfo |date=17 January 2020 |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref>

==International career==
He made his [[Twenty20 International]] debut for Pakistan against the United Arab Emirates in the [[2016 Asia Cup]] on 29 February 2016.<ref name="T20I">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/966755.html |title=Asia Cup, 6th Match: Pakistan v United Arab Emirates at Dhaka, Feb 29, 2016 |access-date=29 February 2016 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref> He was hit for 38 runs from 3 overs after being called to bowl by captain [[Shahid Afridi]]. [[Waqar Younis]], the head coach, criticised Afridi for this and said that it was 'unfair' for him to call Nawaz up being relatively new and that it 'destroyed the youngster's confidence'.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/35928883|title=Waqar Younis blames Shahid Afridi for World Twenty20 exit|work=BBC Sport |date=30 March 2016 |access-date=1 April 2016}}</ref>

He made his [[One Day International]] debut for Pakistan against [[Ireland national cricket team|Ireland]] on 18 August 2016, scoring a half-century.<ref name="ODI">{{cite news |title=Pakistan tour of England and Ireland, 1st ODI: Ireland v Pakistan at Dublin (Malahide), Aug 18, 2016 |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/913649.html |work=ESPNcricinfo |publisher=ESPN Sports Media |date=18 August 2016 |access-date=18 August 2016 }}</ref> In September 2016, he was named man of the match in the final of the [[2016–17 National T20 Cup]].<ref name="MOTM">{{cite news |title=National T20 Cup, Final: Karachi Blues v Karachi Whites at Multan, Sep 16, 2016 |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1047817.html |work=ESPNcricinfo |publisher=ESPN Sports Media |date=16 September 2016 |access-date=16 September 2016 }}</ref>

He made his [[Test cricket|Test]] debut for Pakistan [[West Indian cricket team against Pakistan in the UAE in 2016–17|against the West Indies]] in [[Dubai]] on 13 October 2016.<ref name="Test">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1050229.html |title=West Indies tour of United Arab Emirates, 1st Test: Pakistan v West Indies at Dubai (DSC), Oct 13-17, 2016 |access-date=13 October 2015 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref>

In June 2020, he was named as one of four reserve players for Pakistan's [[Pakistani cricket team in England in 2020|tour to England]] during the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/29300707/haider-ali-new-face-pakistan-name-29-man-touring-party-england |title=Haider Ali the new face as Pakistan name 29-man squad for England Tests and T20Is |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=12 June 2020}}</ref> In September 2021, he was named in Pakistan's squad for the [[2021 ICC Men's T20 World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/asif-ali-khusdil-shah-included-in-pakistan-t20-wc-squad-sharjeel-khan-left-out-1276467| title=Sharjeel Khan dropped from T20 World Cup squad; Asif Ali, Khushdil Shah make 15-man cut |work= ESPN Cricinfo |access-date= 6 September 2021}}</ref>

In July 2022, in the first match [[Pakistani cricket team in Sri Lanka in 2022|against Sri Lanka]], he took his first [[five-wicket haul]] in Test cricket.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/pakistan-tour-in-sri-lanka-2022-1320948/sri-lanka-vs-pakistan-1st-test-1320953/match-report-3 |title=Fifties from Oshada Fernando, Kusal Mendis and Dinesh Chandimal put Sri Lanka in command |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=18 July 2022}}</ref>

In September 2022, he was instrumental in a record win against India during the [[2022 Asia Cup|Asia Cup]], being Pakistan's highest successful run-chase against India in a T20I,<ref>{{Cite web |date=4 September 2022 |title=Rizwan, Nawaz set up Pakistan's record win over India |url=https://apnews.com/article/sports-pakistan-asia-india-dubai-295d20230a191c5e85892bd0b6aaa42e |website=[[AP News]]}}</ref> eventually named [[Player of the Match awards (cricket)|Player of the Match]] for his all-round contributions.

In September 2025, in the match against Afghanistan in [[2025 United Arab Emirates T20I Tri-Nation Series|UAE T20I Tri-series]], he took his first [[five-wicket haul]] in T20I cricket, which also included a [[Hat-trick (cricket)|hat-trick]], bowling out Afghanistan for 66, their second-lowest ever T20I total. Nawaz had previously contributed a 21-ball 25 with the bat in a low-scoring game. For his all-round performance he was adjudged [[Player of the Match awards (cricket)|Player of the Match]] as well [[Player of the Series awards (cricket)|Player of the Series]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=7 September 2025 |title=Nawaz hat-trick helps Pakistan down Afghanistan in tri-series final |url=https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20250907-nawaz-hat-trick-helps-pakistan-down-afghanistan-in-tri-series-final |website=[[France24]]}}</ref>

In February 2026, in the third and final T20I of [[Australian cricket team in Pakistan in 2025–26|Australia's 2025-26 tour of Pakistan]] in Lahore, Pakistan completed a 3–0 series whitewash with a dominant 111-run victory over Australia, Australia's worst-ever T20I loss. Nawaz was named Player of the Match, delivering a career-best T20I bowling performance with figures of 5 for 18, spinning a major collapse in the Australian batting lineup and playing a pivotal role in Pakistan's triumph.<ref>{{cite web|last=Lavalette|first=Tristan|title=Ayub, Shadab and Nawaz lead Pakistan to 3-0 sweep|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/australia-in-pakistan-2025-26-1519629/pakistan-vs-australia-3rd-t20i-1519638/match-report|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN|date=1 February 2026|access-date=1 February 2026}}</ref> That series was effectively a warm up for both teams for the [[2026 Men's T20 World Cup|T20 World Cup]]. After a match against the [[Netherlands national cricket team|Netherlands]] on the 7th of February in that tournament, Nawaz tested positive for [[11-Nor-9-carboxy-THC|Carboxy-THC]] in a post-match doping test.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cricinfo.com/story/mohammad-nawaz-under-pcb-investigation-after-positive-test-for-recreational-drug-use-1533083|title=Nawaz under investigation after positive test for recreational drug use|publisher=[[Cricinfo]]|date=22 April 2026}}</ref> It was announced in July that Nawaz had received a three-month suspension, which by then he had already voluntarily provisionally served.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/pakistan-spinner-sanctioned-for-breaching-icc-anti-doping-code|title=Pakistan spinner sanctioned for breaching ICC Anti-Doping Code|publisher=[[International Cricket Council]]|date=17 July 2026}}</ref>

'''Mohammad Rizwan''' ({{langx|ur|محمد رضوان}}, {{IPA|ur|mʊɦəmməd rɪzwɑːn|pron}}; born 1 June 1992) is a Pakistani international [[cricket]]er and a maulana. He is a right-handed [[batsman|batter]] and [[wicket-keeper]]. He captains [[Pakistan Super League]] franchise [[Rawalpindiz]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Muhammad Rizwan appointed vice-captain of T20 team |url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/latest/1145842-muhammad-rizwan-appointed-vice-captain-of-t20-team |access-date=2024-01-08 |website=www.thenews.com.pk |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Mohammad Rizwan profile|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/player/mohammad-rizwan-323389 |access-date=2022-04-10 |website=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref><ref name="icc-cricket.com">{{Cite web |date=2022-08-30 |title=ICC Men's T20I Player Batting Rankings |url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/rankings/mens/player-rankings/t20i/batting |access-date=2022-09-05 |website=ICC|language=en-US}}</ref> and the [[Khyber Pakhtunkhwa cricket team|Khyber Pakhtunkhwa team]] in domestic cricket.<ref name="riz">{{cite web |title=Sarfaraz Ahmed and Babar Azam to take charge of Pakistan domestic teams |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/sarfaraz-ahmed-and-babar-azam-to-take-charge-of-pakistan-domestic-sides-1199464 |access-date=8 September 2020 |work=ESPNCricinfo}}</ref> He has previously been the [[Captain (cricket)|captain]] of the [[Pakistan national cricket team|Pakistan team]] in [[One Day International|ODIs]] and [[Vice Captain (cricket)|vice-captain]] in [[Test cricket]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-06-30 |title='Never been desperate for captaincy': Pakistan Test vice-captain Mohammad Rizwan |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cricket/never-been-desperate-for-captaincy-pakistan-test-vice-captain-mohammad-rizwan-101625047568520.html |access-date=2022-04-10 |website=Hindustan Times |language=en}}</ref> and [[T20I]]s.<ref>{{cite news |title=Mohammad Rizwan named Pakistan T20I vice-captain |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/mohammad-rizwan-appointed-pakistan-t20i-vice-captain-1416038 |work=ESPNcricinfo |date=9 Jan 2024}}</ref> 
He played for [[Lahore Qalandars]] in the PSL from 2016 to 2017, for [[Karachi Kings]] from 2018 to 2020, and captained [[Multan Sultans]] from 2021 till 2025. He also led the Multan Sultans to victory in the [[2021 Pakistan Super League]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-06-25 |title=Multan Sultans win maiden PSL title, beat Peshawar Zalmi in final |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/sports/cricket/multan-sultans-win-maiden-psl-title-beat-peshawar-zalmi-in-final-7374941/ |access-date=2022-04-10 |website=The Indian Express |language=en}}</ref>

In 2021, he was named the [[ICC Men's T20I Cricketer of the Year]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=All the winners of the 2021 ICC Awards announced |url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/2462323 |access-date=2022-04-10 |website=www.icc-cricket.com |language=en}}</ref> and was also among the [[Wisden Cricketers of the Year]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-04-14 |title=Darren Stevens Named Among Five Wisden Cricketers Of The Year In 2021 |url=https://www.wisden.com/wisden-cricketers-almanack/wisden-almanack-cricketers-of-the-year-2021 |access-date=4 April 2025 |website=Wisden |language=en-GB}}</ref>

He has scored [[century (cricket)|centuries]] in [[List of cricketers with centuries in all international formats|all three formats]]: [[Test cricket|Tests]], [[One Day International|ODI]] and [[Twenty20 International|T20I]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Mohammad Rizwan becomes first-ever Pakistani wicket-keeper to score 100 in T20I |url=https://www.geo.tv/latest/334531-mohammad-rizwan |work=www.geo.tv |date=February 11, 2021 |language=en}}</ref> He holds the record for most runs in T20 Internationals in a calendar year with 1326 runs in 26 innings at an average of 73.66.<ref name="stats.espncricinfo.com">{{Cite web |title=Most runs in a calendar year|url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/records/284247.html |access-date=2022-06-05 |website=Cricinfo}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-08-29 |title=From Mohammad Rizwan to KL Rahul: Know the batters with the highest averages in T20 internationals |url=https://www.sportsadda.com/cricket/features/highest-average-t20-internationals |access-date=2022-09-05 |website=SportsAdda|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="icc-cricket.com" /> Rizwan is the only player to score 2000 runs in a calendar year in T20s.<ref>{{Cite web |title=PAK vs WI: Mohammad Rizwan Becomes 1st Batter to Score 2,000 T20 Runs in a Calendar Year |url=https://www.news18.com/cricketnext/news/pak-vs-wi-mohammad-rizwan-becomes-1st-batter-to-score-2000-t20-runs-in-a-calendar-year-4562951.html |access-date=2022-04-10 |website=www.news18.com |language=en}}</ref>

== Early career ==
Rizwan was born on 1 June 1992 in [[Peshawar]] to Akhter Parvez into a [[Pashtuns|Pashtun]] family of six siblings, with Rizwan being the second of three brothers. He began his cricket career with [[Tape ball cricket|tape ball]] before joining clubs such as the [[Islamia College University|Islamia College]] and later the Shama Club, eventually playing for Peshawar Under-19 in 2007.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Samiuddin |first=Osman |date=22 May 2021 |title=Mohammad Rizwan: 'The pain of letting through four byes will never go' |url=https://www.wisden.com/wisden-cricketers-almanack/mohammad-rizwan-the-pain-of-letting-through-four-byes-will-never-go |access-date=4 April 2025 |website=[[Wisden]]}}</ref>

==Domestic career==

=== Pakistan ===
Making his first-class debut with [[Peshawar cricket team|Peshawar]] during the 2008–09 season, Rizwan hit five 50s, including four [[not out|unbeaten]], in his first seven innings. His good form, both with the bat and behind the wickets, attracted the attention of [[Basit Ali]], the coach of [[Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Limited cricket team|Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Limited]], who recruited him to his team for the 2011–12 season.<ref name=":0" />

Playing for Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Limited in the final of the [[Quaid-e-Azam Trophy]] in 2014–15, Rizwan scored 224 to help Sui Northern to a 301-run first-innings lead and their second title.<ref>[https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/707/707189.html National Bank of Pakistan v Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Limited 2014–15]</ref> He kept wicket for [[Pakistan A cricket team|Pakistan A]] in the five limited-overs matches against [[Kenya cricket team|Kenya]] in December 2014.<ref>[https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Events/24/Kenya_in_Pakistan_2014-15.html Kenya in Pakistan 2014–15]</ref>

In April 2018, he was named the vice-captain of [[Punjab cricket team (Pakistan)|Punjab]]'s squad for the [[2018 Pakistan Cup]].<ref name="squads1">{{cite web|url=https://www.geo.tv/latest/191967-pakistan-cup-one-day-tournament-to-begin-in-faisalabad |title=Pakistan Cup one-day tournament to begin in Faisalabad next week |access-date=21 April 2018 |work=Geo TV}}</ref><ref name="squads2">{{cite web|url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/print/306831-pakistan-cup-cricket-from-25th |title=Pakistan Cup Cricket from 25th |access-date=21 April 2018 |work=The News International}}</ref> On 1 May 2018, he scored his highest total in List A cricket, with 140 off 123 balls against [[Federal Areas cricket team|Federal Areas]].<ref name="Rizwan140">{{cite web|url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/print/311614-pakistan-cricket-cup-kamran-hammers-170-off-96-balls |title=Pakistan Cricket Cup: Kamran hammers 170 off 96 balls |work=The News International |access-date=2 May 2018}}</ref> In March 2019, he was named as the captain of [[Federal Areas cricket team|Federal Areas]] squad for the [[2019 Pakistan Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pcb.com.pk/press-release-detail/federal-areas-aim-to-complete-hat-trick-of-pakistan-cup-titles.html |title=Federal Areas aim to complete hat-trick of Pakistan Cup titles |work=Pakistan Cricket Board |date=10 January 2014 |access-date=25 March 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/print/447913-pakistan-cup-one-day-cricket-from-april-2 |title=Pakistan Cup one-day cricket from April 2 |access-date=25 March 2019 |work=The International News}}</ref>

In September 2019, Rizwan was named as the captain of [[Khyber Pakhtunkhwa cricket team|Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]] for the [[2019–20 Quaid-e-Azam Trophy]] tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pcb.com.pk/press-release-detail/pcb-announces-squads-for-2019-20-domestic-season.html |title=PCB announces squads for 2019-20 domestic season |work=Pakistan Cricket Board |date=10 January 2014 |access-date=4 September 2019}}</ref><ref name="riz"/> In October 2019, he was named the player of the tournament in the [[2019–20 National T20 Cup]], for scoring 215 runs and taking six wickets.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pcb.com.pk/press-release-detail/northern-beat-balochistan-to-be-crowned-national-t20-cup-champions.html |title=Northern beat Balochistan to be crowned National T20 Cup champions |work=Pakistan Cricket Board |date=10 January 2014 |access-date=25 October 2019}}</ref>

He was retained by [[Khyber Pakhtunkhwa cricket team|Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]] for the 2020–21 domestic season, both as player and captain of the team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pcb.com.pk/press-release-detail/six-cricket-association-squads-confirmed.html |title=Six Cricket Association squads confirmed |work=Pakistan Cricket Board |date=10 January 2014 |access-date=28 August 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.geosuper.tv/latest/6359-pcb-reveals-squads-for-national-t20-cup|title=PCB reveals squads for National T20 Cup|work=Geo Super|access-date=9 September 2020}}</ref>

Rizwan started his PSL career with [[Lahore Qalandars]] in the inaugural [[2016 Pakistan Super League|2016 season]]. His two-year stint with the team proved underwhelming as Qalandars failed to qualify for the playoffs in both seasons, while Rizwan managed only 233 runs in 16 matches.

He represented [[Karachi Kings]] from the [[2018 Pakistan Super League|2018]] to the [[2020 Pakistan Super League|2020 season]]. Despite becoming Pakistan's first-choice wicket-keeper batter in international cricket, Rizwan struggled to secure a consistent place in the Kings' top order and was often deployed lower down the batting lineup.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rizwan bitter at being left out by captain Imad |url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/print/630166-rizwan-bitter-at-being-left-out-by-captain-imad |access-date=2 July 2023 |website=The News}}</ref>

Rizwan's breakthrough came in the [[2021 Pakistan Super League|2021 season]] when he was appointed captain of the [[Multan Sultans]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mohammad Rizwan replaces Shan Masood as Multan Sultans captain for PSL 2021 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/psl-2021-mohammad-rizwan-replaces-shan-masood-as-multan-sultans-captain-1251823 |access-date=2 July 2023 |website=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> Under his leadership, Multan Sultans won their maiden PSL title in 2021 and finished as runners-up in the following two seasons.<ref>{{Cite web |title=HBL PSL8 Qualifier: Same characters, new story |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/2406226/hbl-psl8-qualifier-same-characters-new-story |access-date=2 July 2023 |website=The Express Tribune |date=15 March 2023}}</ref>

Individually, Rizwan has cemented his place among PSL's elite performers, amassing 2,735 runs in 82 matches with a highest score of 110.<ref>{{cite web |title=Mohammad Rizwan PSL Stats |url=https://www.cricmetric.com/sage/?q=Mohammad+Rizwan+PSL+stats |website=Cricmetric |access-date=15 October 2025}}</ref> He has recorded [[List of Pakistan Super League centuries|two centuries]] in the league 110* in 2023<ref>{{Cite web |date=22 February 2023 |title=Mohammad Rizwan blasts first PSL century for Multan against Karachi |url=https://www.thenationalnews.com/sport/cricket/2023/02/22/mohammad-rizwan-blasts-first-psl-century-for-multan-against-karachi/ |website=The National |access-date=2 July 2023}}</ref> and 105* in 2025 and 20 half-centuries.<ref>{{cite web |title=Mohammad Rizwan PSL Stats |url=https://advancecricket.com/player/mohammad-rizwan-psl-stats/8070 |website=Advance Cricket |access-date=15 October 2025}}</ref> In the [[2025 Pakistan Super League|2025 season]], he scored 367 runs in 10 innings at an average of 52.43, including his second PSL century.<ref>{{cite web |title=PSL 2025 Batting Averages |url=https://www.pcb.com.pk/averages-reports.php?action=batting_averages&match_type_id=8&sort_by=total_runs&sort_order=desc&tournament_id=1404 |website=Pakistan Cricket Board |access-date=15 October 2025}}</ref>

=== Other leagues ===

* [[Sylhet Strikers]] ([[Bangladesh Premier League]]): Rizwan played off and on for the [[Sylhet Strikers]] in the [[Bangladesh Premier League]] between the [[2017 Bangladesh Premier League|2017]] and [[2022 Bangladesh Premier League|2022]] seasons.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mohammad Rizwan's consistent run continues in BPL |url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/latest/1019820-mohammad-rizwan-s-consistent-run-continues-in-bpl |website=The News International |date=14 February 2022 |access-date=15 October 2025}}</ref>
* [[Comilla Victorians]] (Bangladesh Premier League): Rizwan represented Comilla Victorians during the [[2023 Bangladesh Premier League|2023]] and [[2024 Bangladesh Premier League|2024]] seasons. He scored 351 runs in ten matches in the 2023 season at an average of over 50, helping Comilla qualify for the playoffs.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mohammad Rizwan retained by Comilla Victorians for BPL 2024 |url=https://www.geosuper.tv/latest/28014-mohammad-rizwan-retained-by-bpl-team-comilla-victorians |website=Geo Super |access-date=15 October 2025}}</ref> In one of the league matches, he struck an unbeaten 73 off 39 balls against Khulna Tigers, guiding his team to victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Watch: Mohammad Rizwan's storming knock helps Comilla Victorians chase down mammoth target in BPL 2023 |url=https://crickettimes.com/2023/02/watch-mohammad-rizwans-storming-knock-helps-comilla-victorians-chase-down-a-mammoth-target-in-bpl-2023/ |website=Cricket Times |date=12 February 2023 |access-date=15 October 2025}}</ref>
* [[St Kitts and Nevis Patriots]] ([[Caribbean Premier League]]): Rizwan joined St Kitts and Nevis Patriots for the [[2025 Caribbean Premier League|2025 CPL season]] as a replacement for Fazalhaq Farooqi.<ref>{{Cite web |title=CPL 2025: Mohammad Rizwan signs for St Kitts and Nevis Patriots for remainder of season |url=https://www.espn.in/cricket/story/_/id/46030446/cpl-2025-mohammad-rizwan-signs-st-kitts-nevis-patriots-remainder-season |website=ESPNcricinfo |date=3 September 2025 |access-date=15 October 2025}}</ref> He made an immediate impact with a match-winning 85 off 62 balls against Guyana Amazon Warriors, earning the Player of the Match award.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mohammad Rizwan stars as Patriots edge past Warriors in CPL 2025 thriller |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2025/9/5/mohammad-rizwan-stars-as-patriots-edge-past-warriors-in-cpl-2025 |website=Al Jazeera |date=5 September 2025 |access-date=15 October 2025}}</ref>
* [[Melbourne Renegades]] ([[Big Bash League]]): In June 2025, Rizwan was selected with the fourth overall pick by Melbourne Renegades in the draft for the [[2025–26 Big Bash League season|2025–26 season]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-06-19 |title=Renegades land world class keeper-batter Muhammad Rizwan {{!}} Melbourne Renegades |url=https://www.melbournerenegades.com.au/news/4290319/muhammad-rizwan-drafted |access-date=2025-06-23 |website=www.melbournerenegades.com.au |language=en}}</ref>

==International career==
Rizwan made his [[One Day International]] (ODI) debut for Pakistan [[Pakistani cricket team in Bangladesh in 2014–15|against Bangladesh]] in April 2015, scoring 67 runs off 58 balls.<ref name="ODI">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/858485.html |title=Pakistan tour of Bangladesh, 1st ODI: Bangladesh v Pakistan at Dhaka, Apr 17, 2015 |access-date=17 April 2015 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref> He made his [[Twenty20 International]] debut for Pakistan in the same series.<ref name="T20I">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/858491.html |title=Pakistan tour of Bangladesh, Only T20I: Bangladesh v Pakistan at Dhaka, Apr 24, 2015 |access-date=24 April 2015 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref> He made his [[Test cricket|Test]] debut for Pakistan [[Pakistani cricket team in New Zealand in 2016–17|against New Zealand]] on 25 November 2016.<ref name="Test">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1019995.html |title=Pakistan tour of New Zealand, 2nd Test: New Zealand v Pakistan at Hamilton, Nov 25–29, 2016 |access-date=26 November 2016 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref> He was out for a [[Duck (cricket)|golden duck]] in his maiden Test innings.<ref name="duck1">{{cite web |title=A rare slump for Younis Khan |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/a-rare-slump-for-younis-khan-1068899 |access-date=26 November 2016 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref>

In August 2018 he was one of the 33 players awarded a central contract for the 2018–19 season by the [[Pakistan Cricket Board]] (PCB).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pcb.com.pk/press-release-detail/pcb-central-contracts-2018-19.html |title=PCB Central Contracts 2018–19 |work=Pakistan Cricket Board |date=10 January 2014 |access-date=6 August 2018}}</ref><ref name="ESPN Cricinfo">{{cite web |title=New central contracts guarantee earnings boost for Pakistan players |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/new-central-contracts-guarantee-earnings-boost-for-pakistan-players-1154598 |access-date=6 August 2018 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref> He captained Pakistan's team in the [[2018 ACC Emerging Teams Asia Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pcb.com.pk/press-release-detail/pakistan-squad-announced-for-emerging-asia-cup-2018-to-co-host-by-pakistan-and-sri-lanka.html |title=Pakistan squad announced for Emerging Asia Cup 2018 to Co-Host by Pakistan and Sri Lanka |work=Pakistan Cricket Board |date=10 January 2014 |access-date=3 December 2018}}</ref> Pakistan reached the semi-finals.<ref>{{cite web |title=Asian Cricket Council Emerging Teams Cup 2018 |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/_/id/17914/season/2018/asian-cricket-council-emerging-teams-cup |website=Cricinfo |access-date=4 February 2019}}</ref> He scored his maiden century against [[Australian cricket team against Pakistan in the UAE in 2018–19|Australia]], in March 2019, with an innings of 115 runs.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://au.news.yahoo.com/ton-rizwan-guides-pakistan-284-7-second-odi-144156812--spt.html |title=Ton-up Rizwan guides Pakistan to 284-7 in second ODI |work=Yahoo News |date=24 March 2019 |access-date=24 March 2019}}</ref>

In November 2019, Rizwan was recalled to the Pakistan team [[Sri Lankan cricket team in Pakistan in 2019–20|against Sri Lanka]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Pakistan recall Iftikhar, Rizwan and Nawaz for Sri Lanka ODIs |url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/1351308 |website=Icc |access-date=21 Sep 2019}}</ref> He was also selected [[Pakistani cricket team in Australia in 2019–20|against Australia]] later that month, where in the first innings of the First Test it was debated as to whether he was given out on a [[no ball]],<ref>{{cite web |title='That's the wrong call': Legends question no-ball decision |url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/no-ball-pat-cummins-mohammad-rizwan-third-umpire-decision-australia-pakistan-first-test/2019-11-21 |website=Cricket.com.au}}</ref> he scored 95 runs in the second innings.<ref>{{cite web |title=1st Test, ICC World Test Championship at Brisbane, Nov 21-24 2019 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/19430/scorecard/1183530/australia-vs-pakistan-1st-test-icc-world-test-championship-2019-2021 |website=Cricinfo |access-date=26 November 2019}}</ref>

[[File:Mohammad Rizwan.png|thumb|Rizwan in 2020.]]
In June 2020, he was named in a 29-man squad for Pakistan's [[Pakistani cricket team in England in 2020|tour to England]] during the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Sarfaraz Ahmed returns, Haider Ali the new face in 29-man Pakistan squad for England Tests and T20Is |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/sarfaraz-ahmed-returns-haider-ali-the-new-face-in-29-man-pakistan-squad-for-england-tests-and-t20is-1224948 |access-date=12 June 2020 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pcb.com.pk/press-release-detail/haider-ali-named-in-29-player-squad-for-england-tour.html |title= Haider Ali named in 29-player squad for England tour |access-date=23 June 2020 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref> In July, he was shortlisted in Pakistan's 20-man squad for the Test matches against England.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pcb.com.pk/press-release-detail/pakistan-shortlist-players-for-england-tests.html |title= Pakistan shortlist players for England Tests |work=Pakistan Cricket Board |date= 10 had an excellent Test series, both with the bat and gloves, managing to score 161 runs with two-half centuries, therefore, cementing his place as first choice wicket-keeper in Test matches, above the returning former captain [[Sarfaraz Ahmed]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Most runs / 2020 / England v Pakistan / Test series|url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/batting/most_runs_career.html?id=13284;type=series|publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=8 September 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite
