In December 2020, Rizwan was named as the captain of Pakistan's Test team for the first match [[Pakistani cricket team in New Zealand in 2020–21|against New Zealand]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/nz-vs-pak-2020-21-babar-azam-imam-ul-haq-ruled-out-of-first-test-mohammad-rizwan-named-captain-1244816 |title=Babar Azam, Imam-ul-Haq ruled out of first Test; Mohammad Rizwan named captain |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=21 December 2020}}</ref> He replaced [[Babar Azam]], who was ruled out due to injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pcb.com.pk/press-release-detail/imran-butt-named-in-17-player-test-squad.html |title=Imran Butt named in 17-player Test squad |work=Pakistan Cricket Board |date=10 January 2014 |access-date=21 December 2020}}</ref> In the same tour, he was also added to Pakistan's T20I squad against New Zealand.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Singh|first=Anirudh|title=Pakistan announces squad for the upcoming T20I series against New Zealand|url=https://crickettimes.com/2020/12/pakistan-announces-squad-for-the-upcoming-t20i-series-against-new-zealand/|access-date=2020-12-22|website=CricketTimes.com|date=6 December 2020 |language=en-US}}</ref> In the 3rd T20I of the series against [[New Zealand]], Rizwan scored his career-best T20I score of 89 to give Pakistan a win and saved them from getting white-washed by New Zealand.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Rachit|date=2020-12-22|title=NZ vs Pak 3rd T20: Mohammad Rizwan helps Pakistan beat New Zealand by 4 wickets|url=https://www.insidesport.co/nz-vs-pak-3rd-t20-mohammad-rizwan-helps-pakistan-beat-new-zealand-by-4-wickets/|access-date=2020-12-22|website=InsideSport|language=en-gb}}</ref>

In February 2021, in Pakistan's series [[South African cricket team in Pakistan in 2020–21|against South Africa]], Rizwan scored his first century in Test cricket, with an unbeaten 115 as he was awarded the player of the series.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.geosuper.tv/latest/7853-rizwan-yasir-extend-pakistan-lead-after-hasan-fell-early |title=Rizwan's heroics help Pakistan put up a 370-run target in the second Test |work=Geo Super |access-date=7 February 2021}}</ref> In February 2021, in Pakistan's series [[South African cricket team in Pakistan in 2020–21|against South Africa]], Rizwan scored his first century in T20I cricket, with an unbeaten 104 including 6 boundaries and 7 sixes.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Full Scorecard of Pakistan vs South Africa 1st T20I 2020/21 - Score Report {{!}} ESPNcricinfo.com|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/south-africa-in-pakistan-2020-21-1242968/pakistan-vs-south-africa-1st-t20i-1243019/full-scorecard|access-date=2021-06-01|website=ESPNcricinfo|language=en}}</ref> He also became the first wicket-keeper batter for Pakistan to score a century in T20I cricket and became only the second [[wicket-keeper]] batter after [[Brendon McCullum]] to score centuries in all three formats of international cricket.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mohammad Rizwan – first Pakistani wicket-keeper to score T20I hundred|url=https://www.geosuper.tv/latest/7891-mohammad-rizwan-first-pakistani-wicket-keeper-to-score-t20i-hundred|access-date=2021-06-01|website=www.geosuper.tv|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-02-11|title=Pakistan's Mohammad Rizwan hits record-breaking T20I ton against South Africa|url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cricket/pakistans-mohammad-rizwan-hits-record-breaking-t20i-ton-against-south-africa-101613057563037.html|access-date=2021-06-01|website=Hindustan Times|language=en}}</ref> He also became only the second Pakistani batter to score a century in T20I cricket after [[Ahmed Shehzad]] and also became the fifth designated wicket-keeper batter to notch a T20I century.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-02-12|title=Muhammad Rizwan: First wicket-keeper batsman to score century across all formats|url=https://nation.com.pk/12-Feb-2021/muhamamd-rizwan-first-pakistani-wicket-keeper-batsman-to-score-century-across-all-formats|access-date=2021-06-01|website=The Nation|language=en}}</ref>

In April 2021, during the [[Pakistani cricket team in South Africa in 2020–21|third T20I between Pakistan and South Africa]] he along with Babar Azam had a 197-run partnership for the opening wicket which is also the [[List of Pakistan Twenty20 International cricket records#Highest partnerships by runs|highest partnership recorded by a pair for Pakistan for any wicket in T20I cricket]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Exceptional Babar secures record win for Pakistan|url=https://supersport.com/cricket/south-africa-v-pakistan-202021/news/210414_Exceptional_Babar_secures_record_win_for_Pakistan|access-date=2021-06-01|website=supersport.com|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Heinrich Klaasen: Babar Azam and Mohammad Rizwan 'made a lot of good balls look bad'|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/sa-vs-pak-3rd-t20i-heinrich-klaasen-babar-azam-mohammad-rizwan-made-a-lot-of-good-balls-look-bad-1259030|access-date=2021-06-01|website=ESPNcricinfo|language=en}}</ref> It was also the highest ever partnership for any wicket by a pair in T20I cricket while chasing.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-04-14|title=Babar Azam and Mohammad Rizwan smash record knocks against South Africa|url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/latest/820112-babar-azam-and-mohammad-rizwan-hit-record-knocks-against-south-africa|access-date=2021-06-01|website=The News International|language=en}}</ref>

In September 2021, he was named in Pakistan's squad for the [[2021 ICC Men's T20 World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/asif-ali-khusdil-shah-included-in-pakistan-t20-wc-squad-sharjeel-khan-left-out-1276467| title=Sharjeel Khan dropped from T20 World Cup squad; Asif Ali, Khushdil Shah make 15-man cut |work= ESPN Cricinfo |access-date= 6 September 2021}}</ref> In December 2021, in the third match [[West Indian cricket team in Pakistan in 2021–22|against the West Indies]], Rizwan became the first batter to score 2,000 runs in [[Twenty20]] cricket in a calendar year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aninews.in/news/sports/cricket/rizwan-becomes-first-batter-to-score-2000-t20-runs-in-single-calendar-year20211216221818/ |title=Rizwan becomes first batter to score 2,000 T20 runs in single calendar year |work=ANI News |access-date=16 December 2021}}</ref> In September 2022, Rizwan and Babar scored a record T20 cricket partnership of 203 without being dismissed.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Abdullah |first1=Mohammad |title=Most T20 Runs for Pakistan in Cricket History |url=https://cricket-newz.com/most-t20-runs-for-pakistan-in-cricket-history/ |website=Cricket News |access-date=24 December 2022 |date=24 December 2022}}</ref>

In October 2023, Rizwan scored an unbeaten century against [[Sri Lanka national cricket team|Sri Lanka]], leading Pakistan to successfully chase a mammoth total of 345 in the [[2023 Cricket World Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-10-10 |title=Pakistan vs Sri Lanka, World Cup 2023 Highlights: Mohammad Rizwan and Abdullah Shafique score tons as Pakistan defeat Sri Lanka by 6 wickets |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/sports/cricket/pakistan-vs-sri-lanka-live-score-world-cup-2023-8th-match-pak-vs-sl-scorecard-updates-hyderabad-8975471/ |access-date=2023-10-15 |website=The Indian Express |language=en}}</ref>

In December 2023 and January 2024, Rizwan participated in Pakistan's tour of Australia. For the first match, he was sidelined for [[Sarfaraz Ahmed]]. After a poor showing by Sarfaraz, he was bought back into the team. In the second match's first innings, he scored 42 off 51, and then a 35 off 62 in the second innings. In the third match's first innings, he scored 88 off 103, and then a 28 off 57 in the second innings. The innings also had a FC against Victoria XI. He made 50 off 70 before [[Retire hurt|retiring hurt]].

In May 2024, he participated in Pakistan's tour of Ireland. In the first match, he scored just 1 run before being run out.<ref>{{Cite web |title=IRE vs PAK Cricket Scorecard, 1st T20I at Dublin, May 10, 2024 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/ireland-vs-pakistan-2024-1426828/ireland-vs-pakistan-1st-t20i-1426830/full-scorecard |access-date=2024-06-29 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref> However, he redeemed himself by scoring 75 off 46, not out in the second match.<ref>{{Cite web |title=IRE vs PAK Cricket Scorecard, 2nd T20I at Dublin, May 12, 2024 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/ireland-vs-pakistan-2024-1426828/ireland-vs-pakistan-2nd-t20i-1426831/full-scorecard |access-date=2024-06-29 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref> In the third and final match, he scored 58 off 38.<ref>{{Cite web |title=IRE vs PAK Cricket Scorecard, 3rd T20I at Dublin, May 14, 2024 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/ireland-vs-pakistan-2024-1426828/ireland-vs-pakistan-3rd-t20i-1426832/full-scorecard |access-date=2024-06-29 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref>

In May 2024, he participated in Pakistan's tour of England. The first match was washed out.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ENG v PAK {{!}} 2024 Pakistan tour of England {{!}} Live Score, Schedule, News |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/pakistan-in-england-2024-1385666 |access-date=2024-06-29 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref> In the second match, he was caught out on just the 3rd ball of the innings.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ENG vs PAK Cricket Scorecard, 2nd T20I at Birmingham, May 25, 2024 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/pakistan-in-england-2024-1385666/england-vs-pakistan-2nd-t20i-1385688/full-scorecard |access-date=2024-06-29 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref> The third match was also washed out. In the fourth and final match, he was bowled after scoring 23 runs off 16 balls.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ENG vs PAK Cricket Scorecard, 4th T20I at London, May 30, 2024 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/pakistan-in-england-2024-1385666/england-vs-pakistan-4th-t20i-1385690/full-scorecard |access-date=2024-06-29 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref>

In May 2024, he was named in Pakistan's squad for the [[2024 ICC Men's T20 World Cup]] tournament.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pakistan Squad for ICC Men's T20I World Cup 2024 |url=https://www.scorewaves.com/news-details/pakistan-squad-for-t20-world-cup |access-date=2024-06-11 |website=ScoreWaves |language=en}}</ref> In Pakistan's first match of the tournament, against the [[United States national cricket team|United States]], he scored only 9 runs off 8 balls before being seen off by [[Saurabh Netravalkar]]. In that same game, he took the catches of [[Steven Taylor (American cricketer)|Steven Taylor]] and [[Monank Patel]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=USA vs PAK Cricket Scorecard, 11th Match, Group A at Dallas, June 06, 2024 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/icc-men-s-t20-world-cup-2024-1411166/united-states-of-america-vs-pakistan-11th-match-group-a-1415711/full-scorecard |access-date=2024-06-29 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref> In Pakistan's second match of the tournament, against [[India national cricket team|India]], he scored a crucial 31 runs off 44 balls, before being bowled by [[Jasprit Bumrah]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=IND vs PAK Cricket Scorecard, 19th Match, Group A at New York, June 09, 2024 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/icc-men-s-t20-world-cup-2024-1411166/india-vs-pakistan-19th-match-group-a-1415719/full-scorecard |access-date=2024-06-29 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref> In Pakistan's third match of the tournament against [[Canada national cricket team|Canada]], he scored a match winning knock of 53 off 53, not out.<ref>{{Cite web |title=CAN vs PAK Cricket Scorecard, 22nd Match, Group A at New York, June 11, 2024 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/icc-men-s-t20-world-cup-2024-1411166/canada-vs-pakistan-22nd-match-group-a-1415722/full-scorecard |access-date=2024-06-29 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref> In Pakistan's fourth and last match of the tournament against [[Ireland cricket team|Ireland]], he scored 17 runs off 16 balls.<ref>{{Cite web |title=IRE vs PAK Cricket Scorecard, 36th Match, Group A at Lauderhill, June 16, 2024 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/icc-men-s-t20-world-cup-2024-1411166/ireland-vs-pakistan-36th-match-group-a-1415736/full-scorecard |access-date=2024-06-29 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref> Overall, in the tournament, he scored 110 runs, the 33rd most out of every participant.

In August 2024, he scored 171 not out and 51, top-scoring in each innings, in the First Test against Bangladesh at [[Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium|Rawalpindi cricket stadium]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Pakistan vs Bangladesh, 1st Test at Rawalpindi, Aug 21 2024 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/bangladesh-in-pakistan-2024-1442203/pakistan-vs-bangladesh-1st-test-1442213/full-scorecard |website=Cricinfo |access-date=27 August 2024}}</ref>

In October 2024, the [[Pakistan Cricket Board]] announced Rizwan as [[Captain (cricket)|captain]] of the [[Pakistan national cricket team]] for the white-ball format of [[One Day International]]s and [[Twenty20]]s.<ref>{{cite news |title=PCB announces Mohammad Rizwan as captain for white-ball cricket |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1867976/pcb-announces-mohammad-rizwan-as-captain-for-white-ball-cricket |work=DAWN |date=27 October 2024 |language=en}}</ref>

In November 2024, during the second ODI [[Pakistani cricket team in Australia in 2024–25|against Australia]], Rizwan took six catches to equal the record for the most catches in a single ODI match.<ref>{{cite news |title=PAK vs AUS: Mohammad Rizwan ties record for most catches in a single ODI match |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/2508322/mohammad-rizwan-equals-record-for-most-catches-in-single-odi |work=The Express Tribune |date=8 November 2024 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Pak vs Aus: Haris Rauf, Saim Ayub star as Green Shirts thrash hosts by 9 wickets in 2nd ODI, level series 1-1 |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1870977/pak-vs-aus-haris-rauf-saim-ayub-star-as-green-shirts-thrash-hosts-by-9-wickets-in-2nd-odi-level-series-1-1 |work=DAWN |date=8 November 2024 |language=en}}</ref>

'''Muhammad Waseem''' (born 12 February 1996) is a Pakistani-born [[cricket]]er who plays for the [[United Arab Emirates national cricket team]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/1241277.html |title=Muhammad Waseem |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=5 October 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/abu-dhabi-t10-league-waseem-muhammad-uae-cricket-next-big-thing-1250097 |title=Waseem Muhammad: UAE cricket's next big thing? |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=5 October 2021}}</ref> He is also the current captain of the [[Twenty20 International|T20I]] side of the UAE and the highest ranked batter of the nation in [[ICC T20 Ranking]].

==Personal life==
Waseem was born in Pakistan,<ref name=class>{{cite news|url=https://www.thenationalnews.com/sport/cricket/mohammed-wasim-shows-uae-selectors-his-class-after-leading-fujairah-to-successive-wins-in-dream-11-emirates-d20-1.1127384|title=Mohammed Wasim shows UAE selectors his class after leading Fujairah to successive wins in Dream 11 Emirates D20|publisher=The National|date=13 December 2020|accessdate=3 February 2022|first=Paul|last=Radley}}</ref> growing up in the Punjab's city of [[Mian Channu]]. His nickname is Babba.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.thenationalnews.com/sport/cricket/psl-2021-mohammed-wasim-hopes-to-make-uae-proud-after-call-up-to-multan-sultans-squad-1.1227477|title=PSL 2021: Mohammed Wasim hopes to 'make UAE proud' after call-up to Multan Sultans squad|publisher=The National|date=23 May 2021|accessdate=3 February 2022|first=Paul|last=Radley}}</ref> He qualified to play for the UAE in April 2021 by meeting the ICC's three-year residency requirement.<ref name=class/>

==Franchise career==
On 3 February 2021, in the 2021 T10 League, Waseem equalled the record for the fastest fifty in a [[T10 cricket]] match, doing so in 12 balls.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.indiatvnews.com/sports/cricket/t10-league-waseem-muhammad-fastest-t10-half-century-equal-chris-gayle-mohammad-shahzad-682620 |title=Watch: UAE'S Waseem Muhammad slams 7 sixes in 13 balls to equal Gayle, Shahzad for fastest T10 fifty |work=India TV News |access-date=5 October 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/news/abu-dhabi-t10-waseem-muhammads-half-century-helps-northern-warriors-thrash-pune-devils/articleshow/80682266.cms |title=Abu Dhabi T10: Waseem Muhammad's half-century helps Northern Warriors thrash Pune Devils |work=Times of India |access-date=5 October 2021}}</ref> In May 2021, he was called into the [[Multan Sultans]] squad as a replacement player for the [[2021 Pakistan Super League]].<ref name=sultans>{{cite news|url=https://www.thenationalnews.com/sport/cricket/psl-2021-mohammed-wasim-hopes-to-make-uae-proud-after-call-up-to-multan-sultans-squad-1.1227477|title=PSL 2021: Mohammed Wasim hopes to 'make UAE proud' after call-up to Multan Sultans squad|publisher=The National|date=23 May 2021|accessdate=3 February 2022|first=Paul|last=Radley}}</ref> In September 2023, he was picked by the [[Chattogram Challengers]] following the [[2024 Bangladesh Premier League players' draft|players' draft]] to play for them in the [[2024 Bangladesh Premier League]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-09-24 |title=BPL 2024: Updated squads of all 7 teams |url=https://www.tbsnews.net/sports/bpl-2024-updated-squads-all-7-teams-706294 |access-date=2024-01-05 |website=The Business Standard |language=en}}</ref>

==International career==
In October 2021, Waseem was named in the UAE's [[Twenty20 International]] (T20I) squad for the [[2021 Summer T20 Bash]] tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sportsunfold.com/united-arab-emirates-vs-namibia-1st-t20i-match-details-prediction-team-squad-pitch-report-weather-report2101014/ |title=United Arab Emirates vs Namibia, 1st T20I Match Details, Prediction, Team Squad |work=Sports Unfold |access-date=4 October 2021}}</ref> He made his T20I debut on 5 October 2021, for the UAE against [[Namibia national cricket team|Namibia]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1280057.html |title=Only T20I, ICCA Dubai, Oct 5 2021, Namibia tour of United Arab Emirates |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=5 October 2021}}</ref> Five days later, in the UAE's match against [[Ireland cricket team|Ireland]], Waseem scored his first century in T20I cricket, with 107 [[not out]] from 62 balls.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thenationalnews.com/sport/cricket/2021/10/10/mohammed-waseem-announces-arrival-as-uae-complete-turnaround-against-ireland/ |title=Mohammed Waseem announces arrival as UAE complete turnaround against Ireland |work=The National |access-date=10 October 2021}}</ref>

In November 2021, he was named in the UAE's [[One Day International]] (ODI) squad for the [[2021 Namibia Tri-Nation Series]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.emiratescricket.com/whatsnew/Emirates%20Cricket%20Board%20announce%20team%20to%20compete%20in%20ICC%20Men's%20Cricket%20World%20Cup%20League%202%20in%20Namibia |title=Emirates Cricket Board announce team to compete in ICC Men's Cricket World Cup League 2 in Namibia |work=Emirates Cricket Board |access-date=23 November 2021}}</ref> In February 2022, he was also named in the UAE's ODI squad for their series [[Emirati cricket team in Oman in 2021–22|against Oman]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.emiratescricket.com/whatsnew/ECB%20announce%20teams%20that%20will%20represent%20the%20UAE%20ahead%20of%20intense%203-series%20campaign%20in%20Oman |title=ECB Announce teams that will represent the UAE ahead of intense 3-series campaign in Oman |work=Emirates Cricket Board |access-date=2 February 2022}}</ref> He made his ODI debut on 5 February 2022 against [[Oman national cricket team|Oman]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1299586.html |title=57th Match, Al Amerat, Feb 5 2022, ICC Men's Cricket World Cup League 2 |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=5 February 2022}}</ref>

Waseem was appointed captain of the UAE in March 2023, replacing [[CP Rizwan]] for the final match of the [[2023 United Arab Emirates Tri-Nation Series]]. His first full series was the [[2023 Nepal Tri-Nation Series (round 21)|Nepal Tri-Nation Series]] which was UAE's final series of the [[2019–2023 ICC Cricket World Cup League 2]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.thenationalnews.com/sport/cricket/2023/03/07/muhammad-waseem-retained-as-uae-captain-but-cp-rizwan-keeps-place-in-squad-for-nepal-tour/|title=Muhammad Waseem takes over UAE captaincy ahead of clash with Nepal|newspaper=The National|location=Abu Dhabi|date=6 March 2023|access-date=6 March 2023|first=Paul|last=Radley}}</ref> Waseem scored his maiden ODI century against [[Papua New Guinea national cricket team|Papua New Guinea]] in the Nepal series, scoring 119 from 76 balls including twelve sixes. His century came from 61 balls and set a new UAE record for the fastest ODI century,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.thenationalnews.com/sport/cricket/2023/03/15/uaes-muhammad-waseem-warms-up-for-epic-finale-against-nepal-with-record-breaking-blitz/|title=UAE's Muhammad Waseem warms up for epic finale against Nepal with record-breaking blitz|newspaper=The National|location=Abu Dhabi|date=15 March 2023|access-date=6 March 2023|first=Paul|last=Radley}}</ref> but was surpassed the following day by [[Asif Khan (Pakistani cricketer)|Asif Khan]]'s 41-ball century.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/3111861 |title=Asif Khan slams fourth fastest hundred in Men's ODIs |work=International Cricket Council|access-date=16 March 2023}}</ref>

In January 2026, Waseem was named as the captain of UAE's squad for the [[2026 ICC Men's T20 World Cup|2026 T20 World Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://emiratescricket.com/news-detail/og5m6QnXe0LGexrLjlyq|title=ICC Men’s T20 World Cup 2026 – Muhammad Waseem to lead UAE's 15-member squad|work=[[International Cricket Council]]|date=30 January 2026|access-date=2 February 2026}}</ref>

web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/1158088.html |title=Naseem Shah |access-date=1 September 2018 |work=[[ESPNcricinfo]]}}{{Cite [[Pakistan national cricket team|Pakistan cricket team]] for their [[Test cricket|Test]] series against [[Australia national cricket team|Australia]].{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/story/1206978.html |title=Naseem Shah finds inner strength to bounce back from personal tragedy |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=19 November 2019|date=19 November 2019 }} He made his international debut for Pakistan in November 2019 against Australia, becoming the ninth-youngest player to make his debut in Test cricket.{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/50486740 |title=Australia v Pakistan: Naseem Shah, 16, to make Test debut |newspaper=BBC Sport |access-date=21 November 2019|date=20 November 2019 }} In December 2019, in the second Test match against [[Sri Lanka national cricket team|Sri Lanka]], he became the second youngest bowler to take a [[five-wicket haul]] in a Test match, and also the youngest [[Pace bowling|pace bowler]] to do so.{{cite web|url=https://www.thecricketmonthly.com/story/1224850/20-cricketers-for-the-2020s |title=20 cricketers for the 2020s |work=The Cricketer Monthly |access-date=6 July 2020}} In February 2020, in the first Test against [[Bangladesh national cricket team|Bangladesh]], he became the youngest bowler to [[List of Test cricket hat-tricks|take a hat-trick in a Test match]].{{cite web|url=https://www.france24.com/en/20200209-pakistan-s-naseem-shah-becomes-youngest-to-take-test-hat-trick |title=Pakistan's Naseem Shah becomes youngest to take Test hat trick |work=France24 |access-date=9 February 2020}}{{cite web|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/1751967 |title=Celebrating up and coming cricketers this International Youth Day |work=International Cricket Council |access-date=12 August 2020}} ==Early and personal life== Naseem hails from [[Mayar, Lower Dir|Mayar Jandool]], a town in the [[Lower Dir District|Lower Dir district]] of [[Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]] province, Pakistan and was born into a [[Pashtuns|Pashtun]] family. He is fluent in [[Pashto]] and [[Urdu]].{{cite web |title=Family over the moon after Nasim Shah's inclusion in Test sq... {{!}} MENAFN.COM |url=https://menafn.com/1099179710/Family-over-the-moon-after-Nasim-Shahs-inclusion-in-Test-squad |access-date= |website=menafn.com}}{{Cite web |date=25 November 2019 |title=Naseem Shah |url=https://www.pakpedia.pk/naseem-shah/ |access-date= }}{{Cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wN4ya84k11M|title=Rising U19 star Naseem Shah When talent meets resilience | PCB|via=www.youtube.com}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/video/clip/_/id/28078452|title=From Lower Dir to top tier, the Naseem Shah story | ESPNcricinfo.com|date=14 November 2019|website=ESPNcricinfo}} His father, Abbas Shah, was against his decision to play cricket, preferring him to concentrate on his studies. Naseem eventually completed his education to the [[tenth grade]] following which his father wanted him to seek employment abroad.{{Cite web |date=11 September 2022 |title=Shocking revelation about Naseem Shah! |url=https://dailytimes.com.pk/995707/shocking-revelation-about-naseem-shah/ |access-date=2 September 2023 |website=Daily Times |quote=He said that Naseem had completed his education to the tenth grade and that he had wished for him to seek employment abroad.}} His mother died in 2019, just a day before his Test debut at the age of 16.{{Cite web |date=11 September 2022 |title='He thinks of her and cries a lot. He was traded to [[Islamabad United]] before the [[2024 Pakistan Super League|2024 season]].{{Cite web |title=Naseem Shah set to move to Islamabad United from Quetta Gladiators |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/psl-2024-naseem-shah-set-to-move-to-islamabad-united-from-quetta-gladiators-1411328 |access-date=2023-12-03 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}} On 11 Feb 2026, the Rawalpindi franchise signed him for PKR 8.65 crore, making him the most expensive player in the first-ever [[Pakistan Super League]] auction.{{Cite web|url=https://www.khelwire.com/articles/psl-2026-auction-here-is-what-happened|title=PSL 2026 auction: Here is what happened!|website=KhelWire|date=11 February 2026|access-date=12 February 2026}} === Other leagues === On 15 September 2021, Naseem Shah took the crucial two wickets in the final of the [[2021 Caribbean Premier League]] (CPL), which helped [[st Kitts and Nevis Patriots]] register their first CPL title. In January 2022, he was signed by [[Gloucestershire County Cricket Club]] to play in domestic tournaments during the first half of the 2022 season in England.{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/naseem-shah-joins-gloucestershire-for-county-championship-and-t20-blast-1296381 |title=Naseem Shah joins Gloucestershire for County Championship and T20 Warner described Naseem as an exceptional talent capable of replicating the impact [[Mohammad Amir]] had early in his career.{{cite web |author=Daniel Brettig |date=22 November 2019 |title=Warner likens Naseem to a young Mohammad Amir |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/warner-likens-naseem-to-a-young-mohammad-amir-1207325 |access-date=27 November 2025 |website=ESPNcricinfo |location=Brisbane}} In December 2019, he was named in Pakistan's Test squad for the two-match series [[Sri Lankan cricket team in Pakistan in 2019–20|against Sri Lanka]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/28242407/fawad-alam-returns-pakistan-test-squad-sri-lanka-series |title=Fawad Alam returns to Pakistan's Test squad for Sri Lanka series |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=7 December 2019}} In the second match, he took his first [[five-wicket haul]] in Test cricket.{{cite web|url=https://www.news.com.au/sport/cricket/naseem-shah-becomes-youngest-pace-bowler-to-claim-fivewickethaul-in-test-cricket-history/news-story/85e91bca7fd38d0fd667d5ed2ba11310 |title=Naseem Shah becomes youngest pace bowler to claim five-wicket-haul in Test cricket history |work=News Australia |access-date=23 December 2019}} At the age of 16 years and 307 days, he became the youngest [[Pace bowling|fast bowler]], and the second-youngest among all bowlers,{{cite web|title=Naseem Shah takes five as Pakistan clinch series |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/19430/report/1206636/day/5/pakistan-vs-sri-lanka-2nd-test-icc-world-test-championship |work=ESPNcricinfo |quote=... Shah named in men's central contract list for 2020-21 |work=Pakistan Cricket Board |access-date=13 May 2020}} In June 2020, he was named in a 29-man squad for Pakistan's [[Pakistani cricket team in England in 2020|tour to England]] during the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/29300707/haider-ali-new-face-pakistan-name-29-man-touring-party-england |title=Haider Ali the new face as Pakistan name 29-man touring party for England |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=12 June 2020}}{{cite web |url=https://www.pcb.com.pk/press-release-detail/haider-ali-named-in-29-player-squad-for-england-tour.html |title=Haider Ali named in 29-player squad for England tour |work=Pakistan Cricket Board |access-date=12 June 2020 |archive-date=12 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200612071011/https://www.pcb.com.pk/press-release-detail/haider-ali-named-in-29-player-squad-for-england-tour.html |url-status=dead }} In July, he was shortlisted for Pakistan's 20-man squad for the Test matches against England.{{cite web|url=https://www.pcb.com.pk/press-release-detail/pakistan-shortlist-players-for-england-tests.html |title= Pakistan shortlist players for England Tests |work=Pakistan Cricket Board |access-date=27 July 2020}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/29548095/wahab-riaz,-sarfaraz-ahmed-20-man-pakistan-squad-england-tests |title=Wahab Riaz, Sarfaraz Ahmed in 20-man Pakistan squad for England Tests |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=27 July 2020}} On 21 August, he was named in Pakistan's [[Twenty20 International]] (T20I) squad, also for the series against England.{{cite web|url=https://www.pcb.com.pk/press-release-detail/pakistan-shortlist-17-players-for-england-t20is.html |title=Pakistan shortlist 17 players for England T20Is |work=Pakistan Cricket Board |access-date=21 August 2020}} In November 2020, he was named in Pakistan's 35-man squad for their [[Pakistani cricket team in New Zealand in 2020–21|tour to New Zealand]].{{cite web|url=https://www.pcb.com.pk/press-release-detail/pakistan-name-35-player-squad-for-new-zealand.html |title=Pakistan name 35-player squad for New Zealand |work=Pakistan Cricket Board |access-date=11 November 2020}} In October 2021, he was named in the [[Pakistan A cricket team|Pakistan Shaheens]] squad for their tour of Sri Lanka.{{cite web|url=https://www.pcb.com.pk/press-release-detail/pakistan-shaheens-for-sri-lanka-tour-named.html |title=Pakistan Shaheens for Sri Lanka tour named |work=Pakistan Cricket Board |access-date=2 October 2021}} In August 2022, he was named in Pakistan's ODI squad, for their [[Pakistani cricket team in the Netherlands in 2022|tour of the Netherlands]].{{cite web|url=https://www.pcb.com.pk/press-release-detail/pakistan-name-squads-for-netherlands-odis-and-t20-asia-cup.html |title=Pakistan name squads for Netherlands ODIs and T20 Asia Cup |work=Pakistan Cricket Board |access-date=3 August 2022}} He made his ODI debut on 16 August 2022, for Pakistan, against the [[Netherlands national cricket team|Netherlands]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1311737.html |title=1st ODI, Rotterdam, August 16, 2022, Pakistan tour of Netherlands |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=16 August 2022}} During the last ODI, Naseem took his maiden wicket in ODIs.{{cite web |title=Naseem's fifer helps Pakistan overcome spirited Dutch fight {{!}} Cricbuzz.com |url=https://www.cricbuzz.com/cricket-news/123546/naseems-fifer-helps-pakistan-overcome-spirited-dutch-fight-cricbuzzcom |access-date=10 January 2023 |website=Cricbuzz }} Later the same month, he was named in Pakistan's T20I squad for the [[2022 Asia Cup]].{{cite web|url=https://www.pcb.com.pk/press-release-detail/pakistan-name-squads-for-netherlands-odis-and-t20-asia-cup.html |title=Pakistan name squads for Netherlands ODIs and T20 Asia Cup| work=Pakistan Cricket Board |access-date=3 August 2022}} He made his T20I debut on 28 August 2022, against [[India national cricket team|India]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1327270.html |title=2nd Match, Group A (N), Dubai (DSC), August 28, 2022, Asia Cup |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=28 August 2022}} On 7 September 2022, Naseem Shah made history by delivering 2 [[Six (cricket)|sixes]] against [[Afghanistan national cricket team|Afghanistan]] to save [[Pakistan national cricket team|Pakistan]] from a defeat and help qualify for the finals.{{Cite web |title=Full Scorecard of Afghanistan vs Pakistan 10th Match, Super Four 2022 - Score Report {{!}} ESPNcricinfo.com |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/asia-cup-2022-1327237/afghanistan-vs-pakistan-10th-match-super-four-1327278/full-scorecard |access-date=10 January 2023 |website=ESPNcricinfo}} In September T20I Tri-Series Squad: Full Team Lists For NZ, BAN & PAK For 2022 Tri-Series |url=https://www.wisden.com/cricket-news/new-zealand-t20i-tri-series-squad-full-team-lists-for-nz-ban-pak-for-2022-tri-series |access-date=4 April 2025 |website=Wisden}} Later in October, Naseem was named in Pakistan's T20I squad for the [[2022 Men's T20 World Cup|2022 ICC Men's T20 World Cup]].{{cite web |title=All the squads for ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2022 |url=https://www.t20worldcup.com/news/2773147 |access-date=10 January 2023 |website=www.t20worldcup.com |archive-date=5 June 2023 Men's T20 World Cup final|2022 ICC Men's T20 World Cup Final]], but lost it.{{Cite web |date=2022-11-13 |title=Pak vs Eng: Fans dismayed as Naseem Shah gives runs with no gain |url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/latest/1009545-pak-vs-eng-fans-dismayed-as-naseem-shah-gives-runs-with-no-gain |access-date=2025-10-30 |website=www.thenews.com.pk}} In November 2022, he was named in }}{{cite web |date=13 December 2022 |title=Injured Naseem Shah ruled out of 3rd test against England |url=https://apnews.com/article/sports-pakistan-england-cricket-f2f003dd35b41460557ab7b5942e1a62 |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2023/9/22/pakistan-name-icc-cricket-world-cup-squad-injured-pacer-naseem-shah-out |access-date=1 November 2023 |website=Al Jazeera }} In May 2024, he was named in Pakistan's squad for the [[2024 Men's T20 World Cup|2024 ICC Men's T20 World Cup]] tournament.{{Cite web |title=Pakistan Squad for ICC Men’s T20I World Cup 2024 |url=https://www.scorewaves.com/news-details/pakistan-squad-for-t20-world-cup |access-date=2024-06-11 |website=ScoreWaves |language=en}} == Playing style == [[File:Naseem Shah bowling action, Sri Lanka vs Pakistan - 2nd TEST Match - SSC, Colombo (cropped).jpg|thumb|Shah during his bowling action]] In February 2020, ''[[ESPNcricinfo]]'' journalist Osman Samiuddin wrote a reflective piece on Naseem Shah's emergence, praising the technical precision of his bowling action. Samiuddin noted that Naseem's mechanics evoked shades of former New Zealand internationals [[Richard Hadlee]] and [[Shane Bond]], highlighting the measured run-up, the compact alignment at the crease, and the assertive follow-through. '''Noor Ahmad Lakanwal''' ({{Langx|ps|نور احمد لکنوال}}) (born 3 January 2005) is an [[Afghans|Afghan]] [[cricket]]er.<ref name="Bio">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/1182529.html |title=Noor Ahmad |access-date=11 October 2019 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He made his international debut for the [[Afghanistan national cricket team|Afghanistan national team]] in June 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thecricketmonthly.com/story/1224850/20-cricketers-for-the-2020s |title=20 cricketers for the 2020s |work=The Cricketer Monthly |access-date=6 July 2020}}</ref>

==Early life==
Noor Ahmad was born on 3 January 2005 as the youngest of eight children. His family hails from Lakan Spinki Bori village in [[Khost Province]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Acharya |first1=Shayan |title=Tracing the journey of Noor Ahmad - Afghanistan cricket's next big thing |url=https://sportstar.thehindu.com/cricket/ipl/ipl-news/noor-ahmad-gujarat-titans-cricket-journey-afghanistan-under-19-team-idol-rashid-khan/article66781371.ece |access-date=23 March 2025 |work=Sportstar |date=26 April 2023 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=At 18, Noor Ahmad is living his cricket dream |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/at-18-noor-ahmad-is-living-his-cricket-dream-1372736 |access-date=23 March 2025 |work=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref>

Noor began pursuing cricket at a local academy at age 12.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/asia-cup-2025-noor-ahmad-is-soaring-both-on-and-off-the-field-1502003|title='Maybe I have something...' - the phenomenal rise of Noor Ahmad |first=Shashank |last=Kishore
|date=September 8, 2025}}</ref>

==Career==
He made his [[first-class cricket|first-class]] debut on 29 April 2019, for [[Kabul Eagles|Kabul Region]] in the [[2019 Ahmad Shah Abdali 4-day Tournament]].<ref name="FC">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1179626.html |title=13th Match, Ahmad Shah Abdali 4-day Tournament at Kabul, Apr 29 - May 2 2019 |access-date=11 October 2019 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He made his [[Twenty20]] debut on 8 October 2019, for [[Mis Ainak Knights]] in the [[2019 Shpageeza Cricket League]].<ref name="T20">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1202452.html |title=2nd Match, Shpageeza Cricket League at Kabul, Oct 8 2019 |access-date=11 October 2019 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

In December 2019, he was named in Afghanistan's squad for the [[2020 Under-19 Cricket World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cricket.af/post/afghanistan-u19-squad-announced-for-icc-u19-world-cup |title=Afghanistan U19 squad announced for ICC U19 World Cup |work=Afghanistan Cricket Board |access-date=8 December 2019 |archive-date=8 December 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191208083124/https://cricket.af/post/afghanistan-u19-squad-announced-for-icc-u19-world-cup |url-status=dead }}</ref> In July 2020, he was named in the [[St Lucia Zouks]] squad for the [[2020 Caribbean Premier League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/29417692/nabi,-lamichhane,-dunk-earn-big-cpl-2020-draft |title=Nabi, Lamichhane, Dunk earn big in CPL 2020 draft |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=6 July 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.windiescricket.com/news/teams-selected-hero-cpl-2020/ |title=Teams Selected for Hero CPL 2020 |work=Cricket West Indies |access-date=6 July 2020}}</ref> He made his [[List A cricket|List A]] debut on 14 October 2020, for [[Mis Ainak Knights|Mis Ainak Region]] in the [[2020 Ghazi Amanullah Khan Regional One Day Tournament]].<ref name="LA">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1234669.html |title=5th Match, Kandahar, Oct 14 2020, Ghazi Amanullah Khan Regional One Day Tournament |access-date=14 October 2020 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

In December 2020, at the age of 15, he was signed by the [[Melbourne Renegades]] to play in the [[2020–21 Big Bash League season]] in Australia.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/55192038 |title=Noor Ahmad: Meet the 15-year-old signed by Melbourne Renegades for the Big Bash League |work=BBC Sport |access-date=11 December 2020}}</ref> In March 2021, [[Chennai Super Kings]] included Noor as a net bowler in their squad for [[2021 Indian Premier League]].<ref>{{Cite news|title=IPL 2021: CSK bring in two Afghanistan players as net bowlers|url=https://crickettimes.com/2021/03/ipl-2021-csk-bring-in-two-aghanistan-players-as-net-bowlers/|website=CricketTimes.com|language=en-US|access-date=30 March 2021}}</ref> In June 2021, Noor also played for the [[Karachi Kings]] in the [[2021 Pakistan Super League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/psl-2020-21-2021-1238103/karachi-kings-vs-lahore-qalandars-27th-match-1247037/match-report |title=16-year-old Noor Ahmad leads Karachi Kings to nail-biting win |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=18 June 2021}}</ref>

In July 2021, Noor was named in Afghanistan's [[One Day International]] (ODI) squad for their series [[Afghan cricket team in Pakistan in 2021–22|against Pakistan]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/fazalhaq-farooqi-noor-ahmad-in-afghanistan-squad-for-their-first-bilateral-odi-series-against-pakistan-1270774 |title=Fazalhaq Farooqi, Noor Ahmad in Afghanistan squad for their first bilateral ODI series against Pakistan |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=23 July 2021}}</ref> In December 2021, he was named in Afghanistan's team for the [[2022 ICC Under-19 Cricket World Cup]] in the West Indies.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://cricket.af/post/suliman-safi-to-lead-afghanistan-at-the-icc-u19-cricket-world-cup-2022 |title=Suliman Safi to lead Afghanistan at the ICC U19 Cricket World Cup |work=Afghanistan Cricket Board |access-date=6 December 2021 |archive-date=6 December 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211206203805/https://cricket.af/post/suliman-safi-to-lead-afghanistan-at-the-icc-u19-cricket-world-cup-2022 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Later in the same month, he was signed by the [[Quetta Gladiators]] following the players' draft in the Supplementary category for the [[2022 Pakistan Super League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pcb.com.pk/press-release-detail/franchises-finalise-squad-for-hbl-psl-2022-.html |title=Franchises finalise squad for HBL PSL 2022 |work=Pakistan Cricket Board |access-date=12 February 2022}}</ref> On 12 February 2022, he made his debut for the team, against [[Islamabad United]] at the [[Gaddafi Stadium]] in [[Lahore]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/pakistan-super-league-2021-22-1292999/islamabad-united-vs-quetta-gladiators-18th-match-1293017/live-cricket-score |title=QG vs IU (N), 18th match, PSL 2022|work=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=12 February 2022}}</ref>

In February 2022, he was bought by the [[Gujarat Titans]] in the [[List of 2022 Indian Premier League personnel changes|auction]] for the [[2022 Indian Premier League]] tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ipl-2022-auction-the-list-of-sold-and-unsold-players-1300689 |title=IPL 2022 auction: The list of sold and unsold players |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=13 February 2022}}</ref>

In November 2024, he was bought by the [[Chennai Super Kings]] in the [[List of 2024 Indian Premier League personnel changes|auction]] for the [[2025 Indian Premier League]] tournament. During his debut on 23 March 2025, he picked 4 wickets for just 18 runs against [[Mumbai Indians]]. He finished as the [[Chennai Super Kings]]'s highest wicket-taker and the second highest in the tournament, with 24 wickets.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.iplt20.com/|title=Home|website=IPL}}</ref>

==International career==

In May 2022, Ahmad was named in Afghanistan's [[Twenty20 International]] (T20I) squad for their series [[Afghan cricket team in Zimbabwe in 2022|against Zimbabwe]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/zim-vs-afg-2022-afghanistan-call-up-zia-ur-rehman-akbar-for-odis-in-zimbabwe-gulbadin-naib-dropped-1316434 |title=Afghanistan call up Zia-ur-Rehman Akbar for ODIs in Zimbabwe; Gulbadin dropped |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=24 May 2022}}</ref> and as a reserve in Afghanistan's [[One Day International]] (ODI) squad for the same tour.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/2633443 |title=Zia-ur-Rehman gets maiden call-up in Afghanistan squad for Zimbabwe ODIs |work=International Cricket Council |access-date=24 May 2022}}</ref> He made his T20I debut on 14 June 2022, against [[Zimbabwe national cricket team|Zimbabwe]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1310948.html |title=3rd T20I, Harare, June 14, 2022, Afghanistan tour of Zimbabwe |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=14 June 2022}}</ref>

Ahmad made his ODI debut on 30 November 2022, against [[Sri Lanka national cricket team|Sri Lanka]]. He also made his [[2023 Cricket World Cup|ODI World Cup]] debut on 23 October 2023, playing against [[Pakistan national cricket team|Pakistan]] in Chennai.<ref>{{Cite web |date=23 October 2023 |title=Who is Noor Ahmad, the Afghanistan Spin Sensation Who Dismissed Babar Azam and Mohammad Rizwan? |url=https://www.probatsman.com/odi-world-cup-2023-who-is-noor-ahmad-the-afghanistan-spin-sensation-who-dismissed-babar-azam-and-mohammad-rizwan |website=Probatsman.com}}</ref> This marked his World Cup debut at the age of 18, making him the youngest debutant in the tournament.

In May 2024, he was named in Afghanistan's squad for the [[2024 ICC Men's T20 World Cup]] tournament.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Afghanistan's squad for the ICC Men's T20I World Cup |url=https://www.scorewaves.com/news-details/afghanistan-squad-icc-mens-t20i-world-cup-2024 |access-date=2024-06-07 |website=ScoreWaves |language=en}}</ref>
