'''Peter Matthew Siddle''' (born 25 November 1984) is an Australian cricketer. He is a specialist right-arm [[fast bowling|fast-medium]] bowler who played mostly for [[Victoria cricket team|Victoria]] in [[first-class cricket|first-class]] and [[List A cricket]], then also spent two seasons at Tasmania. In the [[Big Bash League]], he was a foundation member of the [[Melbourne Stars]], although he never played a game for them. He then had a short stint for cross town rivals the [[Melbourne Renegades]], before a significant stint with the [[Adelaide Strikers]]. Siddle returned to play for the Renegades in the 2023-24 season. Since the 2024-25 BBL, Siddle has been playing with the Stars. He played [[Test cricket]] for [[Australia national cricket team|Australia]] over an eight-year period from 2008 to 2016, before being recalled for the [[Australian cricket team in the United Arab Emirates in 2018–19|Test series against Pakistan]] in 2018. He retired from international cricket in December 2019. Siddle was part of the winning Australia team in the [[2009 ICC Champions Trophy]].

Early in Siddle's career he faced multiple injury setbacks, but was able overcome them in 2009 to be named the [[ICC Men's Emerging Cricketer of the Year|ICC Emerging Player of the Year]]. Though injuries continued to plague him throughout his career, he rose to prominence in the [[2010–11 Ashes series]] when he became the ninth Australian to take a Test [[hat-trick (cricket)|hat-trick]], and the first Australian since [[Shane Warne]] in 1994–95 to do so in an Ashes test. He was also the first player in cricket history to take a hat-trick on his birthday. He remained a regular fixture in Australia's team until his bowling pace started to drop in 2014, with Australia's selectors beginning to focus on younger, faster bowlers.

Siddle became a [[veganism|vegan]] in 2012, subsequently receiving criticism that suggested his diet had a negative effect on his performance, which he disputed. He announced his international retirement on 29 December 2019, effective immediately.{{Citation needed|date=March 2025}}

==Early life and career==
Siddle was born in [[Traralgon]], [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]] and grew up in nearby [[Morwell, Victoria|Morwell]] in the [[Gippsland]] region.<ref name=cricinfoprofile/> Originally a competitive [[woodchopping|woodchopper]], he began playing cricket at the age of 14 for the Latrobe Cricket Club. As a teenager he experienced success, taking 11/47 in a state match at under-17 level. It was in that match that Siddle broke the Victorian state record set by [[John Scholes (cricketer)|John Scholes]].<ref name=cricinfoprofile>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/7898.html|title=Peter Siddle {{!}} Cricket Players and Officials|work=[[ESPNcricinfo]]|access-date=7 January 2018|last=Coverdale|first=Brydon}}</ref><ref name=crunch>{{cite web|url=http://www.smh.com.au/news/sport/cricket/crunch-time-as-axeman-cometh/2008/12/16/1229189622722.html|title=Crunch time as axeman cometh|last=Saltau|first=Chloe|date=17 December 2008|access-date=7 January 2018|work=[[The Sydney Morning Herald]]}}</ref>

In 2003, Siddle attended the [[Australian Cricket Academy]] and made his first-class debut playing for [[Victoria cricket team|Victoria]] against a touring [[West Indies cricket team|West Indian]] team at the [[Melbourne Cricket Ground]] in November 2005.<ref name=cricinfoprofile/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/14740/scorecard/224892/|title=Tour Match, West Indies tour of Australia at Melbourne, Nov 11–13 2005 {{!}} Match Summary|access-date=7 January 2018|work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> In 2006, he attended the academy again and was offered a full contract with the [[Victorian Bushrangers]] for the 2006–07 season. Shoulder injuries began to hamper Siddle, with a shoulder reconstruction sidelining him for most of the 2006–07 season and further problems interrupting the 2007–08 season.<ref name=cricinfoprofile/> Despite his injury problems, he made himself an important part of Victoria's bowling attack, returning figures of 6/57 in an innings against [[South Australia cricket team|South Australia]],<ref name=crunch/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/8043/scorecard/298334/victoria-vs-south-australia--sheff-shield-pura-2007-08/|title=Pura Cup at Melbourne, Jan 21–24 2008 {{!}} Match Summary|access-date=7 January 2018|work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> and taking nine wickets in Victoria's [[2007–08 Pura Cup season|Pura Cup]] final loss to [[New South Wales cricket team|New South Wales]].<ref name=cricket>{{cite web|url=https://www.cricket.com.au/players/peter-siddle/etLzfYVWOU-tHh0yWcDeCA|title=Peter Siddle|access-date=7 January 2018|work=[[Cricket Australia|cricket.com.au]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/8043/scorecard/298345/new-south-wales-vs-victoria-final-sheff-shield-pura-2007-08/|title=Final, Pura Cup at Sydney, Mar 15–19 2008 {{!}} Match Summary|access-date=7 January 2018|work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> Siddle required a second shoulder reconstruction at the end of the season and, despite missing more than half of the season due to shoulder injuries, took 33 wickets at an average of 15.75 to attract attention from national selectors.<ref name=cricinfoprofile/><ref name=crunch/><ref name=symonds>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/indvaus2008/content/story/369466.html|title=Symonds out, McGain in for India|date=12 September 2008|access-date=7 January 2018|work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

== Test career (2008–2019) ==
===Emerging Player of the Year (2008–2009)===
After touring [[India]] with [[Australia A cricket team|Australia A]], Siddle was named in the [[Australia national cricket team|national 15-man squad]] for the [[Australian cricket team in India in 2008–09|four-Test tour of India]] on 12 September 2008, as back up to established bowlers [[Brett Lee]], [[Stuart Clark]] and [[Mitchell Johnson (cricketer)|Mitchell Johnson]].<ref name=symonds/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/indvaus2008/content/story/369501.html|title=Siddle sidles into Test reckoning|date=12 September 2008|access-date=7 January 2018|work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> When Clark injured his elbow prior to the second Test, Siddle was selected in the match squad. He made his Test debut at the [[Punjab Cricket Association Stadium]] in [[Mohali]] on 16 October 2008.<ref name=debut>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/13874/scorecard/345670/india-vs-australia-2nd-test-australia-tour-of-india-2008-09/|title=2nd Test, Australia tour of India at Chandigarh, Oct 17–21 2008 {{!}} Match Summary|work=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=7 January 2018}}</ref> His first ball was a bouncer which hit Indian batsman [[Gautam Gambhir]] in the head,<ref name=cricinfoprofile/><ref name=cricket/> before taking his maiden Test wicket, that of [[Sachin Tendulkar]].<ref name=cricinfoprofile/> He picked up figures of 3/114 in the first innings, and finished the match with figures of 4/176.<ref name=debut/>

Siddle lost his position in the team when Clark recovered, but regained his position in the team for the first Test against [[South African national cricket team|South Africa]] at the [[WACA Ground|WACA]] due to Clark's elbow injury recurring.<ref name=crunch/> Siddle then solidified his place in the team during Australia's back-to-back series against South Africa.<ref name=cricinfoprofile/> He broke through with three wickets in front of his home crowd at the Melbourne Cricket Ground during the [[Boxing Day Test Match]] against the Proteas on his way to figures of four for 81 in the first innings.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/13804/scorecard/351682/australia-vs-south-africa-2nd-test-south-africa-tour-of-australia-2008-09/|title=2nd Test, South Africa tour of Australia at Melbourne, Dec 26–30 2008 {{!}} Match Summary|work=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=7 August 2009}}</ref> Siddle backed this performance up in the next Test at the [[Sydney Cricket Ground]], taking five for 59 in South Africa's first innings.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/13804/scorecard/351682/australia-vs-south-africa-2nd-test-south-africa-tour-of-australia-2008-09/|title=2nd Test, South Africa tour of Australia at Melbourne, Dec 26–30 2008 {{!}} Match Summary|work=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=7 August 2009}}</ref> His efforts were not enough, however, to prevent Australia from succumbing to a historic home series defeat.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/series/351610.html|title=Results {{!}} Global|work=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=7 August 2009}}</ref>

Siddle also gave a fine account of himself on the South African leg of the rubber, in which the Australians triumphed 2–1. Going into the [[2009 Ashes series]], he had notched up 29 Test wickets at an average of 27.65. The fact that it had come in six Tests against the South Africans and one against India in India, with an economy rate of only 2.57 an over, helped make his record look even more impressive.<ref>{{cite news|last=Booth|first=Lawrence|date=30 June 2009|title=Myths; And stereotypes|work=[[The Guardian]]|department=The Spin}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/player/7898.html?class=1;season=2008%2F09;template=results;type=bowling|title=Bowling records {{!}} Test matches {{!}} Cricinfo Statsguru|access-date=7 January 2018|work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

In the first Test of the [[2009 Ashes series|Ashes]] series against [[England national cricket team|England]], Siddle took 2/97 on the first day's play.<ref name="cricinfofirstashestest">{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/13659/scorecard/345970/england-vs-australia-1st-test-australia-tour-of-england-and-scotland-2009/|title=1st Test, Australia tour of England and Scotland at Cardiff, Jul 8–12 2009 {{!}} Match Summary|work=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=9 July 2009}}</ref> Siddle then took 5/21 on the first day of the fourth Test, which, to that point, were his career best bowling figures in an innings in Test cricket.<ref name=cricinfoprofile/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/13659/scorecard/345973/england-vs-australia-4th-test-australia-tour-of-england-and-scotland-2009/|title=4th Test, Australia tour of England and Scotland at Leeds, Aug 7–9 2009 {{!}} Match Summary|access-date=7 January 2018|work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> After the Ashes, Siddle was named the ICC Emerging Player of the Year for 2009.<ref name=cricinfoprofile/>

===Hat-trick and injury problems (2009–2013)===
Siddle had a relatively quiet 2009–10 season before a back stress fracture ruled him out of cricket in January 2010.<ref name=cricinfoprofile/><ref name=hat>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/the-ashes-2010-11/content/story/488911.html|title=Siddle hat-trick gives Australia control|last=McGlashan|first=Andrew|date=25 November 2010|access-date=7 January 2018|work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> Siddle was able to recover from the injury in time for the 2010–11 Ashes series in Australia the next summer.<ref name=cricinfoprofile/>

In his first Test match back, on 25 November 2010, Siddle's 26th birthday, he became the ninth Australian to take a Test [[hat-trick (cricket)|hat-trick]], and first cricketer to take a hat-trick on his birthday.<ref name=cricinfoprofile/><ref name=cricket/> Siddle had been controversially brought into the Australian team ahead of [[Doug Bollinger]], despite not having played since January, but he proved doubters wrong early in the match by taking the key wickets of [[Kevin Pietersen]] and [[Paul Collingwood]] early in England's first innings.<ref name=hat/> When England reached 4/197, Siddle was brought back into the attack and ended up taking the wickets of [[Alastair Cook]] and [[Matt Prior]] in consecutive balls to be on a hat-trick.<ref name=hat/> [[Stuart Broad]] came to the crease for the hat-trick ball, for which Siddle bowled a [[yorker]]. Broad attempted to tap the ball down the leg side but missed the ball with his bat, with the ball hitting his foot and was given out [[leg before wicket|lbw]].<ref name=cricinfoprofile/> Broad [[Umpire Decision Review System|referred the decision to the third umpire]], but the wicket was not overturned.<ref name=hat/> Siddle went on to dismiss [[Graeme Swann]] for his sixth wicket of the innings, and could have had a seventh when wicket-keeper [[Brad Haddin]] dropped [[James Anderson (cricketer)|James Anderson]] off Siddle's bowling.<ref name=hat/> He finished with figures of six wickets for only 54 runs, his best-ever in Test match cricket, having bowled 16 overs in total.<ref name="BBC Sport">{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/cricket/9226319.stm |title=Ashes: Peter Siddle hat-trick shocks England at Gabba |access-date=25 November 2010|work=[[BBC Sport]] |date=25 November 2010|last=Brett|first=Oliver}}</ref>

Despite a heavy series defeat to England, Siddle had another successful match in the Boxing Day Test Match at the Melbourne Cricket Ground, taking 6/75 in an innings defeat.<ref name=cricinfoprofile/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/13062/scorecard/428752/australia-vs-england-4th-test-england-tour-of-australia-2010-11/|title=4th Test, England tour of Australia at Melbourne, Dec 26–29 2010 {{!}} Match Summary|access-date=7 January 2018|work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> Siddle started to enjoy more consistent success, starring against [[Indian cricket team in Australia in 2011–12|India]] the next summer with 23 wickets at an average of 18.65.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/bowling/most_wickets_career.html?id=6636;type=series|title=Cricket Records {{!}} Records {{!}} / {{!}} Border-Gavaskar Trophy, 2011/12 {{!}} Most wickets|work=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=28 January 2012}}</ref> During the series, he took his 100th Test wicket at the SCG on 3 January 2012, to rise to a career-high seventh in the ICC's Test bowler rankings.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.abc.net.au/news/2010-12-30/siddle-trott-jump-up-rankings/1890550?site=sport|title=Siddle, Trott jump up rankings|work=[[Australian Broadcasting Corporation|abc.net.au]]|date=30 December 2010|access-date=31 December 2010}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.indiablooms.com/SportsDetailsPage/2011/sportsDetails301211c.php|title=Siddle, Herath achieve career-best rankings|date=30 December 2010|access-date=6 January 2012|work=India Blooms|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130126011707/http://www.indiablooms.com/SportsDetailsPage/2011/sportsDetails301211c.php|archive-date=26 January 2013|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref> In the final match of the series he took impressive innings bowling figures of 5/49 on a batting wicket at the [[Adelaide Oval]],<ref name=cricinfoprofile/><ref name=cricket/> even being on a hat-trick at one stage in the match.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.abc.net.au/news/2012-01-26/kohli-stands-tall-on-australia27s-day/3795350|title=Kohli stands tall on Australia's day|last=Goraya|first=Raman|date=27 January 2012|access-date=7 January 2018|work=abc.net.au}}</ref><ref name=adelaide>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/12641/scorecard/518953/australia-vs-india-4th-test-india-tour-of-australia-2011-12/|title=4th Test, India tour of Australia at Adelaide, Jan 24–28 2012 {{!}} Match Summary|access-date=7 January 2018|work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> For this performance he was named the man of the match.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.smh.com.au/sport/cricket/rising-from-the-ashes-20120128-1qnbx.html|title=Rising from the Ashes|last=Barrett|first=Chris|date=29 January 2012|work=The Sydney Morning Herald|access-date=28 January 2012}}</ref><ref name=adelaide/>

During [[Australian cricket team in the West Indies in 2011–12|Australia's tour of the West Indies]] in early 2012, Siddle suffered another back injury and had to fly home early from the tour.<ref name=cricinfoprofile/> Siddle had signed for English county club [[Essex County Cricket Club|Essex]], for the [[2012 Friends Life t20|2012 FriendsLife T20]], England's premier [[Twenty20]] competition,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/county-cricket-2012/content/story/555442.html|title=Siddle to join Essex for T20|date=22 February 2012|work=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=21 April 2012}}</ref> but due to his injury he was unable to fulfill his contract with the club.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/county-cricket-2012/content/current/story/562775.html|title=Injury rules out Siddle for Essex|date=26 April 2012|work=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=26 April 2012}}</ref> Siddle returned to the Australian Test team for their [[South African cricket team in Australia in 2012–13|series against South Africa]] at the end of 2012. Whilst out injured, he decided to become a vegetarian.<ref name=cricinfoprofile/> The series was very difficult for Siddle because of the very heavy workload he faced.<ref name=cricinfoprofile/> In the first Test of the series at [[the Gabba]], he was forced to bowl 53 overs in a draw.<ref name=australian>{{cite web|url=http://www.theaustralian.com.au/sport/cricket/peter-siddle-toiled-manfully-to-the-brink-of-breaking-down/news-story/1fed4867c3931c949ad193901351e11b?sv=fcc1f04b0d14b2bcaa572df8df5d3444&nk=c12855ad84e52edb48b553d4a7bcdebc-1515303315|title=Peter Siddle toiled manfully to the brink of breaking down|last=Smith|first=Wayne|date=27 November 2012|access-date=7 January 2018|work=[[The Australian]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/12276/scorecard/573007/australia-vs-south-africa-1st-test-south-africa-tour-of-australia-2012-13/|title=1st Test, South Africa tour of Australia at Brisbane, Nov 9–13 2012 {{!}} Match Summary|access-date=7 January 2018|work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> Siddle was forced to bowl for a long time again in the second Test at the Adelaide Oval, he bowled 63.5 overs — the most by any Australian fast bowler in a single Test match in the 21st century — as his workload had been compounded by an injury to teammate [[James Pattinson]] mid-match. Australia needed to bowl South Africa out in the final two days of the Test match to avoid a second consecutive draw, with Siddle being the most successful Australian bowler with four wickets. Whilst showing clear signs of exhaustion throughout the final day, Siddle pushed through and took wickets late in the match but was unable to get Australia the win.<ref name=cricinfoprofile/><ref name=australian/><ref name=tired>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/12276/scorecard/573008/australia-vs-south-africa-2nd-test-south-africa-tour-of-australia-2012-13/|title=2nd Test, South Africa tour of Australia at Adelaide, Nov 22–26 2012 {{!}} Match Summary}}</ref>

Following his heavy workload in the first two Tests of the series, Siddle was rested for the final match.<ref name=cricinfoprofile/> Some of his critics blamed this on his new vegetarian diet, though Siddle denied that his diet was responsible for the fatigue.<ref name=vegetarian>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/australia-v-sri-lanka-2012/content/story/596840.html|title=Siddle stares down vegetarian critics|last=Brettig|first=Daniel|date=12 December 2012|access-date=7 January 2018|work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> When Siddle returned to the Test team for the series against [[Sri Lankan cricket team in Australia in 2012–13|Sri Lanka]], he registered his career-best bowling figures in Test cricket, taking nine wickets across both of Sri Lanka's innings.<ref name=cricinfoprofile/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/12264/scorecard/573011/australia-vs-sri-lanka-1st-test-sri-lanka-tour-of-australia-2012-13/|title=1st Test, Sri Lanka tour of Australia at Hobart, Dec 14–18 2012 {{!}} Match Summary|access-date=7 January 2018|work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> His spell of 4 for 50 at Hobart was nominated to be one of the best Test bowling performances of the year by ESPNCricinfo.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/awards2012/content/story/599152.html|title=Monty, Vernon and Co|date=2013-01-10|website=Cricinfo|language=en|access-date=2019-12-28}}</ref> Siddle then struggled to make an impact with his bowling [[Australian cricket team in India in 2012–13|in India]],<ref name=cricinfoprofile/> though he did make history by becoming the first number 9 batsman to score a half century in both innings of a Test match.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/12214/scorecard/598815/india-vs-australia-4th-test-australia-tour-of-india-2012-13/|title=4th Test, Australia tour of India at Delhi, Mar 22–24 2013 {{!}} Match Summary|access-date=7 January 2018|work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

===Back-to-back Ashes series (2013–2014)===
Despite nearly constant speculation about his place in the Test team, Siddle was the only Australian bowler to play all ten Tests across the [[2013 Ashes series|2013]] and [[2013–14 Ashes series|2013–14]] Ashes series against England, bowling reliably throughout the two series.<ref name=cricinfoprofile/><ref name=cricket/> At [[Trent Bridge]], in Australia's first bowling innings of either series, Siddle took figures of 5/50 to help bowl England out, proving his value to the team.<ref name=cricket/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/12088/scorecard/566932/england-vs-australia-1st-test-australia-tour-of-england-and-scotland-2013/|title=1st Test, Australia tour of England and Scotland at Nottingham, Jul 10–14 2013 {{!}} Match Summary|access-date=7 January 2018|work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> But his form waned towards the end of the season and he only took one wicket across the last two Tests of the series, which Australia lost 3–0.<ref name=fuel>{{cite web|url=https://www.dailytelegraph.com.au/sport/cricket/vegan-diet-to-fuel-australian-bowler-peter-siddles-bid-to-beat-englands-batsmen-this-summer/news-story/0e7abd34f31f5080144e8e36fa657657?nk=c12855ad84e52edb48b553d4a7bcdebc-1515309149|title=Vegan diet to fuel Australian bowler Peter Siddle's bid to beat England's batsmen this summer|last=Conn|first=Malcolm|work=[[The Daily Telegraph (Sydney)|The Daily Telegraph]]|date=25 October 2013|access-date=7 January 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/12088/scorecard/566935/england-vs-australia-4th-test-australia-tour-of-england-and-scotland-2013/|title=4th Test, Australia tour of England and Scotland at Chester-le-Street, Aug 9–12 2013 {{!}} Match Summary|access-date=7 January 2018|work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/12088/scorecard/566936/england-vs-australia-5th-test-australia-tour-of-england-and-scotland-2013/|title=5th Test, Australia tour of England and Scotland at London, Aug 21–25 2013 {{!}} Match Summary|access-date=7 January 2018|work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> Again, there were critics who blamed Siddle's poor form on his diet, but Siddle continued to deny that his diet had anything to do with his poor form.<ref name=fuel/>

Siddle was also an integral part of Australia's bowling attack when they won the second series in Australia 5–0.<ref name=cricket/> He had particular success through both series against English batsman Kevin Pietersen. He dismissed Pietersen 6 times during the two series, making it 10 times in total that Siddle had dismissed Pietersen in Test cricket.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/player/7898.html?class=1;filter=advanced;orderby=dis_dismissals;spanmax1=31+Mar+2014;spanmin1=1+Apr+2013;spanval1=span;template=results;type=bowling;view=batsman_summary|title=Bowling records {{!}} Test matches {{!}} Cricinfo Statsguru|access-date=7 January 2018|work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/player/7898.html?class=1;filter=advanced;orderby=dis_dismissals;template=results;type=bowling;view=batsman_summary|title=Bowling records {{!}} Test matches {{!}} Cricinfo Statsguru|access-date=7 January 2018|work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> Pietersen said that the reason for this was that he didn't have the patience to work through Siddle's 'robotic' and 'suffocating' tactics, and Siddle would bowl with consistently good line and length for long periods of time,<ref name=suffocating>{{cite web|url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/kevin-pietersen-peter-siddle-ashes-nemesis/2014-10-14|title=KP admits to Siddle torment|last=Ramsey|first=Andrew|date=14 October 2014|access-date=7 January 2018|work=cricket.com.au}}</ref> resulting in Pietersen scoring much slower against Siddle than against any of the other bowlers in the Australian team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/the-ashes-2013-14/content/story/700287.html|title=Siddle maintains stranglehold over Pietersen|last=Coverdale|first=Brydon|date=14 December 2013|access-date=7 January 2018|work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> No other bowler dismissed Pietersen on more occasions in Test cricket than Siddle did.<ref name=suffocating/>

=== More Test matches (2014–2016)===
Siddle became a victim of the Australian selectors' changing policy, focusing more on outright pace than consistent line and length, resulting in him being dropped from the team when he started to lose some of his bowling speed in early 2014.<ref name=cricinfoprofile/> Siddle had lost weight over the last two years, making it difficult for him to bowl as fast as he had previously, so when Australian coach [[Darren Lehmann]] emphasized the importance of him bowling at speeds of around 140 kmph, he worked hard to rebuild his frame and improve his pace.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.smh.com.au/sport/cricket/peter-siddle-puts-meat-on-his-bones-not-his-diet-in-bid-for-pace-20140730-zyges.html|title= Peter Siddle puts meat on his bones, not his diet, in bid for pace |last=Saltau|first=Chloe|date=30 July 2014|access-date=7 January 2018|work=The Sydney Morning Herald}}</ref> There were again critics who blamed his weight loss and slower bowling on his diet, but Siddle blamed it on the fatigue associated with bowling regularly for long periods of time.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/magazine/content/story/775593.html|title=How much does overtraining have to do with loss of form?|last=Bowden|first=Alex|date=4 September 2014|access-date=7 January 2018|work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> No longer a regular part of the Test team, Siddle lost his contract with [[Cricket Australia]] in early 2015.<ref name=contract>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/australia/content/story/993963.html|title=Siddle keeps Cricket Australia contract|last=Coverdale|first=Brydon|date=1 April 2016|access-date=7 January 2018|work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

Siddle signed to play for Nottinghamshire in 2014, making himself available for all of the LV County Championship and 50-over matches, but not the Twenty20 matches.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.trentbridge.co.uk/news/2013/november/nottinghamshire-sign-peter-siddle-for-2014-season.html|title=NOTTINGHAMSHIRE SIGN PETER SIDDLE FOR 2014 SEASON|date=13 November 2013|work=[[Nottinghamshire County Cricket Club|trentbridge.co.uk]]|access-date=3 April 2014}}</ref> In July 2014, he played for the Rest of the World team in the [[Bicentenary Celebration match]] at [[Lord's]].<ref>{{cite web |title=MCC v Rest of the World – 5 July |url=http://www.lords.org/fixtures/fixtures-and-tickets/mcc-v-rest-of-the-world-5-july/ |work=[[Lord's|lords.org]] |date=5 July 2014 |access-date=5 July 2014 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20140621161324/http://www.lords.org/fixtures/fixtures-and-tickets/mcc-v-rest-of-the-world-5-july/ |archive-date=21 June 2014 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }}</ref>

Siddle started to make a comeback to Test cricket in 2015, being brought into Australia's team for the [[2015 Ashes series]].<ref name=cricbuzz>{{cite web|url=http://www.cricbuzz.com/profiles/1444/peter-siddle|title=Peter Siddle Profile – ICC Ranking, Age, Career Info & Stats|last=Sadanandan|first=Hariprasad|access-date=7 January 2018|work=[[CricBuzz|cricbuzz.com]]}}</ref> He subsequently became a regular part of the Australian bowling lineup due to the retirement of Mitchell Johnson and an injury to [[Mitchell Starc]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.smh.com.au/sport/cricket/need-for-speed-not-everything-for-australian-fast-bowlers-insists-peter-siddle-20151206-glglhs.html|title= Need for speed not everything for Australian fast bowlers, insists Peter Siddle |last=Barrett|first=Chris|date=6 December 2015|access-date=7 January 2018|work=The Sydney Morning Herald}}</ref> He played enough Test cricket to get himself back on a Cricket Australia contract,<ref name=contract/> but in February 2016, he again had stress fractures in his back. As a result, he was sidelined for most of 2016, with a likely implication being that he had played his final Test match.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.abc.net.au/news/2016-02-25/peter-siddle-has-stress-fractures-in-his-back/7200498|title=Peter Siddle has stress fractures in his back, Cricket Australia reveals|date=25 February 2016|access-date=7 January 2018|work=abc.net.au}}</ref>

Despite the stress fractures in his back keeping him out of cricket for most of 2016, Siddle still retained his contract with Cricket Australia for the 2016–17 season.<ref name=contract/> He returned from injury in October to play for Victoria in three one-day games and a Sheffield Shield match and was selected to play another Test match against [[South African cricket team in Australia in 2016–17|South Africa]] at the WACA. He had bowling figures of 1/36 and 2/62 in the two innings, as Australia lost the match by 177 runs.<ref name=second>{{cite web|url=http://www.heraldsun.com.au/sport/cricket/peter-siddle-forced-out-of-second-test-with-back-injury/news-story/1b2e9255983015b6f0717d0a3688f81a?nk=c12855ad84e52edb48b553d4a7bcdebc-1515333573|title=Peter Siddle forced out of second Test with back injury|last=Buckle|first=Greg|date=8 November 2016|access-date=8 January 2018|work=[[Herald Sun]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/10615/scorecard/1000851/australia-vs-south-africa-1st-test-sa-tour-of-australia-2016-17/|title=1st Test, South Africa tour of Australia at Perth, Nov 3–7 2016 {{!}} Match Summary|access-date=8 January 2018|work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> This appeared to be Siddle's final Test match for Australia, as he was dropped from the team for the second Test with a back injury.<ref name=cricbuzz/><ref name=second/><ref name=statement>{{cite web|url=http://www.adelaidenow.com.au/sport/cricket/big-bash/peter-siddle-has-more-tests-in-the-tank-but-wants-to-make-a-statement-in-bbl-for-strikers/news-story/78ad2fbb656713d5b4d74897a344ab31|title=Peter Siddle has more Tests in the tank but wants to make a statement in BBL for Strikers|last=Earle|first=Richard|date=14 December 2017|access-date=8 January 2018|work=[[The Advertiser (Adelaide)|The Advertiser]]}}</ref> During this summer, the Australian selectors worked on reshaping their bowling attack by focusing more on youth and outright pace, which left Siddle off of their radar moving forwards.<ref name=cricbuzz/>

===Injury and return to Test cricket (2016–2019)===
[[File:Peter Siddle 2019.jpg|thumb|left|Siddle bowling for Essex in 2019]]

Siddle's injury kept him out of cricket for a year<ref name=fire>{{cite web|url=https://www.dailytelegraph.com.au/sport/cricket/ashes-fire-still-burns-bright-for-peter-siddle-as-he-pushed-his-claims-for-test-selection/news-story/d1717a1f5c4fa102bccbad04549e67aa?nk=c12855ad84e52edb48b553d4a7bcdebc-1515334099|title=Ashes fire still burns bright for Peter Siddle as he pushed his claims for Test selection|last=Horne|first=Ben|date=11 October 2017|access-date=8 January 2018|work=The Daily Telegraph}}</ref> but, when he returned for the 2017–18 season, he was told that he was still in contention to play Test cricket as James Pattinson was injured and the selectors were looking to protect their young pace attack from being overworked in the upcoming [[2017–18 Ashes series]].<ref name=statement/><ref name=worth>{{cite web|url=http://www.smh.com.au/sport/cricket/the-ashes/the-ashes-2017-peter-siddle-worth-spot-in-australian-attack-says-victoria-coach-20171010-gyy8w9.html|title= The Ashes 2017: Peter Siddle worth spot in Australian attack, says Victoria coach |last=Barrett|first=Chris|date=10 October 2017|access-date=8 January 2018|work=The Sydney Morning Herald}}</ref> He played every game for Victoria in the [[2017–18 JLT One-Day Cup]], including an impressive 2/20 performance against the [[Cricket Australia XI]] at the tiny [[Hurstville Oval]], a difficult ground to bowl at due to its short boundaries.<ref name=statement/><ref name=fire/><ref name=worth/> He then played four of Victoria's first five matches in the [[2017–18 Sheffield Shield season]], but he only took four wickets and was not included in Australia's squad for the Ashes. This was the first Ashes series he had missed since the [[2006–07 Ashes series]] before his Test debut.<ref name=statement/>

In July 2019, he was named in [[2019 Ashes series#Squads|Australia's squad]] for the [[2019 Ashes series]] in England, marking his return to the Ashes since the 2015 series. He played 3 matches, with them being at [[Lord's]], [[Edgbaston Cricket Ground|Edgbaston]], and [[The Oval]]. He took 7 wickets throughout the series, at an average 42.14.<ref>{{cite web|title=PM Siddle Test Records|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/records/series/bowling-most-wickets-career/the-ashes-2019-12492|publisher=[[ESPNCricinfo]]}}</ref>

==Later career==
On 29 December 2019, Siddle retired from international cricket, effective immediately.<ref>{{cite web |title=Australia name 17-man Ashes squad |url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/australia-2019-ashes-squad-england-tests-paine-smith-warner-pattinson-wade-marsh-bancroft-neser/2019-07-27 |website=cricket.com.au |date=26 July 2019 |access-date=29 July 2019 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Bancroft, Wade and Mitchell Marsh earn Ashes call-ups |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/27261124/bancroft-wade-mitchell-marsh-earn-ashes-call-ups |website=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=29 July 2019 |language=en |date=26 July 2019}}</ref>

In January 2026, while 41 years old, Siddle bowled a delivery at 145.8kph against the [[Hobart Hurricanes]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Watch: 41-year-old Peter Siddle bowls 145.8kph delivery |url=https://www.khelwire.com/articles/watch-41-year-old-peter-siddle-bowls-1458kph-delivery |website=KhelWire |date=January 2026 |access-date=January 23, 2026}}</ref>

In February 2026, Siddle was signed by the [[Multan Sultans]] for the [[2026 Pakistan Super League]] season, following the league’s first player auction format. He became one of the experienced overseas fast bowlers in the tournament and delivered notable performances in the latter stages of the season. In April 2026, he played a key role against the [[Karachi Kings]], dismissing [[Abbas Afridi (cricketer)|Abbas Afridi]] and helping defend a late chase.<ref>{{cite news |title=PSL 2026 match report |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/articles/c79jgdwvzp9o |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=15 June 2026}}</ref>

==Player profile==
Siddle is a right-arm [[Fast bowling|fast-medium bowler]] who also [[Batting (cricket)|bats]] right-handed.<ref name=cricinfoprofile/> He has primarily been used as a workhorse, bowling for long periods of time, such as bowling the most overs by an Australian fast bowler in a 21st-century Test match against South Africa in 2012.<ref name=australian/><ref name=cricbuzz/> His charging run-up and powerful delivery is followed by worrying bounce off the pitch.<ref name=cricinfoprofile/><ref name=cricbuzz/>

Siddle is a Test cricket specialist, bowling with great consistency over long periods of time, worrying aggressive batsmen like [[Kevin Pietersen]].<ref name=cricinfoprofile/><ref name=suffocating/><ref name=cricbuzz/> Though he did have a brief stint in Australia's [[Limited overs cricket|limited overs]] team, issues with his playing style made it difficult for him to make the same impact that he made in Test cricket. His consistent line and length was easy for batsmen to predict in [[One Day International|ODI's]] and he did not have enough variations in his bowling to succeed in T20 International's.<ref name=cricbuzz/>
Over his career, he toured England 4 times for the Ashes series.

==Veganism==
Siddle has been a vegan since 2012 when his partner, Anna, an animal rights activist, convinced him to adopt the lifestyle.<ref name=cricinfoprofile/><ref name=fuel/> He is well known for his diet, which involves him eating as many as 20 bananas a day.<ref name=cricinfoprofile/> After becoming a vegan, Siddle faced criticism that his change of diet led to fatigue and slower bowling speeds.<ref name=vegetarian/><ref name=fuel/>

{{Blockquote
|text=In India [at [[MRF Pace Foundation]]], our guys have got to eat protein even if they are considered vegetarian – they have got to eat fish and chicken. I think you have to rebuild muscle after you have had a 50-over Test. I know there is more to it than clouds and grass but I have not seen too many (vegetarian fast bowlers) survive. [[Colin Croft|[Colin] Croft]] tried it for 18 months and couldn't do it. Sidds is trying it and good luck to him.
|author=[[Dennis Lillee]], former Australian fast bowler<ref name=vegetarian/>

'''Rachin Ravindra''' (born 18 November 1999) is a New Zealand professional cricketer who [[Batting (cricket)|bats]] left-handed and [[Bowling (cricket)|bowls]] left-arm [[Left-arm orthodox spin|orthodox spin]]. He represents the [[New Zealand national cricket team|New Zealand national team]] and [[Wellington cricket team|Wellington]]. {{As of|2026|June}}, he is signed with the [[Washington Freedom (cricket)|Washington Freedom]] in [[Major League Cricket]] (MLC) and the [[Kolkata Knight Riders]] in the [[Indian Premier League]] (IPL).

==Early life==
Rachin Ravindra was born in [[Wellington]] on 18 November 1999 to parents from [[Bangalore]], Karnataka. His father Ravi Krishnamurthy, a [[software architect]], played club-level cricket in Bangalore before settling in [[New Zealand]] in 1997.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/meticulous-rachin-building-on-father-s-cricket-genes-1132964 |title=Rachin building on father's cricket genes |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=19 May 2024}}</ref><ref name="taste">{{cite news |last1=Vivan |first1=Sridhar |title=Batsman with taste |url=https://bangaloremirror.indiatimes.com/bangalore/others/batsman-with-taste/articleshow/104266462.cms |access-date=13 October 2023 |work=Bangalore Mirror |date=9 October 2023 |language=en |archive-date=22 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231022094731/https://bangaloremirror.indiatimes.com/bangalore/others/batsman-with-taste/articleshow/104266462.cms |url-status=live }}</ref> His grandfather Balakrishna Adiga is an educationist and former principal of Vijaya College.<ref>{{Cite news |date=4 November 2023 |title=New Zealand's Rachin Ravindra manifests his talent at 'home' turf as grandparents watch from stands |work=The Times of India |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/icc-world-cup/news/new-zealands-rachin-ravindra-manifests-his-talent-at-home-turf-as-grandparents-watch-from-stands/articleshow/104972648.cms?from=mdr |access-date=9 November 2023 |issn=0971-8257 |archive-date=9 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231109175256/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/icc-world-cup/news/new-zealands-rachin-ravindra-manifests-his-talent-at-home-turf-as-grandparents-watch-from-stands/articleshow/104972648.cms?from=mdr |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="taste"/>

===ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2023 ===
{{Main|2023 Cricket World Cup}}

Rachin was named in New Zealand's squad for the [[2023 Cricket World Cup|2023 World Cup]]. He was not officially in contention to make it into the final squad for the 2023 World Cup, but he found his way into the 15 man squad replacing injured [[Michael Bracewell (cricketer)|Michael Bracewell]]. Rachin was not a first choice option for New Zealand going into the World Cup preparations in full swing, as he was predominantly used by New Zealand team as a spin bowling all-rounder who could bat way down the order. However, a fitness concerns to New Zealand skipper Kane Williamson brought about a [[paradigm shift]] approach within the team management which opted to promote Rachin to bat at number three position in New Zealand's opening match against [[England cricket team|England]]. Prior to the start of the World Cup, he didn't bat at a position higher than number 6 slot in the limited ODI appearances he featured for the Black Caps.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Anderson |first=Ian |date=29 October 2023 |title=Cricket World Cup: Rachin Ravindra labelled a superstar for the Black Caps |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/cricket/black-caps/300998330/cricket-world-cup-rachin-ravindra-labelled-a-superstar-for-the-black-caps |access-date=9 November 2023 |website=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |language=en |archive-date=9 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231109182206/https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/cricket/black-caps/300998330/cricket-world-cup-rachin-ravindra-labelled-a-superstar-for-the-black-caps |url-status=live }}</ref>

In the [[2023 Cricket World Cup group stage|opening match against England]], batting at no. 3 in place of Williamson, he became only the fourth Kiwi player to hit a century on World Cup debut by scoring 123* runs off just 96 balls. It was also coincidentally his maiden ODI century.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Kumar |first=P. K. Ajith |date=14 October 2023 |title=Rachin Ravindra: the World Cup breakout star from New Zealand with Indian roots |language=en-IN |work=The Hindu |url=https://www.thehindu.com/sport/cricket/icc-world-cup/rachin-ravindra-the-world-cup-breakout-star-from-new-zealand-with-indian-roots/article67420643.ece |access-date=9 November 2023 |issn=0971-751X |archive-date=9 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231109175256/https://www.thehindu.com/sport/cricket/icc-world-cup/rachin-ravindra-the-world-cup-breakout-star-from-new-zealand-with-indian-roots/article67420643.ece |url-status=live }}</ref> This was also the fastest century by a New Zealand player in World Cup, reaching 100 in 82 balls. He also became the youngest New Zealand player to score a World Cup century at the age of 23 years and 321 days.<ref>{{Cite web |date=28 October 2023 |title=Who is Rachin Ravindra – New Zealand's new World Cup hero with strong Indian roots |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/cricket/rachin-ravindra-india-new-zealand-world-cup-2023-b2437563.html |access-date=9 November 2023 |website=The Independent |language=en |archive-date=9 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231109175259/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/cricket/rachin-ravindra-india-new-zealand-world-cup-2023-b2437563.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Also, along === Indian Premier League ===
In December 2023, Rachin was signed by the [[Chennai Super Kings]] in the player auction for the [[2024 Indian Premier League]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sportstar |first=Team |date=19 December 2023 |title=Chennai Super Kings signs Rachin Ravindra for Rs 1.8 crore in IPL auction 2024 |url=https://sportstar.thehindu.com/cricket/ipl/ipl-news/rachin-ravindra-sold-to-chennai-super-kings-18-crores-ipl-2024-auction-news-updates/article67647758.ece |access-date=19 December 2023 |website=Sportstar |language=en |archive-date=19 December 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231219185649/https://sportstar.thehindu.com/cricket/ipl/ipl-news/rachin-ravindra-sold-to-chennai-super-kings-18-crores-ipl-2024-auction-news-updates/article67647758.ece |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 22 March 2024, Rachin made his [[Indian Premier League]] debut as a player of Chennai Super Kings against [[Royal Challengers Bangalore]]. He scored the first six for his team in the league. He scored 37 runs in just 15 balls before being caught out by [[Rajat Patidar]] of the bowling of [[Karn Sharma]]. The following match he scored 46 off 20 (Strike rate 230) Rashid Khan got him out. He scored his first fifty against RCB on May 18. Rachin scored a total of 222 runs in the 10 matches he played for CSK.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Get Ball by Ball Commentary of CSK vs RCB, Indian Premier League, 1st Match {{!}} ESPNcricinfo.com |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/indian-premier-league-2024-1410320/chennai-super-kings-vs-royal-challengers-bengaluru-1st-match-1422119/ball-by-ball-commentary |access-date=2024-03-23 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref>

===ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2024 ===
In May 2024, he was named in New Zealand's squad for the [[2024 Men's T20 World Cup|2024 ICC Men's T20 World Cup]] tournament.<ref>{{Cite web |title=New Zealand Squad for ICC Men's World Cup 2024 |url=https://www.scorewaves.com/news-details/new-zealand-squad-icc-mens-world-up-2024-new-zealand-jersey |access-date=2024-06-10 |website=ScoreWaves |language=en}}</ref> Rachin played three of New Zealand's four games before the team exited the tournament at the group stage following defeats to Afghanistan and the West Indies.{{citation needed|date=March 2025}}

=== Champions Trophy 2025 ===
In January 2025, Rachin was named as part of New Zealand's squad for the [[2025 Champions Trophy|2025 ICC Champions Trophy]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=icc |date=2025-01-11 |title=Santner-led New Zealand |website=www.icc-cricket.com |language=en}}</ref> He did not play New Zealand's first game, a win against Pakistan, due to continuing recovery from a facial injury he sustained in the [[2024–25 Pakistan Tri-Nation Series|Pakistan-New Zealand tri-series]] earlier in February.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-02-10 |title=Black Caps star ruled out with head injury |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/sport/cricket/black-caps/black-caps-v-pakistan-rachin-ravindra-ruled-out-of-tri-series-final-with-head-injury/ECK6PJY3RRFE5J7V4PYXOYBY3E/ |access-date=2025-02-25 |website=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |language=en-NZ}}</ref> On his Champions Trophy debut against Bangladesh, Rachin scored 112 runs off of 105 balls, becoming the first player in history to score a century on debut in both the World Cup and Champions Trophy.<ref>{{Cite web |last=icc |date=2025-02-25 |title='Grateful' Ravindra credits love and support after making clutch return from injury |website=www.icc-cricket.com |language=en}}</ref> In the semifinal against South Africa, Rachin scored another century, his first in an ODI knockout match.{{citation needed|date=March 2025}} In [[2025 Champions Trophy final|the final]] against India, he scored 37 runs off 29 balls in a losing cause.<ref>{{Cite web |title=IND vs NZ Cricket Scorecard, Final at Dubai, March 09, 2025 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/icc-champions-trophy-2024-25-1459031/india-vs-new-zealand-final-1466428/full-scorecard |access-date=2025-03-11 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref> He was the leading run scorer in the Champions Trophy, amassing 263 runs with an average of 65.75,<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2025-03-09 |title=Most runs in ICC Champions Trophy 2025: Rachin |access-date=2025-03-11 |website=Sportstar |language=en}}</ref> and was named as the Player of the Tournament on 9 March 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=2025-03-10 |title=ICC announces Champions '''Saim Ayub''' ({{langx|ur|{{nq|صائم ایوب}}}}; born 24 May 2002) is a Pakistani international [[cricket]]er.<ref>{{cite web |title=Saim Ayub |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/1161031.html |access-date=20 February 2021 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref> He plays for the [[Pakistan national cricket team|Pakistan national team]] as an [[all-rounder]], who [[Batting (cricket)|bats]] left-handed and bowls right-arm [[Off spin|off break]]. He represents [[List of Karachi first-class cricket teams|Karachi Whites]] in domestic cricket and [[Peshawar Zalmi]] in the [[Pakistan Super League]].

== Early life ==
His father Ayub Ahmed and uncle [[Mohammad Javed]] both played cricket at the [[Club cricket|club level]]. Saim was initiated into the game at a young age with tape ball cricket from [[Gulistan-e-Johar]], helped by his father as well as by two elder brothers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tariq |first=Aamir |date=18 April 2023 |title=Profile: Saim Ayub |url=https://en.dailypakistan.com.pk/18-Apr-2023/profile-saim-ayub |access-date=17 June 2023 |website=[[Daily Pakistan]]}}</ref>

==Domestic and franchise career==
In February 2021, Saim made his [[Twenty20]] debut for the [[Quetta Gladiators]] in the [[2021 Pakistan Super League]].<ref name="T20">{{cite web |title=1st Match (N), Karachi, Feb 20 2021, Pakistan Super League |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1247011.html |access-date=20 February 2021 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref>

In March 2022, he made his [[List A cricket|List A]] debut for [[Sindh cricket team|Sindh]] in the [[2021–22 Pakistan Cup]].<ref>{{cite web |title=23rd Match, Islamabad, Mar 19 2022, Pakistan Cup |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1277398.html |access-date=19 March 2022 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref>

In September 2022, he made his [[First-class cricket|first-class]] debut for Sindh in the 2022–23 [[Quaid-e-Azam Trophy]].

=== Pakistan Super League ===

In 2021, Ayub played for the [[Quetta Gladiators]] but failed to secure a regular place in the playing XI and was not retained for the following season.   In the 2023 PSL, playing for [[Peshawar Zalmi]], he scored his maiden PSL half-century in 33 deliveries, drawing comparisons from some observers to [[Saeed Anwar]].<ref>{{cite web |date=17 February 2023 |title=WATCH: Classy knock by Saim Ayub reminds fans of Saeed Anwar |url=https://cricketpakistan.com.pk/en/news/detail/watch-classy-knock-by-saim-ayub-reminds-fans-of-saeed-anwar |website=Cricket Pakistan}}</ref> In match 25 of PSL 2023 (Peshawar vs Quetta), he scored 74 off 34 balls, helping Zalmi post 240/2 in 20 overs. He also produced a knock of 58 off 33 in match 27.<ref>{{cite web |title=PSL 2023: Peshawar vs Multan / Match 27 / Scorecard |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/pakistan-super-league-2022-23-1332128/peshawar-zalmi-vs-multan-sultans-27th-match-1354950/full-scorecard |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=17 April 2023}}</ref> He finished the season with 341 runs at an average of 28.41 and a strike rate of 165.53 over 12 matches.<ref>{{cite web |title=PSL 2023: Most runs / Record / Batting Record |url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/batting/most_runs_career.html?id=14923;type=tournament |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=17 April 2023}}</ref>

Ahead of the [[2026 Pakistan Super League]], Ayub was released by [[Peshawar Zalmi]] and was pre-signed by [[Hyderabad Kingsmen]] for 12.6 crore [[Pakistani rupees]], making him the most expensive local player in the tournament.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Alam |first1=Sher |title=Young Cricketer Becomes the Most Expensive Pakistani Player in PSL History |url=https://propakistani.pk/2026/02/07/young-cricketer-becomes-the-most-expensive-pakistani-player-in-psl-history/ |website=ProPakistani |date=6 February 2026}}</ref>

==International career==
In December 2022, Ayub, along with fast bowler [[Ihsanullah (Pakistani cricketer)|Ihsanullah]] and wicket-keeper batsman [[Haseebullah Khan]], was included in Pakistan's Test squad for the second match of the [[New Zealand cricket team in Pakistan in 2022–23 (December 2022)|series against New Zealand]] in Karachi. The trio were added to gain international exposure and experience the team environment.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lakhani |first=Faizan |date=31 December 2022 |title=Three youngsters to be inducted to Pak squad for second Test against NZ |url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/latest/1025715-three-youngsters-to-be-inducted-to-pakistan-squad-for-2nd-nz-test |website=[[The News International]]}}</ref>

In March 2023, he was named in Pakistan's [[Twenty20 International]] (T20I) squad for the [[Pakistani cricket team against Afghanistan in the UAE in 2022–23|series against Afghanistan]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://icc-cricket.com/news/3108872 |title=Pakistan name new captain for Afghanistan T20Is |work=International Cricket Council |accessdate=13 March 2023}}</ref> making his debut in the first match on 24 March 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1362815.html |title=1st T20I (N), Sharjah, March 24, 2023, Afghanistan v Pakistan |work=ESPNcricinfo |accessdate=24 March 2023}}</ref> He was named in Pakistan's Test squad for the [[Pakistani cricket team in Australia in 2023–24|2023–24 tour of Australia]] and made his debut in the third Test at Sydney on 3 January 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pakistan call up Saim Ayub and Khurram Shahzad for Australia Test tour |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/pakistan-call-up-saim-ayub-and-khurram-shahzad-for-australia-test-tour-1409844 |access-date=2023-11-20 |website=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=AUS vs PAK, Pakistan in Australia 2023/24, 3rd Test at Sydney, January 03 - 07, 2024 - Full Scorecard |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/pakistan-in-australia-2023-24-1375835/australia-vs-pakistan-3rd-test-1375844/full-scorecard |access-date=2024-01-04 |website=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

In May 2024, Ayub was named in Pakistan's squad for the [[2024 ICC Men's T20 World Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pakistan Squad for ICC Men’s T20I World Cup 2024 |url=https://www.scorewaves.com/news-details/pakistan-squad-for-t20-world-cup |access-date=2024-06-11 |website=ScoreWaves}}</ref> Later that year, he was selected for the [[Bangladeshi cricket team in Pakistan in 2024|Test series against Bangladesh]] and for the [[English cricket team in Pakistan in 2024–25|three-match series against England]], where he recorded his highest Test score of 77 at Multan in October 2024.

He was subsequently named for Pakistan's tours of [[Pakistani cricket team in Zimbabwe in 2024–25|Zimbabwe]] and [[Pakistani cricket team in Australia in 2024–25|Australia]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Pakistan squads for Australia and Zimbabwe tours named |url=https://www.pcb.com.pk/press-release-detail/pakistan-squads-for-australia-and-zimbabwe-tours-named.html |access-date=2025-01-04 |website=Pakistan Cricket Board}}</ref> Ayub made his [[One Day International|ODI]] debut against Australia in Melbourne on 4 November 2024, scoring one run before being dismissed by [[Mitchell Starc]].<ref>{{cite web |title=AUS vs PAK Cricket Scorecard, 1st ODI at Melbourne, November 04, 2024 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/australia-vs-pakistan-2024-25-1426544/australia-vs-pakistan-1st-odi-1426549/full-scorecard |website=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He rebounded strongly in the second match, scoring 82 off 71 balls to help Pakistan to a commanding win, and was among the leading run-scorers as Pakistan claimed the series 2–1.<ref>{{Cite web |title=AUS vs PAK Cricket Scorecard, 2nd ODI at Adelaide, November 08, 2024 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/australia-vs-pakistan-2024-25-1426544/australia-vs-pakistan-2nd-odi-1426550/full-scorecard |access-date=2025-01-04 |website=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=AUS vs PAK Cricket Scorecard, 3rd ODI at Perth, November 10, 2024 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/australia-vs-pakistan-2024-25-1426544/australia-vs-pakistan-3rd-odi-1426551/full-scorecard |access-date=2025-01-04 |website=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

In Zimbabwe later that month, he struck his maiden ODI century, a 53-ball hundred, the second-fastest by a Pakistani, helping Pakistan to a 10-wicket win in the second match of the series.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ayub's 53-ball century levels series after Abrar and Salman strangle Zimbabwe |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/pakistan-in-zimbabwe-2024-25-1444642/zimbabwe-vs-pakistan-2nd-odi-1444650/match-report |access-date=2024-11-26 |website=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He finished the series as the leading run-scorer and was named [[Player of the Series awards (cricket)|Player of the Series]] after contributing 155 runs and three wickets across three matches.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-11-28 |title=Zimbabwe vs Pakistan, 3rd ODI Highlights: Pakistan win by 99 runs, clinch series 2-1 |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/sports/story/zimbabwe-vs-paklstan-live-score-3rd-odi-live-score-bulawayo-series-decider-2641558-2024-11-28 |access-date=2025-01-04 |website=India Today}}</ref>

In December 2024, Ayub was named in Pakistan's squad for the [[Pakistani cricket team in South Africa in 2024–25|tour of South Africa]]. He scored an unbeaten 98 in the second T20I, narrowly missing a maiden T20I century,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sports |first=A. |date=2024-12-14 |title=Saim Ayub opens up after missing maiden T20I century against South Africa |url=https://a-sports.tv/saim-ayub-missing-t20i-century-pakistan-south-africa/ |access-date=2024-12-14 |website=ASports.tv}}</ref> and followed with back-to-back ODI centuries, including a match-winning 101 in the third ODI that sealed Pakistan's first-ever ODI whitewash in South Africa.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Moonda |first1=Firdose |title=Saim Ayub hundred condemns South Africa to maiden home ODI whitewash |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/south-africa-vs-pakistan-2024-25-1432205/south-africa-vs-pakistan-3rd-odi-1432216/match-report |website=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=24 December 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2024-12-23 |title=Pakistan's batting sensation Saim Ayub joins Virat Kohli in this elite list |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/news/pakistans-batting-sensation-saim-ayub-joins-virat-kohli-in-this-elite-list/articleshow/116589098.cms |access-date=2024-12-24 |work=The Times of India}}</ref> His performances made him the youngest player to score an ODI century against South Africa while chasing, surpassing a record previously held by [[Brian Lara]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-12-18 |title=Saim Ayub breaks legendary batter's record in first South Africa ODI |url=https://arynews.tv/saim-ayub-breaks-brian-lara-record-in-first-pak-v-sa-odi/ |access-date=2024-12-18 |website=ARY News}}</ref> His tour ended prematurely due to an ankle injury sustained during the second Test in Cape Town.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Update on Saim Ayub's injury |url=https://www.pcb.com.pk/press-release-detail/update-on-saim-ayub-s-injury.html |access-date=2025-01-10 |website=Pakistan Cricket Board}}</ref>

In August 2025, during the [[Pakistani cricket team in the West Indies in 2025|T20I series in the West Indies]], Ayub was a key contributor in Pakistan's 2–1 series win, earning the Player of the Match award in the first game for a half-century and two wickets. He finished as the leading run-scorer with 130 runs across the series.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nawaz, Saim lead Pakistan to victory in first T20I against West Indies |url=https://www.pcb.com.pk/news-detail/nawaz-saim-lead-pakistan-to-victory-in-first-t20i-against-west-indies.html |access-date=2025-08-07 |website=Pakistan Cricket Board}}</ref>

In the [[2025 Asia Cup]], Ayub endured a poor run with the bat, including three consecutive ducks, but impressed with his off-spin bowling, taking six wickets at an economy rate of 5.6, including three against [[India national cricket team|India]]. His performances prompted analysts to suggest he could evolve into an [[all-rounder]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Rasool |first=Danyal |date=20 September 2025 |title=The myth and math of Saim Ayub |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/asia-cup-2025-pakistan-the-myth-and-math-of-saim-ayub-1503831 |access-date=20 September 2025 |website=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> Following the tournament, he became the ICC's No. 1-ranked all-rounder in men's T20Is.<ref>{{Cite news |date=1 October 2025 |title=ICC T20I rankings: Saim Ayub new No.1 allrounder; Abhishek Sharma attains career-high rating points |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/icc-t20i-rankings-saim-ayub-new-no-1-allrounder-abhishek-sharma-attains-career-high-rating-points-1505182 |access-date=1 October 2025 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

In October 2025, in the second [[South African cricket team in Pakistan in 2025–26|home T20I against South Africa]], Saim hit 72 (not out) off 38 deliveries, making his first T20I fifty at home. He was noted for his aggressive 360-degree innings, punishing width and short deliveries while mixing power with improvisation.<ref>{{cite web |last=Moonda |first=Firdose |date=31 October 2025 |title=Mirza, Faheem and Ayub star as marauding Pakistan make it 1-1 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/south-africa-in-pakistan-2025-26-1501888/pakistan-vs-south-africa-2nd-t20i-1501896/match-report |access-date=1 November 2025 |website=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> During the ODI home series against South Africa, Ayub hit two consecutive ODI half-centuries, 53 (66) in the second ODI and 77 (70) in the third and last ODI of the series, which Pakistan won, Ayub's knock being instrumental in the chase.<ref>{{cite web |last=Brar |first=Hemant |date=8 November 2025 |title=Abrar, Ayub deliver as Pakistan outplay South Africa to take series |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/south-africa-in-pakistan-2025-26-1501888/pakistan-vs-south-africa-3rd-odi-1501900/match-report |access-date=8 November 2025 |website=ESPNcricinfo |publisher=ESPN}}</ref>

In January 2026, In the 1st T20I of [[Australian cricket team in Pakistan in 2025–26|Australia's tour of Pakistan]], Pakistan recorded a comfortable victory, led by an all-round performance from Ayub, who scored 40 in 22 deliveries later took 2 wickets for 29 runs. He was declared Player of the Match.<ref>{{cite web
 |last=Rasool|first=Danyal|title=All-round Ayub hands Pakistan comfortable win|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/australia-in-pakistan-2025-26-1519629/pakistan-vs-australia-1st-t20i-1519636/match-report|website=ESPNcricinfo|publisher=ESPN|date=29 January 2026|access-date=1 February 2026}}</ref>

=== Injury ===
In January 2025, during the [[Pakistani cricket team in South Africa in 2024–25|second Test against South Africa]] in [[Newlands Cricket Ground|Cape Town]], Saim Ayub fractured his right ankle while fielding, ruling him out of the remaining matches on that tour.<ref>{{cite web |title=Update on Saim Ayub's injury |url=https://www.pcb.com.pk/press-release-detail/update-on-saim-ayub-s-injury.html |access-date=2025-01-10 |work=Pakistan Cricket Board}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Ayub ruled out of Cape Town Test after suffering ankle injury |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/43269805/pakistan-opener-saim-ayub-ruled-out-of-cape-town-test-suffering-ankle-injury |access-date=2025-01-10 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> The Pakistan Cricket Board later confirmed that he would also miss the [[2025 ICC Champions Trophy]], prescribing a rehabilitation period of approximately ten weeks.<ref>{{cite web |title=Saim Ayub ruled out of Champions Trophy 2025 (PCB confirms) |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/saim-ayub-ruled-out-of-champions-trophy-2025-pcb-confirms-1472319 |access-date=2025-02-07 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Pakistan issue update on star batter ruled out of Champions Trophy |url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/tournaments/champions-trophy/news/pakistan-issue-update-on-star-batter-ruled-out-of-champions-trophy |access-date=2025-02-07 |work=ICC}}</ref>

Ayub returned to international action during Pakistan's T20I series in the [[Pakistani cricket team in the West Indies in 2025|West Indies in August 2025]], where he featured in the first match and played a key role in the team's victory.<ref>{{cite web |title=Nawaz, Saim lead Pakistan to victory in first T20I against West Indies |url=https://www.pcb.com.pk/news-detail/nawaz-saim-lead-pakistan-to-victory-in-first-t20i-against-west-indies.html |access-date=2025-08-07 |work=Pakistan Cricket Board}}</ref>

== Playing style ==
Ayub is famous for playing a distinctive "''no-look shot''", in which he looks away from the ball while executing a stroke towards the leg side. He first played the shot during a domestic T20 match in 2022, which he later described as an unplanned improvisation based on the field placement.<ref>{{cite web |title=Saim Ayub opens up about 'no-look' shot |url=https://a-sports.tv/saim-ayub-opens-up-about-no-look-shot/ |website=A Sports |date=25 March 2023 |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref> The shot became popular after he used it in the [[Pakistan Super League]] and the [[Quaid-e-Azam Trophy]], notably hitting no-look sixes in both tournaments.<ref>{{cite web |title=Watch: Saim Ayub nails stunning no-look scoop-flick for six in record opening blitz with Babar Azam |url=https://www.wisden.com/amp/series/hbl-pakistan-super-league/cricket-news/watch-saim-ayub-no-look-scoop-flick-six-record-opening-blitz-babar-azam-peshawar-zalmi |website=Wisden |date=26 February 2023 |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Watch: Saim Ayub manufactures astonishing no-look six over fine leg in Quaid-e-Azam final double century |url=https://www.wisden.com/cricket-news/watch-saim-ayub-manufactures-astonishing-no-look-six-over-fine-leg-in-quaid-e-azam-final-double-century |website=Wisden |date=28 December 2023 |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref> According to [[Dawn (newspaper)|''Dawn'']], the shot has since become associated with his batting style.<ref>{{cite news |title=Confident Saim wants to create his own legacy |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1746438/confident-saim-wants-to-create-his-own-legacy |work=Dawn |date=4 April 2023 |access-date=13 October 2025}}</ref>
