'''Samuel William Billings''' (born 15 June 1991) is an English professional [[cricket]]er.<ref name="tory27jan17" /> Billings is a right-handed [[Batsman (cricket)|batsman]] who fields as a [[wicket-keeper]]. He was born at [[Pembury]] in [[Kent]] and has played for [[Kent County Cricket Club]] teams since he was eight years old, making his senior debut for the First XI in 2011. In October 2017, he was appointed as the vice-captain of the team, before being appointed as captain in January 2018, replacing [[Sam Northeast]].<ref name=ko10oct17 /><ref name=bbc17jan18>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/42718988 Sam Billings: England limited-overs player replaces Sam Northeast as Kent captain], [[BBC Sport]], 17 January 2018. Retrieved 30 January 2018.</ref> He served as the club's captain until the end of the 2023 season when he resigned, although he retained the captaincy of the club's [[Twenty20 cricket]] team.<ref name=bbc12oct23>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/67092095 Kent: Daniel Bell-Drummond appointed as club captain to replace Sam Billings], [[BBC Sport]], 12 October 2023. Retrieved 12 October 2023.</ref>

Billings has appeared mainly in limited overs formats for the [[England cricket team]] and made his [[Test cricket]] debut in January 2022. He has played [[Twenty20]] franchise cricket in the [[Pakistan Super League]], [[Indian Premier League]], [[Bangladesh Premier League]] and in the [[Big Bash League]] in Australia and captained [[Oval Invincibles]] in all four seasons of [[The Hundred (cricket)|The Hundred]].

==Early and personal life==
Billings was born at [[Pembury]] in [[Kent]] and grew up on his family's farm in the north of the county.<ref name=tory27jan17>Liew J (2017) [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/cricket/2017/01/27/far-typical-cricketer-posh-sam-billings-reaping-rewards-studies/ Far from the typical cricketer, 'posh' Sam Billings is reaping the rewards of his studies], ''[[The Daily Telegraph]]'', 27 January 2017.</ref><ref name=ci31jan15>[http://www.espncricinfo.com/england/content/story/825185.html The inevitable rise of Billings], ESPNcricinfo, 31 January 2015. Retrieved 28 November 2015.</ref> He developed as a good all-round sportsman, playing tennis for Kent and being offered a trial for [[Tottenham Hotspur Football Club]] after scoring a hat-trick against the team's academy team whilst playing for [[Corinthian F.C. (Kent)|Corinthian under-14s]].<ref name=db>Bauckham D (2016) [https://dbauckham.exposure.co/the-last-corinthian The Last Corinthian], 26 October 2016. Retrieved 29 November 2016.</ref> He also played [[Rackets (sport)|racquets]], squash, and rugby.<ref name=ci31jan15 /><ref name=gran7may15>[https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2015/may/07/sam-billings-england-ireland-dublin-ab-de-villiers-international Sam Billings looks to De Villiers' method as he prepares for England debut], ''[[The Guardian]]'', 7 May 2015. Retrieved 28 November 2015.</ref> His grandfather, Ron Billings, was a racquets champion and his cousin, Tom Billings, has been world champion of the sport.<ref name=ci31jan15 /><ref name=gran7may15 /> Billings attributes racquets with helping to develop his batting skills, in particular his hand-eye coordination.<ref name=gran7may15 />

Billings attended [[New Beacon School]] in Sevenoaks, and then [[Haileybury College]] in Hertfordshire, appearing regularly for their cricket XI throughout his school career. He studied for a degree in Sport and Exercise Science at [[Loughborough University]].<ref name=lboro>[https://web.archive.org/web/20111016051513/http://www.loughboroughmccu.com/player-profiles/sam-billings Player profile: Sam Billings], [[Loughborough MCCU]]. Retrieved 17 August 2011.</ref><ref name=ci12jan17>MacPherson W (2017) [http://www.espncricinfo.com/india-v-england-2016-17/content/story/1077075.html Unflagging and zealous, Billings seeks new peaks], ESPNcricinfo, 12 January 2017. Retrieved 12 January 2017.</ref> Billings has said that he was "nowhere near good enough"<ref name=ci12jan17/> to become a professional cricketer before his time at university and credits it with encouraging him to work hard to develop his talent.<ref name=ci12jan17/>

==Early career==
Billings made his [[first-class cricket|first-class]] debut for [[Loughborough MCC University|Loughborough MCCU]] against [[Northamptonshire County Cricket Club|Northamptonshire]] in 2011. He made a further first-class appearance for the team in 2011, against [[Leicestershire County Cricket Club|Leicestershire]].<ref name=ca>[https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/119/119895/119895.html Sam Billings], CricketArchive. Retrieved 17 August 2011. {{subscription required}}</ref> In his four first-class matches for Loughborough MCCU, he scored 321 runs at an [[batting average (cricket)|average]] of 45.85, with a highest score of 131.<ref name=ca /> This score came in his debut match against Northamptonshire.<ref name=ci14aug16>Harman J (2016) [http://www.espncricinfo.com/magazine/content/story/1045585.html Play it again, Sam], ESPNcricinfo, 14 August 2016 (previously published in ''All Out Cricket''). Retrieved 25 August 2016.</ref>

==Kent career==
Whilst at university Billings was also a member of the [[Kent County Cricket Club|Kent]] squad, and he made his debut for the county in May 2011 in a first-class match against his university team, [[Loughborough MCCU]].<ref name=ca /> During the [[2011 English cricket season|2011 season]] he also made his [[List A cricket|List A]] debut for Kent against the [[Netherlands national cricket team|Netherlands]] in the [[2011 Clydesdale Bank 40]], standing in for regular wicket-keeper [[Geraint Jones]]. Billings made three further List A appearances in the 2011 season, as well as playing in four matches in the [[2011 Friends Provident t20]].<ref name=ca /> After leading the county in one-day runs scored in 2012, Billings replaced former England wicket-keeper Jones in Kent's [[2013 Friends Life t20]] campaign.<ref name=bbc4jul13>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/23169306 Sam Billings aiming to seize FLt20 opportunity], BBC Sport, 4 July 2013. Retrieved 16 November 2013.</ref> At the end of the season he kept wicket in the [[County Championship]], breaking Jones' string of 115 consecutive Championship appearances for Kent<ref name=times17sep13>[https://www.thetimes.com/sport/cricket/article/kent-replace-geraint-jones-with-sam-billings-0pz83v30qq7 Kent replace Geraint Jones with Sam Billings], ''[[The Times]]'', 17 November 2013. Retrieved 25 August 2016.</ref> before playing [[Sydney Grade Cricket]] for [[Penrith District Cricket Club]] during the 2013–14 English winter.<ref name=dt8nov13>Cheng K (2013) [http://www.dailytelegraph.com.au/newslocal/west/english-county-cricketer-sam-billings-arrives-in-penrith/story-fngr8j33-1226755718875 English county cricketer Sam Billings arrives in Penrith], ''Penrith Press'', 8 November 2013. Retrieved 29 November 2016.</ref>

Billings became the first choice wicket-keeper for Kent in the 2014 season. He played in the champion county match in [[Abu Dhabi]] at the beginning of the 2015 season before scoring 693 runs at an average of 29.80 in the [[2015 County Championship]] season and making his England One Day and T20 debuts. He was awarded his Kent [[county cap]] in August 2015 during the annual [[Canterbury Cricket Week]] and signed a contract extension with Kent, in January 2016.<ref name=ko27jan16>Hoad, Alex (2016). [http://www.kentonline.co.uk/canterbury/sport/new-deal-for-billings-69886/ England wicketkeeper-batsman Sam Billings has signed a contract extension at Kent], ''Kent Online'', 27 January 2016. Retrieved 11 June 2016.</ref><ref name=capped>[http://www.kentcricket.co.uk/news/daniel-bell-drummond-and-sam-billings-awarded-county-caps Daniel Bell-Drummond and Sam Billings awarded county caps], [[Kent County Cricket Club]], 5 August 2015. Retrieved 30 September 2015.</ref><ref name=bbc27jan16>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/35418637 England's Sam Billings signs Kent contract extension], BBC Sport, 27 January 2016. Retrieved 30 January 2016.</ref>

After spending the winter playing [[one-day international]] cricket with England and featuring in both the [[Pakistan Super League]] (PSL) and [[Indian Premier League]] (IPL) T20 competitions, Billings returned to Kent at the end of May having missed six County Championship matches as well as the start of both one-day competitions.<ref name=ko2jun16>[http://www.kentonline.co.uk/canterbury/sport/billings-wants-to-make-an-96752/ Kent and England wicketkeeper batsman Sam Billings hopes to add to club's winning formula after return from IPL], ''[[Kent Online]]'', 2 June 2016. Retrieved 25 August 2016.</ref> During the 2016 season he became only the second Kent wicket-keeper to take seven catches in an innings and the tenth to claim nine dismissals in a first-class match, both one short of equalling the record for the county,<ref name=ci3aug16>[http://www.espncricinfo.com/county-cricket-2016/content/story/1042021.html Claydon and Billings combine to hand Kent control], ESPNcricinfo, 3 August 2016. Retrieved 7 August 2016.</ref><ref name=bbc3aug16>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/36965501 County Championship: Kent's Mitch Claydon takes five Worcestershire wickets], BBC Sport, 3 August 2016. Retrieved 7 August 2016.</ref><ref name=ci6aug16>[http://www.espncricinfo.com/county-cricket-2016/content/story/1043271.html Kent victory dents Worcestershire promotion hopes], ESPNcricinfo, 6 August 2016. Retrieved 7 August 2016.</ref> and made his highest score in first-class cricket.<ref name=ci25aug16>Ehantharajah V (2016) [http://www.espncricinfo.com/county-cricket-2016/content/story/1050253.html Billings takes satisfaction in epic show of restraint], ESPNcricinfo, 25 August 2016. Retrieved 25 August 2016.</ref>

Billings spent the following winter playing for [[English cricket team in Bangladesh in 2016–17|England in Bangladesh]], [[Sydney Sixers]] in the [[Big Bash League]] and for [[English cricket team in India in 2016–17|England again in India]] and the [[English cricket team in the West Indies in 2016–17|West Indies]] as well as once again playing in the PSL and IPL.<ref name=ci11jan17>Venugopal A (2017) [http://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/18450027/sam-billings-the-job-job Sam Billings is up for the job – any job], ESPNcricinfo, 11 January 2017. Retrieved 11 October 2017.</ref><ref name=ci4may17>McGlashan A (2017) [http://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/19309751/sam-billings-back-ipl-hail-england-buzz Billings back from IPL to hail England 'buzz'], ESPNcricinfo, 4 May 2017. Retrieved 11 October 2017.</ref> England duty again kept him away from Kent for parts of the 2017 season and he played in only six of the county's County Championship matches during the season, although he was ever present during the [[2017 NatWest t20 Blast|T20 Blast]].<ref name=bbc10oct17>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/41573273 Sam Billings: England wicketkeeper-batsman extends Kent contract], [[BBC Sport]], 10 October 2017. Retrieved 11 October 2017.</ref><ref name=times19mar17>Wilde, Simon (2017). [https://www.thetimes.com/sport/cricket/article/billings-is-ready-to-shine-dl5qbq3bj Billings is ready to shine], ''[[The Times]]'', 19 March 2017. Retrieved 31 October 2017.</ref> He averaged 43.66 in the Championship games he played and captained the team in a tour match against the West Indies in August.<ref name=bbc10oct17 /><ref name=ko10oct17>Hoad, Alex (2017). [http://www.kentonline.co.uk/canterbury/sport/new-deal-for-billings-133428/ Kent Cricket wicketkeeper-batsman Sam Billings signs new deal with the club], ''[[Kent Online]]'', 10 October 2017. Retrieved 11 October 2017.</ref> At the end of the season he signed a new contract with Kent and was appointed officially as the team's vice-captain.<ref name=ko10oct17 /><ref name=bbc10oct17 />

Following [[Sam Northeast]]'s removal as Kent captain in early 2018 Billings was appointed to the post as his replacement, despite some disquiet about his participation in the [[2018 Indian Premier League]]. This meant that he missed the first part of the County Championship and One Day Cup seasons.<ref name=ko10oct17 /> The team was captained by [[Joe Denly]] in Billings' absence. Later in the season Billings once again signed a contract extension.<ref name=bbc10jul18>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/44785619 Sam Billings and Joe Denly: Kent captain and vice-captain sign new contracts], [[BBC Sport]], 10 July 2018. Retrieved 12 September 2018.</ref>

Billings captained Kent Spitfires to the [[2021 T20 Blast]] title, beating [[Somerset County Cricket Club|Somerset]] in the final by 25 runs to win the tournament and their second domestic T20 title.<ref name=bbc18sep21>Scott G (2021) [https://www.bbc.com/sport/cricket/58609102 Kent beat Somerset to win T20 Blast], [[BBC Sport]], 18 September 2021. Retrieved 26 July 2022.</ref>

==International career==
[[File:England vs. New Zealand 2015 (31).jpg|thumb|right|Billings batting for England against New Zealand in 2015.]]
Billings was first called into the England Performance Programme in 2014 and took part in a training camp in Sri Lanka during the English winter.<ref name=ci12dec14>Hopps S (2014) [http://www.espncricinfo.com/england/content/story/809739.html Billings replaces Kieswetter in England 30], ESPNcricinfo, 12 December 2014. Retrieved 15 October 2017.</ref><ref name=kccc2dec14>[http://www.kentcricket.co.uk/news/riley-and-billings-play-in-england-performance-programme-win-in-sri-lanka/ Riley and Billings play in England Performance Programme win in Sri Lanka], [[Kent County Cricket Club]], 14 December 2014.</ref><ref name=kn19dec14>Miles T (2014) [http://www.kentnews.co.uk/sport/kent-s-sam-billings-chuffed-at-joining-world-cup-squad-1-3891846 Kent's Sam Billings 'chuffed' at joining World Cup squad], ''Kent News'', 19 December 2014. Retrieved 15 October 2017.</ref> He had played for an [[England and Wales Cricket Board|ECB]] under-16 team in 2006 and for England age group teams at under-17 and under-18 level before touring Bangladesh with the [[England under-19 cricket team|England under-19 team]] in 2009.<ref name=ca /><ref name=kccc9aug09>[http://www.kentcricket.co.uk/news/goodman-and-billings-to-be-monitored-by-england-u19s/ Goodman and Billings to be monitored by England U19s], [[Kent County Cricket Club]], 9 August 2017. Retrieved 15 October 2017.</ref><ref name=ind11jan17>Edwards R (2017) [https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/cricket/sam-billings-interview-england-india-t20-a7522111.html 'The more you play with the best, the better you become' – Sam Billings is relishing life at the top], ''[[The Independent]]'', 11 January 2017. Retrieved 15 October 2017.</ref>

He was named in the squad for the [[England Lions cricket team]] in the 2014/15 off-season in South Africa,<ref name=ci12dec14 /> making his debut and scoring 53 against a Gauteng Invitation XI in January 2015 and going on to play for the Lions in four of the five unofficial [[one-day international]] matches on the tour.<ref name=ct28oct14>Riley and Billings named in England Lions squads, ''Canterbury Times'', 28 October 2014.</ref><ref name=gran7jan15>[https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2015/jan/07/jonathan-trott-england-lions-gauteng-south-africa Jonathan Trott hits unbeaten 79 in England Lions draw against Gauteng], ''[[The Guardian]]'', 7 January 2015. Retrieved 28 November 2015.</ref> In late 2014 he had been named in the provisional squad for the [[England cricket team]] before the [[2015 Cricket World Cup]], replacing the injured [[Craig Kieswetter]],<ref name=ci12dec14 /><ref name=kn19dec14 /><ref name=bbc12dec14>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/30447341 Sam Billings added to England's provisional World Cup squad], BBC sport website, 12 December 2014. Retrieved 28 November 2015.</ref> but did not feature in the final squad for the tournament.

===International debut===
Billings made his senior [[England cricket team|England]] international debut in an ODI against [[New Zealand cricket team in England in 2015|the touring New Zealand team]] in June 2015, playing as a batsman and scoring three runs.<ref name=ci9jun15>[http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/743943.html New Zealand tour of England, 1st ODI: England v New Zealand at Birmingham, Jun 9, 2015], ESPNcricinfo, 9 June 2015. Retrieved 9 June 2015.</ref> After playing in all five ODIs during the series, he made his [[Twenty20 International]] (T20I) debut on 23 June 2015, scoring 21 runs.<ref name=ci25jun15>[http://www.espncricinfo.com/england-v-new-zealand-2015/content/story/890557.html Electric England sweep to victory], ESPNcricinfo, 25 June 2015. Retrieved 26 November 2015.</ref> He was an unused member of the ODI squad against [[Australia cricket team in England in 2015|Australia]] later the same summer before playing in the only T20I against the Australians at the end of August.

After the New Zealand series, Billings was a regular in England ODI and T20I squads, but played infrequently for two years, never appearing in two consecutive England ODI teams until March 2017.<ref name=tory4mar17>Berry S (2017) [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/cricket/2017/03/04/west-indies-vs-england-fast-learner-sam-billings-add-substance/ West Indies vs England: Fast-learner Sam Billings out to add substance to style], ''[[Daily Telegraph]]'', 4 March 2017. Retrieved 15 October 2017.</ref> He made his England debut as a wicketkeeper in the first T20I against [[Pakistan national cricket team|Pakistan]] in [[Dubai International Cricket Stadium|Dubai]] in November 2015. He made his maiden international half-century in the match,<ref name=ko27nov15>Gidley A (2015) [http://www.kentonline.co.uk/canterbury/sport/billings-stars-for-england-in-47035/ Sam Billings hits first international half century in exciting style as England beat Pakistan in Dubai], ''Kent Online'', 27 November 2015. Retrieved 11 June 2016.</ref> reaching his fifty in 24 balls, before being run out for 53 off the last ball of the England innings. He took two catches and completed a stumping during the Pakistan innings as England won by 14 runs.<ref name=ci26nov15>[http://www.espncricinfo.com/pakistan-v-england-2015-16/content/story/944471.html Billings and Plunkett inspire England win], ESPNcricinfo, 26 November 2015. Retrieved 26 November 2015.</ref><ref name=bbc26nov15>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/34938408 Sam Billings leads England to T20 win over Pakistan in Dubai], BBC sport website, 26 November 2015. Retrieved 28 November 2015.</ref><ref name=ecb26nov15>[http://www.ecb.co.uk/news/articles/billings-revels-match-winning-knock Billings revels in match-winning knock], England and Wales Cricket Board, 26 November 2015. Retrieved 28 November 2015.</ref> He was adjudged man of the match for his performance during the match.<ref name=kccc26nov15>[http://www.kentcricket.co.uk/news/billings-wins-man-of-the-match-with-maiden-england-50 Billings wins man-of-the-match with maiden England 50], Kent County Cricket Club, 26 November 2015. Retrieved 28 November 2015.</ref>

He played for the Lions against [[Pakistan A cricket team|Pakistan A]] in Dubai in January 2016,<ref name=ko27jan16 /> against South Africa in 2016 and was selected for the England squad for the [[2016 World Twenty20]] competition. He did not make an appearance for England during the competition, other than as a substitute fielder.<ref name=bbc10feb16>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/35539301 England World T20 squad: Liam Dawson in, Chris Woakes out], BBC Sport website, 10 February 2016. Retrieved 10 February 2016.</ref> He was named in a 30-man England Performance Squad for the 2016 domestic season<ref name=kccc12may16>[http://kentcricket.co.uk/news/sam-billings-in-england-performance-squad Sam Billings in England Performance squad], [[Kent County Cricket Club]], 12 May 2016. Retrieved 18 May 2016.</ref> and played for the full England T20 team against [[Sri Lankan cricket team in England and Ireland in 2016|Sri Lanka in July 2016]]<ref name=kccc13jun16>[http://www.kentcricket.co.uk/news/sam-billings-in-england-t20-squad-to-play-sri-lanka Sam Billings in England T20 squad to play Sri Lanka], [[Kent County Cricket Club]], 13 June 2016. Retrieved 7 July 2016.</ref> and for the Lions team against Pakistan A and [[Sri Lanka A cricket team|Sri Lanka A]], scoring his highest [[List A cricket]] score of 175 against Pakistan at [[St Lawrence Ground|Canterbury]],<ref name=ci24jul16>[http://www.espncricinfo.com/england/content/story/1038829.html Billings 175 sets up comprehensive Lions win], ESPNcricinfo, 24 July 2016. Retrieved 13 October 2016.</ref> before [[English cricket team in Bangladesh in 2016–17|touring Bangladesh with the England One Day International team]] in October, scoring his maiden ODI half-century with a score of 62 in the final match of the series batting as a replacement [[opening batsman]], to help England to a 2–1 series win.<ref name=ci12jan17 /><ref name=ci11oct16>Hopps D (2016) [http://www.espncricinfo.com/bangladesh-v-england-2016-17/content/story/1061352.html Duckett and Billings show their promise to earn series win], ESPNcricinfo, 11 October 2016. Retrieved 13 October 2016.</ref><ref name=ci12oct16>Isam M (2016) [http://www.espncricinfo.com/bangladesh-v-england-2016-17/content/story/1061488.html Buttler praises stand-in openers], ESPNcricinfo, 12 October 2016. Retrieved 13 October 2016.</ref><ref name=ko12oct16>Hoad, Alex (2016). [http://www.kentonline.co.uk/canterbury/sport/billings-seizes-england-chance-103998/ Kent's Sam Billings scores 62 as opener for England to help secure four-wicket win and series victory in Bangladesh], ''[[Kent Online]]'', 12 October 2016. Retrieved 16 October 2016.</ref>

In early 2017 Billings was part of the [[England cricket team in India in 2016-17|England ODI and T20 squad which toured India]]. He played in the opening List A match of the tour against [[India A cricket team|India A]] again as a specialist batsman, scoring 93 runs,<ref name=ci10jan17>Venugopal A (2017) [http://www.espncricinfo.com/india-v-england-2016-17/content/story/1076919.html Billings' 93 helps England XI hunt down 305], ESPNcricinfo, 10 January 2017. Retrieved 11 January 2017.</ref> and in an ODI and T20 match on the tour<ref name=tory27jan17 /> before playing back to back ODI matches for the first time since his debut series against the [[England cricket team in the West Indies in 2017|West Indies]].<ref name=tory4mar17 /><ref name=gran4mar17>Martin A (2017) [https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2017/mar/04/sam-billings-england-alex-hales-west-indies-second-odi Sam Billings up for a scrap to keep his England spot from Alex Hales], ''[[The Guardian]]'', 4 March 2017. Retrieved 15 October 2017.</ref> He was an unused member of the England squad for the [[2017 Champions Trophy]] but played against [[Irish cricket team in England in 2017|Ireland]], [[South African cricket team in England in 2017|South Africa]] and [[West Indies cricket team in England in 2017|West Indies]] during the summer of 2017.<ref name=cilist>[http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/player/297628.html?class=11;template=results;type=allround;view=match SW Billings, combined Test, ODI and T20I records], ESPNcricinfo. Retrieved 15 October 2017.</ref> In early 2018 he joined the [[English cricket team in Australia in 2017–18|England squad in Australia]] for the ODI element of their tour, although he did not appear in any of the matches, before playing in the [[2017–18 Trans-Tasman Tri-Series]] T20 matches against Australia and New Zealand in February. He was, again, an unused member of the [[English cricket team in New Zealand in 2017–18|England squad for the ODI series against New Zealand]] which followed.

In October 2019, Billings was named as the vice-captain and first-choice wicket-keeper in England's T20I squad for their [[English cricket team in New Zealand in 2019–20|tour of New Zealand]].<ref name=ci24oct19>Dobbell G (2019) [https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/27916968/sam-billings-named-england-t20-vice-captain-new-zealand-tour Sam Billings named England's T20 vice-captain for New Zealand tour], ESPNcricinfo, 24 October 2019. Retrieved 24 October 2019.</ref> He played in all five T20I matches on the tour, although he only scored 34 runs in his five innings and was not selected for the limited-overs team [[English cricket team in South Africa in 2019–20|in South Africa early 2020]].<ref name=ci3jun20>Baynes V (2020) [https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/29258601/sam-billings-want-pigeonholed-white-ball-player.-better-that Sam Billings: 'Don't want to be pigeonholed as a white-ball player. I'm better than that'], ESPNcricinfo, 3 June 2020. Retrieved 24 June 2020.</ref> In May 2020, he was named in a group of 55 players to begin [[Behind closed doors (sport)|behind closed doors]] training ahead of international fixtures starting in England following the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref name=ecb29may20>[https://www.ecb.co.uk/england/men/news/1674230/england-men-confirm-back-to-training-group England Men confirm back-to-training group], [[England and Wales Cricket Board]], 29 May 2020. Retrieved 29 May 2020.</ref> He was not selected in the Test team to face the West Indies but in July was named in the squad for the ODI series [[Irish cricket team in England in 2020|against Ireland]]<ref>[https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/29433420/injured-chris-jordan-misses-england-odi-squad-face-ireland Injured Chris Jordan misses England's ODI squad to face Ireland], ESPNcricinfo, 9 July 2020. Retrieved 9 July 2020.</ref><ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/53553282 England v Ireland: David Willey & Reece Topley recalled for ODI series], [[BBC Sport]], 27 July 2020. Retrieved 27 July 2020.</ref> After playing in all three matches against Ireland without being dismissed and making scores of 67 and 46,<ref name=ht4aug20>[https://www.hindustantimes.com/cricket/ireland-will-learn-a-lot-from-this-series-against-england-panesar/story-OxBCPBklT1Xg4OfdEOinAI.html Sam Billings should be an automatic selection, says Panesar], ''[[Hindustan Times]]'', 4 August 2020. Retrieved 13 September 2020.</ref> he played in the three T20I matches against the touring Pakistanis. Following the return of more established players for matches at the end of the summer against Australia, Billings played in only the last T20I of the three-match series, but was selected for the opening ODI. He went on to make his first senior international century in the match, scoring 118 runs,<ref name=ci11sep20>Gardner A (2020) [https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/19496/report/1198238/england-vs-australia-1st-odi-england-v-australia-2020 Australia close out victory for 1–0 series lead despite Sam Billings hundred], ESPNcricinfo, 11 September 2020. Retrieved 12 September 2020.</ref><ref name=bbc11sep20/><ref name=times12sep20>Wilde S (2020) [https://www.thetimes.com/sport/cricket/article/brave-battle-ends-in-defeat-for-sam-billings-despite-innings-of-his-life-6wxjtgnd5 Lone battle ends in defeat for Sam Billings despite innings of his life], ''[[The Times]]'', 12 September 2020. Retrieved 12 September 2020. {{subscription required}}</ref> before playing in both of the other matches in the series. ''[[Wisden]]'' named him in their ODI team of 2020, the only member of the England team to be selected.<ref>[https://www.wisden.com/cricket-news/2020-in-review-wisdens-odi-team-of-the-year 2020 in Review: Wisden's ODI Team of the Year], ''[[Wisden]]'' online, 13 December 2020. Retrieved 17 December 2020.</ref>

===Test cricketer===
Following an injury to [[Ben Foakes]] in May 2021, Billings was added to England's [[Test cricket|Test]] squad for the first time ahead of the [[New Zealand cricket team in England in 2021|series against New Zealand]].<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/57256555 England v New Zealand: Ben Foakes out, Haseeb Hameed and Sam Billings into hosts' squad], [[BBC Sport]], 26 May 2021. Retrieved 26 May 2021.</ref> He did not play in either of the matches in the series but in August was again added to England's Test squad, this time as wicket-keeper cover for the fourth Test [[Indian cricket team in England in 2021|against India]].<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/58336156 England v India: Jos Buttler to miss fourth Test at Kia Oval], [[BBC Sport]], 29 August 2021. Retrieved 29 August 2021.</ref> In September 2021, Billings was named in England's squad for the [[2021 ICC Men's T20 World Cup]].<ref>[https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/t20-world-cup-2021-tymal-mills-makes-englands-t20-world-cup-squad-no-return-for-ben-stokes-1276997 Tymal Mills makes England's T20 World Cup squad, no return for Ben Stokes], ESPNcricinfo, 9 September 2021. Retrieved 9 September 2021.</ref>

Billings made his Test debut for England in the final Test of the [[2021–22 Ashes series]]. Following injuries to both of the team's wicket-keepers, [[Jos Buttler]] and [[Jonny Bairstow]], Billings was added to the team as a replacement, having been playing in the Big Bash League for Sydney Thunder, driving more than {{convert|500|mi|km}} from [[Brisbane]] as a precaution against [[COVID-19]].<ref name=bbc8jan22>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/59912811 Ashes: Sam Billings drives 500 miles to join England squad], [[BBC Sport]], 8 January 2022. Retrieved 25 June 2022.</ref> He made his debut at the [[Bellerive Oval]] in Hobart scoring 29 runs in England's first innings and taking five catches in Australia's second in a debut which was described as composed.<ref name=ci15jan22a>Baynes V (2022) [https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/england-in-australia-2021-22-1263452/australia-vs-england-5th-test-1263466/match-report-2 Pat Cummins takes four as England stutter again on 17-wicket day], ESPNcricinfo, 15 January 2022. Retrieved 23 January 2022.</ref><ref name=ci15jan22b>Miller A (2022) [https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/men-ashes-2021-22-england-positives-negated-by-latest-bout-of-brittle-batting-1297102 England positives negated by latest bout of brittle batting], ESPNcricinfo, 15 January 2022. Retrieved 23 January 2022.</ref><ref name=ci18jan22>Miller A (2022) [https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ashes-inquest-who-will-captain-england-in-the-caribbean-1297424 Ashes inquest: Who will captain England in the Caribbean?], ESPNcricinfo, 18 January 2022. Retrieved 23 January 2022.</ref> After being "overlooked" for selection for [[England cricket team in the Netherlands in 2022|England's ODI series against the Netherlands]] in June 2022,<ref name=ci31may22>Roller M (2022) [https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/netherlands-vs-england-2022-sam-billings-overlooked-as-england-name-strong-squad-for-netherlands-odis-1317714 Sam Billings overlooked as England name strong squad for Netherlands ODIs], ESPNcricinfo, 31 May 2022. Retrieved 28 June 2022.</ref> he was again called into the England Test team as a replacement, this time during a match against the [[New Zealand cricket team in England in 2022|touring New Zealanders]] after [[Ben Foakes]] had tested positive for COVID-19 during the match. Billings took Foakes' place as the team's wicket-keeper on the fourth day of the third Test of the series at [[Headingley Cricket Ground|Headingley]].<ref name=bbc26jun22>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/61939737 England v New Zealand: Ben Foakes out of third Test after testing positive for Covid-19], [[BBC Sport]], 26 June 2022. Retrieved 26 June 2022.</ref> He was retained in the Test squad for the single Test to be played at the start of July against India. This match had been postponed in September 2021 due to an outbreak of COVID-19 in the Indian squad.<ref name=bbc27jun21>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/61958488 England v India: Sam Billings added to squad for fifth Test at Edgbaston], [[BBC Sport]], 27 June 2022. Retrieved 28 June 2022.</ref>

After missing out on selection for England's squad for the [[2022 T20 World Cup]] in October 2022, Billings returned to the England ODI team for their [[English cricket team in Australia in 2022–23|series against Australia]] in November.<ref name=bbc15nov22>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/63635347 Sam Billings: England wicketkeeper on IPL and congested schedule], [[BBC Sport]], 15 November 2022. Retrieved 20 November 2022.</ref> He was the team's top-scorer in the second ODI of the series, showing "the necessary grit" to build an innings of 77 runs after England had lost early wickets.<ref name=bbc19nov22>Drury S (2022) [https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/63686825 Australia v England: Hosts clinch ODI series win with victory in Sydney], [[BBC Sport]], 19 November 2022. Retrieved 20 November 2022.</ref>

==Twenty20 franchise leagues==
Billings is a regular participant in [[Twenty20]] franchise leagues around the world. He has played for teams in the [[Pakistan Super League]], Australian [[Big Bash]] and [[Indian Premier League]] and was scheduled to play in the first season of the abortive South African [[T20 Global League]].<ref name=ht11apr18>Ananthanarayanan N (2018) [https://www.hindustantimes.com/cricket/ipl-2018-england-s-sam-billings-for-fast-forward-t20-leagues-as-counties-fume/story-xIZkNVamDqs5k66qF41S3L.html IPL 2018: England's Sam Billings for 'fast forward' T20 leagues as Counties fume], ''[[Hindustan Times]]'', 18 April 2018. Retrieved 12 September 2018.</ref>

In December 2015, Billings was selected by [[Islamabad United]] in the [[2016 Pakistan Super League]] draft, the first of three overseas Twenty20 leagues he took part in during 2016.<ref name=ci12jan17 /><ref name=ko22dec15>[http://www.kentonline.co.uk/tunbridge-wells/sport/billings-gets-pakistan-call-48182/ Kent and England star Sam Billings drafted by Islamabad United ahead of first Pakistan Super League in UAE in February], Kent Online, 22 December 2015. Retrieved 25 January 2016.</ref> The tournament took place in the [[United Arab Emirates]] in February 2016 and was the inaugural season of the competition. Billings played in five matches for Islamabad, scoring 34 runs with a top score of 26, but saw the opportunity to learn from players such as Australian Test wicket-keeper [[Brad Haddin]] as "invaluable".<ref name=et11feb16>[https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/cricket/pakistan-super-league-sam-billings-hoping-brad-haddin-tutelage-prepares-him-for-t20-a6857876.html Billings labels PSL 'cracking experience'], ''[[The Express Tribune]]'', 11 February 2016. Retrieved 11 June 2016.</ref><ref name=indy6feb16>Reynolds C (2016) [https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/cricket/pakistan-super-league-sam-billings-hoping-brad-haddin-tutelage-prepares-him-for-t20-a6857876.html Pakistan Super League: Sam Billings hoping Brad Haddin tutelage prepares him for T20], ''[[The Independent]]'', 6 February 2016. Retrieved 11 June 2016.</ref> He was retained by Islamabad for the [[2017 Pakistan Super League|2017 season]], playing in the team's first five matches of the tournament before leaving to join the [[English cricket team in the West Indies in 2016–17|England ODI team in the Caribbean]].<ref name=bt19oct16>[http://sport.bt.com/more-sport-hub/more-sport/kevin-pietersen-set-to-play-in-pakistan-super-league-for-quetta-gladiators-again-S11364106583179 Kevin Pietersen set to play in Pakistan Super League for Quetta Gladiators again], Bt Sport, 19 October 2016. Retrieved 1 November 2016.</ref><ref name=kccc19dec16>[http://www.kentcricket.co.uk/news/sam-billings-retained-by-delhi-daredevils-for-ipl-2017 Sam Billings retained by Delhi Daredevils for IPL 2017], [[Kent County Cricket Club]], 19 December 2016. Retrieved 19 December 2016.</ref><ref name=ko20dec16>Hoad, Alex (2016). [http://www.kentonline.co.uk/canterbury/sport/billings-to-miss-start-of-117700/ Kent and England wicketkeeper-batsman Sam Billings to miss start of English season after IPL return to Delhi Daredevils], ''[[Kent Online]]'', 20 December 2016. Retrieved 20 December 2016.</ref> In 2018 Billings was with England in New Zealand at the start of the tournament and, despite joining Islamabad towards the end of the group stage, did not play a match during the PSL season.

Billings was purchased by [[Delhi Daredevils]] in the [[2016 Indian Premier League]] auction in February 2016 for £30,000.<ref name=bbc6feb16>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/35511544 Indian Premier League: Jos Buttler bought by Mumbai Indians], BBC Sport website, 6 February 2016. Retrieved 6 February 2016.</ref><ref name=ci7feb16>[http://www.espncricinfo.com/pakistan-super-league-2015-16/content/story/970177.html Billings revels in T20 adventure land], ESPNcricinfo, 7 February 2016. Retrieved 12 February 2016.</ref> He scored 54 runs on his debut for Delhi, helping the team to a victory over [[Kolkata Knight Riders]],<ref name=ct30apr16>[http://www.canterburytimes.co.uk/Sam-Billings-swipes-50-IPL-debut-Delhi-Daredevils/story-29203945-detail/story.html Sam Billings swipes 50 on IPL debut for Delhi Daredevils], ''Canterbury Times'', 30 April 2016. Retrieved 2 May 2016.</ref><ref name=ie1may16>[http://indianexpress.com/article/sports/cricket/cashing-in-on-foreign-exchange/ IPL 2016: Cashing in on foreign exchange], ''[[Indian Express]]'', 1 May 2016. Retrieved 2 May 2016.</ref><ref name=ci2may16>Venugopal A (2016) [http://www.espncricinfo.com/indian-premier-league-2016/content/story/1007505.html Off field bonding puts Billings at ease on the field with Daredevils], ESPNcricinfo, 2 May 2016. Retrieved 18 May 2016.</ref> before going on to play in four further matches before Delhi were eliminated at the end of the group stage.<ref name=ct23may16>[http://www.canterburytimes.co.uk/IPL-2016-Sam-Billings-heading-home-Delhi/story-29306912-detail/story.html IPL 2016: Sam Billings heading home after Delhi Daredevils miss out], ''Canterbury Times'', 23 May 2016. Retrieved 11 June 2016.</ref><ref name=kn2jun16>Pennell M (2016) [http://www.kentnews.co.uk/sport/sam_billings_pleased_to_be_back_in_kent_after_crazy_ipl_experience_1_4560518 Sam Billings pleased to be back in Kent after 'crazy' IPL experience]{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}, ''Kent News'', 2 June 2016. Retrieved 11 June 2016.</ref> Despite playing in only five matches in the tournament,<ref name=bbc19dec16>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/38363732 Indian Premier League: England's Jos Buttler and Sam Billings retained for 2017], BBC Sport, 19 December 2016. Retrieved 20 December 2016.</ref> Billings again saw the experience as one which would help him "improve as a player".<ref name=toi3may16>Singh S (2016) [http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/ipl/news/IPL-9-Will-be-stupid-to-not-pick-Dravids-brain-says-Billings/articleshow/52088739.cms IPL 9: Will be stupid to not pick Dravid's brain, says Billings], ''[[The Times of India]]'', 3 May 2016. Retrieved 11 June 2016.</ref> In particular, he cited the influence of Delhi's coach [[Rahul Dravid]] and had approached the IPL, which he rated as a "phenomenal experience",<ref name=ko2jun16 /> with the intention of developing his skills, particularly against [[spin bowling]].<ref name=ci11jan17 /><ref name=toi3may16 /><ref name=ssl2may16>Viswanath G (2016) [http://www.sportstarlive.com/cricket/ipl/sam-billings-relishes-involvement-in-massive-ipl/article8547765.ece Sam Billings relishes involvement in 'massive' IPL], ''Sport Star Live'', 2 May 2016. Retrieved 11 June 2016.</ref><ref name=tcp16may16>[http://www.thecricketpaper.com/news/twenty20/1586/sam-is-happy-to-follow-ipl-route-to-top-billings/ Sam is happy to follow IPL route to top Billings], ''The Cricket Paper'', 16 May 2016. Retrieved 11 June 2016.</ref> He has credited the experience of working with players from around the world as a major factor in the improvement of his game, from the use of different training methods to eating more effectively.<ref name=tory27jan17 /><ref name=times19mar17 /> Billings was retained by Delhi for the [[2017 Indian Premier League]] with the intention of him playing until 1 May to return to England to [[Irish cricket team in England in 2017|play against Ireland]] and prepare for the [[2017 ICC Champions Trophy]].<ref name=kccc19dec16 /><ref name=ko20dec16 /><ref name=bbc19dec16 /><ref name=ci21feb17>[http://www.espncricinfo.com/england/content/story/1083673.html Stokes, Woakes, Buttler to miss Ireland ODIs], ESPNcricinfo, 21 February 2017. Retrieved 26 February 2017.</ref>

In November 2016 Billings signed to play for [[Sydney Sixers]] in the [[2016–17 Big Bash League season|2016–17 Big Bash League]] in Australia.<ref name=kccc28nov16>[http://www.kentcricket.co.uk/news/sam-billings-signs-for-sydney-sixers Sam Billings signed for Sydney Sixers], [[Kent County Cricket Club]], 28 November 2016. Retrieved 29 November 2016.</ref><ref name=ko29nov16>Hoad, Alex (2016). [http://www.kentonline.co.uk/canterbury/sport/billings-set-for-bbl-116544/ Kent and England star Sam Billings signs for Sydney Sixers ahead of Big Bash League], ''[[Kent Online]]'', 29 November 2016. Retrieved 29 November 2016.</ref><ref name=gran19dec16>Australian Associated Press (2016) [https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2016/dec/20/big-bash-league-preview-all-the-ins-and-outs-for-the-2016-17-tournament Big Bash League preview: all the ins and outs for the 2016–17 tournament], ''[[The Guardian]]'', 19 December 2016. Retrieved 20 December 2016.</ref> He made his debut for the Sixers in the opening match of the tournament, taking two catches as the team beat [[Sydney Thunder]] by nine wickets.<ref name=ko20dec16 /><ref name=kccc20dec16>[http://www.kentcricket.co.uk/news/billings-takes-two-catches-in-bbl-debut-win Billings takes two catches in BBL debut win], [[Kent County Cricket Club]], 20 December 2016. Retrieved 20 December 2016.</ref> After appearing in the Sixers first five matches of the tournament, Billings left the team to join the [[English cricket team in India in 2016–17|England squad in India]] at the beginning of January 2017. He batted four times for Sydney, averaging 31.25 runs.<ref name=kccc3jan17>[http://www.kentcricket.co.uk/news/billings-bows-out-bbl-with-brisbane-win Billings bows out BBL with Brisbane win], [[Kent County Cricket Club]], 3 January 2017. Retrieved 3 January 2017.</ref>

After playing again for Sydney in the [[2017–18 Big Bash League season|Big Bash League in 2017/18]], Billings was bought by the [[Chennai Super Kings]] in the [[2018 Indian Premier League|2018 IPL]] [[List of 2018 Indian Premier League personnel changes|auction]] for £71,000.<ref name=bbc28jan18>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/42851844 IPL: Eoin Morgan and Alex Hales miss out on contracts], [[BBC Sport]], 28 January 2018. Retrieved 30 January 2018.</ref><ref name=tory1feb18>Berry S (2018) [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/cricket/2018/02/01/sam-billings-defends-playing-ipl-fury-kent-fans/ Sam Billings defends playing in IPL after fury from Kent fans], ''[[The Daily Telegraph]]'', 1 February 2018. Retrieved 11 February 2018.</ref> Although he scored a match-winning 56 runs in Chennai's second match of the tournament, a rather disappointing tournament<ref name=tory9may18>Bloom B (2018) [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/cricket/2018/05/09/have-englands-players-fared-2018-ipl/ How have England's players fared at the 2018 IPL?], ''[[The Daily Telegraph]]'', 9 May 2018. Retrieved 28 May 2018.</ref> saw him score 108 runs at an [[batting average (cricket)|average]] of 13.60 in 10 matches and he did not play in the final as Chennai won the title.<ref name=ko28may18>Fordham J (2018) [http://www.kentonline.co.uk/canterbury/sport/billings-set-to-return-for-somerset-game-183692/ Sam Billings set to feature in Kent's next One-Day Cup game], ''[[Kent Online]]'', 28 May 2018. Retrieved 28 May 2018.</ref>

In 2018 he captained Bengal Tigers in the [[T10 League]] played in the [[United Arab Emirates]]<ref name=bt23oct18>Bengal Tigers [BengalTigersUAE] [https://twitter.com/BengalTigersUAE/status/1054625344710459392 We are pleased to announce @sambillings as the captain of Bengal Tigers fully endorsed by our super coach @SPFleming7 for the season 2 of the @T10LeagueTweets], (Tweet), via [[Twitter]], 23 October 2018. Retrieved 23 October 2018.</ref> having been picked second in the competition's draft in July.<ref name=kt24jul18>[https://www.khaleejtimes.com/bengal-tigers-sign-roy-billings-and-ali-for-t10-cricket-league Bengal Tigers sign Roy, Billings and Ali for T10 Cricket League], ''[[Khaleej Times]]'', 24 July 2018. Retrieved 23 October 2018.</ref> A break from overseas T20 leagues saw him play more frequently for Kent, before he was signed to play for [[Sydney Thunder]] in the 2020/21 Big Bash. In February 2021, he was bought again by Delhi ahead of the [[2021 Indian Premier League]], missing the start of Kent's season, although he did not play a match for the team during the competition.<ref name=ca/><ref>Roller M (2021) [https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/england-players-at-ipl-2021-the-teams-the-stats-and-the-form-guide-1258044 England players at IPL 2021 – the teams, the stats, and the form guide], ESPNcricinfo, 7 April 2021. Retrieved 10 April 2021.</ref>

During the 2021 home season, Billings captained [[Oval Invincibles]] during the [[2022 season of The Hundred]], the ECB's new franchise competition.<ref name=cric22jul21>McLaughlin E (2021) [https://www.thecricketer.com/Topics/news/sam_billings_proves_natural_100_ball_captain_oval_invincibles.html Sam Billings proves a natural 100-ball captain as Oval Invincibles stay true to their name], ''[[The Cricketer]]'' online, 22 July 2021. Retrieved 28 June 2022.</ref> The team were eliminated from the competition during the last round of group-stage matches.<ref name=ci16aug21>Roller M (2021) [https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/the-hundred-men-s-competition-2021-1252040/southern-brave-men-vs-oval-invincibles-men-30th-match-1252695/match-report Jake Lintott pegs back Invincibles before Alex Davies, Colin de Grandhomme seal Brave passage], ESPNcricinfo, 16 August 2022. Retrieved 28 June 2022.</ref> He was retained by the team for the 2022 season.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/60477088 The Hundred 2022: latest squads as Draft picks revealed], [[BBC Sport]], 5 April 2022. Retrieved 28 June 2022.</ref> In February 2022, he was bought by [[Kolkata Knight Riders]] ahead of the [[2022 Indian Premier League]], once more mission the start of Kent's domestic season.<ref name=cric15mar22>Botcherby E (2022) [https://www.thecricketer.com/Topics/countycricket/kent_confirm_captains_for_2022_season.html Kent confirm captains for 2022 season], ''[[The Cricketer]]'' online, 15 March 2022. Retrieved 28 June 2022.</ref> He played in eight matches for the team, missing games due to illness, and scored 169 runs during the competition.<ref name=ca/><ref name=tn23apr22>[https://www.timesnownews.com/sports/cricket/sam-billings-to-return-for-kolkata-predicting-kkrs-likely-playing-xi-against-gt-article-91019697 Sam Billings to return for Kolkata? Predicting KKR's likely playing XI against GT], ''[[Times Now]]'', 22 April 2022. Retrieved 28 June 2022.</ref><ref name=bbc14nov22>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/63622062 Sam Billings: Kent captain will miss 2023 IPL season to focus on County Championship], [[BBC Sport]], 14 November 2022. Retrieved 20 November 2022.</ref> In August 2022 Billings was selected by [[Brisbane Heat]] as the third pick in the first Big Bash league draft ahead of the [[2022–23 Big Bash League season|2022–23 Big Bash]].<ref name=gran28aug22>[https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2022/aug/28/england-batter-liam-livingstone-named-as-first-pick-in-big-bash-league-draft-cricket England batter Liam Livingstone named as first pick in Big Bash League draft], ''[[The Guardian]]'', 28 August 2022. Retrieved 20 November 2022.</ref> In November, however, he pulled out of the following IPL season, citing his desire to focus on long-form cricket with Kent and burn-out associated with having spent 18 months playing cricket around the globe.<ref name=bbc14nov22/><ref name=bbc15nov22/> He did take part in the [[2023 Pakistan Super League]], winning the tournament with [[Lahore Qalandars]], his second PSL title.<ref name=bbc18mar23>[https://www.bbc.com/sport/cricket/65003947 Qalandars beat Sultans by one run to win PSL title], [[BBC Sport]], 18 March 2023. Retrieved 1 April 2023.</ref>

==Career best performances==
As of November 2022, Billings has made six [[first-class cricket|first-class]], seven [[List A cricket|List A]] centuries, including one in international cricket, and one [[Twenty20]] century. His first senior century was a score of 131 made on his first-class debut for [[Loughborough MCCU]] against [[Northamptonshire County Cricket Club|Northamptonshire]] at the beginning of the 2011 season.<ref name=ko5apr11>Hoad, Alex (2011). [http://www.kentonline.co.uk/kent/news/kent-county-cricket-club-wicketk-a76019/ Kent County Cricket Club wicketkeeper Sam Billings hits maiden century for Loughborough MCCU against Northamptonshire], ''Kent Online'', 5 April 2011. Retrieved 11 June 2016.</ref> He scored his first first-class century for Kent in July 2015 against [[Essex County Cricket Club|Essex]] at [[Nevill Ground|Tunbridge Wells]], having been out for 99 earlier in the same month against [[Surrey County Cricket Club|Surrey]].<ref name=kccc14jul16>[http://www.kentcricket.co.uk/news/billings-disappointed-to-fall-for-99 Billings disappointed to fall for 99], [[Kent County Cricket Club]], 14 July 2015. Retrieved 11 June 2016.</ref><ref name=ksn21jul15>[http://www.kentsportsnews.com/billings-elated-for-maiden-century-21-07-2015/ Billings elated for maiden century], ''Kent Sports News'', 21 July 2015. Retrieved 11 June 2016.</ref> His third first-class century, 171 runs, came against [[Gloucestershire County Cricket Club|Gloucestershire]] in August 2016 and is his current highest first-class score.<ref name=ci25aug16 /> Billings' fourth, fifth and sixth centuries were scored in back-to-back innings in September 2019, including two in the same match against [[Yorkshire County Cricket Club|Yorkshire]] at [[Headingley Cricket Ground|Headingley]], the first time two centuries had been scored by the same player on the ground in a County Championship match.<ref name=bbc18sep19>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/49742524 County Championship: Kent captain Sam Billings hits second ton of match against Yorkshire], [[BBC Sport]], 18 September 2019. Retrieved 18 September 2019.</ref><ref name=ci18sep19>[https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/8052/report/1166964 Sam Billings backs up with the bat as Kent close in on big win], ESPNcricinfo, 18 September 2019. Retrieved 18 September 2019.</ref>

Billings has scored seven [[List A cricket]] centuries and in 2014 shared the [[Walter Lawrence Trophy]] for the quickest century in County cricket during the season, scored off 46 balls against [[Somerset County Cricket Club|Somerset]] in a [[2014 Royal London One-Day Cup]] match.<ref name=kccc30sep14>[http://www.kentcricket.co.uk/news/sam-billings-wins-walter-lawrence-trophy-for-fastest-century-in-county-cricket Sam Billings wins Walter Lawrence trophy for fastest century in County cricket], [[Kent County Cricket Club]], 30 September 2014. Retrieved 11 June 2016.</ref> His highest List A score of 175 was made for [[England Lions cricket team|England Lions]] against [[Sri Lanka A cricket team|Sri Lanka A]] at his home ground of [[St Lawrence Ground|Canterbury]] during July 2016<ref name=ci24jul16 /> whilst his highest [[Twenty20]] score of 106 was made for Kent against [[Somerset County Cricket Club|Somerset]] at Canterbury in June 2024.<ref name=ci7jun24>[https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/vitality-blast-2024-1410370/kent-vs-somerset-south-group-1410396/match-report Sam Billings century steers Kent to mighty comeback against Somerset], [[CricInfo]], 7 June 2024. Retrieved 8 June 2024.</ref>

In September 2020 Billings scored his debut senior international century, making a score of 118 in a One Day International match between England and Australia at [[Old Trafford cricket ground]].<ref name=bbc11sep20>Lofthouse A (2020) [https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/54119878 England v Australia: Sam Billings hits ton but tourists win by 19 runs], [[BBC Sport]], 11 September 2020. Retrieved 12 September 2020.</ref>

In July 2022 Billings set a new County Championship record of 12 catches in a match as his Kent team beat [[Warwickshire County Cricket Club|Warwickshire]].<ref>Scott G (2022) [https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/62264807 County Championship: Sam Billings breaks catching record as Kent beat Warwickshire at Edgbaston], [[BBC Sport]], 22 July 2022. Retrieved 26 July 2022.</ref>

==Support for cricketing causes==
Billings has been involved in supporting the development of cricket by charitable organisations and globally. He has supported activities organised by the [[Lord's Taverners]] and worked with disabilities cricket teams with the charity and with [[NatWest]]'s Cricket has no boundaries campaign.<ref name=times19mar17 /><ref name=aoc15aug17>Harman J (2017) [http://www.alloutcricket.com/features/sam-billings-list-record-stands-anyone Sam Billings: My one day record stands up against anyone], All Out Cricket, 15 August 2017. Retrieved 31 October 2017.</ref><ref name=bxtimes17oct17>May L (2017) [http://www.bexleytimes.co.uk/news/young-cricketers-get-tips-from-kent-and-england-batsman-sam-billings-at-disability-cricket-finals-1-5240511 Young cricketers get tips from Kent and England batsman Sam Billings at Disability Cricket Finals], ''[[Bexley Times]]'', 17 October 2017. Retrieved 31 October 2017.</ref> He is an ambassador for the Taverners and launched a cricket ambassador programme for them in 2016.<ref name=able16>[http://ablemagazine.co.uk/sam-billings-lords-taverners/ England Cricketer, Sam Billings Teams Up With Lord's Taverners], ''Able'', 2016. Retrieved 31 October 2017.</ref> He has worked with youth cricket teams<ref name=bbc2nov16>Wilson J (2016) [https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/get-inspired/37853153 Chance to Shine: ECB set to double its investment in future of cricket], [[BBC Sport]], 2 November 2016. Retrieved 31 October 2017.</ref><ref name=seven8oct17>Rowley S (2017) [http://sevenoakssports.co.uk/sam-billings-discovers-the-treasures-of-the-plaxtol-pirates Sam Billings discovers the treasures of the Plaxtol Pirates], Sevenoaks Sports, 8 October 2017. Retrieved 31 October 2017.</ref> and in October 2017 visited [[Rwanda]] to play in a T20 cricket match to mark the opening of the [[Rwanda Cricket Stadium]].<ref name=tory27oct17>Hoult N (2017) [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/cricket/2017/10/27/rwanda-crickets-field-dreams-becomes-reality/ Rwanda cricket's field of dreams becomes a reality], ''[[The Daily Telegraph]]'', 27 October 2017. Retrieved 31 October 2017.</ref> He is a patron of cricket in Rwanda.<ref name=twit31oct17>Rwanda Cricket [RwandaCricket] [https://twitter.com/RwandaCricket/status/925443118819921921 A big thank you to @sambillings for taking part last week. We are also delighted to announce him as our new patron! #cricketbuildshope], (Tweet), via [[Twitter]], 31 October 2017. Retrieved 1 November 2017.</ref>

born 14 October 1989) is a Pakistani left-handed [[Batting (cricket)|batter]] who has played for the [[Pakistan national cricket team]] since 2013. He [[Captain (cricket)|captained]] Pakistan in [[Test cricket|Test matches]] from 2023 to 2026. Previously, he served as a captain of [[Karachi Kings]], [[Multan Sultans]], [[Southern Punjab cricket team (Pakistan)|Southern Punjab]], and [[Yorkshire County Cricket Club]]. In August 2018, he was one of thirty-three players to be awarded a central contract for the 2018–19 season by the [[Pakistan Cricket Board]] (PCB).{{cite web|url=https://www.pcb.com.pk/press-release-detail/pcb-central-contracts-2018-19.html |title=PCB Central Contracts 2018–19 |work=Pakistan Cricket Board |date=10 January 2014 |access-date=6 August 2018}}{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/24301169/new-central-contracts-guarantee-earnings-boost-pakistan-players |title=New central contracts guarantee earnings boost for Pakistan players |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=6 August 2018}} ==Early life and education== Shan Masood was born in 1989 in Kuwait, where his father worked in a bank. Following the [[Iraqi invasion of Kuwait]] and the start of the Gulf War, the family left for their native Pakistan, settling down in [[Karachi]] again.{{Cite web |last=Alderson |first=Andrew |date=21 November 2014 |title=Cricket: Masood credits dad for career |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/sport/cricket-masood-credits-dad-for-career/7FZL2FIJTEQOWITEDUYGREDMJM/ |website=[[The New Zealand Herald]]}} His father Mansoor Masood Khan, apart from being a professional banker, always had an interest in sports, himself playing hockey at provincial level while loving cricket as well and encouraging his son to be invested in the field.{{Cite web |last=Ali |first=Liaqat |date=13 November 2013 |title=Passion for cricket runs in Masood's sports-loving family |url=https://www.khaleejtimes.com/cricket/passion-for-cricket-runs-in-masoods-sports-loving-family |website=[[Khaleej Times]] |quote=Mansoor has played hockey at provincial level and has seen ups and downs in cricket. He has witnessed Pakistan playing best and worst cricket.}} Mansoor became a member of the governing board in the [[Pakistan Cricket Board]] in 2014.{{Cite web |last=Hussain |first=S.M. |date=30 August 2020 |title=CRICKET: FIGHTING ON TWO FRONTS |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1577081 |website=[[Dawn News]] |quote=Things went bad to worse for Masood when his father became a member of the governing board in the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) in 2014. The label of nepotism seemed to follow him everywhere.}} His paternal uncle, [[Waqar Masood Khan]], is a retired civil servant who served as Pakistan's longest serving Federal Secretary for Finance. His elder sister died in 2021 while his younger brother Ali is a barrister.{{Cite web |date=27 November 2022 |title=Pakistan cricketer Shan Masood to tie the knot on January 21 |url=https://www.geo.tv/latest/455056-pakistan-cricketer-shan-masood-to-tie-the-knot-on-january-21 |website=[[Geo News]] |quote=The left-handed batter is the son of renowned banker Mansoor Masood Khan, while his paternal uncle Waqar Masood Khan has served as federal finance secretary. He is the second among his three siblings. Shan's elder sister passed away last year and his younger brother, Ali, is a barrister.}} After moving to the United Kingdom with his parents, he studied at [[Stamford School]], [[Lincolnshire]] and then [[Durham University]] where he studied economics. He studied Management and Sports Sciences at [[Loughborough University]] through a [[distance learning]] programme.{{Cite web|title=Shan Masood returns to familiar surroundings {{!}} ESPNcricinfo.com|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/17050735/shan-masood-returns-familiar-surroundings|access-date=2020-08-07|website=www.espncricinfo.com|language=en}}{{Cite web|last=Masood|first=Shan|date=2015-07-08|title=Shan Masood: My journey to the top|url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1193131|access-date=2020-08-07|website=DAWN.COM|language=en}} ==Domestic career== [[File:1 21 Shakeel & Masood.jpg|thumb|left|220px|Masood captained [[Yorkshire County Cricket Club|Yorkshire]] in the [[2023 County Championship]].]] === Pakistan === In his first-class debut in the [[2007–08 Quaid-e-Azam Trophy|2007–08 season]] of [[Quaid-e-Azam Trophy]], Masood scored 54 for [[Karachi Whites]] against [[Hyderabad cricket team (Pakistan)|Hyderabad]] as part of a 154-run opening stand with [[Asad Shafiq]].{{cite news |title=Karachi Whites poised to take first-innings lead |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/karachi-whites-poised-to-take-first-innings-lead-316751 |work=ESPNcricinfo |date=24 October 2007 |language=en}} In April 2018, he was named the vice-captain of [[Khyber Pakhtunkhwa cricket team|Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]]'s squad for the [[2018 Pakistan Cup]].{{cite web|url=https://www.geo.tv/latest/191967-pakistan-cup-one-day-tournament-to-begin-in-faisalabad |title=Pakistan Cup one-day tournament to begin in Faisalabad next week |access-date=21 April 2018 |work=Geo TV}}{{cite web|url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/print/306831-pakistan-cup-cricket-from-25th |title=Pakistan Cup Cricket from 25th |access-date=21 April 2018 |work=The News International}} In September 2019, Masood was named as the captain of [[Southern Punjab cricket team (Pakistan)|Southern Punjab]] for the [[2019–20 Quaid-e-Azam Trophy]] tournament.{{cite web |url=https://www.pcb.com.pk/press-release-detail/pcb-announces-squads-for-2019-20-domestic-season.html |title=PCB announces squads for 2019-20 domestic season |work=Pakistan Cricket Board |date=10 January 2014 |access-date=4 September 2019 |archive-date=3 September 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190903183721/https://www.pcb.com.pk/press-release-detail/pcb-announces-squads-for-2019-20-domestic-season.html |url-status=dead }}{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/27527401/sarfaraz-ahmed-babar-azam-take-charge-pakistan-domestic-sides |title=Sarfaraz Ahmed and Babar Azam to take charge of Pakistan domestic teams |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=4 September 2019}} He is captain of [[Bagh Stallions]] in the [[Kashmir Premier League (Pakistan)|Kashmir Premier League]]. === England === Earlier, he had played three first-class games for [[Durham University]]. In December 2021, he was signed by [[Derbyshire County Cricket Club|Derbyshire]] for the 2022 county season.{{Cite news |title=Derbyshire sign Pakistan's Masood |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/cricket/59560758 |access-date=2022-04-14}} In April 2022, in the second round of matches in the [[2022 County Championship]], Shan scored his maiden double century in first-class cricket, scoring an unbeaten 201 runs on the opening day against [[Sussex County Cricket Club|Sussex]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/county-championship-division-two-2022-1310355/derbyshire-vs-sussex-1297679/match-report-1 |title=Shan Masood's unbeaten double century dominates first day in Derby |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=14 April 2022}} In the following match, Shan scored another double century, becoming the first batsman for Derbyshire to score back-to-back double centuries in first-class cricket.{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/61190249 |title=County Championship: Derbyshire batter Shan Masood scores another double century |work=BBC Sport |access-date=22 April 2022}} In May 2022, he scored his third century for Derbyshire against Worcestershire.{{Cite news |title=Prolific Masood hits another Derbyshire century |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/cricket/61432296 |access-date=2022-05-17}} Masood was appointed captain of the [[Yorkshire County Cricket Club]] for the 2023 County season.{{cite web |title=Shan Masood: Yorkshire appoint Pakistan batter as captain from 2023 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/63073596 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=25 March 2025 |date=29 September 2022}} ==International career== In October 2013, Masood made his Test debut in the first test [[South African cricket team against Pakistan in the UAE in 2013–14|against South Africa]] scoring 75 runs, at the [[Sheikh Zayed Cricket Stadium]]. He became only the third Pakistan batsman to score a half-century and a duck on Test debut.{{cite news |title=Pakistan beat South Africa, Pakistan won by 7 wickets |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/south-africa-tour-of-united-arab-emirates-2013-14-649073/pakistan-vs-south-africa-1st-test-649087/live-cricket-score |work=ESPNcricinfo |date=14 October 2013 |language=en}} In July 2015, he scored his maiden century [[Pakistani cricket team in Sri Lanka in 2015|against Sri Lanka]] at [[Pallekele International Cricket Stadium|Pallekele]], putting on 242 for the third wicket with [[Younis Khan]] as Pakistan scored 382 to complete their highest successful chase.{{cite news |title=Younis Khan hits stunning 171 to lead Pakistan to series victory over Sri Lanka |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2015/jul/07/younis-khan-pakistan-sri-lanka-match-report-cricket |work=The Guardian |date=7 July 2015}} Masood, a part-time medium pacer, bowled for the first time in Test cricket on 23 July 2016 against England at Old Trafford. His first delivery was a [[no ball]].{{cite web|url=http://sports.ndtv.com/cricket/news/261079-live-cricket-score-england-vs-pakistan-day-2-second-test|title=Live Cricket Score England vs Pakistan Day 2, Second Test: Joe Root Double Ton Puts England On Top|last=NDTVSports.com|work=ndtv.com|access-date=23 July 2016}} In September 2018, he was named in Pakistan's [[One Day International]] (ODI) squad for the [[2018 Asia Cup]], but he did not play.{{cite web|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/844507 |title=Shaheen Afridi included in Pakistan squad for Asia Cup 2018 |work=International Cricket Council |access-date=4 September 2018}} In January 2019, he was named in Pakistan's ODI squad for their series [[Pakistani cricket team in South Africa in 2018–19|against South Africa]], but again he did not play.{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/story/1171176.html |title=Mohammad Amir, Mohammad Rizwan back in Pakistan ODI squad |access-date=9 January 2019 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}} In March 2019, he was named in Pakistan's ODI squad for their series [[Australian cricket team against Pakistan in the UAE in 2018–19|against Australia]].{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/story/1177055.html |title=Shoaib Mailk to lead ODI squad in UAE, Sarfaraz Ahmed among six players rested |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=8 March 2019}}{{cite web|url=https://www.pcb.com.pk/press-release-detail/pakistan-squad-for-australia-odis-announced.html |title= Pakistan squad for Australia ODIs announced |work=Pakistan Cricket Board |date= 10 January 2014 |access-date=8 March 2019}} He made his ODI debut for Pakistan against [[Australia national cricket team|Australia]] on 22 March 2019.{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1174238.html |title=1st ODI (D/N), Australia tour of United Arab Emirates at Sharjah, Mar 22 2019 |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=22 March 2019}} In December 2019, he scored his second Test century, against the [[Sri Lankan cricket team in Pakistan in 2019–20|touring Sri Lankans]] at the [[National Stadium, Karachi]].{{cite web|url=https://www.brecorder.com/2019/12/21/555330/abid-ali-shan-masood-flay-sri-lanka-in-second-test/|title=Abid Ali, Shan Masood flay Sri Lanka in second Test|work=Business Recorder|date=21 December 2019 |access-date=21 December 2019}} In the same match, he also scored his 1,000th run in Test cricket.{{cite web|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/1539722 |title=Monumental opening stand puts Pakistan in firm control |work=International Cricket Council |access-date=21 December 2019}} In February 2020, Masood made his third Test century, [[Bangladeshi cricket team in Pakistan in 2019–20|against Bangladesh]] at [[Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium|Rawalpindi]].{{cite web |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/19430/report/1213062/day/1/pakistan-vs-bangladesh-1st-test-icc-world-test-championship-2019-2021|title=Babar Azam, Shan Masood tons put Pakistan on top|work=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=8 February 2020}} In June 2020, he was named in a 29-man squad for Pakistan's [[Pakistani cricket team in England in 2020|tour to England]] during the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/29300707/haider-ali-new-face-pakistan-name-29-man-touring-party-england |title=Haider Ali the new face as Pakistan name 29-man touring party for England |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=12 June 2020}}{{cite web |url=https://www.pcb.com.pk/press-release-detail/haider-ali-named-in-29-player-squad-for-england-tour.html |title=Haider Ali named in 29-player squad for England tour |work=Pakistan Cricket Board |date=10 January 2014 |access-date=12 June 2020 |archive-date=12 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200612071011/https://www.pcb.com.pk/press-release-detail/haider-ali-named-in-29-player-squad-for-england-tour.html |url-status=dead }} In July, he was shortlisted in Pakistan's 20-man squad for the Test matches against England.{{cite web|url=https://www.pcb.com.pk/press-release-detail/pakistan-shortlist-players-for-england-tests.html |title= Pakistan shortlist players for England Tests |work=Pakistan Cricket Board |date= 10 January 2014 |access-date=27 July 2020}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/29548095/wahab-riaz,-sarfaraz-ahmed-20-man-pakistan-squad-england-tests |title=Wahab Riaz, Sarfaraz Ahmed in 20-man Pakistan squad for England Tests |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=27 July 2020}} In August 2020, Masood scored 156 in the first Test against England, his fourth century in Test cricket, at the [[Old Trafford Cricket Ground|Old Trafford]].{{cite news |last1=Marks |first1=Vic |title=England get first Test jitters again after Shan Masood century inspires Pakistan |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2020/aug/06/england-pakistan-first-test-day-two-match-report |work=The Guardian |date=6 August 2020}} In November 2020, he was named in Pakistan's 35-man squad for their [[Pakistani cricket team in New Zealand in 2020–21|tour to New Zealand]].{{cite web|url=https://www.pcb.com.pk/press-release-detail/pakistan-name-35-player-squad-for-new-zealand.html |title=Pakistan name 35-player squad for New Zealand |work=Pakistan Cricket Board |date=10 January 2014 |access-date=11 November 2020}} In September 2022, he was named in the Pakistan's T20I squad for the [[English cricket team in Pakistan in 2022–23|series against England]].{{cite web |access-date=15 September 2022 |title=Pakistan name squad for ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2022 |url=https://www.pcb.com.pk/press-release-detail/pakistan-name-squad-for-icc-men-s-t20-world-cup-.html |website=Pakistan Cricket Board|date=10 January 2014}} He made his T20I debut on 20 September 2022, against [[England cricket team|England]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1327228.html |title=1st T20I (N), Karachi, September 20, 2022, England tour of Pakistan |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=20 September 2022}} Masood was also named as part of the [[2022 ICC Men's T20 World Cup squads|Pakistan squad]] for the [[2022 ICC Men's T20 World Cup|2022 T20 World Cup]].{{cite news |title=Pak vs Eng: PCB names squads for England series, T20 world cup 2022 |url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/latest/991558-pak-vs-eng-pakistan-unveils-squad-for-england-series-t20-world-cup |work=www.thenews.com.pk |date=15 September 2022 |language=en}} In January 2023, he was named as the vice-captain of the Pakistan's ODI team for their [[New Zealand cricket team in Pakistan in 2022–23 (December 2022)|home series against New Zealand]].{{Cite web |title=Shan appointed vice-captain for NZ ODI series |url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/print/1028008-shan-appointed-vice-captain-for-nz-odi-series |access-date=2023-01-07 |website=The News International |language=en}} === Captaincy === In November 2023, he was named as the [[Captain (cricket)|captain]] of the [[Pakistan national cricket team]] in the [[Test cricket|test]] format.{{cite web | url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/shaheen-afridi-to-lead-pakistan-in-t20is-shan-masood-appointed-test-captain-1408974?platform=amp | title=Shaheen Afridi to lead Pakistan in T20Is; Shan Masood appointed Test captain | date=15 November 2023 }} Under his captaincy, Pakistan lost the three-match test [[Pakistani cricket team in Australia in 2023–24|series against Australia]] by 3-0{{cite news |title=Recapping a summer down under: No shame in losing 3-0 for Shan Masood's Pakistan |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/aus-vs-pak-recapping-a-summer-down-under-no-shame-in-3-0-for-shan-masoods-pakistan-1415880 |work=ESPNcricinfo |date=7 January 2024 |language=en}} where he scored a total of 181 runs.{{cite web |title=Cricket Records in Benaud-Qadir Trophy, 2023/24 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/records/series/batting-most-runs-career/benaud-qadir-trophy-2023-24-15390 |work=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}} Masood was retained as Pakistan's captain for the two-match [[Bangladeshi cricket team in Pakistan in 2024|Test series against Bangladesh]]{{cite news |title=Shan Masood retained as captain for Bangladesh Test series |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/2478754/shan-masood-retained-as-captain-for-bangladesh-test-series |work=The Express Tribune |date=11 July 2024 |language=en}} that ended in a 2–0 home series loss in [[Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium|Rawalpindi]].{{cite news |title=Pakistan retain Shan Masood as Test cricket captain despite poor record |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2024/9/25/pakistan-retain-shan-masood-as-test-cricket-captain-despite-poor-record |work=Al Jazeera |date=25 September 2024 |language=en}} Masood was again retained as Pakistan's captain for the three-test [[English cricket team in Pakistan in 2024–25|home series against England]].{{cite news |title=Pakistan retains Masood as captain for opening test match against England |url=https://apnews.com/article/cricket-pakistan-england-3a8964da5e9da34484c7a6b4a9579e91 |work=AP News |date=24 September 2024 |language=en}} In the first Test, Masood scored his fifth test century and surpassed the 2,000 runs milestone in Tests.{{cite news |title=Shan Masood reaches 2,000 Test Runs in first Test against England |url=https://dunyanews.tv/en/Cricket/842606-shan-masood-reaches-2000-test-runs-in-first-test-against-england |work=Dunya News |date=8 October 2024 |language=en}} He also became the 17th Pakistan captain to score a hundred in the test format.{{cite news |title=Full list: Shan Masood Becomes 17th Pakistan Captain To Score A Men's Test Hundred |url=https://www.wisden.com/series/pakistan-vs-england-m-2024/cricket-news/full-list-shan-masood-becomes-17th-pakistan-captain-to-score-a-mens-test-hundred |work=Wisden |date=7 October 2024 |language=en}} In the second test, Pakistan's win marked Masood's first victory since taking over as captain, after six consecutive defeats in a row.{{cite news |last1=Gardner |first1=Alan |title=Noman Ali eight-for seals Pakistan's first home win since 2021 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/england-in-pakistan-2024-25-1442205/pakistan-vs-england-2nd-test-1442216/match-report-4 |work=ESPNcricinfo |date=18 October 2024 |language=en}} Pakistan won the third Test in Rawalpindi for a 2–1 series win.{{cite news |title=Shan Masood says Pakistan need stability after famous England win |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1867793 |work=DAWN.COM |date=26 October 2024 |language=en}} His next assignment as Pakistan's Test captain was a two-match [[Pakistani cricket team in South Africa in 2024–25|away series against South Africa]]. In the first Test, he got a couple of starts but was unable to convert them into a big score, as Pakistan lost a nail-biter by two wickets.{{Cite web |title=SA vs PAK Cricket Scorecard, 1st Test at Centurion, December 26 - 29, 2024 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/south-africa-vs-pakistan-2024-25-1432205/south-africa-vs-pakistan-1st-test-1432217/full-scorecard |access-date=2025-01-11 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}} In the second Test, after being dismissed for a low score in the first innings, he scored his sixth Test century in the second innings.{{Cite web |title=SA vs PAK Cricket Scorecard, 2nd Test at Cape Town, January 03 - 06, 2025 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/south-africa-vs-pakistan-2024-25-1432205/south-africa-vs-pakistan-2nd-test-1432218/full-scorecard |access-date=2025-01-11 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}} Despite his hundred, Pakistan went on to lose the match and the series 2–0.{{Cite web |title=Pakistan search for positives after South Africa complete Test series sweep |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2025/1/6/pakistan-search-for-positives-after-south-africa-complete-test-series-sweep#:~:text=South%20Africa%20have%20wrapped%20up,battled%20to%20478%20all%20out. |access-date=2025-01-11 |website=Al Jazeera |language=en}} After the [[Pakistani cricket team in Bangladesh in 2025–26|2-0 away series against Bangladesh]] in May 2026, Masood stepped down as captain.[https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ban-vs-pak-shan-masood-leaves-captaincy-future-to-pcb-but-calls-for-structural-changes-1537589 Ban vs Pak -
