'''Shayan Jahangir''' (born December 24, 1994) is a [[cricket]]er who plays for the [[United States national cricket team]].<ref name="Bio">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/647771.html |title=Shayan Jahangir |access-date=6 July 2020 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://emergingcricket.com/events/major-league-cricket/minor-league-cricket-with-cpl-experience/ |title=Jessy Singh and Shayan Jahangir bring CPL experiences to Minor League Cricket |work=Emerging Cricket |access-date=15 September 2020}}</ref> He is a right-handed batsman and [[wicket-keeper]].

==Domestic and franchise career==
He made his [[first-class cricket|first-class]] debut for [[Pakistan International Airlines cricket team|Pakistan International Airlines]] in the [[2014–15 Quaid-e-Azam Trophy]] on 12 October 2014.<ref name="FC">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/783319.html |title=Group I, Quaid-e-Azam Trophy Silver League at Karachi, Oct 12-15 2014 |access-date=6 July 2020 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref> In July 2020, he was named in the [[Barbados Tridents]] squad for the [[2020 Caribbean Premier League]] (CPL).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/29417692/nabi,-lamichhane,-dunk-earn-big-cpl-2020-draft |title=Nabi, Lamichhane, Dunk earn big in CPL 2020 draft |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=6 July 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.windiescricket.com/news/teams-selected-hero-cpl-2020/ |title=Teams Selected for Hero CPL 2020 |work=Cricket West Indies |access-date=6 July 2020}}</ref> He made his [[Twenty20]] debut on 5 September 2020, for the Barbados Tridents in the CPL.<ref name="T20">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1227892.html |title=28th Match, Tarouba, Sep 5 2020, Caribbean Premier League |access-date=5 September 2020 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref>

==International career==
Jahangir played seven youth one-dayers for the [[Pakistan national under-19 cricket team]] in 2013.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/cricketers/shayan-jahangir-647771/bowling-batting-stats|title=Shayan Jahangir: Career Statistics|publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=17 July 2023}}</ref>

In January 2021, [[USA Cricket]] named Jahangir in a 44-man squad to begin training in Texas ahead of the [[2021 Oman Tri-Nation Series (round 6)|2021 Oman Tri-Nation Series]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/former-west-indies-player-narsingh-deonarine-part-of-usa-training-camp-1248966 |title=Former West Indies player Narsingh Deonarine part of USA training camp |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=23 January 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.usacricket.org/media-release/usa-cricket-selection-update/ |title=USA Cricket Selection Update |work=USA Cricket |access-date=23 January 2021}}</ref> In November 2022, Jahangir made his ODI debut for [[USA national cricket team|USA]] against [[Namibia national cricket team|Namibia]].<ref name="Bio"/>

Jahangir made his first ODI century against [[Nepal national cricket team|Nepal]] in the [[2023 Cricket World Cup Qualifier]] in Zimbabwe, scoring 100 not out from 79 balls from seventh in the batting order.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/icc-cricket-world-cup-qualifier-2023-1377745/nepal-vs-united-states-of-america-6th-match-group-a-1377751/match-report|title=Karan KC's new-ball burst stamps Nepal's dominance over USA|publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=17 July 2023|first=Peter|last=Della Penna|date=20 June 2023}}</ref>

In January 2026, Jahangir was named in USA's squad for the [[2026 ICC Men's T20 World Cup|2026 T20 World Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/media-releases/usa-announce-squad-for-icc-men-s-t20-world-cup-2026|title=USA announce squad for ICC Men’s T20 World Cup 2026|work=[[International Cricket Council]]|date=30 January 2026|access-date=2 February 2026}}</ref>

'''Mohammad Shoriful Islam''' ([[Bangla language|Bangla]]: মোহাম্মদ শরিফুল ইসলাম; born 3 June 2001) is a Bangladeshi [[cricket]]er. He made his international debut for the [[Bangladesh national cricket team|Bangladesh cricket team]] in March 2021.<ref name="Bio">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/990039.html |title=Shoriful Islam |access-date=15 September 2017 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref>

==Domestic and under-19 career==
Shoriful made his [[first-class cricket|first-class]] debut for [[Rajshahi Division cricket team|Rajshahi Division]] in the [[2017–18 National Cricket League]] on 15 September 2017.<ref name="FC">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1120457.html |title=Tier 2, National Cricket League at Rajshahi, Sep 15-18 2017 |access-date=15 September 2017 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref> He made his [[List A cricket|List A]] debut for [[Prime Bank Cricket Club]] in the [[2017–18 Dhaka Premier Division Cricket League]] on 7 February 2018.<ref name="LA">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1135522.html |title=4th match, Dhaka Premier Division Cricket League at Fatullah, Feb 7 2018 |access-date=7 February 2018 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref>

Shoriful was the joint-leading wicket-taker for Prime Bank Cricket Club in the [[2017–18 Dhaka Premier Division Cricket League]], with 17 dismissals in 8 matches.<ref name="1718wkts">{{cite web |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/averages/batting_bowling_by_team.html?id=12250;team=5189;type=tournament |title=Dhaka Premier Division Cricket League, 2017/18: Prime Bank Cricket Club |publisher=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=5 April 2018}}</ref>

Shoriful made his [[Twenty20]] debut for [[Bangladesh A cricket team|Bangladesh A]] against [[Ireland A cricket team|Ireland A]] on 13 August 2018.<ref name="T20">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1153421.html |title=1st unofficial T20, Bangladesh A Tour of Ireland at Dublin, Aug 13 2018 |access-date=13 August 2018 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref> The next day, he was one of twelve debutants to be selected for a 31-man preliminary squad for Bangladesh ahead of the [[2018 Asia Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/810764 |title=Liton Das recalled as Bangladesh reveal preliminary squad for Asia Cup 2018 |work=International Cricket Council |access-date=14 August 2018}}</ref>

In October 2018, Shoriful was named in the squad for the [[Khulna Titans]] team, following the draft for the [[2018–19 Bangladesh Premier League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tigercricket.com.bd/2018/10/29/full-players-list-of-the-teams-following-players-draft-of-bpl-t20-2018-19/ |title=Full players list of the teams following Players Draft of BPL T20 2018-19 |work=Bangladesh Cricket Board |access-date=29 October 2018}}</ref> In December 2018, he was named in Bangladesh's team for the [[2018 ACC Emerging Teams Asia Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tigercricket.com.bd/2018/11/29/media-release-acc-emerging-teams-asia-cup-2018-bangladesh-emerging-squad-announced/ |title=Media Release : ACC Emerging Teams Asia Cup 2018: Bangladesh emerging squad announced |work=Bangladesh Cricket Board |access-date=3 December 2018}}</ref> In December 2019, he was named in Bangladesh's squad for the [[2020 Under-19 Cricket World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tigercricket.com.bd/2019/12/21/media-release-icc-u19-cwc-south-africa-2020-bangladesh-under-19-team-announced/ |title=Media Release : ICC U19 CWC South Africa 2020 : Bangladesh Under 19 Team Announced |work=Bangladesh Cricket Board |access-date=21 December 2019}}</ref>

In July 2024, he was selected to play for [[Kandy Falcons]] in the [[2024 Lanka Premier League]].

==International career==
In January 2021, Shoriful was one of four uncapped players to be named in a preliminary squad for the [[One Day International]] (ODI) series [[West Indian cricket team in Bangladesh in 2020–21|against the West Indies]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thedailystar.net/sports/cricket/news/no-place-mashrafe-against-west-indies-2022181 |title=No place for Mashrafe against West Indies |work=The Daily Star |date=4 January 2021 |access-date=4 January 2021}}</ref> Later the same month, he was named in Bangladesh's ODI squad for their matches against the West Indies.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ban-vs-wi-shakib-al-hasan-named-in-bangladesh-squad-for-west-indies-odis-1248059 |title=Shakib Al Hasan named in Bangladesh squad for West Indies ODIs |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=16 January 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/bangladesh-vs-west-indies-shoriful-islam-call-up-causes-much-delight-but-little-surprise-1248088 |title=Shoriful Islam's Bangladesh call-up causes much delight but little surprise |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=16 January 2021}}</ref> The following month, he was named in Bangladesh's squad for their series [[Bangladeshi cricket team in New Zealand in 2020–21|against New Zealand]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/bangladesh-leave-out-taijul-islam-for-new-zealand-tour-1252314 |title=Bangladesh leave out Taijul Islam for New Zealand tour |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=19 February 2021}}</ref> He made his T20I debut on 28 March 2021, against [[New Zealand national cricket team|New Zealand]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1233979.html |title=1st T20I, Hamilton, Mar 28 2021, Bangladesh tour of New Zealand |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=28 March 2021}}</ref>

In April 2021, Shoriful was named in Bangladesh's preliminary [[Test cricket|Test]] squad for their series [[Bangladeshi cricket team in Sri Lanka in 2020–21|against Sri Lanka]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tigercricket.com.bd/2021/04/09/media-release-bangladesh-preliminary-squad-for-tour-of-sri-lanka-2021-announced/ |title=Media Release : Bangladesh Preliminary Squad for Tour of Sri Lanka 2021 announced |work=Bangladesh Cricket Board |access-date=9 April 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/sl-vs-ban-2021-uncapped-mukidul-islam-shohidul-islam-in-bangladesh-21-player-test-squad-that-will-travel-to-sri-lanka-1258327 |title=Uncapped Mukidul, Shohidul in Bangladesh 21-player Test squad that will travel to Sri Lanka |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=9 April 2021}}</ref> before being named in the final 15-man squad for the first Test.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bdcrictime.com/uncapped-shoriful-in-bangladesh-squad-for-first-test/ |title=Uncapped Shoriful in Bangladesh squad for first Sri Lanka Test |work=BD Crictime |access-date=20 April 2021}}</ref> He made his Test debut on 29 April 2021, for Bangladesh against [[Sri Lanka national cricket team|Sri Lanka]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1255829.html |title=2nd Test, Kandy, Apr 29 - May 3 2021, Bangladesh tour of Sri Lanka |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=29 April 2021}}</ref> In May 2021, he was named in Bangladesh's ODI squad for their series [[Sri Lankan cricket team in Bangladesh in 2021|against Sri Lanka]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ban-vs-sl-2021-bangladesh-drop-najmul-hossain-shanto-for-first-two-odis-against-sri-lanka-shakib-al-hasan-returns-1263627 |title=Bangladesh drop Najmul Hossain Shanto for first two ODIs against Sri Lanka, Shakib Al Hasan returns |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=20 May 2021}}</ref> He made his ODI debut for Bangladesh on 25 May 2021, against [[Sri Lanka national cricket team|Sri Lanka]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1262346.html |title=2nd ODI (D/N), Dhaka, May 25 2021, Sri Lanka tour of Bangladesh |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=25 May 2021}}</ref>

In September 2021, he was named in Bangladesh's squad for the [[2021 ICC Men's T20 World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/t20-world-cup-2021-bangladesh-squad-no-surprises-mahmudullah-captain-shakib-mushfiqur-rahim-in-1276979 |title=No surprises as Bangladesh name Mahmudullah-led squad for T20 World Cup |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=9 September 2021}}</ref> In September 2022, he was named in Bangladesh' squad for the [[2022 ICC Men's T20 World Cup]].<ref name="ban">{{cite web |title=Veteran star missing as Bangladesh name T20 World Cup squad |url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/2790115 |access-date=14 September 2022 |work=International Cricket Council}}</ref>

In September 2023, he was named in Bangladesh's squad for the [[2023 Cricket World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Senior player misses out as Bangladesh reveal CWC23 squad |url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/3674334 |access-date=26 September 2023 |work=International Cricket Council}}</ref> On 23 December 2023, during the third ODI [[Bangladeshi cricket team in New Zealand in 2023–24|against New Zealand]], he became the third fastest bowler for Bangladesh, in terms of matches (32), to take 50 wickets in ODIs.<ref>{{Cite web |last=আনোয়ার |first=সাইফুল্লাহ্ বিন |date=2023-12-23 |title=বাংলাদেশের ঐতিহাসিক জয়ের ম্যাচের যত রেকর্ড |url=https://www.prothomalo.com/sports/cricket/ngjyne4u3u |access-date=2023-12-23 |website=Prothomalo |language=bn}}</ref>

In May 2024, he was named in Bangladesh's squad for the [[2024 ICC Men's T20 World Cup]] tournament.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bangladesh Squad for Upcoming T20 World Cup |url=https://www.scorewaves.com/news-details/bangladesh-squad-for-t20-world-cup |access-date=2024-06-06 |website=ScoreWaves |language=en}}</ref>

'''Steven Peter Devereux Smith''' (born 2 June 1989) is an Australian international [[cricket]]er, former captain of the [[Australia national cricket team|Australian national team]] in all three formats of the game and since 2021, the vice-captain of the Australian Test team. He is regarded as one of the greatest Test batsmen of his generation, scoring over [[List of players who have scored 10,000 or more runs in Test cricket|10,000 Test runs]], having reached an [[ICC Player Rankings#Batsmen and Bowlers with a peak rating of 900 points or more|ICC Test batting rating]] of 947, the second-highest figure of all time, only behind [[Don Bradman]]'s 961 and was named [[ICC Awards of the Decade|ICC Men's Test Player of the Decade]] for 2011–2020.<ref>
*{{cite web |title=Steve Smith is best Test batsman of this generation: Virat Kohli. |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/icc-world-test-championship/steve-smith-is-best-test-batter-of-this-generation-virat-kohli/articleshow/100829733.cms |website=Times of India |access-date=29 June 2023 |date=7 June 2023}}
*{{cite web |title="Steve Smith is the best ever test batsman after Sir Don Bradman," Marnus Labuschagne makes big statement ahead of the start of Australian test summer |url=https://sportsamaze.com/news/steve-smith-is-the-best-ever-test-batsman-after-sir-don-bradman-marnus-labuschagne-makes-big-statement-ahead-of-the-start-of-australian-test-summer/ |website=SportsAmaze |access-date=29 June 2023 |date=18 November 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/sl-vs-aus-smith-joins-the-10000-club-of-elite-batters-in-galle-1467449|title=Steven Smith joins the 10k club of elite batters|work=ESPNCricInfo}}</ref>

Although he was initially selected for Australia as a [[leg-spin]]ning [[all-rounder]] in all formats in 2010, Smith was always earmarked as a batting prospect following successful batting campaigns in domestic cricket early in his career.<ref>*{{cite web |title=Steve Smith's early red-ball career is misunderstood. |url=https://www.theroar.com.au/2023/05/11/steve-smiths-early-red-ball-career-is-misunderstood/|website=The Roar |access-date=18 March 2024 |date=10 May 2023}}</ref> After playing five Test matches from 2010 to 2011 as a bowling all-rounder, he was recalled to the Australian Test team in 2013 as a batsman and took over the captaincy from [[Michael Clarke (cricketer)|Michael Clarke]] in late 2015. Smith now plays primarily as a batsman, and has predominantly batted at number 4 in Test cricket and number 3 in ODIs and T20Is.

Awards he has won include the [[Sir Garfield Sobers Trophy]] (ICC Cricketer of the Year) in 2015 becoming the youngest player to ever win the award, [[ICC Men's Test Cricketer of the Year|ICC Test Player of the Year]] in 2015 and 2017 becoming the only player to win the award more than once, the [[Compton–Miller Medal]] for [[player of the match|player of the series]] in the 2017–18 and 2019 [[The Ashes|Ashes]] being the only player to win the award more than once, the [[Allan Border Medal]] for the best player in Australian Cricket in 2015, 2018, 2021 and 2023 which is tied for the most of all time, [[Allan Border Medal#Shane Warne Men's Test Player of the Year|Australian Test Player of the Year]] in 2015 and 2018, [[Allan Border Medal#Men's One Day International Player of the Year|Australian One Day International Player of the Year]] in 2015 and 2021, [[ICC Awards of the Decade|ICC Men's Test Team of the Decade]] for 2011–2020, [[ICC Test Team of the Year]] in 2015, 2016, 2017 and 2019 and [[ICC ODI Team of the Year]] in 2015. He was named by ''[[Wisden Cricketers' Almanack|Wisden]]'' as one of their [[Wisden Cricketers of the Year|Cricketers of the Year]] in the 2016 [[Wisden Cricketers' Almanack|Wisden Almanack]].

Smith was a core member of the Australian white-ball teams that won the [[2015 Cricket World Cup|2015 ICC Cricket World Cup]], [[2021 ICC T20 World Cup|2021 ICC Men's T20 World Cup]] and the [[2023 Cricket World Cup|2023 ICC Cricket World Cup]] and was vice-captain of the Australia Test team that won the [[2021–2023 World Test Championship|2021–23 ICC World Test Championship]].

In March 2018, Smith as Australian captain was widely criticised for the [[2018 Australian ball-tampering scandal|ball tampering]] incident which occurred in the [[Australian cricket team in South Africa in 2017–18|third Test against South Africa]]. During the Test, Smith stood down from the team captaincy following immediate backlash and was replaced by [[Tim Paine]]. Following an investigation by [[Cricket Australia]], Smith was banned from all international and domestic cricket in Australia for one year, and from consideration for any leadership role for an additional year.

In November 2021, Smith returned to an official Australian leadership role, as Test vice-captain starting in the [[2021–22 Ashes series]]. In December 2021, Smith returned to Test captaincy duties when [[Pat Cummins]] was unavailable due to [[COVID-19]] for the 2nd Test. He has since captained in 6 Tests for 5 wins and a draw, including Australia's only [[Australian cricket team in India in 2022–23|Test victory]] in India since 2017 when he was captain. In March 2023, Smith returned to ODI captaincy duties, he went on to captain another 13 ODIs, winning the [[Australian cricket team in India in 2022–23|2022–23 ODI series]] vs [[India national cricket team|India]], the [[West Indian cricket team in Australia in 2023–24|2023–24 ODI series]] vs [[West Indies cricket team|West Indies]] and the [[Australian cricket team in England in 2024|2024 ODI series]] v [[England cricket team|England]] and captaining Australia in the [[2025 Champions Trophy|2025 ICC Champions Trophy]]. He retired from ODI cricket on 5 March 2025, leading Australia in his last ODI as captain.

==Early and personal life==

Steve Smith was born on 2 June 1989 in [[Kogarah, New South Wales|Kogarah]], a suburb of the [[St George, Sydney|St George region]] of [[Southern Sydney]] to an Australian father, Peter, who has a degree in chemistry,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.smh.com.au/sport/cricket/steve-smith-goes-from-teenage-club-sensation-to-australian-cricket-captain-20141215-127mi3.html|title=Steve Smith goes from teenage club sensation to Australian cricket captain|work=The Sydney Morning Herald|date=15 December 2014|first=Chris|last=Barrett|access-date=26 January 2015}}</ref> and an English mother, Gillian. Smith attended [[Menai High School]] and left at age 17 to play cricket in England.{{citation needed|date=June 2025}}

Because his mother was born in [[London]], Smith has dual British and Australian citizenship.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.news.com.au/sport/cricket/the-ashes/steve-smith-almost-played-cricket-for-england/news-story/8b98dda106523b6d52ad71a5904ace63|title=Steve Smith almost played cricket for England|date=20 November 2017|work=news.com|access-date=29 April 2018}}</ref> In 2011, Smith started dating Dani Willis, a commerce and law student at [[Macquarie University]].<ref name="smithlove">{{cite news|url=https://www.smh.com.au/sport/cricket/how-love-turned-steve-smith-from-cricket-tragic-to-australian-test-captain-20141216-128dsf.html|title=How love turned Steve Smith from cricket tragic to Australian Test captain|date=16 December 2014|work=The Sydney Morning Herald|first=Andrew|last=Webster|access-date=26 January 2015}}</ref> In June 2017, the couple announced their engagement while on holiday in New York.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.news.com.au/sport/sports-life/australian-cricket-captain-steve-smith-announces-engagement-to-dani-willis/news-story/a92a345245742068751d7a51e3826c48|date=29 June 2017|title=Australian cricket captain Steve Smith announces engagement to Dani Willis|work=news.com.au}}</ref> The couple married at [[Berrima, New South Wales]] on 15 September 2018.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/steve-smith-wedding-dani-willis-married-berrima-southern-highlands-new-south-wales-nsw-ceremony/2018-09-16|date=16 September 2018|title=Smith, Willis marry in Southern Highlands|work=cricket.com.au|publisher=Cricket Australia}}</ref>

Smith is a supporter of the [[Sydney Roosters]] in the [[National Rugby League]].<ref>{{Cite web | title=Steve Smith and David Warner flying NRL flag in the Australian cricket team {{!}} Daily Telegraph | url=https://www.dailytelegraph.com.au/sport/nrl/teams/roosters/steve-smith-and-david-warner-flying-nrl-flag-in-the-australian-cricket-team/news-story/5ff721555c2656b7fc17d9a25cc202e5 | access-date=2024-12-26 | website=www.dailytelegraph.com.au}}</ref>

==Youth and domestic career==
[[File:STEVE SMITH (3072377456).jpg|thumb|upright=0.8|Smith fielding for New South Wales in 2008]]
During his junior years of cricket, Smith's role was primarily batting all-rounder, bowling fast-medium until the age of 15 before switching to leg-spin.<ref>*{{cite web |title=Special Q&A: Steve Smith and Virat Kohli's full chat. |url=https://www.cricket.com.au/videos/2966890/special-qa-steve-smith-and-virat-kohlis-full-chat|website=cricket.com.au |access-date=18 March 2024 |date=16 December 2020}}</ref> In 2007, Smith temporarily left Australia to play cricket in England, where he played club cricket for [[Sevenoaks Vine]] in the [[Kent Cricket League]]. His outstanding performances for Sevenoaks resulted in being selected to play for Surrey County's second XI.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2010/may/08/steve-smith-england-australia|title=Steve Smith spins from England's grasp to boost Australia's attack|work=The Guardian|date=9 May 2010|first=Andy|last=Bull|access-date=24 March 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.heraldsun.com.au/sport/young-leg-spin-tyro-steven-smith-sets-his-sights-on-test-cricket-heights/story-e6frf9if-1225817877445|title=Young leg-spin tyro Steven Smith sets his sights on Test cricket heights|work=Herald Sun|date=11 January 2010|first=James|last=Hooper|access-date=26 January 2015}}</ref><ref name="smithwoodhill">{{cite news|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/magazine/content/story/689705.html|title=Learning on the job|work=ESPNcricinfo Magazine|date=18 November 2013|first=Daniel|last=Brettig|access-date=26 January 2015}}</ref>
Smith was a member of the [[Australia national under-19 cricket team|Australian team]] at the [[2008 Under-19 Cricket World Cup]] in [[Malaysia]]. In the tournament he scored 114 runs and took seven wickets in four matches.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/u19wc2008/engine/records/batting/most_runs_career.html?id=3138;type=tournament|title=Statistics batting|access-date=29 June 2018|publisher=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/u19wc2008/engine/records/bowling/most_wickets_career.html?id=3138;type=tournament|title=Statistics bowling|access-date=29 June 2018|publisher=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

Smith made his first-class debut for [[New South Wales cricket team|New South Wales]] against [[Western Warriors|Western Australia]] at the [[Sydney Cricket Ground|SCG]] on 25 January 2008. He scored 33 runs in his only innings as New South Wales defeated Western Australia.<ref>{{cite web |title=Full Scorecard of New South Wales vs Western Australia, Sheffield Shield – Score Report |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/8043/scorecard/298335/new-south-wales-vs-western-australia-pura-cup-2007-08 |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=13 June 2019}}</ref> He was part of the New South Wales team that won the [[2009 Champions League Twenty20|2009 Twenty20 Champions League]]. In the final against [[Trinidad and Tobago national cricket team|Trinidad and Tobago]] at [[Hyderabad]], Smith delivered an all-round performance, scoring 33 runs with the bat and taking two wickets.<ref>{{cite web |title=Full Scorecard of New South Wales vs Trinidad & Tobago, Champions League Twenty20, Final – Score Report|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/8082/scorecard/416946/new-south-wales-vs-trinidad-&-tobago-final-champions-league-twenty20-2009-10 |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=18 June 2019}}</ref>

By the end of the 2009–10 domestic season, Smith had a first-class batting average of over 50 after 13 first-class matches. While his first-class bowling average in the high forties was not as impressive, his bowling appeared to be steadily improving following some well-publicised mentoring and praise from [[Shane Warne]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.smh.com.au/sport/cricket/is-that-your-real-heir-warnie-20091227-lg8x.html |title=Is that your real heir, Warnie? |author=Hogan, Jesse |work=The Sydney Morning Herald |date=28 December 2009 |access-date=14 January 2015}}</ref> In the final match of the season he took 7 for 64 in the second innings against [[South Australia cricket team|South Australia]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ausdomestic-09/engine/match/417666.html |title=Scorecard: New South Wales v. South Australia at Sydney, 10–12 March 2010 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=14 January 2015}}</ref>

In October 2013, Smith as captain and No.3 batsman, led NSW to their first One-Day Final for the first time since [[2006–07 Ford Ranger One Day Cup season|2006]] when they beat South Australia. In the [[2013–14 Ryobi One-Day Cup]] Final against Queensland, Smith scored 61 runs, after QLD elected to bowl first. NSW reached a total of 317, and QLD chased it down in the final over with 5 balls left to spare in the match.<ref>{{cite web |title=Determined Queensland claim Ryobi title |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/ryobi-one-day-cup-2013-14-669165/new-south-wales-vs-queensland-final-669269/match-report |website=ESPN}}</ref>

In March 2014, Smith batting No.3, scored 75 and 103 not out to lead NSW to draw against Western Australia in the [[2013-14 Sheffield Shield season|2013–14 Sheffield Shield]] final in Canberra. NSW finished 1st in the season so they claimed the title, for the first time since [[2007–08 Sheffield Shield season|2007–08]].<ref>{{cite web |title=NSW claim Shield after Smith ton |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/sheffield-shield-2013-14-669163/new-south-wales-vs-western-australia-final-669229/match-report |website=ESPN}}</ref>

In 2014–15, Smith did not feature in the 2014–15 domestic season, due to international commitments.

In October 2015, Smith as captain led NSW to beat South Australia in the [[2015–16 Matador BBQs One-Day Cup]] Final at [[North Sydney Oval]] with 2 catches and 84 runs, batting No.3. NSW winning by 9 wickets with 20 overs to spare with Smith and [[Ed Cowan]] remaining not out, comfortably chasing the 221 target in 29.5 overs.<ref>{{cite web |title=Smith, Cowan drive NSW to one-day title|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/matador-bbqs-one-day-cup-2015-16-895855/new-south-wales-vs-south-australia-final-895911/match-report |website=ESPN}}</ref> Smith was the highest run scorer of the season with 435 runs, averaging 145 with 2 hundreds, 3 fifties and a highest score of 143, striking at over 100, undismissed in 3 of the 6 matches he played.<ref>{{cite web |title=Most runs in Matador BBQs One-Day Cup, 2015/16|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/records/tournament/batting-most-runs-career/matador-bbqs-one-day-cup-2015-16-10263|website=ESPN}}</ref>

In October 2015, following the win in the [[2015–16 Matador BBQs One-Day Cup]] Final, Smith made his only Sheffield Shield appearance for the 2015–16 season, playing again against South Australia, Smith scored 67 in the first innings and scored 152 runs from 192 deliveries in the second innings.

In October 2016, Smith scored his third consecutive Sheffield Shield century, scoring 117 against Queensland at [[The Gabba]].<ref>{{cite web |title=NSW vs Queensland, 2nd Match at Brisbane, Oct 25 2016 – Full Scorecard|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/sheffield-shield-2016-17-1036353/queensland-vs-new-south-wales-2nd-match-1036373/full-scorecard|website=ESPN}}</ref> This was his 10th consecutive score of 50 or more in a Sheffield Shield match innings, dating back to the 2012–13 Sheffield Shield season, when Smith scored 90 against Queensland in Canberra, November 2012.<ref>{{cite web |title=Queensland vs NSW, 17th Match at Canberra, Nov 27 2012 – Full Scorecard|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/sheffield-shield-2012-13-576078/new-south-wales-vs-queensland-17th-match-576098/full-scorecard|website=ESPN}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=SHEFFIELD SHIELD MATCHES PLAYED BY STEVEN SMITH|url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/113/113416/Sheffield_Shield_Matches.html|website=cricketarchive}}</ref>

In November 2017, against Western Australia in the Sheffield Shield at the [[Hurstville Oval]] Smith scored 76 from 130 in NSWs first innings, striking at 58.46 and in the second innings, scored 127 from 167, at strike rate of 76.01.<ref>{{cite web |title=NSW vs West Aust, 5th match at Sydney, Sheffield Shield, Nov 04 2017 – Full Scorecard|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/sheffield-shield-2017-18-1118861/new-south-wales-vs-western-australia-5th-match-1118868/full-scorecard|website=ESPN}}</ref>

In 2018–19, Smith was banned from the domestic competitions for the 2018–19 cricket season due to [[Sandpaper Gate]].

In October 2019, Smith played his first match back in Australia since returning from his [[Sandpaper Gate]] suspension, playing for NSW against Queensland at the Gabba in the opening round of the [[2019–20 Sheffield Shield season]]. In Queensland's first innings, Smith took 2 catches and bowled 2 overs. Smith was dismissed for 0 from 5 late on day 1 by [[Cameron Gannon]], while fellow returnee Warner scored 125 runs. In Queensland's second innings, Smith again took 2 catches and bowled 6 wicket-less overs. Smith scored 21 from 31 in the second innings.<ref>{{cite web |title=Queensland vs NSW, 2nd Match at Brisbane, Marsh Shield, Oct 10 2019 – Full Scorecard|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/marsh-sheffield-shield-2019-20-1196060/queensland-vs-new-south-wales-2nd-match-1196115/full-scorecard|website=ESPN}}</ref>

In October 2019, Smith scored his first century in Australia since 2017, playing against Tasmania at the [[Drummoyne Oval]] in the Sheffield Shield, Smith scored a patient 106 runs from 258 deliveries at a strike rate of 41.08.<ref>{{cite web |title=Tasmania vs NSW, 4th Match at Sydney, Marsh Shield, Oct 18 2019 – Full Scorecard|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/marsh-sheffield-shield-2019-20-1196060/new-south-wales-vs-tasmania-4th-match-1196117/full-scorecard|website=ESPN}}</ref> In the following One-Day Cup match, Smith returned to the NSW One-Day team for the first time since he captained the [[2015–16 Matador BBQs One-Day Cup]] Final win. Smith was out of 9 from 6 deliveries.<ref>{{cite web |title=NSW vs Tasmania, 13th Match at Sydney, Marsh Cup, Oct 23 2019 – Full Scorecard|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/the-marsh-cup-2019-20-1196059/new-south-wales-vs-tasmania-13th-match-1196104/full-scorecard|website=ESPN}}</ref>

In November 2019, Smith scored his 12th Sheffield Shield century, playing against Western Australia, at the SCG, Smith scored an even more patient century than the previous one against Tasmania, scoring 103 runs from 295 deliveries, at a strike rate of 34.91. Smith took 1 catch and 1 wicket in the match.<ref>{{cite web |title=NSW vs West Aust, 10th Match at Sydney, Marsh Shield, Nov 11 2019 – Full Scorecard|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/marsh-sheffield-shield-2019-20-1196060/new-south-wales-vs-western-australia-10th-match-1196123/full-scorecard|website=ESPN}}</ref>

In February 2021, Smith scored 127 runs from 124 deliveries against Victoria in the [[2020–21 Marsh One-Day Cup]] at North Sydney Oval. Smith also bowled 2 wicket-less overs with the ball.<ref>{{cite web |title=NSW vs Victoria, 1st Match at Sydney, Marsh Cup, Feb 15 2021 – Full Scorecard|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/the-marsh-cup-2020-21-1244113/new-south-wales-vs-victoria-1st-match-1244127/full-scorecard|website=ESPN}}</ref>

In October 2024, Smith returned to the Sheffield Shield for the first time since the 2020–21 Shield season. Playing against Victoria, batting in his customary No.3 position for NSW, Smith was out caught for 3 off 29 in the 1st innings and was out for 0 from 4, lbw to [[Scott Boland]]. Smith also made an appearance for NSW in the [[Dean Jones Trophy]] for the first time since the 2020–21 Marsh One-Day Cup. Smith scored 56 from 53 deliveries before falling lbw to [[Peter Siddle]].

In October 2025, Smith scored his 13th Sheffield Shield century, for NSW, against Queensland at the Gabba. Smith batted at No.4 for NSW for the first time since 2013, with Smith only batting No.4 once when [[Nathan Lyon]] was used as a nightwatchman in 2021 against Victoria.

In November 2025, Smith was re-instated as NSW captain. In his first game as NSW captain since 2017, against Victoria at the SCG, Smith batted fluently in both innings scoring half centuries in both innings, while the rest of his teammates struggled with the bat. Smith was undismissed in the 4th innings while he only was dismissed taking a risk while wickets fell around him in the 2nd innings. Victoria won by 300 runs.<ref>{{cite web |title=Victoria vs NSW, 10th Match at Sydney, Sheffield Shield, Nov 10 2025 – Full Scorecard|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/sheffield-shield-2025-26-1495274/new-south-wales-vs-victoria-10th-match-1495288/full-scorecard|website=ESPN}}</ref>

In Australia's One-Day Domestic Competition, Smith has the second highest average of all time with 58.09, only behind [[Michael Bevan]]s 61.18 for those that have scored at least 500 runs.<ref>{{cite web |title=Highest averages For Australian Domestic One-Day Competition|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/records/trophy/batting-highest-career-batting-average/australian-domestic-one-day-competition-122|website=ESPN}}</ref>

===Big Bash League===

Smith made his [[Twenty20]] cricket debut for [[New South Wales cricket team|New South Wales]] in a match against South Australia at Adelaide on 1 January 2008 during the six team [[KFC Big Bash]] competition.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/298379.html |title=Scorecard: South Australia v New South Wales at Adelaide, 1 January 2008 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=11 January 2015}}</ref> Smith was the leading wicket taker at the 2008 Big Bash tournament. He took 4/15 against Queensland and finished with 9 wickets overall.<ref name=ciprofile>{{cricinfo|id=267192|name=Steven Smith|access-date=2 January 2018}}</ref> He was also named the second-best player of the tournament.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://content-aus.cricinfo.com/australia/content/current/story/342209.html |title=Katich crowned Pura Cup Player of the Year |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=13 March 2008|date=13 March 2008}}</ref> Smith batted across the order from 3 to 7 during the two seasons of the competition.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/player/267192.html?class=6;filter=advanced;orderby=start;template=results;trophy=124;type=batting;view=innings|title=Steve Smith Big Bash (State Competition) Batting Innings Records|work=ESPNCricInfo|date=17 January 2010}}</ref>

In 2011–12, the Australian T20 competition became the city-based [[Big Bash League]] featuring eight teams. Smith joined the [[Sydney Sixers]] and filled in as captain when Brad Haddin could not play due to Test duties,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.sportsnewsfirst.com.au/articles/2012/01/28/sixers-smash-scorchers-to-win-bbl/ |title=Sixers smash Scorchers to win BBL |work=Sports News First |date=28 January 2012 |access-date=9 August 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120512062742/http://www.sportsnewsfirst.com.au/articles/2012/01/28/sixers-smash-scorchers-to-win-bbl/ |archive-date=12 May 2012}}</ref> subsequently leading the team to victory in the inaugural season. As an all-rounder, he scored 166 runs with the bat from nine matches with a strike rate of 130.71, including one half century. With the ball, he took 6 wickets at an economy rate of 8.06 per over. He also took nine catches throughout the tournament.<ref>{{cite web |first=Trevor |last=Bayliss |author-link=Trevor Bayliss |url=http://www.sydneysixers.com.au/team/player-profiles/steven-smith |title=Steven Smith – Sydney Sixers – Big Bash League |publisher=Sydney Sixers |date=6 June 2012 |access-date=9 August 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130628072516/http://www.sydneysixers.com.au/team/player-profiles/steven-smith |archive-date=28 June 2013}}</ref> In the [[2011–12 Big Bash League season|BBL01]] final, Smith captained the Sixers to the title against the [[Perth Scorchers]] by 7 wickets while chasing down the target of 157 within 18.5 overs after the Scorchers made 5/156 in 20 overs. Smith batted at No. 4 and No.5 for the Sixers during this period.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/player/267192.html?class=6;host=2;spanmax1=30+Jan+2035;spanval1=span;template=results;type=batting;view=innings|title=Smith T20 records|work=ESPN|date=25 June 2024}}</ref>

In October 2016, Smith took on an official ambassador role for the Sixers, given his international commitments as Australian captain in all formats, he was unable to appear in a playing capacity.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sydneysixers.com.au/news/3398840/smith-becomes-clubs-official-ambassador|title=Smith becomes Club's official ambassador|work=Sydney Sixers|date=28 October 2016}}</ref>

In 2019–20, Smith returned to the Sixers in a playing capacity for the Sixers' final four matches of [[2019–20 Big Bash League season|BBL09]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/cricket/domestic-cricket/big-bash/big-bash-league-201920-steve-smith-signs-with-sydney-sixers-for-bbl-09/news-story/a8c6a2dc319cf6377af694445bb051b2|title=Steve Smith signs with Sydney Sixers for BBL 09 |work=Fox Cricket|date=14 November 2019}}</ref> Smith took on the No.3 role for the Sixers for the first time. His best performance was a man of the match performance against the Renegades, scoring 66 not out from 44 deliveries.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/big-bash-league-2019-20-1195572/sydney-sixers-vs-melbourne-renegades-52nd-match-1195624/match-report|title=Josh Philippe and Steven Smith guide impressive Sydney Sixers chase|work=ESPNCricInfo}}</ref> In February 2020, Smith played in the BBL09 final against the Melbourne Stars, scoring 21 runs from 12 deliveries.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/big-bash-league-2019-20-1195572/sydney-sixers-vs-melbourne-stars-final-1195633/full-scorecard|title=Josh Philippe fires Sydney Sixers to second BBL title in rain-hit encounter|work=ESPN CricInfo}}</ref> This was Smith's second BBL title, after winning the inaugural title as captain.

In October 2020, during COVID-19, Smith ruled out playing for the Sixers during BBL10.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.smh.com.au/sport/cricket/no-chance-of-playing-bbl-says-bubble-weary-smith-20201031-p56aaz.html|title='No chance' of playing BBL, says bubble-weary Smith |work=Sydney Morning Herald|date=30 October 2020}}</ref>

In January 2022, Cricket Australia blocked Steve Smith from playing in the BBL11 finals on a technicality that he wasn't registered in the player pool, having expected international commitments to have made him unavailable. This decision drew criticism from past players including former England captain [[Michael Vaughan]] who labelled the decision "bonkers" and [[Michael Hussey]] who said "I can't believe it." .<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/3318719|title='Sad for cricket': CA blocks Smith's Big Bash return|work=Cricket.com.au}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/cricket/domestic-cricket/big-bash/bbl-2022-steve-smith-denied-place-in-finals-series-sydney-sixers-big-bash-league-schedule-teams/news-story/9f5de0c77ff3a5daa1e83877ff0fbe21|title='Wouldn't happen to LeBron in the NBA': Inside Smith's 'bonkers' BBL ban as Cricket NSW chief fumes |work=Fox Cricket|date=21 January 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/cricket/domestic-cricket/big-bash/bbl-2022-steve-smith-sydney-sixers-big-bash-league-cricket-news-michael-vaugh-and-mike-hussey-slam-cricket-australia/news-story/b98fc9dd37ecab750914e771fdc3dbbb|title='I can't believe it': Legends roast 'laughable' call that crushed Smith's BBL dream |work=Fox Cricket|date=21 January 2022}}</ref>

In December 2022, Smith signed a "marquee" 2-year contract to return to the Sixers for [[2022–23 Big Bash League season|BBL12]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/cricket/bbl12-steve-smith-signs-with-the-sixers-marquee-player-replacement-player-david-warner-sydney-thunder-signings-news-cricket-australia/news-story/508ffc23e625fb2f4b024dc69a543a89n|title=Smith's whopping $250k Sixers deal as blockbuster Sydney Smash firms|work=Fox Cricket}}</ref> In his first match back, Smith was promoted to open the batting for the first time in the Big Bash. Smith scored 36 runs in a 6 run win against the Scorchers. In his second match, against [[Adelaide Strikers]], Smith scored his maiden BBL century, he scored 101 runs off 56 deliveries as the Sixers won by 59 runs.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://live.cricket.com.au/match/3034/54547/sydney-sixers-men-vs-adelaide-strikers-men-kfc-bbl-12/scorecard?_gl=1*1h8xatw*_ga*OTI0OTgyMDQzLjE2Njk3ODkxMjM.*_ga_1GQDGSTHMG*MTY3NDEwNTU4Ni4xLjEuMTY3NDEwNTYwNC4wLjAuMA. |title=Steve Smith 2 year return results in a century |access-date=17 January 2023 |website=Live Cricket|date=17 January 2023}}</ref> In the next match, Smith scored back to back BBL hundreds with 125* runs off 66 deliveries against [[Sydney Thunder]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/big-bash-league-2022-23-1324623/sydney-sixers-vs-sydney-thunder-50th-match-1324673/match-report|title=Smith's career-best T20 knock puts Sixers in hunt for top spot|work=ESPNCricInfo|date=23 January 2023}}</ref>

In December 2023, Smith was only available for 2 matches of [[2023–24 Big Bash League season|BBL13]]. He produced another man of the match performance against the Renegades', scoring 61 from 42 deliveries.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/big-bash-league-2023-24-1386092/sydney-sixers-vs-melbourne-renegades-2nd-match-1386095/match-report|title=Smith and Dwarshuis shine in Sixers' narrow win over Renegades|work=ESPN CricInfo}}</ref>

In August 2024, Smith signed a three-year contract with the Sixers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sydneysixers.com.au/news/4087920/smith-to-be-a-sixer-for-life|title=Smith to be a Sixer for life|work=Sydney Sixers|date=19 August 2024}}</ref>

In January 2025, Smith scored his 3rd BBL century, in [[2024–25 Big Bash League season|BBL14]], against the Perth Scorchers at the SCG, scoring 121 runs from 64 deliveries in a 14-run win.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/big-bash-league-2024-25-1443056/sydney-sixers-vs-perth-scorchers-30th-match-1443086/match-report|title=Smith flays 121* to send a reminder of his T20 worth |work=ESPN CricInfo}}</ref> Smith backed it up with a second straight man of the match, against the Strikers, scoring 52 runs from 31 deliveries, in a 3-wicket win.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/big-bash-league-2024-25-1443056/sydney-sixers-vs-sydney-thunder-37th-match-1443093/full-scorecard|title=Steven Smith fifty sets up Sydney Sixers' nervy win over Adelaide Strikers|work=ESPN CricInfo}}</ref>

Smith has the most BBL centuries of all time with 4 from 35 innings and has the highest batting average in the competition's history of any player with more than 1150 runs scored.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/records/trophy/batting-highest-career-batting-average/big-bash-league-158|title=Highest averages For Big Bash League|work=ESPN CricInfo}}</ref>

===Indian Premier League===
Smith was first bought by [[Royal Challengers Bangalore]] for the [[2010 Indian Premier League]] as a replacement for [[Jesse Ryder]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Rising all-rounder Steven Smith has become the latest Australian to join the Indian Premier League by signing a rich deal with Bangalore.|url=http://www.dailytelegraph.com.au/sport/cricket/steve-smith-strikes-rich-in-ipl/story-e6frey50-1225829827517|work=The Daily Telegraph|location=Sydney|access-date=6 April 2012|date=12 February 2010}}</ref> During the [[List of 2011 Indian Premier League personnel changes|2011 IPL player auction]], he was bought by [[Kochi Tuskers Kerala]] for $200,000,<ref>{{cite news |title=IPL auction, Day 1: Who got whom |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/cricket/ipl-2012/news/IPL-auction-Day-1-Who-got-whom/iplarticleshow/7238072.cms |newspaper=The Times of India |access-date=15 July 2019}}</ref> but he had to have an ankle operation and was not available to play for them that season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Steven Smith to have ankle surgery |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/australia/content/story/511007.html |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=10 June 2019 |date=14 April 2011}}</ref>

The next season, Kochi Tuskers were dropped from the IPL and Smith was put up for auction. He went unsold at the [[List of 2012 Indian Premier League personnel changes|2012 IPL Players Auction]], but was later bought as a replacement for [[Mitchell Marsh]] by the [[Pune Warriors India]] following Smith's good form during the Big Bash League, attracted the attention of former India Captain [[Sourav Ganguly]], and was recruited to play for the [[Pune Warriors India]] team captained by [[Sourav Ganguly]] in the 2012 [[Indian Premier League]]. Smith was also made captain of the team for one match, when Ganguly was rested, despite Australian captain [[Michael Clarke (cricketer)|Michael Clarke]] being the vice-captain. He continued to play for the same franchise in 2013, under the captaincy of [[Angelo Mathews]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Steven Smith replaces Mitchell Marsh in Pune squad  |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/news/Steven-Smith-replaces-Mitchell-Marsh-in-Pune-squad/articleshow/12210634.cms |website=The Times of India |date=10 March 2012 |access-date=16 July 2019}}</ref> In his first match for his new team, he scored 39 runs off 32 balls to lead his team to victory against the [[Mumbai Indians]]. He received the Man of the Match award for this effort.<ref>{{cite web |title=Full Scorecard of Mumbai Indians vs Pune Warriors, Indian Premier League, 3rd match – Score Report |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/8048/scorecard/548308/mumbai-indians-vs-pune-warriors-3rd-match-indian-premier-league-2012 |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=16 July 2019}}</ref>

In the auction for IPL 2014, Smith was bought by [[Rajasthan Royals]] for $600,000.<ref name=SAL>{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/india/content/story/957061.html |title=Kohli the highest-paid cricketer in IPL |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |date=1 January 2016|access-date=5 January 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/indian-premier-league-2014/content/story/703627.html |title=IPL franchises allowed to retain up to five players |date=24 December 2013 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=5 January 2017}}</ref> Smith was given the captaincy of the Royals in the latter half of the 2015 season and led the team to significant victories, thus ensuring a berth for his team in the play-off part of the tournament.<ref>{{cite web |title=Watson hands IPL captaincy to Smith |url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/chennai-super-kings-rajasthan-royals-shane-watson-james-faulkner-match-report/2015-05-10?mode=amp |website=cricket.com.au |access-date=15 July 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Indian Premier League 2015 – Points Table |url=https://cricbuzz.com/cricket-series/2330/indian-premier-league-2015/points-table |website=[[Cricbuzz]] |access-date=15 July 2019}}</ref>

During the 2016 IPL Auction, Smith was bought by new franchise, the [[Rising Pune Supergiant]]s for the same price as in the previous auction ($600,000),<ref name=SAL /> and struggled early for form. Smith finally broke a run of low scores against [[Sunrisers Hyderabad]], scoring 46*. His form continued as he registered his maiden T20 century against the [[Gujarat Lions]], scoring 101 off 54 balls.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.iplt20.com/news/2016/match-reports/7494/match-report-m25-rps-vs-gl|title=Match Report M25 RPS v GL|access-date=9 May 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160502102711/http://www.iplt20.com/news/2016/match-reports/7494/match-report-m25-rps-vs-gl|archive-date=2 May 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> He then went on to score a further 45 against the [[Mumbai Indians]], before being ruled out of the remainder of the tournament with a wrist injury.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.iplt20.com/news/2016/match-reports/7543/match-report-m29-rps-vs-mi |title=Match Report M29 RPS v MI |website=IPL |access-date=5 January 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170313150451/http://www.iplt20.com/news/2016/match-reports/7543/match-report-m29-rps-vs-mi |archive-date=13 March 2017 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

The Supergiant management axed [[MS Dhoni]] as captain and named Smith as captain for the 2017 season. In RPS's first game against [[Mumbai Indians]], Smith led his team to victory in style, scoring 84* and was awarded the Man of The Match. However, three consecutive losses left his team in last position on the points table. A total of 8 wins in 10 matches helped the Supergiants finish in the second position, and thus qualify for the playoffs, with Smith receiving praise for his captaincy from renowned cricketers and experts like [[Sunil Gavaskar]] and [[Kevin Pietersen]]. He led his team to the final with a 20-run victory over Mumbai Indians in Qualifier 1. In the final, Smith's men faced Mumbai yet again. Smith scored 51 off 50 balls but could not lead RPS to victory. Supergiants lost the match by one run.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/8048/scorecard/1082650/mumbai-indians-vs-rising-pune-supergiant-final-ipl-2017/|title=Final (N), Indian Premier League at Hyderabad, May 21 2017 – Match Summary – ESPNcricinfo|work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> Smith was RPS's highest run scorer in the tournament, scoring 472 runs at an average of 39.33, including three 50's.<ref>{{cite web |title=Most runs in 2017 season of Indian Premier League |url=https://www.iplt20.com/stats/2017/most-runs |website=www.iplt20.com |access-date=23 March 2019}}</ref>

In February 2018, he was named as captain of [[Rajasthan Royals]] for the [[2018 Indian Premier League|IPL 2018]].<ref>{{cite web|title= Steve Smith named Rajasthan Royals captain|work=Cricbuzz |date=24 February 2018 |url=https://www.cricbuzz.com/cricket-news/100573/steve-smith-named-rajasthan-royals-captain-for-ipl-2018|access-date=24 February 2018}}</ref> However, following his admission of involvement in the Australian test team's ball tampering controversy in the Third Test in South Africa in March 2018, it was announced by the team that Smith has stood down from that role and [[Ajinkya Rahane]] took charge as the new captain for Rajasthan Royals team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.news.com.au/sport/cricket/steve-smith-stands-down-as-rajasthan-royals-captain/news-story/43a40d11acd0cb7e683aca65e066707c|title=Steve Smith stood down as Rajasthan Royals skipper following ball tampering scandal|access-date=26 March 2018|work=news.com.au|date=26 March 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/cricket/news/15811/11304741/steve-smith-steps-down-as-rajasthan-royals-skipper|title=Steve Smith finds himself guilty conscious and resigned from the captaincy post for RR|access-date=26 March 2018|work=Sky Sports}}</ref>

On 28 March 2018, after being banned by Cricket Australia for his involvement in a ball tampering incident, Smith's player contract with the Royals was terminated by the [[Board of Control for Cricket in India]] as Steve Smith and fellow Australian batsman [[David Warner (cricketer)|David Warner]] were banned from playing for their respective teams for the upcoming 2018 IPL edition.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/david-warner-steve-smith-banned-ipl-2million-sunrisers-hyderabad-rajasthan-royals-ball-tampering/2018-03-28|title=IPL tear up $2.4m Warner, Smith deals|access-date=28 March 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/22939978/david-warner-steven-smith-axed-ipl-2018|title=Warner and Smith axed from IPL 2018|publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=30 March 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.firstpost.com/firstcricket/sports-news/steve-smith-and-david-warner-banned-from-ipl-2018-by-bcci-over-ball-tampering-scandal-4409235.html|title=Steve Smith and David Warner banned from IPL 2018 by BCCI over ball-tampering scandal|website=FirstCricket|date=28 March 2018 |access-date=30 March 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.express.co.uk/sport/cricket/938162/IPL-2018-Steve-Smith-David-Warner-OUT-competition-ball-tampering-scandal|title=IPL 2018: Steve Smith and David Warner OUT of competition for ball-tampering in HUGE blow|last=Gray|first=James|date=28 March 2018|work=Daily Express|access-date=30 March 2018}}</ref>

In November 2018, Smith was retained by [[Rajasthan Royals]] for the [[2019 Indian Premier League]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Acharya |first1=Shayan |title=IPL: Rajasthan Royals retains Steve Smith |url=https://sportstar.thehindu.com/cricket/ipl/rajasthan-royals-steve-smith-indian-premier-league-ipl-auctions/article25506863.ece |website=Sportstar |date=15 November 2018 |access-date=20 January 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=IPL 2019: Rajasthan Royals retain 16 players including Steve Smith |url=https://www.bignewsnetwork.com/news/258314371/ipl-2019-rajasthan-royals-retain-16-players-including-steve-smith |website=Big News Network.com |access-date=20 January 2019}}</ref> After losing six out of first eight matches of the season, Smith was appointed as the captain of the Rajasthan Royals by replacing Ajinkya Rahane.<ref>{{cite web |title=Smith takes over from Rahane as Rajasthan Royals captain |url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/1190191 |website=www.icc-cricket.com |access-date=20 April 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Smith replaces Rahane as captain as Royals look for 'fresh approach' |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/26564605/steven-smith-replaces-ajinkya-rahane-captain-rajasthan-royals-look-fresh-approach?platform=amp |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=20 April 2019 |date=20 April 2019}}</ref> In the tournament, he scored 319 runs at an average of 39.87, including three fifties.<ref>{{cite web |title=Indian Premier League-most fifties in 2019 season |url=https://www.iplt20.com/stats/2019/most-fifties |website=www.iplt20.com |access-date=1 May 2019}}</ref>

He went unsold in the [[List of 2022 Indian Premier League personnel changes|2022 IPL auctions]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Derek |first=Vikas Singh |date=12 February 2022 |title=Steve Smith Goes Unsold In IPL 2022 Mega Auction |work=CricketAddictor |url=https://cricketaddictor.com/indian-premier-league-ipl-2022/steve-smith-goes-unsold-in-ipl-2022-mega-auction/ |access-date=3 April 2022}}</ref>
