===English domestic cricket===

In June 2010, Smith played 5 matches in the [[2010 Twenty20 Cup]] for [[Worcestershire County Cricket Club|Worcestershire]]. Smith  scored 67 runs from 4 innings batting No.5 and picked up 6 wickets.

In October 2019, Smith alongside Australia teammate [[Mitchell Starc]] was selected by the [[Welsh Fire]] for the inaugural [[The Hundred (cricket)|The Hundred]] season in 2020.<ref>{{cite web |title=The Hundred: Welsh Fire pick Steve Smith and Mitchell Starc|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/cricket/50119125|website=BBC |date=20 October 2019 }}</ref>

In February 2020, Smith was appointed as the inaugural Welsh Fire captain for the inaugural season of The Hundred.<ref>{{cite web |title=STEVE SMITH NAMED WELSH FIRE CAPTAIN FOR THE HUNDRED|url=https://glamorgancricket.com/news/steve-smith-named-welsh-fire-captain-for-the-hundred|website=Glamorgan Cricket}}</ref>

In May 2020, The Hundred was postponed for a year due to COVID-19.<ref>{{cite web |title=The Hundred postponed as English uncertainty grows|url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/3306314/the-hundred-postponed-as-english-uncertainty-grows|website=Cricket.com.au}}</ref>

In February 2021, Smith, along with Starc opted against playing in The Hundred.<ref>{{cite web |title=Shakib, Warner, Pollard, Pooran, de Kock among overseas players in the Hundred draft|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/the-hundred-draft-2021-shakib-warner-pollard-pooran-de-kock-among-overseas-players-in-the-hundred-draft-1252122|website=ESPN}}</ref>

In January 2023, Smith signed a short-term deal with [[Sussex County Cricket Club|Sussex]] for three games in 2023.<ref>{{cite web |title=Steven Smith signs for three Championship games with Sussex|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/australias-steven-smith-signs-for-2023-ashes-warm-up-spell-with-sussex-1354703|website=ESPN}}</ref>

In May 2023, Smith made his debut for Sussex in the [[County Championship]] against Worcestershire, batting at No.5, Smith scored 30 runs, took 3 catches and bowled 2.4 overs in a draw. Against Leicestershire, Smith only managed to score 3 runs before he was out lbw. He took 1 catch and bowled 1 over, with the match resulting in another draw. In his third match for Sussex, against Glamorgan, Smith scored 89 runs before he was again out lbw. He bowled 10.5 overs, taking 2 wickets, and bowled 2 maidens, along with taking 2 catches in the field.

In February 2025, Smith again signed with the Welsh Fire.<ref>{{cite web |title=STEVE SMITH TO PLAY AT SOPHIA GARDENS IN 2025 WITH WELSH FIRE|url=https://glamorgancricket.com/news/steve-smith-to-play-at-sophia-gardens-with-welsh-fire|website=Glamorgan Cricket}}</ref>

In August 2025, Smith made his debut in The Hundred, playing all 8 matches with the Fire failing to reach the finals. Smith opened the batting but struggled to make a big impact, with a highest score of 47 not out from 36 deliveries.

== International career ==

=== 2010–2011: Debut and early international career ===
Steve Smith made his international cricket debut in a [[Twenty20 International]] match playing as a leg spinner against [[Pakistan national cricket team|Pakistan]] at [[Melbourne Cricket Ground|Melbourne]] in February 2010. The same month, he made his [[One Day International]] debut against the [[West Indies cricket team|West Indies]] also at Melbourne, playing in the fifth match of the series.<ref name=ciprofile/>

In the [[2010 World Twenty20|2010 ICC World Twenty20]] competition held in the West Indies, Australia finished runners up to England. Smith took 11 wickets in seven matches at an average of 14.81 to finish as the equal-second-highest wicket-taker of the tournament.<ref>{{cite web |title=ICC World Twenty20, 2010 Cricket Team Records & Stats-most wickets |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/world-twenty20-2010/engine/records/bowling/most_wickets_career.html?id=5195;type=tournament |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=13 June 2019}}</ref>

Smith made his [[Test cricket|Test]] debut at [[Lord's]] in July 2010, playing both Tests against Pakistan in the [[Australian cricket team against Pakistan in England in 2010|2010 Test series played in England]].<ref name=ciprofile/> He was selected mainly for his bowling, and batted down the order, although his bowling was not required in the first innings. In the second innings, he took 3 wickets for 51 as Australia won by 150 runs.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/426394.html |title=Scorecard: 1st Test: Australia v. Pakistan at Lord's, 13–16 July 2010 |work=Cricinfo |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=13 January 2015}}</ref> In the second Test he was called to bowl only ten overs and took no wickets, although he played an impressive role with the bat in the second innings. Batting with the tail, he scored 77 including nine fours and two sixes off successive balls, helping Australia to set a competitive target after having been bowled out for 88 in the first innings.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/pakistan-v-australia-2010/engine/match/426395.html |title=Scorecard: 2nd Test: Australia v. Pakistan at Headingley, 21–24 July 2010 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=13 January 2015}}</ref>

Smith's fielding attracted attention during the 2009–10 season with some spectacular catches in the outfield.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dailytelegraph.com.au/sport/cricket/super-leg-spinner-catches-the-eye/story-e6frey50-1225834068179 |title=Super leg-spinner catches the eye |work=The Daily Telegraph|location=Sydney |access-date=9 August 2013|date=24 February 2010}}</ref>

In the 2010–11 Australian summer, Smith played three Tests in the [[2010–11 Ashes series]], this time playing more as a batsman, taking the number six spot in the order. His performances were solid during the series, getting a number of starts and scoring two half centuries. Following the 2010–11 Ashes, Smith did not play another Test for two years, his next Test series coming against India in March 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/22022087/steven-smith-lucky-break|title=Steven Smith's lucky break|publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=29 March 2018|date=14 March 2013}}</ref>

=== 2013–15: Return and breakthrough ===

==== Tour of India and back-to-back Ashes 2013–14 ====
{{Main|2012–13 Border–Gavaskar Trophy |2013 Ashes series|2013-14 Ashes series}}
Smith's return to the test team came during the [[Australian cricket team in India in 2012–13|2013 tour of India]]. In the previous two Sheffield seasons his form had been middling, averaging 37, but he was chosen for the 17-man squad, primarily as a backup batsman, rather than an allrounder as he had been in the Test team previously.<ref name="Smith India 2013">{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/india-v-australia-2013/content/story/624959.html|title=Steven Smith's lucky break|publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=24 December 2016|date=14 March 2013}}</ref> Smith was selected for the third test in Mohali, his first in over two years, when four players were dropped for "not doing their homework", in a scandal known as [[Homeworkgate]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-21767567|title=Australia cricket: 'Homework failure' sparks debate|newspaper=BBC News |access-date=24 December 2016|date=13 March 2013|last1=Bryant|first1=Nick}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/india-v-australia-2013/content/story/624494.html|title=Watson leaves tour after Australia axe four|publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=24 December 2016|date=11 March 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/cricket/australia-send-four-players-home-1756816|title=Frown Under: Dressing room unrest leaves Australia in turmoil|website=Daily Mirror|access-date=24 December 2016|date=11 March 2013}}</ref>

In his first Test innings in India, batting at No.5 for the first time in Test cricket, he scored 92 before being stumped by Dhoni from a delivery by [[Pragyan Ojha]], and in the second innings he managed 5 runs.<ref>{{cite web |title=Full Scorecard of India vs Australia 3rd Test 2013 – Score Report |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/12214/scorecard/598814/india-vs-australia-3rd-test-australia-tour-of-india-2012-13 |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=14 June 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=The evolution of Steven Smith |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/australia-v-india-2014-15/content/story/811903.html |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=14 June 2019 |date=19 December 2014}}</ref> In the final Test match at Delhi, Smith made 46 and 18 runs, respectively, but Australia was unable to win the Test match as India secured a 4–0 series win.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/india-v-australia-2013/engine/series/598808.html|title=Results – India v Australia – ESPNcricinfo|work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

Following the defeat to India, Australia's next series was against England in the British Isles in July. Although the squad for the [[2013 Ashes series|2013 Ashes]] was finalised in April, Smith was the vice-captain of Australia's A team and was later called into the main squad after showing some promise in the Australia's A tour to the United Kingdom in June where he made 133 runs against Ireland in Belfast but also as a backup batsman due to Michael Clarke's fitness concerns.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ireland/content/story/642021.html|title=Smith lifts Australians after top-order trouble|publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=24 December 2016|date=14 June 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/cricket/23024460|title=Ashes 2013: Australia add Steve Smith to squad|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=24 December 2016|date=23 June 2013}}</ref> He played his first-class tour match with the main squad on 2 July 2013 in Worcester making 111 runs in both innings combined. In the first Test match at [[Trent Bridge]] he made a half century in his first innings but fell cheaply in the second innings getting out lbw to [[Graeme Swann]]. While making little impact at Lord's, Smith produced a century at Hove against Sussex on 27 July.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/the-ashes-2013/content/story/655769.html|title=Taylor and Bird make Test auditions|publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=24 December 2016|date=27 July 2013}}</ref>

In the third Test being 2–0 down to England, Australia moved up north to [[Old Trafford Cricket Ground]] in Manchester needing to win or draw to save the series. Smith made 89 and 19 runs, respectively, but the third Test match stirred controversy about the on-field umpire's decisions and DRS (Decision Review System) causing Smith to survive on two occasions and his teammate [[Usman Khawaja]] to be dismissed.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2013/aug/01/third-umpire-appeal-ashes-australia|title=Ashes 2013: Umpire howler in third Test leaves Australia furious|newspaper=The Guardian|access-date=24 December 2016|date=August 2013|author=<!--Not stated-->}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2013-08-02/drs-flashpoints-at-the-ashes-2013/4860796|title=The Ashes 2013: DRS flashpoints and controversial umpire decisions|work=ABC News|access-date=24 December 2016|date=2 August 2013}}</ref> In the final Test, Smith scored his maiden Test century, which came in the first innings of the last Test of the series at [[The Oval]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Full Scorecard of England vs Australia 5th Test 2013 – Score Report |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/series/12088/scorecard/566936/england-vs-australia-5th-test-australia-tour-of-england-and-scotland-2013 |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=14 June 2019}}</ref> reaching the total in style by hitting a six off the bowling of [[Jonathan Trott]]. He remained unbeaten on 138.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Full Scorecard of Australia vs England 5th Test 2013 – Score Report {{!}} ESPNcricinfo.com|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/12088/scorecard/566936/england-vs-australia-5th-test-australia-tour-of-england-and-scotland-2013|access-date=3 December 2020|work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> Smith became only the sixth Australian to reach his maiden Test 100 with a six.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/23786923/7.app|title=England v Australia fifth Test day two as it happened|date=22 August 2013|last1=Higginson|first1=Marc|first2=Mark|last2=Mitchener|work=BBC Sport|access-date=14 January 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150114081148/http://m.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/23786923/7.app|archive-date=14 January 2015}}</ref> At the end of the series, the urn was retained by England after winning the series 3–0. Smith played in all five Tests, scoring 345 runs at an average of 38.33.{{citation needed|date=September 2025}}

Smith remained in the team for the first Test of [[2013–14 Ashes series]] in Brisbane.<ref>{{cite web|first=Brydon |last=Coverdale|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/the-ashes-2013-14/content/story/687669.html|date=12 November 2013|title=Bailey named in Test squad|publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=24 December 2016}}</ref> Despite starting slowly in the first two Tests, Smith produced his first Test century on home soil in the third Test at Perth, scoring 111 from 208 balls,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Scorecard – 2013–2014 The Ashes – 13/12/2013|url=https://www.howstat.com/cricket/Statistics/Matches/MatchScorecard.asp?MatchCode=2126|access-date=3 December 2020|website=www.howstat.com}}</ref> helping Australia display a total of 6–326 at stumps on the second day to later win the Test match and be awarded man of the match.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2013-12-13/smith-rescues-australia-with-crucial-ton/5156664|title=The Ashes: Steven Smith rescues Australia with century to edge England on day one of third Test|publisher=ABC News|access-date=24 December 2016|date=13 December 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/the-ashes-2013-14/content/story/699835.html|title=Smith stands up with hugely significant innings| publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=24 December 2016|date=13 December 2013}}</ref> It was during this innings at the [[WACA Ground|WACA]] which he decided to take a "prelim movement back and across" to counter short-pitched bowling<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.smh.com.au/sport/cricket/steve-smith-technically-different-statistically-better-20190808-p52f8l.html|title=Steve Smith: technically different, statistically better|last=Cherny|first=Daniel|date=13 August 2019|website=The Sydney Morning Herald|access-date=13 August 2019}}</ref> and has even exaggerated it, according to Smith, "I was probably batting on middle and leg and going to middle at that point ... I've sort of moved things a little bit across to leg stump and now I'm going just outside off stump".<ref name=":1" /> Smith remarked "Everything sort of just clicked into place and it felt really good so I've continued doing it".<ref name=":1" /> Despite his success in the first innings, he mistimed a pull shot in the second innings, the ball caught in the deep by substitute fielder Bairstow off Ben Stokes' bowling, being dismissed for 15 from 50 deliveries.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Scorecard – 2013–2014 The Ashes – 13/12/2013|url=https://www.howstat.com/cricket/Statistics/Matches/MatchScorecard.asp?MatchCode=2126|access-date=3 December 2020|website=www.howstat.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Full WACA Test Highlights – YouTube|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-G3weE6NUMo| archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211107/-G3weE6NUMo| archive-date=7 November 2021 | url-status=live|access-date=3 December 2020|website=www.youtube.com| date=17 December 2013}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

In the fourth Test at the [[Melbourne Cricket Ground|MCG]] he was dismissed on 19 by [[Stuart Broad]], but made another century with 115 runs from 154 deliveries in the first innings of the fifth and final Test at the [[Sydney Cricket Ground|SCG]]. His 128-run partnership with [[Brad Haddin]] helped Australia come back from 5–97 to 326 all out in the first innings and eventually went on to win the Test match by 281 runs.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2014-01-03/haddin2c-smith-rescue-aussie-innings/5184190|title=The Ashes: Brad Haddin, Steve Smith rescue Australia's innings in fifth Test at SCG|publisher=ABC News|access-date=24 December 2016|date=3 January 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2014-01-05/australia-completes-ashes-clean-sweep/5185418|title=The Ashes: Australia completes series whitewash with fifth Test win at SCG|publisher=ABC News|access-date=24 December 2016|date=5 January 2014}}</ref> The victory in Sydney marked a 5–0 victory towards Australia after a dismal 3–0 loss during the winter period of 2013. Smith made two centuries with a total of 327 runs at an average of 36. Smith played just one ODI match during England's tour during 2013–14, in the 4th ODI at Perth where he made 19 runs.{{citation needed|date=September 2025}}

==== Tour of South Africa 2014 ====
{{Main|Australian cricket team in South Africa in 2013–14}}

Following a 5–0 victory against England in the Ashes, Australia were scheduled [[Australian cricket team in South Africa in 2013–14|three Test matches and three T20 matches in South Africa]]. In the first Test at [[SuperSport Park|Centurion]], Johannesburg, Smith made his fourth century and first in South Africa, where he and [[Shaun Marsh]] made a 233 run partnership from 4–98.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dailytelegraph.com.au/centuries-by-steve-smith-and-shaun-marsh-mean-no-brad-haddin-rescue-mission-needed/news-story/daea5d76820a777d30c113f05f0ed975|title=Centuries by Steve Smith and Shaun Marsh mean no Brad Haddin rescue mission needed|work=The Daily Telegraph|location=Sydney|access-date=24 December 2016|date=13 February 2014}}</ref> Smith was not required in the second innings and Australia won the Test by 281 runs.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2014-02-16/johnson-runs-riot-as-australia-wins-first-test/5262682|title=Mitchell Johnson takes 12 wickets as Australia beats South Africa in first Test in Centurion|publisher=ABC News|access-date=24 December 2016|date=15 February 2014}}</ref> The second Test in Port Elizabeth saw a slower pitch as Smith made 49 and a duck and South Africa levelled the series 1–1. In the deciding Test match in Cape Town, Smith made 84 runs from 155 deliveries in the first innings and finished 36 not out in the second innings as Australia won the series 2–1.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2014-03-06/australia-seals-test-series-with-245-run-victory/5301758|title=Australia beats South Africa by 245 runs to win third Test in Cape Town, clinches series 2–1|work=Fox Sports|access-date=24 December 2016|date=5 March 2014}}</ref> Steve Smith produced 269 runs at an average of 67.25, the third-best in the series and the second-best by an Australian, second to David Warner.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Australia in South Africa Test Series, 2013/14 Cricket Team Records & Stats {{!}} ESPNcricinfo.com|url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/batting/most_runs_career.html?id=8275&type=series|access-date=8 December 2020|work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

==== Tri-Series in Zimbabwe and the UAE 2014 ====
{{Main|2014 Zimbabwe Tri-Series}}

The five-month break from cricket activity saw a surprise pick of Smith called up for the [[2014 Zimbabwe Tri-Series]] on the August 2014. Smith prior to the tour had two ODI matches in the last two years.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/zimbabwe-triangular-series-2014/content/story/766763.html|title=Lyon back in Australia's ODI squad|publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=24 December 2016|date=4 August 2014}}</ref> In his first match against Zimbabwe, he was run out by [[Sikandar Raza]]. He made scores in his thirties in his participating matches but only made 10 runs in the final against South Africa on 6 September, where South Africa went on to win the Tri-Series.{{citation needed|date=September 2025}}

The squad later travelled to the UAE to face Pakistan in a [[Australian cricket team against Pakistan in the UAE in 2014–15|T20 Match, three ODIs and two Tests]]. In the first and only T20 match, Pakistan won the toss and made 96 runs in their allotment of 20 overs, setting Australia a target of 97 runs to win.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Full Scorecard of Pakistan vs Australia Only T20I 2014 – Score Report {{!}} ESPNcricinfo.com|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/11581/scorecard/727917/australia-vs-pakistan-only-t20i-australia-tour-of-united-arab-emirates-2014-15|access-date=8 December 2020|work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> Smith made three runs before being dismissed. Despite this, Australia won by six wickets.<ref>{{Cite web|date=5 October 2014|title=Australia tour of UAE 2014: Glenn Maxwell says Australia are one of the best in T20 format|url=https://www.cricketcountry.com/news/australia-tour-of-uae-2014-glenn-maxwell-says-australia-are-one-of-the-best-in-t20-format-195947|access-date=8 December 2020|website=Cricket Country}}</ref>

Following the T20 came the 3-match ODI series. In the first ODI at [[Sharjah Cricket Stadium]], Smith made his first ODI century scoring 101 runs off 118 balls to push the visitors to a 1–0 lead in the series.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/pakistan-v-australia-2014/content/story/787759.html|title=Smith ton sets up big Australia win|publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=24 December 2016|date=7 October 2014}}</ref> In the second ODI he made 12 runs and in the third and final ODI he made 77 runs off 105 balls to win the ODI match by 1 run. However, during the match, Steve Smith's catch on [[Fawad Alam]] questioned whether his catch was within the ICC laws. The incident occurred when in the 18th over of Pakistan's chase of 231 where [[Xavier Doherty]] delivered the ball and before Fawad made contact with his paddle sweep, Smith had moved from first slip towards leg slip to intercept the shot. The legality of the catch continued to be the main talking point after the ODI Series and afterwards ICC made a press statement stating that: "As long as the movement of a close catching fielder is in response to the striker's actions (the shot he/she is about to play or shaping to play), then movement is permitted before the ball reaches the striker. On the day, if umpires believe any form of significant movement is unfair (in an attempt to deceive the batsman), then the Law still applies."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/pakistan-v-australia-2014/content/story/789015.html|title=Why Smith's catch to dismiss Fawad was allowed|publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=25 December 2016|date=13 October 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cricketcountry.com/articles/steven-smiths-controversial-catch-to-dismiss-fawad-alam-a-frame-by-frame-analysis-198468|title=Steven Smith's controversial catch to dismiss Fawad Alam: A frame-by-frame analysis|website=cricketcountry.com|date=12 October 2014 |publisher=India Webportal|access-date=25 December 2016}}</ref> The win saw Australia rise back to number one in the ICC ODI Rankings and Steve Smith was made man of the series for his batting performances.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/pakistan-v-australia-2014/content/story/788771.html|title=Australia turn tables for one-run win|publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=25 December 2016|date=12 October 2014}}</ref>

Transitioning into the Test series saw Australia's continued failure against reverse swing and spin in the subcontinent. In the warm-up match against Pakistan A in Sharjah, Australia lost by 153 runs where Smith made 58 but retired out.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/pakistan-v-australia-2014/content/story/790305.html|title=Australians done by spin, reverse swing|publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=25 December 2016|date=18 October 2014}}</ref> In the first Test in Dubai, Smith made 22 runs in the first innings and 55 runs in the second innings but collectively lost the Test match by 221 runs. In the second Test, Smith made a duck and 97 runs but Australia's woes against spin continued as Australia lost by 356 runs.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/pakistan-v-australia-second-test-day-five-match-report/2014-11-04|title=Pakistan complete 2–0 series sweep|website=cricket.com.au|publisher=Cricket Australia|access-date=25 December 2016}}</ref> In the series he made 174 runs at an average of 43.5.{{citation needed|date=September 2025}}

==== South Africa and India in Australia 2014–15 ====
{{Main|South African cricket team in Australia in 2014–15|Indian cricket team in Australia in 2014–15}}

Arriving back from the subcontinent following their 2–0 Test defeat against Pakistan. Smith played in the [[South African cricket team in Australia in 2014–15|series against South Africa]] where Australia defeated South Africa 4–1 in the ODI Series. He missed the first match due to selectors picking Shane Watson instead but later joined the remainder of the games due to [[Michael Clarke (cricketer)|Michael Clarke]]'s hamstring injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/australia-v-south-africa-2014-15/content/story/799627.html|title=Australia look to keep momentum in Clarke's absence|publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=25 December 2016|date=15 November 2014}}</ref> In his first match in Perth he registered 10 runs but in the following games he made 73*, 104 and 67 runs. His hundred in the 4th ODI at the MCG was Smith's first on Australian soil. Smith scored 254 runs at an average of 84.66, the highest Australian total in the series and consequently receiving the man of the series award.<ref>{{cite web |title=South Africa in Australia ODI Series, 2014/15 Cricket Team Records & Stats (Most runs) |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/batting/most_runs_career.html?id=9319;type=series |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=22 March 2019}}</ref>

India arrived in Australia to play the Border–Gavaskar [[Indian cricket team in Australia in 2014–15|Test match series]] and a tri-series ODI competition with England. The first Test was scheduled to begin on 4 December in Brisbane, but was later postponed because of the death of [[Phillip Hughes]]. The first Test was later rescheduled to the [[Adelaide Oval]] on 9 December and Brisbane would be hosting the second Test on 17 December.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/series/754713.html?template=fixtures |title=Border–Gavaskar Trophy, 2014/15 |access-date=3 September 2014 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> In the first Test match in Adelaide, the Australian players wore Hughes' Test cap number 408 on their playing shirts for the match as well as black armbands in honour of their former teammate.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/first-test-to-honour-phillip-hughes/2014-12-07|title=First Test to honour Phillip Hughes|website=cricket.com.au|publisher=Cricket Australia|access-date=25 December 2016}}</ref> In the first Test match in Adelaide, Smith scored 162* from 298 balls in the first and made 52* in the second innings, defeating India by 48 runs on day five.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Full Scorecard of Australia vs India 1st Test 2014 – Score Report {{!}} ESPNcricinfo.com|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/8525/scorecard/754737/australia-vs-india-1st-test-border-gavaskar-trophy-2014-15|access-date=8 December 2020|work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> This also marked Steve Smith's first Test century against India and at the [[Adelaide Oval]].{{Citation needed|date=December 2020}}

On 15 December, Smith was named Australia's new vice-captain and following an injury to Michael Clarke, he was appointed stand-in skipper against India with Brad Haddin as his deputy.<ref name=captain>{{cite web|url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/steve-smith-captain-australia-india-series-vice-captain/2014-12-15|title=Smith to captain Australia for Test series against India|access-date=28 March 2018}}</ref> He made his captaincy debut for Australia in the Second Test match against India at the Gabba.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cricketaustralia.com.au/media/media-releases/ca-announce-australia-test-team-leadership-changes/2014-12-15 |title=CA announce Australia Test team leadership changes |publisher=[[Cricket Australia]] |date=15 December 2014 |access-date=19 December 2014 |archive-date=19 December 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141219062650/http://www.cricketaustralia.com.au/media/media-releases/ca-announce-australia-test-team-leadership-changes/2014-12-15 |url-status=dead}}</ref>
He continued his batting form and made 133 runs in the first innings before being run-out in the second innings with a score of 28. Smith was awarded man of the match as Australia defeated India by 4 wickets. Australia were then up 2–0 in the series.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Full Scorecard of India vs Australia 2nd Test 2014 – Score Report {{!}} ESPNcricinfo.com|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/8525/scorecard/754739/australia-vs-india-2nd-test-border-gavaskar-trophy-2014-15|access-date=8 December 2020|work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> In the third Test at the [[Melbourne Cricket Ground]], Smith made his third consecutive century in the first innings of the Test match scoring 192 runs from 433 balls. He also scored his 1,000th run in the 2014 calendar year, and became the eighth-fastest Australian to reach 2000 Test runs, beating previous Australian captains such as [[Michael Clarke (cricketer)|Michael Clarke]] and [[Ricky Ponting]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/cricket/australia/australia-v-india-steve-smith-scores-192-at-mcg-six-amazing-statistics/story-fn2mcu3x-1227167936718 |title=Australia v India: Steve Smith scores 192 at MCG, six amazing statistics  |work=Fox Sports|date=27 December 2014 |access-date=14 January 2015}}</ref>

The final Test match at the [[Sydney Cricket Ground]] saw Smith in his fourth consecutive century against India. The achievement saw Smith join [[Don Bradman]] (6), [[Neil Harvey]], [[Jack Fingleton]] and [[Matthew Hayden]] (4 each) as Australian centurions in four or more consecutive Tests, a streak Smith started during the 1st Test at Adelaide. Smith also became the first Australian skipper to open their captaincy with three consecutive centuries, and the second batsman since [[Jacques Kallis]] against West Indies to score a century in every match of a Test series.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/australia-v-india-2014-15/content/current/story/817571.html |title=Australia on top after making 572 |author=Coverdale, Brydon |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |date=7 January 2015 |access-date=5 January 2017}}</ref> The Test match ended in a draw as Australia defeated India 2–0 in the series, thus returning the [[Border–Gavaskar Trophy]] to Australia. The conclusion of the Test series saw Smith be given the man of the series award, scoring 769 runs at an average of 128.16, the highest aggregate score in a four-test match series in Australia and also marked the highest number of runs scored against India by an Australian, surpassing [[Donald Bradman]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/australia-india-statistics-analysis-day-four-sydney-test/2015-01-10|title=Skipper Smith joins all-time greats|website=cricket.com.au|publisher=Cricket Australia|access-date=25 December 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.dnaindia.com/sport/report-steve-smith-surpasses-don-bradman-s-record-in-sydney-test-becomes-highest-australian-run-getter-in-test-series-against-india-2051093 |title=Steve Smith surpasses Don Bradman's record in Sydney Test; becomes highest Australian run-getter in Test series against India |date=9 January 2015 |work=DNA India |access-date=14 January 2015}}</ref>

Following the Test series, an ODI tri-series with India and England was confirmed in preparation for the upcoming Cricket World Cup hosted by Australia and New Zealand.
In his first ODI match against England in Sydney, he was dismissed at 37 runs by [[Moeen Ali]] but continued to provide runs in the following matches leading to the final against England. En route to the tri-series final, Smith was handed his first ODI match on 20 January as the skipper after [[George Bailey (cricketer, born 1982)|George Bailey]] was suspended for a slow-over rate earlier in the series.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/steve-smith-odi-captain-cameron-white-shaun-marsh-called-up-australia-squad-hobart-v-england/2015-01-20|title=Smith to skipper as White and Marsh added to ODI squad|first=Dave|last=Middleton|website=cricket.com.au|publisher=Cricket Australia|access-date=26 December 2016}}</ref> Three days later, Smith scored his first ODI century against England producing 102 runs in 95 balls; the win saw Australia qualify for the final<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/carlton-mid-triangular-series-2015/content/story/823143.html|title=Smith ton leads Australia to final|first=Brydon|last=Coverdale|publisher=ESPNcricinfo|date=23 January 2015}}</ref> and later defeating England to win the [[Carlton Mid Triangular Series in Australia in 2014–15|Carlton Mid Triangular Series in Australia 2014–15]].{{citation needed|date=September 2025}}

==== Cricket World Cup in Australia 2015 ====
{{Main|2015 Cricket World Cup}}
In the World Cup, Smith played a vital role as versatile batsman as he played in numerous batting positions from number three down to as a middle-order batsman. In Australia's opening match of the World Cup, against [[England cricket team|England]], he was dismissed early on 5 but later improved as the tournament progressed. After making half centuries against Afghanistan, Sri Lanka and Pakistan, he later steered Australia into the final after making a century against India in the semi-finals at the [[Sydney Cricket Ground]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2015/mar/26/australia-india-cricket-world-cup-semi-final-match-report|title=Steve Smith century helps Australia crush India to reach World Cup final|first=Vic|last=Marks|author-link=Vic Marks|newspaper=The Guardian|access-date=26 December 2016|date=26 March 2015}}</ref> In the final, Australia drew against fellow neighbours New Zealand after defeating South Africa. Australia's target to chase 183 runs after a New Zealand collapse saw Steve Smith score 58 not out alongside the skipper, [[Michael Clarke (cricketer)|Michael Clarke]] as Australia won by 7 wickets with 101 balls remaining.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/wisdenalmanack/content/story/1006053.html|title=Australia v New Zealand|first=Steven |last=Lynch|via=ESPNcricinfo|work=Wisden Cricketers' Almanack|access-date=26 December 2016|date=30 April 2016}}</ref> Smith was Australia's highest run scorer in the tournament, scoring 402 runs at an average of 67, including a century and four fifties.<ref name="WC2015">{{cite web |title=ICC Cricket World Cup, 2014/15 Most runs |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/icc-cricket-world-cup-2015/engine/records/batting/most_runs_career.html?id=6537;type=tournament |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=3 March 2019}}</ref> He was named in the team of the tournament for the 2015 World Cup by the ICC.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bilton |first1=Dean |title=World Cup team of the tournament revealed |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2015-03-30/world-cup-team-of-the-tournament-revealed/6358716 |website=ABC News |access-date=17 July 2019 |date=30 March 2015}}</ref> He was also named in the team of the tournament by ESPNcricinfo and Cricbuzz.<ref>{{cite web |title=NZ 5, Australia 4 in our World Cup team |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/icc-cricket-world-cup-2015/content/story/857187.html |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=18 July 2019 |date=30 March 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=ICC Cricket World Cup 2015: Cricbuzz team of the tournament |url=https://www.cricbuzz.com/cricket-news/71431/icc-cricket-world-cup-2015-cricbuzz-team-of-the-tournament |website=Cricbuzz |date=31 March 2015 |access-date=18 July 2019}}</ref>

==== Tour of the West Indies 2015 ====
{{main|Australian cricket team in the West Indies in 2015}}
After winning the World Cup in March, Australia's winter schedule was later released with the Test team returned from their short break towards their two Test series against the West Indies in the Caribbean. Due to IPL commitments, Smith missed out on Australia's maiden warm up match against the West Indies Cricket Board President's XI on 27 May. He later joined the Test squad in the first Test match in [[Windsor Park (Dominica)|Windsor Park]], and scored 25 and 5 runs, respectively. In the second Test match in [[Sabina Park]], Smith steered Australia to a first innings score of 399, where he made 199 and became the eighth man in Test history to be dismissed on 199.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/cricket/west-indies-v-australia-steve-smith-199-sees-him-join-unwanted-exclusive-club/news-story/420d845f7dfe9241dd3be504b2f24861?nk=e83fdddd486be5df61af2f999b8a1693-1483087148|title=West Indies v Australia: Steve Smith 199 sees him join unwanted exclusive club|first=Greg|last=Buckle|work=Fox Sports|access-date=30 December 2016|date=12 June 2015}}</ref> Australia later won the match in positive fashion, beating the West Indies by 277 runs within four days and retained the Frank Worrell Trophy.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/west-indies-v-australia-2015/content/story/887731.html|title=Australia complete 277-run demolition|first=George|last=Binoy|publisher=ESPNcricinfo|date=14 June 2015|access-date=30 December 2016}}</ref> After his man of the match effort against the West Indies in the second Test, Smith became the second-youngest player ever to reach the number 1 ICC Test batsmen ranking and just the eighth Australian to do so.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/steve-smith-number-one-in-the-world-key-stats-in-purple-patch-test-matches/2015-06-16|title=Smith's numbers up there with best ever|date=16 June 2015 |work=cricket.com.au|publisher=Cricket Australia|access-date=18 June 2015}}</ref>

==== Ashes in England 2015 ====
{{main|2015 Ashes series}}
[[File:SPDSmith.png|thumb|right|upright=0.8|Smith fielding for Australia in the 2nd Test of the [[2015 Ashes series|2015 Ashes]]]]
The 2–0 victory against the West Indies gave Australia some momentum into the long-awaited Ashes series in the British Isles. While Australia's last Ashes tour was in 2013, the emergence of England's [[Joe Root]] and Australia's Steve Smith saw an awaited clash to determine the better batsman in the upcoming series.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/cricket/news/16303/9900235/joe-root-v-steve-smith-ashes-2015-stars-assessed-by-nasser-hussain|title=Joe Root v Steve Smith: Ashes 2015 stars assessed by Nasser Hussain|first=Nasser|last=Hussain|author-link=Nasser Hussain|work=skysports.com|date=8 July 2015|access-date=30 December 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/cricket/the-ashes-2015-englands-joe-root-and-australias-steve-smith-will-determine-ashes-says-macgill/news-story/3264bef92b5d95d607afeebfacc6f2d3?nk=e83fdddd486be5df61af2f999b8a1693-1483090830|title=The Ashes 2015: England's Joe Root and Australia's Steve Smith will determine Ashes, says MacGill|first=Stuart|last=MacGill|author-link=Stuart MacGill|work=Fox Sports|access-date=30 December 2016|date=8 July 2015}}</ref> With the Australians in good form and England drawing to New Zealand and West Indies gave Australia some confidence to the countdown to the first Test in Cardiff. Smith started positively in his first-class match with a century against Kent in Canterbury.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/the-ashes-2015/content/story/891621.html|title=Confident Smith limbers up for Ashes|first=Daniel|last=Brettig|publisher=ESPNcricinfo|date=26 June 2015|access-date=30 December 2016}}</ref> He was rested for the second first-class match and in the first Test match in Cardiff, Smith made 33 in both innings as England took a 1–0 lead in the series.{{citation needed|date=September 2025}}

In the second Test at [[Lord's]], Smith produced 215 runs in his first innings, his highest Test score and became the first Australian to score a double-ton at Lord's since World War II. His double century also saw Smith pass 3000 Test runs, the third-youngest Australia to reach the feat.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/cricket/australia/ashes-2015-steve-smith-hits-11th-test-ton-thanks-to-steven-finn-noball/news-story/251c86b81d42450e0a08f3ca1ab34072?nk=e83fdddd486be5df61af2f999b8a1693-1483092926 |title=Ashes 2015: Steve Smith hits 11th Test ton thanks to Steven Finn no-ball |work=Fox Sports |date=18 July 2015 |access-date=30 December 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.smh.com.au/sport/cricket/the-ashes/ashes-2015-steve-smith-scores-double-century-nine-years-after-visit-to-lords-as-teen-20150717-gif5vt.html |title=Ashes 2015: Steve Smith scores double century nine years after visit to Lord's as teen |first=Chris |last=Barrett |website=The Sydney Morning Herald |date=18 July 2015 |access-date=30 December 2016}}</ref> In his second innings he made 58 runs before Australia levelled the series in a 405 run rout.{{citation needed|date=September 2025}}

In the third Test in Edgbaston, Smith made 7 and 8 runs, respectively, both dismissed by [[Steven Finn]], as England take a 2–1 lead into the series. In the fourth Test in [[Trent Bridge]], Australia needed a win to draw the series. With overcast conditions and a green top, Alastair Cook won the toss and elected to field. In the first innings, Smith was dismissed again cheaply by [[Stuart Broad]] with a score of 6, as Australia capitulated in the first session of a total 60 runs from 18.3 overs. It was the quickest—in terms of balls faced—a team has been bowled out in the first innings of a Test match.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/cricket/33723587|title=Ashes 2015: Stuart Broad takes 8–15 as England eye Ashes win|first=Phil|last=Dawkes|work=BBC Sport|date=6 August 2016|access-date=30 December 2016}}</ref> In the second innings, Smith was again caught by [[Ben Stokes]] in the slips from Stuart Broad with a meagre score of 5. England within three days regained the Ashes and took an unassailable 3–1 lead and critics began to question Smith's performances in seaming conditions.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2015-08-08/steve-smith-slated-for-throwing-wicket-away-at-trent-bridge/6682538|title=Ashes 2015: Australian Test greats Shane Warne and Ricky Ponting blast Steve Smith for throwing his wicket away on day two at Trent Bridge|publisher=ABC News|date=8 August 2015|access-date=30 December 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/cricket/australia/ashes-2015-geoffrey-boycott-leads-english-medias-dismantling-of-australia/news-story/d6f08ce56ceafd1092b540b5ca42e420?nk=e83fdddd486be5df61af2f999b8a1693-1483097436|title=Ashes 2015: Geoffrey Boycott leads English media's dismantling of Australia|work=Fox Sports|date=8 August 2015|access-date=30 December 2016}}</ref> Into the fifth and final Test match back at [[The Oval]], Smith made his second century in the series registering 143 runs off 252 balls before being bowled by Finn.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/the-ashes-2015/content/story/911881.html|title=Feeble England collapse after Smith ton|first=David|last=Hopps|publisher=ESPNcricinfo|date=21 August 2015|access-date=30 December 2016}}</ref> Australia later defeated England by an innings and 46 runs. England had regained the Ashes 3–2 which saw the Test retirements of Australia's senior players: [[Michael Clarke (cricketer)|Michael Clarke]], [[Chris Rogers (cricketer)|Chris Rogers]] and later [[Shane Watson]], [[Ryan Harris (cricketer)|Ryan Harris]] and [[Brad Haddin]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/brad-haddin-announces-test-retirement-australia-nsw-press-conference/2015-09-09|title=Haddin announces Test retirement|first=Dave|last=Middleton|website=cricket.com.au|publisher=Cricket Australia|date=9 September 2015|access-date=30 December 2016}}</ref> Overall, Smith made 508 runs at an average of 56.44, the most runs scored in the series.<ref name="Ashes2015">{{cite web |title=The Ashes, 2015 Cricket Team Records & Stats |url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/batting/most_runs_career.html?id=9249;type=series |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=3 March 2019}}</ref>

The retirement of [[Michael Clarke (cricketer)|Michael Clarke]] following Australia's 3–2 defeat in the [[2015 Ashes series]] saw Smith appointed as the full-time captain of the Australian Test and ODI teams. Fellow New South Welshman [[David Warner (cricketer)|David Warner]] was appointed as his vice-captain.<ref name="Steve Smith Captain 2015">{{cite news|url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2015/08/smith-named-australia-cricket-captain-150814162041374.html|title=Smith named as Australia's new cricket captain|publisher=Al Jazeera|agency=Reuters|date=15 August 2015|access-date=15 August 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite press release|url=http://www.cricketaustralia.com.au/media/media-releases/steven-smith-appointed-australias-next-test-captain-david-warner-his-deputy/2015-08-14|title=Steven Smith appointed Australia's next Test captain, David Warner his deputy|date=14 August 2015|work=cricketaustralia.com.au|publisher=Cricket Australia|access-date=20 September 2015|archive-date=5 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150905123038/http://www.cricketaustralia.com.au/media/media-releases/steven-smith-appointed-australias-next-test-captain-david-warner-his-deputy/2015-08-14|url-status=dead}}</ref>

{{Quote box|width=40%|align=right|quote="At 26, he is a fine young man with extraordinary talent, excellent leadership qualities and a terrific temperament."|source=—former Australian cricketer [[Rod Marsh]] on Steve Smith.<ref name="Steve Smith Captain 2015"/>}}

==== Tour of England and Ireland 2015 ====
{{Main|Australian cricket team in England and Ireland in 2015}}

In August 2015, Smith was announced as Australia's new ODI captain, starting in the ODI and T20I tour of Ireland and England and with an injury to Aaron Finch, he was also named as T20I captain for the first time. In the only ODI against Ireland, at Belfast, the match was affected by rain and in a reduced-over match, Smith scored 21 runs in a 23-run win by DLS.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/australia-tour-of-england-and-ireland-2015-743911/ireland-vs-australia-only-odi-743973/match-report|title=Warner, Burns set up Australia victory|work=ESPN CricInfo}}</ref> Australia returned to England and in the only T20I, at Cardiff, Smith as captain, promoted himself to No.3 in T20Is for the first time, and scored a career-best T20I high score of 90 although that wasn't enough for an Australian victory, Australia falling short by 5 runs in the run-chase.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/australia-tour-of-england-and-ireland-2015-743911/england-vs-australia-only-t20i-743975/match-report|title=Vibrant England show nerve in five-run win|work=ESPN CricInfo}}</ref>

==== New Zealand, West Indies and ascension to captaincy 2015–16 ====
{{Main|New Zealand cricket team in Australia in 2015–16|West Indian cricket team in Australia in 2015–16}}

Next followed a [[New Zealand cricket team in Australia in 2015–16|three Test home series against New Zealand]]. Smith's output in the first Test in Brisbane was modest, scoring 48 and 1, as the team romped home for a win in a high scoring game.<ref>{{cite web |title=Australia cruise to Gabba victory |url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/match-report/australia-new-zealand-first-test-day-five-the-gabba-brisbane-report-highlights-live/2015-11-09 |website=cricket.com.au |access-date=16 July 2019}}</ref> During the second Test, Smith scored 27 in the first innings before breaking the shackles with 138 in the second innings. This was Smith's first-ever second innings century; all previous centuries having been scored in the first innings of a Test match. Australia went on to draw the second Test.<ref>{{cite web|title=Australia vs New Zealand: Second test at the WACA, day five as it happened|url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2015-11-17/australia-v-new-zealand-second-test-day-five-live-blog/6947616|publisher=ABC News|date=17 November 2015 |author=Bilton, Dean |author2=Maasdorp, James}}</ref>
In the third Test, significant for being the first-ever day-night Test held at the Adelaide Oval, Smith defied difficult batting conditions to register 53 in the first innings, before falling for 14 in the second innings. Australia won the match in a tight contest.<ref>{{cite web|title=Australia beats New Zealand in day-night test to win series 2–0|url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2015-11-29/australia-beats-new-zealand-day-night-test-adelaide/6984624|publisher=ABC News|author=Lemon, Geoff |date=29 November 2015}}</ref>

Shortly after the series against New Zealand, a [[West Indian cricket team in Australia in 2015–16|three Test series]] was to be held against the West Indies. During the first innings of the first Test, Smith was caught behind on 10, and did not bat again, due to Australia's dominance. The second Test was successful for the captain, scoring 134* and 70* in each respective innings, as Australia went on to seal a series victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cricket.com.au/tours/Australia%20v%20West%20Indies%20Tests%202015%2016/_QfW0yftY0eA3Jfms0QrXQ |title= Commonwealth Bank Test Series v West Indies: 10 December 2015 – 7 January 2016 |publisher = Cricket Australia |access-date=5 January 2017}}</ref> Due to poor weather conditions, the third Test was a wash out, with very little play able to be held.{{citation needed|date=September 2025}}

In 2015 Smith was awarded the [[Sir Garfield Sobers Trophy]] (ICC Cricketer of the Year) and [[ICC Test Player of the Year]] award and named in [[ICC Test Team of the Year]] and [[ICC ODI Team of the Year]] by the ICC.<ref name="Sir Garfield Sobers Trophy (ICC Cricketer of the Year)">{{cite web |title=Steve Smith wins the Sir Garfield Sobers Trophy for ICC Cricketer of the Year 2015 |url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/182330 |website=www.icc-cricket.com |access-date=15 July 2019}}</ref><ref name="ICC cricketer of the Year">{{cite web |title=Steven Smith claims top ICC awards |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci-icc/content/story/954525.html |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=15 July 2019 |date=23 December 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=ICC Test and ODI Teams of the Year 2015 announced |url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/182259 |website=www.icc-cricket.com |access-date=15 July 2019}}</ref> In the same year, he also received the [[Allan Border Medal]], [[Allan Border Medal#Shane Warne Men's Test Player of the Year|Australian Test Player of the Year]] and [[Allan Border Medal#Men's One Day International Player of the Year|Australian One Day International Player of the Year]] award.<ref>{{cite web |title=Smith dominates Border Medal night |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/australia/content/story/824331.html |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=15 July 2019 |date=27 January 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Smith collects first Allan Border Medal |url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/steve-smith-wins-allan-border-medal-test-player-of-year-odi-player-of-year/2015-01-27 |website=cricket.com.au |access-date=15 July 2019}}</ref> He was also named in the Test XI of the year 2015 by ESPNcricinfo.<ref>{{cite web |title=Made in the antipodes |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/review2015/content/story/956299.html |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=17 July 2019 |date=1 January 2016}}</ref>

==== Tour of New Zealand and T20 World Cup in India 2016 ====
{{Main|Australian cricket team in New Zealand in 2016|2016 World Twenty20}}

A [[Australian cricket team in New Zealand in 2015–16|two Test return tour]] against New Zealand took place in February 2016. Smith looked to be in fine touch, registering 71, 138, and 53* in the three innings in which he batted, as the Australian team won 2–0.<ref>{{cite web |title=Results – New Zealand v Australia |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/new-zealand-v-australia-2015-16/engine/series/914197.html |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=16 July 2019}}</ref>

During the [[2016 ICC World Twenty20|T20 World Cup 2016]], held in India, Smith struggled with form early, before registering 61 against Pakistan in a must-win pool match for Australia.
Smith went on to score only 2 against India, as Australia were knocked out of the tournament.<ref>{{cite web |title=Kohli masterclass knocks Australia out of World T20 |url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/match-report/australia-india-world-t20-match-report-mohali-highlights/2016-03-28 |website=cricket.com.au |access-date=16 July 2019}}</ref> It was believed that Smith was incorrectly given out, having clean missed a ball the umpires deemed to have been edged.<ref>{{cite web |title=The blunders that cost Steve Smith dearly |url=http://www.heraldsun.com.au/sport/cricket/world-twenty20-two-blunders-that-cost-steve-smith-dearly-in-australias-loss-to-india/news-story/72b679375dc709aa7d7e923f52d61592 |website=www.heraldsun.com.au |access-date=16 July 2019 |date=27 March 2016}}</ref>

==== Tour of Sri Lanka 2016 ====
{{Main|Australian cricket team in Sri Lanka in 2016}}

Smith then led the Australian Cricket Team on their [[Australian cricket team in Sri Lanka in 2016|tour of Sri Lanka]]. The three Test series was a disaster for the Aussies, losing 3–0.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/match-report/day-five-sri-lanka-australia-match-report-highlights-third-test-colombo-smith-marsh-warner/2016-08-18 |title=Sri Lanka spin way to clean sweep |website=Cricket Australia|date=18 August 2016|author=Ramsey, Andrew}}</ref> Smith was Australia's highest run scorer in the series, scoring 247 runs at an average of 41, including one century and one fifty. Throughout the following ODI series, Smith averaged in excess of 40 across the first two matches, before leaving early for a rest.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.heraldsun.com.au/sport/cricket/james-faulkner-claims-hattrick-in-odi-against-sri-lanka/news-story/479d9f9089fb022b3c84a112d2163086 |title=Steve Smith to come home after Australia's loss to Sri Lanka in second ODI |author=Buckle, Greg |date=25 August 2016 |website=Herald Sun|access-date=8 September 2016}}</ref>

==== ODI Tour of South Africa 2016 ====
{{Main|Australian cricket team in South Africa in 2016-17}}

Australia's disappointing run of form continued into their [[Australian cricket team in South Africa in 2016–17|ODI tour of South Africa]]. They lost the first 3 matches, largely attesting to their young bowling attack's inability to contain a strong South African batting line-up.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/aaron-finch-australia-loss-to-south-africa-intel-on-test-series-steyn-rabada-cricket/2016-10-09 |title= ODI losses bring valuable Test lessons |date=9 October 2016 |website=Cricket Australia|access-date=9 October 2016}}</ref> Smith was disappointing in output across the first two ODIs, before scoring 108 off 107 balls in the 3rd match, as he and [[David Warner (cricketer)|David Warner]] helped Australia to 371.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/cricket/australia/south-africa-v-australia-coverage-of-the-fourth-odi/news-story/c23463053711eb354d1cea549ddad59f |title=South Africa v Australia: Coverage of the third ODI |work=Fox Sports|access-date=9 October 2016|date=5 October 2016}}</ref> Despite the large total, it was chased down by South Africa in the 50th over.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Full Scorecard of Australia vs South Africa 3rd ODI 2016 – Score Report {{!}} ESPNcricinfo.com|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/8517/scorecard/936139/south-africa-vs-australia-3rd-odi-australia-tour-of-south-africa-2016-17|access-date=9 December 2020|work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> Australia lost the 5-match series 5–0.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Australia in South Africa ODI Series, 2016/17 Cricket Team Records & Stats {{!}} ESPNcricinfo.com|url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/team/match_results.html?id=10703&type=series|access-date=9 December 2020|work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

==== South Africa, New Zealand and Pakistan in Australia 2016–17 ====
{{Main|South African cricket team in Australia in 2016–17|New Zealand cricket team in Australia in 2016–17|Pakistani cricket team in Australia in 2016–17}}

[[File:Steve Smith Cricketer.jpg|thumb|upright=0.8|Smith playing for Australia in 2016]]
Following the 5–0 ODI defeat in South Africa, the Australian team returned home for a [[South African cricket team in Australia in 2016–17|3 Test series against South Africa]]. In the first Test Smith made a duck and 34 runs, and Australia lost the Test match. In the second Test at Hobart, Smith made 48 not out in the first innings but the rest of the team capitulated, making a total score of only 85 runs and losing the Test.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2016-11-15/australia-crushed-in-innings-defeat-to-south-africa/8026334?section=sport|title=Australia v South Africa: Hosts collapse for innings and 80-run defeat on day four, Proteas win series|publisher=ABC News |access-date=24 December 2016|date=15 November 2016}}</ref> Following the defeat, criticism of Smith's captaincy and the team's performance emerged which saw the influx of young players such as [[Matt Renshaw]], [[Peter Handscomb]] and [[Nic Maddinson|Nic Maddison]] for the last Test. After losing five consecutive Tests, Smith made 59 and 40, respectively, with the addition of his team performances to win the day-night Test match in Adelaide. The win avoided a 3–0 whitewash, as the 2–1 defeat marked Smith's first series defeat at home.{{citation needed|date=September 2025}}

After the Test series against South Africa, New Zealand played [[New Zealand cricket team in Australia in 2016–17|3 ODIs]] in between the two Test series against South Africa and Pakistan. In the first ODI, Steve Smith registered 164 runs at the SCG, marking the highest ODI score at the ground, beating the previous score of 162 set by AB De Villiers during the 2015 World Cup.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/steve-smith-odi-record-hundred-164-scg-sydney-highest-score-australia-nz-highlights/2016-12-04|title=Spectacular Smith smashes SCG record|website=cricket.com.au|publisher=Cricket Australia|access-date=24 December 2016}}</ref> He was awarded "man of the match". In the second ODI he made 72 runs and in Melbourne of the final ODI he was dismissed for a duck. The Australian team won the contested [[Chappell–Hadlee Trophy]] 3–0 and returned the trophy to Australia.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/australia-v-new-zealand-2016-17/content/story/1071578.html|title=Warner 156 sets up Australia's 3–0 sweep|work=Cricinfo |publisher=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=24 December 2016}}</ref>

Pakistan was scheduled to have [[Pakistani cricket team in Australia in 2016–17|three Test series and 5 ODIs]]. In the first Test in Brisbane, Smith made 130 and 63 runs. His century in Brisbane marked his 16th Test century and his first against Pakistan. Despite Pakistan being bowled out for a low score of 142 in the first innings, Smith's captaincy tactics sparked a mixed response from critics when the on-field umpires made the decision to extend the fourth day evening session by thirty minutes, believing a result would be determined.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/cricket/umpires-solely-responsible-for-controversial-final-session-at-the-gabba/news-story/e82ef00ea76e3e85960ec5aed3d80ece?nk=e83fdddd486be5df61af2f999b8a1693-1482544762|title=Umpires solely responsible for controversial final session at the Gabba|work=Fox Sports|access-date=24 December 2016|date=19 December 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dailytelegraph.com.au/sport/cricket/steve-smiths-captaincy-condemned-by-test-greats-michael-vaughan-mark-taylor-and-michael-clarke/news-story/9659baeeddad349f3417afc5f4c5917a|title=Steve Smith's captaincy condemned by Test greats Michael Vaughan, Mark Taylor and Michael Clarke|work=The Daily Telegraph|location=Sydney|access-date=24 December 2016|date=19 December 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/cricket/allan-border-mark-waugh-defend-smiths-captaincy-and-tactics-at-the-gabba/news-story/bde53d197d6c5c4c9ca8ceff3eb4b1ad?nk=e83fdddd486be5df61af2f999b8a1693-1482543765|title=Allan Border, Mark Waugh defend Smith's captaincy and tactics at the Gabba|work=Fox Sports|access-date=24 December 2016|date=21 December 2016}}</ref> Pakistan made a 4th innings total of 450, as Australia won by 39 runs. The second Test was held at the [[Melbourne Cricket Ground]] and Smith later placed his seventeenth century, the fourth-fastest to do so and also reaching 1000 runs in the calendar year—his third consecutive achievement of this since 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://wwos.nine.com.au/2016/12/29/15/03/steve-smith-continues-strong-form-with-ton|title=Smith leads from the front with MCG ton|first=Michael |last=Ramsey|website=Nine's Wide World of Sports|date=29 December 2016 |publisher=Nine Digital|access-date=30 December 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/australia-v-pakistan-2016-17/content/story/1074545.html|title=Smith's affair with the Boxing Day Test|first=Bharath|last=Seevri|publisher=ESPNcricinfo|date=29 December 2016}}</ref> Despite intermittent rain, Australia managed an unlikely victory into the last session of day five, resulting in a 2–0 win for Australia.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/match-report/day-five-australia-pakistan-boxing-day-test-second-video-highlights-mcg-melbourne/2016-12-30|title=Australia wrap up Boxing Day miracle|first=Andrew|last=Ramsey|website=cricket.com.au|publisher=Cricket Australia|date=30 December 2016}}</ref> The final Test at the [[Sydney Cricket Ground]] marked Steve Smith's 50th Test match, as Australia whitewashed Pakistan 3–0 . Following the victory, he was awarded "Man of the Series" after making a total of 441 runs—the most in the series from both teams.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/match-report/australia-pakistan-scg-day-five-third-test-highlights-lyon-hazlewood/2017-01-07|title=Smith's Australians secure clean sweep|first=Andrew|last=Ramsey|website=cricket.com.au|publisher=Cricket Australia|date=7 January 2016|access-date=7 January 2016}}</ref>

Smith was once again featured in ICC's 2016 Cricket Awards as a 12th man for the ICC Test team of the year.<ref name="ICC TEST XI 2016">{{cite press release|url=http://www.icc-cricket.com/icc-awards/news/2016/media-releases/97224/icc-test-and-odi-teams-of-the-year-announced|title=ICC Test and ODI Teams of the Year announced|website=ICC Cricket|publisher=International Cricket Council|access-date=24 December 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161224100327/http://www.icc-cricket.com/icc-awards/news/2016/media-releases/97224/icc-test-and-odi-teams-of-the-year-announced|archive-date=24 December 2016}}</ref> In the ODI Series against Pakistan, Smith experienced mixed results but played a vital role, with Australia later ending up routing Pakistan 4–1. On 19 January 2017, Steve Smith produced his 8th ODI century against Pakistan at the [[WACA Ground]]—becoming the quickest Australian to reach 3000 ODI runs within 79 innings.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/steve-smith-fastest-3000-odi-runs-australian-79-innings-record-bevan-bailey-pakistan-perth-odi/2017-01-19|title=Superb Smith breaks another record|website=cricket.com.au|publisher=Cricket Australia|first=Martin|last=Smith|date=19 January 2017|access-date=19 January 2017}}</ref> Following the home series, Smith was scheduled to tour three ODI matches against New Zealand for the [[Chappell–Hadlee Trophy]] but later sustained a mild sprain to the [[medial collateral ligament|medial ligament]] in his left ankle, so he headed to Dubai in preparation for the upcoming four Test tour of India.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/steve-smith-ankle-injury-ruled-out-new-zealand-odi-series-new-captain-dubai/2017-01-27|title=Skipper Smith ruled out of NZ tour|first=Andrew|last=Ramsey|website=cricket.com.au|publisher=Cricket Australia|date=27 January 2017|access-date=28 January 2017}}</ref>

==== Tour of India 2017 ====
{{Main|Australian cricket team in India in 2016–17}}
Following the training at ICC's Cricket Academy Centre in Dubai, Smith began the tour of India with a century in their maiden warm-up match in Mumbai. He replicated his ton in the first Test in Pune where he produced his first century in the Indian Subcontinent, accompanied by the support of his bowlers to win their first Test match in India since 2004 and breaking India's 19 match undefeated streak, stretching from 2012.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/india-v-australia-2016-17/content/story/1084299.html|title=O'Keefe, Smith set up famous Australia victory|first=Brydon|last=Coverdale|publisher=ESPNcricinfo|date=25 February 2017|access-date=25 February 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cricket.com.au/news/match-report/india-australia-first-test-day-three-pune-video-highlights-pune-smith-kohli-ashwin-jadeja-starc-lyon/2017-02-25|title=Australia spin way to massive victory|first=Andrew|last=Ramsey|website=cricket.com.au|publisher=Cricket Australia|date=25 February 2017|access-date=25 February 2017}}</ref> Veteran commentator [[Harsha Bhogle]] and other Indian Media rated Smith's third innings hundred at Pune as one of the best ever by a visiting player in India.<ref name="scroll.in">{{Cite web|title='World's best Test batsman': Twitter praises Steve Smith after heroic Ashes century against England|url=https://scroll.in/field/932561/worlds-best-test-batsman-twitter-praises-steve-smith-after-heroic-ashes-century-against-england|access-date=23 March 2021|website=Scroll.in|date=2 August 2019}}</ref> The [[Wisden]] described Smith's ton as an impossible hundred on a ''minefield'' of a pitch at Pune where all other batsman from both teams struggled to get a decent score.<ref name="wisden.com">{{Cite web |last1=Gardner |first1=Ben |date=2 January 2018 |title=Steve Smith's Impossible Innings {{!}} 2017 In Review {{!}} Innings Of The Year |url=https://www.wisden.com/cricket-news/2017-review-steve-smiths-impossible-innings |access-date=9 April 2025 |website=Wisden}}</ref>

'''Temba Bavuma''' (born 17 May 1990) is a South African [[cricket]]er who has played for [[South Africa national cricket team|the national team]] since 2014. A right-handed [[Batting (cricket)|batter]], he has scored 3,810 [[Run (cricket)|runs]] at an [[Batting average (cricket)|average]] of 38.10 in [[Test cricket|Test]] matches, and 1,987 runs averaging 42.40 in [[One Day International]]s (ODIs). In 2016, Bavuma became the first black African cricketer to score a Test [[Century (cricket)|century]] for South Africa,<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Temba Bavuma wants to be more than South African cricket's first black African captain|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/temba-bavuma-wants-to-be-more-than-south-african-cricket-s-first-black-african-captain-1253782|access-date=2021-07-04|website=ESPNcricinfo|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/south-africa-name-dean-elgar-test-captain-and-temba-bavuma-odi-and-t20i-captain-1253753 |title=South Africa name Dean Elgar Test captain and Temba Bavuma ODI and T20I captain |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=4 March 2021}}</ref> and scored a century on his ODI debut later that same year.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Bavuma ton sets up crushing 206-run win|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/ireland-tour-of-rsa-2016-17-936109/south-africa-vs-ireland-only-odi-936131/match-report|access-date=2021-07-24|website=ESPNcricinfo|language=en}}</ref> He is also the national team's first black African [[Captain (cricket)|captain]],<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> appointed to lead the ODI team in 2021 and the Test team in 2023; under his leadership, South Africa won the [[2023–2025 World Test Championship]]. He had previously served as the [[Twenty20 International]] (T20I) captain from 2021 to 2023.

==Early life==
Brought up in the intense cricket culture of Langa – Bavuma, [[Thami Tsolekile]] and [[Malusi Siboto]] are all from the same street<ref name="lad from Langa"/> – Bavuma was educated at [[South African College Schools|South African College Junior School]]<ref>{{Cite web|title = Bavuma inspires school assembly|url = http://www.sport24.co.za/Cricket/Proteas/bavuma-inspires-school-assembly-20160114|website = [[News24 (website)|Sport24]]| date=14 January 2016|access-date = 5 January 2021}}</ref> in Newlands, and [[St David's Marist Inanda]], a boys high School in [[Sandton]].

==Domestic career==
Temba Bavuma made his debut in 2008 for Gauteng against Eastern Province. Batting in the middle order, he made four runs in the first innings in which he batted, briefly partnering teammate [[Dane Vilas]] to his first-class best score.

He made his franchise debut for the [[Highveld Lions cricket team|Lions]] in the 2010/11 season. In the Supersport Series, he made 242 runs in 4 matches at an average of 60.50 in this first season, including a score of 124 not out against the Knights, which earned him a man of the match.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/469438.html|title=Knights v Lions at Bloemfontein, Jan 20–23, 2011 – Cricket Scorecard – ESPN Cricinfo|work=espncricinfo.com|accessdate=7 November 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/averages/batting_bowling_by_team.html?id=6028;team=3300;type=tournament|title=Cricket Records – Records – SuperSport Series, 2010/11 – Lions – Batting and bowling averages – ESPN Cricinfo|work=espncricinfo.com|accessdate=7 November 2016}}</ref> In his second Supersport season in 2011/12, he made 637 runs at an average of 53.08. This was enough for him to place 11th in the top run scorers.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/batting/most_runs_career.html?id=6838;type=tournament|title=Cricket Records – Records – SuperSport Series, 2011/12 – Most runs – ESPN Cricinfo|work=espncricinfo.com|accessdate=7 November 2016}}</ref> In 2012/13, he was the 5th highest scorer in the now renamed Sunfoil Series, but at a poorer average of 31.58.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/batting/most_runs_career.html?id=7535;type=tournament|title=Cricket Records – Records – Sunfoil Series, 2012/13 – Most runs – ESPN Cricinfo|work=espncricinfo.com|accessdate=7 November 2016}}</ref> In 2013/14, he again scored heavily making 714 runs at an average of 39.66, seeing him place 6th on the Sunfoil Series scorers list.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/batting/most_runs_career.html?id=8339;type=tournament|title=Cricket Records – Records – Sunfoil Series, 2013/14 – Most runs – ESPN Cricinfo|work=espncricinfo.com|accessdate=7 November 2016}}</ref> For his franchise, he has an unusually high conversion rate of 50s to 100s, scoring six 100s and five 50s in Supersport and Sunfoil series cricket.

These performances have earned him five matches so far for the [[South Africa A cricket team]]. The first was in July 2012 against Sri Lanka A in Durban.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/441/441835.html|title=The Home of CricketArchive|work=cricketarchive.com|accessdate=7 November 2016}}</ref> He also played a match against Ireland in the A team's tour of the country in August of that year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/439/439344.html|title=The Home of CricketArchive|work=cricketarchive.com|accessdate=7 November 2016}}</ref> He did not make a significant contribution in either of those two matches. His next appearances for the A team were in the series of matches played in South Africa between South Africa A and the Indian and Australian A teams. He faced Australia once, and India twice.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/549/549739.html|title=The Home of CricketArchive|work=cricketarchive.com|accessdate=7 November 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/549/549747.html|title=The Home of CricketArchive|work=cricketarchive.com|accessdate=7 November 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Scorecards/549/549748.html|title=The Home of CricketArchive|work=cricketarchive.com|accessdate=7 November 2016}}</ref> His best performance was a 65 in the second match of an innings defeat against the Indians. He was included in the [[Gauteng cricket team|Gauteng squad]] for the [[2015 Africa T20 Cup]].<ref>[http://www.espncricinfo.com/africa-t20-cup-2015-16/content/squad/913141.html Gauteng Squad / Players] – ESPNcricinfo. Retrieved 31 August 2015.</ref>

In May 2017, Bavuma announced that he was switching franchises to join [[Cape Cobras]] ahead of the 2017–18 season.<ref>{{cite web |date=2 May 2017 |title=Cobras sign up Bavuma for 2017–18 season |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/cobras-sign-up-temba-bavuma-for-2017-18-season-1095673 |accessdate=2 May 2017 |publisher=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> In June 2018, Bavuma was made captain of the Highveld Lions across all formats.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bavuma named Highveld Lions captain |url=https://www.news24.com/sport/bavuma-named-highveld-lions-captain-20180621 |access-date=2022-10-27 |website=Sport |language=en-US}}</ref> In September 2018, he was named in Gauteng's squad for the [[2018 Africa T20 Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/squad/1158603.html |title=Gauteng Squad |work=ESPN Cricinfo |accessdate=12 September 2018}}</ref> The following month, he was named in [[Durban Heat]]'s squad for the [[2018 Mzansi Super League|first edition]] of the [[Mzansi Super League]] T20 tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sport24.co.za/Cricket/live-mzansi-super-league-player-draft-20181017 |title=Mzansi Super League – full squad lists |work=Sport24 |accessdate=17 October 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.iol.co.za/sport/cricket/domestic/mzansi-super-league-player-draft-the-story-so-far-17521199 |title=Mzansi Super League Player Draft: The story so far |work=Independent Online |accessdate=17 October 2018}}</ref> In September 2019, he was named in the squad for the [[Jozi Stars]] team for the [[2019 Mzansi Super League]] tournament.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://cricket.co.za/news/31555/MSL-20-announces-its-T20-squads |title=MSL 2.0 announces its T20 squads |work=Cricket South Africa |accessdate=4 September 2019 |archive-date=4 September 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190904081427/https://cricket.co.za/news/31555/MSL-20-announces-its-T20-squads |url-status=dead }}</ref> In April 2021, he was
