In September 2022, Bavuma was not picked by any franchise in the auction for the [[2022–23 SA20|first edition of the SA20 League]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ind-vs-sa-2022-almost-let-down-temba-bavuma-on-not-being-picked-for-sa20-1335968|title='Feelings of almost being let down' - Temba Bavuma on not being picked for SA20|work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=22 September 2022}}</ref> but after top-scoring in the ODI series against England was contracted by [[Sunrisers Eastern Cape]] to replace [[Tom Abell]] during the tournament in February 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Moonda |first=Firdose |date=2023-02-02 |title=Temba Bavuma gets SA20 deal after impressive hundred against England |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/temba-bavuma-gets-sa20-deal-after-impressive-knocks-against-england-1357022 |access-date=2023-10-24 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref>

==International career==

=== Early years ===
Bavuma made his [[Test cricket|Test]] debut for South Africa [[West Indian cricket team in South Africa in 2014–15|against the West Indies]] on 26 December 2014.<ref name="Test">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/722331.html |title=West Indies tour of South Africa, 2nd Test: South Africa v West Indies at Port Elizabeth, Dec 26–30, 2014 |accessdate=26 December 2014 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref>
[[File:Starc to Temba Bavuma.jpg|thumb|alt=Bavuma and Starc|[[Mitchell Starc]] bowling to Bavuma during the 3rd test between Australia and South Africa at the [[Adelaide Oval]] in 2016]]
On 5 January 2016, Bavuma became the first black cricketer to score a Test century for South Africa. He scored an unbeaten 102 at the Cape Town in the 2nd Test of the [[English cricket team in South Africa in 2015–16|2015/16 series against England]].<ref name="Bavuma">{{cite news |last=Hopps |first=David |date=5 January 2016 |title=Historic Bavuma ton helps SA achieve parity |work=ESPNcricinfo |publisher=ESPN Sports Media |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/england-tour-of-south-africa-2015-16-800431/south-africa-vs-england-2nd-test-800463/match-report-4 |accessdate=5 January 2021}}</ref>

Bavuma made his One Day International debut for South Africa [[Irish cricket team in South Africa in 2016–17|against Ireland]] on 25 September 2016 and scored his [[List of centuries scored on One Day International cricket debut|maiden ODI century]]. He opened the batting with [[Quinton de Kock]], standing in for [[Hashim Amla]] who was attending the birth of his child. Bavuma was named player of the match for his performance and was the second player to score a century on their ODI debut for South Africa.<ref name="ODI">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/936131.html |title=Ireland tour of South Africa, Only ODI: South Africa v Ireland at Benoni, 25 Sep 2016 |accessdate=25 September 2016 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref><ref name="MaidenODI100">{{cite web |last=Moonda |first=Firdose |date=25 September 2016 |title=Bavuma ton sets up crushing 206-run win |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/ireland-tour-of-rsa-2016-17-936109/south-africa-vs-ireland-only-odi-936131/match-report |url-status=live |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160926154521/http://www.espncricinfo.com/south-africa-v-ireland-2016-17/content/story/1059025.html |archivedate=26 September 2016 |accessdate=25 September 2016 |publisher=[[ESPNcricinfo]]}}</ref>

Bavuma took his first and only Test wicket against [[Australia national cricket team|Australia]] on 7 November 2016.<ref name="first wicket">{{cite web | url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/australia-v-south-africa-2016-17/engine/match/1000851.html | title=Australia v South Africa at Perth | publisher=ESPNcricinfo | accessdate=7 November 2016}}</ref>

In May 2017, Bavuma won the Award of Excellence at [[Cricket South Africa]]'s annual awards.<ref name="awards">{{Cite web |title=De Kock dominates South Africa's awards |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/quinton-de-kock-dominates-south-africa-s-awards-1097632 |accessdate=14 May 2017 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref>

In August 2019, Bavuma was named in South Africa's [[Twenty20 International]] (T20I) squad for their series [[South African cricket team in India in 2019–20|against India]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Nortje, Second and Muthusamy part of South Africa squads to India |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/nortje-second-and-muthusamy-part-of-test-squad-to-india-no-faf-for-t20is-1197305 |accessdate=13 August 2019 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref> He made his T20I debut for South Africa, against [[India national cricket team|India]], on 18 September 2019.<ref>{{cite web |title=2nd T20I (N), South Africa tour of India at Mohali, 18 Sep 2019|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1187005.html|accessdate=18 September 2019|work=ESPN Cricinfo}}
He was the captain of the winning team in [[World Test Championship]] in 2025
</ref>

=== Start of captaincy ===
On 4 March 2021, Bavuma was named as the captain of South Africa's limited over team, taking over the captaincy from [[Quinton de Kock]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=South Africa name Dean Elgar, Temba Bavuma as new captains |url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/2053500 |access-date=2021-07-25 |website=www.icc-cricket.com |language=en}}</ref> With the appointment of him as South Africa's permanent captain, he became the first ever black African player to be appointed as the permanent captain of South Africa's team.<ref>{{Cite web |title=South Africa name Dean Elgar Test captain and Temba Bavuma ODI and T20I captain |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/south-africa-name-dean-elgar-test-captain-and-temba-bavuma-odi-and-t20i-captain-1253753 |access-date=2021-07-25 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=SA name Dean Elgar, Temba Bavuma as new captains |url=https://cricket.yahoo.net/amp/news/sa-name-dean-elgar-temba-062207325 |access-date=2021-07-25 |website=cricket.yahoo.net}}</ref> Bavuma's first series as captain was a home series against Pakistan.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Moonda |first=Firdose |date=2021-03-29 |title=South Africa's Temba Bavuma era begins with sights on 2023 World Cup |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/south-africa-s-temba-bavuma-era-begins-with-sights-on-2023-world-cup-1257179 |access-date=2022-10-27 |website=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He sustained a hamstring injury in the third ODI and as a result missed the T20I portion of the series.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-04-09 |title=Bavuma, Hendricks, Pretorius out of Pakistan T20Is |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/sa-vs-pak-t20i-series-2021-temba-bavuma-reeza-hendricks-dwaine-pretorius-out-of-pakistan-t20is-1258323 |access-date=2022-10-27 |website=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

On 24 July 2021, [[South African cricket team in Ireland in 2021|against Ireland]] in the third T20I, Bavuma scored his maiden T20I half-century, scoring 72 off 51 deliveries before being dismissed by [[Barry McCarthy]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Full Scorecard of South Africa vs Ireland 3rd T20I 2021 - Score Report {{!}} ESPNcricinfo.com |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/south-africa-tour-of-ireland-2021-1251938/ireland-vs-south-africa-3rd-t20i-1251955/full-scorecard |access-date=2021-07-25 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Temba Bavuma, Reeza Hendricks impress as South Africa sweep T20I series |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/south-africa-tour-of-ireland-2021-1251938/ireland-vs-south-africa-3rd-t20i-1251955/match-report |access-date=2021-07-25 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref> In September, South Africa toured Sri Lanka for three ODIs and three T20Is; in the opening match sustained an injury to his right thumb while batting and retired hurt.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-09-03 |title=Fractured thumb rules Bavuma out, Maharaj to lead in remainder of ODI series |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/sl-vs-sa-2021-2nd-odi-keshav-maharaj-to-lead-south-africa-as-fractured-thumb-rules-temba-bavuma-out-1276026 |access-date=2022-10-27 |website=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> The injury required surgery, but Bavuma recovered sufficiently to captain South Africa's squad at the [[2021 ICC Men's T20 World Cup]] in October.<ref>{{cite web |title=T20 World Cup: South Africa leave out Faf du Plessis, Imran Tahir and Chris Morris|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/t20-world-cup-south-africa-leave-out-faf-du-plessis-and-imran-tahir-and-chris-morris-1276995 |access-date=9 September 2021 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref>

Bavuma became Test captain in 2022. He led his team to the WTC final and won it. Till date it remains their second ICC trophy win.

=== 2021 and 2022 T20 World Cups ===
Bavuma batted in 4 games at the 2021 T20 World Cup, scoring 91 runs at an average of 30.33. South Africa initially got off to a bad start, losing to Australia. However they bounced back to win 4 games in a row and beat England, who were the eventual semi finalists. Despite this streak of wins, South Africa would be eliminated in the group stage based on net run rate.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-11-06 |title=Marks Out Of 10: South Africa Player Ratings For The T20 World Cup |url=https://www.wisden.com/series/icc-mens-t20-world-cup-2021-22/cricket-news/marks-out-of-10-south-africa-player-ratings-for-the-t20-world-cup |access-date=9 April 2025 |website=Wisden |language=en-GB}}</ref>

Bavuma scored 46 runs in a win against Sri Lanka and an unbeaten 31 runs in a win against Bangladesh at the tournament.

After the tournament, [[Indian cricket team in South Africa in 2021–22|India toured South Africa]] for 3 tests and 3 ODIs during December to January. Bavuma was the 4th highest run scorer in the test series, with 221 runs at an average of 73.66 while also hitting two fifties and was instrumental in South Africa winning the series 2–1. Bavuma would replicate his success during the ODI series against India as he scored 153 runs with a top score of 110.

[[South African cricket team in India in 2022|South Africa toured India in June 2022]] for five T20Is. South Africa drew the series, but Bavuma sustained an elbow injury in the fourth match and missed South Africa's tour of England later that year.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-06-29 |title=England v South Africa: Temba Bavuma ruled out of multi-format series |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/cricket/61981613 |access-date=2022-10-27 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> Leading into the [[2022 ICC Men's T20 World Cup]] in October and November, sports journalist Katya Witney writing for ''Wisden'' observed that Bavuma was out of form. She suggested that "what Bavuma brings to the team should not be wholly dependent on his batting statistics. His skills and role as captain should not be overlooked lightly."<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-10-03 |title=There is no easy answer to South Africa's Temba Bavuma question |url=https://www.wisden.com/series/south-africa-in-india-2022/cricket-news/temba-bavumas-poor-form-leaves-tricky-question-for-south-africa-ahead-of-world-cup |access-date=9 April 2025 |website=Wisden}}</ref> In a second [[South African cricket team in India in 2022–23|tour of India that year]], preceding the T20 World Cup, Bavuma scored eight runs across four innings in T20Is and ODIs, amidst a tour disrupted by illness, with Bavuma missing the final two ODIs.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Moonda |first=Firdose |date=2022-10-11 |title=South Africa's embarrassment of glitches |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ind-vs-sa-2022-south-africas-embarrassment-of-glitches-ahead-of-t20-world-cup-1339518 |access-date=2022-10-27 |website=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

Bavuma led South Africa at the [[2022 ICC Men's T20 World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.businesslive.co.za/bd/sport/cricket/2022-09-06-bavuma-named-proteas-captain-for-t20-world-cup/|title=Bavuma named Proteas captain for T20 World Cup|work=BusinessDay |access-date= 6 September 2022}}</ref>

On 18 March 2023, in the [[West Indian cricket team in South Africa in 2022–23#2nd ODI|second ODI against the West Indies]], he scored a career-best 144 runs off 118 balls,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Shai Hope 128* trumps Temba Bavuma 144 as West Indies seal victory |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/west-indies-in-south-africa-2022-23-1339568/south-africa-vs-west-indies-2nd-odi-1339602/match-report |access-date=2023-03-26 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref> and crossed the 1000 run-mark in ODIs.<ref>{{Cite web |last=ANI |date=2023-03-19 |title=South Africa skipper Temba Bavuma crosses 1,000-run mark in ODI cricket |url=https://theprint.in/sport/south-africa-skipper-temba-bavuma-crosses-1000-run-mark-in-odi-cricket/1455285/ |access-date=2023-03-26 |website=ThePrint |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== 2025 Test series triumph in India ===
In November 2025, in the first Test of the [[South African cricket team in India in 2025–26|South African tour of India]], Bavuma's unbeaten 55 in the second innings stood out as the only fifty of the match, marking South Africa's first Test victory on Indian soil since 2010.<ref>{{cite web |author=Sampath Bandarupalli |date=16 November 2025 |title=Stats – South Africa’s first win in India since 2010 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/ind-vs-sa-1st-test-stats-south-africa-s-first-win-in-india-since-2010-1511424 |access-date=17 November 2025 |website=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> Having won the second and last Test of the series, Bavuma completed a clean sweep of India, handing them their biggest Test defeat (408 runs), South Africa's first series win in India in 25 years as well not having lost a Test as captain after 12 matches.<ref>{{cite news |last=Monga |first=Sidharth |date=26 November 2025 |title=Harmer's six-for hands India their biggest Test defeat and seals South Africa's 2-0 sweep |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/south-africa-in-india-2025-26-1479563/india-vs-south-africa-2nd-test-1479572/match-report-5 |access-date=26 November 2025 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

'''Tony de Zorzi''' (born 28 August 1997) is a South African [[cricket]]er.<ref name="Bio">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/player/697183.html |title=Tony de Zorzi |access-date=16 September 2016 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://cricket.co.za/news/33974/De-Zorzi-leads-Titans-resistance |title=De Zorzi leads Titans resistance |work=Cricket South Africa |access-date=16 January 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200116130745/https://cricket.co.za/news/33974/De-Zorzi-leads-Titans-resistance |archive-date=16 January 2020}}</ref> He was included in the [[Northerns cricket team|Northerns]] squad for the [[2016 Africa T20 Cup]].<ref name="Northerns">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/squad/1057191.html |title=Northerns Squad |access-date=15 September 2016 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He made his [[Twenty20 cricket|Twenty20]] (T20) debut for Northerns against [[Kenya national cricket team|Kenya]] on 16 September 2016.<ref name="T20debut">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1029629.html |title=Africa T20 Cup, Pool B: Kenya v Northerns at Oudtshoorn, Sep 16, 2016 |access-date=16 September 2016 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> Prior to his T20 debut, he was named as [[captain (cricket)|captain]] of South Africa's squad for the [[2016 Under-19 Cricket World Cup]].<ref name="SouthAfricaU19">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/icc-under-19-world-cup-2016/content/story/953769.html |title=Tony de Zorzi to lead South Africa at U-19 World Cup |access-date=21 December 2015 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

==Personal life==
De Zorzi was born in [[Johannesburg]] on 28 August 1997.<ref name="Bio"/> He was raised by his mother Natasha as a single parent.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/tony-de-zorzi-gets-a-chance-to-be-the-star-of-south-africa-he-never-could-be-before-1362402|title=De Zorzi gets a chance to be the star he always wanted to be, a 'lot of dirty work' later|first=Firdose|last=Moonda|date=9 March 2023|access-date=18 February 2026|publisher=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> His mother is of [[Italians|Italian]] descent and his father is [[Nigeria]]n.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cricket/share-a-laugh-with-tony-de-zorzi-cricket-is-tough-enough-so-why-not-101704266598825.html|title=Share a laugh with Tony de Zorzi: Cricket is tough enough, so why not?|date=3 January 2024|newspaper=Hindustan Times|access-date=18 February 2026}}</ref>

De Zorzi attended [[King Edward VII School, Johannesburg]]. He later studied at the [[University of Pretoria]].<ref name="Bio"/>

==Domestic and franchise career==
He made his [[first-class cricket|first-class]] debut for Northerns in the [[2016–17 Sunfoil 3-Day Cup]] on 28 October 2016.<ref name="FCdebut">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1024745.html |title=Sunfoil 3-Day Cup, Pool A: Northerns v KwaZulu-Natal at Centurion, Oct 28-30, 2016 |access-date=28 October 2016 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> He made his [[List A cricket|List A]] debut for Northerns in the [[2016–17 CSA Provincial One-Day Challenge]] on 31 October 2016.<ref name="ListAdebut">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1024945.html |title=CSA Provincial One-Day Challenge, Pool A: Northerns v KwaZulu-Natal at Centurion, Oct 31, 2016 |access-date=31 October 2016 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

In August 2017, he was named in [[Pretoria Mavericks]]' squad for the first season of the [[T20 Global League]].<ref name="T20GL">{{cite web|url=http://www.t20.gl/news/t20-global-league-announces-final-team-squads|title=T20 Global League announces final team squads|access-date=28 August 2017|work=T20 Global League|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170905185645/https://www.t20.gl/news/t20-global-league-announces-final-team-squads|archive-date=5 September 2017}}</ref> However, in October 2017, [[Cricket South Africa]] initially postponed the tournament until November 2018, with it being cancelled soon after.<ref name="T20GLpostponement">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/southafrica/content/story/1123408.html |title=Cricket South Africa postpones Global T20 league |access-date=10 October 2017 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

In January 2018, he scored his first century in List A cricket, batting for [[Titans (cricket team)|Titans]] against [[Knights (cricket team)|Knights]] in the [[2017–18 Momentum One Day Cup]].<ref name="ListA100">{{cite web |url=http://cricket.co.za/news/22998/Maiden-De-Zorzi-ton-helps-Titans-stretch-lead |title=Maiden De Zorzi ton helps Titans stretch lead |publisher=Cricket South Africa |access-date=20 January 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180120235932/http://cricket.co.za/news/22998/Maiden-De-Zorzi-ton-helps-Titans-stretch-lead |archive-date=20 January 2018}}</ref> In June 2018, he was named in the squad for the [[Titans (cricket team)|Titans]] team for the 2018–19 season.<ref name="con1819">{{cite web|url=http://www.titans.co.za/index.php/categories-1-layout/item/859-multiply-titans-announce-contracts-2018-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180616154504/http://www.titans.co.za/index.php/categories-1-layout/item/859-multiply-titans-announce-contracts-2018-19 |url-status=dead |archive-date=16 June 2018 |title=Multiply Titans Announce Contracts 2018-19 |work=Multiply Titans |access-date=16 June 2018 }}</ref> The following month, he was named as the captain of the Cricket South Africa Emerging Squad.<ref name="EmSq">{{cite web|url=http://cricket.co.za/news/25235/De-Zorzi-to-lead-SA-Emerging-Squad-in-Sri-Lanka |title=De Zorzi to lead SA Emerging Squad in Sri Lanka |work=Cricket South Africa |access-date=19 July 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180719233426/http://cricket.co.za/news/25235/De-Zorzi-to-lead-SA-Emerging-Squad-in-Sri-Lanka |archive-date=19 July 2018}}</ref>

In September 2018, he was named in the Titans' squad for the 2018 Abu Dhabi T20 Trophy.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sport24.co.za/Cricket/titans-name-strong-squad-for-abu-dhabi-t20-league-20180921 |title=Titans name strong squad for Abu Dhabi T20 league |work=Sport24 |access-date=27 September 2018}}</ref> In October 2018, he was named in [[Tshwane Spartans]]' squad for the [[2018 Mzansi Super League|first edition]] of the [[Mzansi Super League]] T20 tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sport24.co.za/Cricket/live-mzansi-super-league-player-draft-20181017 |title=Mzansi Super League - full squad lists |work=Sport24 |access-date=17 October 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.iol.co.za/sport/cricket/domestic/mzansi-super-league-player-draft-the-story-so-far-17521199 |title=Mzansi Super League Player Draft: The story so far |work=Independent Online |access-date=17 October 2018}}</ref> In September 2019, he was named in the squad for the [[Tshwane Spartans]] team for the [[2019 Mzansi Super League]] tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cricket.co.za/news/31555/MSL-20-announces-its-T20-squads |title=MSL 2.0 announces its T20 squads |work=Cricket South Africa |access-date=4 September 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190904081427/https://cricket.co.za/news/31555/MSL-20-announces-its-T20-squads |archive-date=4 September 2019}}</ref>

In January 2020, in the [[2019–20 CSA 4-Day Franchise Series]], he scored his maiden double century in first-class cricket, with an unbeaten 213 runs against [[Cape Cobras]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cricket.co.za/news/33999/De-Zorzi-double-ton-helps-Titans-secure-a-draw |title=De Zorzi double ton helps Titans secure a draw |work=Cricket South Africa |access-date=16 January 2020 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20241031213318/https://www.news24.com/sport/cricket/domestic/4-dayfranchiseseries/de-zorzi-double-ton-helps-titans-secure-a-draw-against-cobras-20200116 |archive-date=31 October 2024}}</ref> In April 2021, he was named in [[Western Province (cricket team)|Western Province]]'s squad, ahead of the 2021–22 cricket season in South Africa.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cricket.co.za/news/38184/CSA-reveals-Division-One-squads-for-2021-22 |title=CSA reveals Division One squads for 2021/22 |work=Cricket South Africa |access-date=20 April 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210420104034/http://cricket.co.za/news/38184/CSA-reveals-Division-One-squads-for-2021-22 |archive-date=20 April 2021}}</ref>

==International career==
In February 2023, he was selected in South Africa Test squad for the series [[West Indian cricket team in South Africa in 2022–23|against West Indies]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/temba-bavuma-named-south-africa-s-test-captain-but-relinquishes-t20i-job-1359417 |title=Bavuma replaces Elgar as South Africa's Test captain, but relinquishes T20I job |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=17 February 2023}}</ref> He made his Test debut against [[West Indies cricket team|West Indies]] on 28 February 2023.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1339599.html |title=1st Test, Centurion, February 28 - March 04, 2023, West Indies tour of South Africa |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=28 February 2023}}</ref> In March 2023, he was named in South Africa's [[One Day International]] (ODI) squad for their series [[West Indian cricket team in South Africa in 2022–23|against the West Indies]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/3098383 |title=Markram announced as new T20I captain; South Africa name squads for West Indies limited-overs leg |work=International Cricket Council |access-date=6 March 2023}}</ref> He made his ODI debut in the second ODI on 18 March 2023.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/match/1339602.html |title=2nd ODI (D/N), East London, March 18, 2023, West Indies tour of South Africa |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=18 March 2023}}</ref> In April 2023, he was named in [[South Africa A cricket team|South Africa A]]'s squad as the captain for their [[South Africa A cricket team in Sri Lanka in 2023|tour to Sri Lanka]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lambley |first=Garrin |date=2023-04-25 |title=South Africa 'A' squad packed with Proteas for Sri Lanka tour |url=https://www.thesouthafrican.com/sport/cricket/south-africa-squad-packed-with-proteas-for-sri-lanka-tour-breaking-result-25-april-2023/ |access-date=2023-04-26 |website=The South African |language=en-ZA}}</ref>

In December 2023, he scored his maiden international century [[Indian cricket team in South Africa in 2023–24|against India during the second One Day International match of the three-match ODI series]] that took place at [[St George's Park Cricket Ground]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nandre Burger, Tony de Zorzi help South Africa draw level against India |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/india-in-south-africa-2023-24-1387592/south-africa-vs-india-2nd-odi-1387601/match-report |access-date=2023-12-20 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-12-20 |title=Tony de Zorzi gives a glimpse of the future, and Sai Sudharsan impresses again |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/cricket-videos/sa-vs-ind-tony-de-zorzi-gives-a-glimpse-of-the-future-and-sai-sudharsan-impresses-again-1413645 |access-date=2023-12-23 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref> His knock of unbeaten 119 came in difficult pitch conditions during the course of the match which eventually helped South Africa to win the game and level the series 1–1.<ref>{{Cite web |title=De Zorzi stirs South Africa up with 'positive' play in bid to make a spot his own |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/tony-de-zorzi-stirs-south-africa-up-with-positive-play-in-bid-to-make-a-spot-his-own-1413602 |access-date=2023-12-23 |website=ESPNcricinfo |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Agarwal |first=Naman |date=2023-12-21 |title=De Zorzi's Arrival And Chahal's Absence: Five Takeaways From India's 2-1 Series Win Over South Africa {{!}} SA Vs IND {{!}} Cricket News Today |url=https://www.wisden.com/series/india-in-south-africa-2023-24/cricket-news/de-zorzis-arrival-chahals-absence-five-takeaways-indias-2-1-series-win-south-africa |access-date=14 April 2025 |website=Wisden |language=en-GB}}</ref>

De Zorzi made his first Test century against [[Bangladesh national cricket team|Bangladesh]] in October 2024.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/south-africa-in-bangladesh-2024-25-1453291/bangladesh-vs-south-africa-2nd-test-1453294/match-report-1|title=De Zorzi and Stubbs hit maiden tons to make it South Africa's day|publisher=ESPNCricinfo|accessdate=10 November 2024}}</ref>

He is one of the members of the winning squad of [[2025 World Test Championship final|2025 World Test Championship]] final.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cruickshank |first=Vaughan |date=2025-06-10 |title=What is cricket's World Test Championship and how did Australia qualify for the final? |url=https://doi.org/10.64628/aa.phvdca6ms |access-date=2025-09-20 |website=doi.org}}</ref>

In January 2026, de Zonzi was named in South Africa's squad for the [[2026 ICC Men's T20 World Cup|2026 T20 World Cup]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/tournaments/mens-t20-world-cup-2026/news/strong-outfit-to-lead-south-africa-s-t20-world-cup-quest|title=Strong outfit to lead South Africa's T20 World Cup quest|work=[[International Cricket Council]]|date=2 January 2026|access-date=2 February 2026}}</ref> but was later removed due to an injury.

'''Trent Alexander Boult''' (born 22 July 1989) is a New Zealand [[cricket]]er who represented the [[New Zealand national cricket team|New Zealand cricket team]] in all formats between 2011 and 2024. He continues to play in various [[Twenty20]] leagues around the globe as a [[Fast bowling|fast bowler]]. Boult was a key member of the New Zealand team that won the [[2019–2021 World Test Championship|2019–2021 ICC World Test Championship]]. He was also a part of the New Zealand squads to finish as runners-up in two [[List of Cricket World Cup finals|Cricket World Cup finals]] in [[2015 Cricket World Cup|2015]] and [[2019 Cricket World Cup|2019]].

He is a left-arm fast-medium bowler and a right-handed batsman,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://content-www.cricinfo.com/ci/content/story/339952.html  |title=New Zealand's prospects hinge on in-form bowlers |publisher=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=16 September 2008}}</ref> Boult made his Test debut for New Zealand in December 2011 and his One Day International debut the following July. He was the joint leading wicket taker at the [[2015 Cricket World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.icc-cricket.com/cricket-world-cup/stats/2015/player/most-wickets |title=Most wickets – player: Cricket World Cup 2015 |year=2015 |publisher=ICC Cricket |access-date=13 April 2015}}</ref> In November 2018, he became the third bowler for New Zealand to [[List of One Day International cricket hat-tricks|take a hat-trick in ODIs]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=Trent Boult, the third New Zealander to take a hat-trick|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/trent-boult-the-third-new-zealander-to-take-a-hat-trick-1164408|access-date=25 January 2022|work=ESPNcricinfo|language=en}}</ref> while in June 2019, Boult became the first bowler for New Zealand to take a hat-trick in the [[Cricket World Cup]].<ref name="CWCHT">{{cite web|url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cricket/world-cup-2019-trent-boult-creates-history-becomes-first-nz-bowler-to-take-hat-trick-in-a-world-cup/story-5siju06GwxPGi0NocslIWJ.html |title=World Cup 2019: Trent Boult creates history, becomes first NZ bowler to take hat-trick in a World Cup |work=Hindustan Times |date=29 June 2019 |access-date=29 June 2019}}</ref>

==Cricket career==
===Domestic and T20 franchise career===
In 2015, Boult was New Zealand's leading wicket taker at the 2015 ICC Cricket World Cup. Following the tournament, Boult received a Maiden call-up into the [[2016 Indian Premier League|Indian Premier League]] by the [[Sunrisers Hyderabad]] and he was purchased for $600,000.

In February 2017, he was bought by the [[Kolkata Knight Riders]] team for the [[2017 Indian Premier League]] for 5 [[crore]]s.<ref name="IPL">{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/indian-premier-league-2017/content/story/1083407.html |title=List of players sold and unsold at IPL auction 2017 |access-date=20 February 2017 |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

He also played for [[Delhi Capitals]] from [[2018 Indian Premier League|2018]] to [[2019 Indian Premier League|2019]] in the IPL.

In June 2019, he was selected to play for the Toronto Nationals franchise team in the [[2019 Global T20 Canada]] tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.canadacricket.com/?p=12755 |title=Global T20 draft streamed live |work=Canada Cricket Online |date=20 June 2019 |access-date=20 June 2019}}</ref>

Boult was traded by Delhi to the [[Mumbai Indians]] prior to the thirteenth season of the IPL. He played a critical role in Mumbai winning the [[2020 Indian Premier League|2020 IPL]] title. He was the [[Player of the Match awards (cricket)|man of the match]] in the final and was also named the player of the season. Boult  claimed 25 wickets in that edition of the IPL and was the third highest wicket taker after [[Kagiso Rabada]] and [[Jasprit Bumrah]]. He also bowled 4 maiden overs, the most by any player in a single season of IPL.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/cricket/300155473/trent-boult-inspires-mumbai-indians-to-fifth-ipl-title-with-victory-over-delhi-capitals|title=Trent Boult inspires Mumbai Indians to fifth IPL title with victory over Delhi Capitals|date=11 November 2020|publisher=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |access-date=11 November 2020}}</ref> His best bowling figures in the IPL are 4/18 against [[Chennai Super Kings]] (on 23 October 2020).

In the [[List of 2022 Indian Premier League personnel changes|2022 IPL auction]], Boult was bought by the [[Rajasthan Royals]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sportstar |first=Team |title=IPL auction: Boult sold to Rajasthan Royals for Rs 8 crore |url=https://sportstar.thehindu.com/cricket/ipl/ipl-auction/ipl-auction-trent-boult-sold-to-rajasthan-royals-for-rs-8-crore/article38417183.ece |access-date=29 March 2022 |website=Sportstar |date=12 February 2022 |language=en}}</ref>

On 2024 November, he was bought by [[Mumbai Indians]] in [[List of 2025 Indian Premier League personnel changes|the 2025 IPL player-auctions]]. He was the highest wicket taker for MI in 2025.

===International career===
Boult accompanied the New Zealand A team on their winter training tour in 2007.<ref>[http://content-www.cricinfo.com/ci/content/story/291053.html ''Under-19 players to join A tour''] ESPNcricinfo retrieved 16 September 2008</ref> On 9 February 2007, he took two wickets for 28 runs and scored seven not out against India's Under-19 team.<ref>[http://content-www.cricinfo.com/newzealand/engine/current/match/277228.html India Under-19s in New Zealand Youth ODI Series – 2nd Youth ODI: New Zealand Under-19s v India Under-19s] ESPNcricinfo retrieved 16 September 2008</ref> He then travelled to [[Malaysia]] in February 2008 for the [[2008 Under-19 Cricket World Cup|Under-19 World Cup]].

On 21 January 2009, Boult was selected for the New Zealand squad for the one-day series against Australia at just 19 years of age. Boult only managed to play in the warm up game against the Prime Minister's XI and went wicketless off seven overs. During the tour Boult was clocked as the fastest bowler touring with the New Zealand team with a highest speed of {{convert|143.3|km/h|abbr=on}}.

Boult made his Test debut in the 2011–12 season, in the [[New Zealand cricket team in Australia in 2011–12#Second Test|Second Test]] against Australia in [[Bellerive Oval|Hobart]], in a match won by New Zealand by 7 runs, New Zealand's first test win in Australia since 1985 and their first test win over Australia since 1993. He took four wickets in the match; additionally, he scored 21 runs in a tenth-wicket partnership with [[Chris Martin (cricketer)|Chris Martin]] in the second innings.

In 2012, Boult produced a string of strong performances with the ball against the West Indies, India and Sri Lanka to consolidate his position as [[Tim Southee]]'s new ball partner. He carried this good form into 2013 when he took 19 wickets in 5 tests against England, including his best test match innings bowling figures of 6/68 at Eden Park in March.

After suffering a side strain during New Zealand's final Test match against England at Leeds, Boult returned to the New Zealand Test team for a two test tour of Bangladesh. Boult struggled in the hot and dry conditions, taking just 3 wickets and frequently straying with his accuracy. However, when back in home conditions against the touring West Indies, Boult swiftly returned to his best. In the second test at the [[Basin Reserve]] Boult won man of the match award, after taking career best figures of 10 for 80 and completing a brilliant one-handed diving catch to his left to dismiss [[Denesh Ramdin]].  In the first innings of the second test on the same venue against India, Boult made another one-handed diving right-handed catch to dismiss [[Ajinkya Rahane]]. He also had bowling figures of 4 for 146.

In 2014 T20 series against West Indies, Boult's squad number switched from 8 to 18, a number previously worn by [[Mathew Sinclair]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=odqx9z2fIgU|title=Trent Boult strikes again|date=6 July 2014|via=YouTube}}</ref>

In the [[New Zealand cricket team in Australia in 2015–16|Trans-Tasman trophy 2015–16 series]], in Australia, in the third Test,  the first ever day-night test in history, Boult became the first New Zealander and second overall after [[Josh Hazlewood]], to take a five-wicket haul in a day-night test. However, Australia won the day-night match by 3 wickets. He was named in the 'Team of the Tournament' for the 2015 World Cup by the ICC.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2015-03-30/world-cup-team-of-the-tournament-revealed/6358716|title=World Cup team of the tournament revealed|first=Dean|last=Bilton|date=30 March 2015|website=ABC News}}</ref>

In 2018, Boult produced his best figures in Test cricket, taking 6/32 in the First Test [[English cricket team in New Zealand in 2017–18|against England]] in [[Eden Park|Auckland]]. England were bowled out for 58 in their first innings and New Zealand went on to win the Test by an innings and 49 runs.<ref>{{cite news |title=New Zealand beat England by an innings and 49 runs in first Test at Auckland |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/cricket/43537497 |access-date=31 January 2019 |work=BBC Sport |date=26 March 2018}}</ref> New Zealand went on the win series 1–0; Boult finished with 15 wickets at an average of 18.33 and was named man of the series.<ref>{{cite news |title=New Zealand vs England: Black Caps' team effort helps end Test jinx against visitors |url=https://www.firstpost.com/firstcricket/sports-news/new-zealand-vs-england-black-caps-team-effort-helps-end-test-jinx-against-visitors-4416547.html |access-date=31 January 2019 |work=Firstpost |date=3 April 2018}}</ref> At the NZC Annual Awards, he received the Men's Test Player of the Year and the Sir Richard Hadlee Medal for best International player of the year.<ref>{{cite news |title=Boult wins Sir Richard Hadlee Medal, Devine sweeps women's awards |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/23025856 |access-date=31 January 2019 |work=ESPNcricinfo |date=4 April 2018 |language=en}}</ref> In May that year, Boult was one of twenty players to be awarded a new contract for the 2018–19 season by [[New Zealand Cricket]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/23512513 |title=Todd Astle bags his first New Zealand contract |work=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=15 May 2018}}</ref>

In the fourth ODI of [[Indian cricket team in New Zealand in 2018–19|India's 2018–19 New Zealand tour]], Boult claimed his fifth five-wicket haul, the joint-most for a New Zealand bowler alongside [[Richard Hadlee]]. He returned figures of 5/21 helping his team dismiss India for their lowest total in ODIs since 2010. New Zealand went on record one of their biggest wins and Boult was named man of the match.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Narayanan |first1=Deepu |title=Boult attack and India's lowest total since 2010 |url=https://www.cricbuzz.com/cricket-news/106430/trent-boult-attack-and-indias-lowest-total-since-2010-india-cricket-tour-of-new-zealand-2019 |website=Cricbuzz |access-date=31 January 2019 |language=en |date=31 January 2019}}</ref>

web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/26426227/sodhi-blundell-named-new-zealand-world-cup-squad |title=Sodhi and Blundell named in New Zealand World Cup squad |work=ESPNcricinfo ==Bowling and fielding style==
Boult is a left-arm fast-medium [[Swing bowling|swing]] bowler who makes up for his relative lack of height with deceptive pace of approximately 140 km/h and ability to swing the ball both ways with different variations. Boult's primary weapon is an [[inswinger]] to a right-handed batsman. Unsurprisingly, his childhood cricketing hero is [[Wasim Akram]]. In 2013, in a radio interview, the former New Zealand captain [[Jeremy Coney]] rated Boult as New Zealand's best bowling discovery since [[Shane Bond]].  He is also known to haul in one-handed catches with either hand.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fgQNoXNAfUw|title=Trent Boult CATCH of the CENTURY Unbelievable! HD 1080p|date=13 January 2014|via=YouTube}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=52S7YGLjqy8|title=WHAT A CATCH BY TRENT BOULT!|date=14 February 2014|via=YouTube}}</ref>  In 2014, he became the 4th test bowler since [[Richard Hadlee]], [[Chris Martin (cricketer)|Chris Martin]] and [[Iain O'Brien]] to claim 30+ wickets in consecutive years. He has developed a good opening bowling partnership with [[Tim Southee]], having taken 46% of all wickets between them since 2013, especially since the retirement of Martin.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/11497/scorecard/749777/new-zealand-vs-sri-lanka-1st-test-sri-lanka-in-new-zealand-test-series-2014-15|title=Full Scorecard of New Zealand vs Sri Lanka 1st Test 2014 – Score Report |work=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> In Tests, they are ably complemented by [[Neil Wagner]]'s short left-arm seam deliveries. In August 2019, in the [[New Zealand cricket team in Sri Lanka in 2019|series against Sri Lanka]], Boult became the third bowler for New Zealand to [[List of New Zealand Test cricket records#Most career wickets|take 250 wickets in Test cricket]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/cricket/black-caps/115246592/black-caps-v-sri-lanka-trent-boult-becomes-third-nz-bowler-to-250-test-wickets |title=Black Caps v Sri Lanka: Trent Boult becomes third NZ bowler to 250 test wickets |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=23 August 2019 |access-date=23 August 2019}}</ref>
