'''Umar Akmal''' ([[Urdu]], {{langx|pa|{{Nastaliq|عمر اکمل}}}}; born 26 May 1990) is a Pakistani [[cricketer]] who played for [[Pakistan national cricket team]] between 2009 and 2019. He was banned by the [[Pakistan Cricket Board]] for eighteen months for not disclosing offers related to [[Spot-fixing|spot fixing]] until August 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Umar Akmal's ban halved from three years to 1.5 years|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/umar-akmal-s-ban-halved-from-three-years-to-1-5-years-1227989|access-date=2021-07-08|website=ESPNcricinfo|language=en}}</ref>

Akmal made his [[One Day International]] (ODI) debut on 1 August 2009 against [[Sri Lanka cricket team|Sri Lanka]], his [[Twenty20 International]] (T20I) debut on 12 August 2009 also against Sri Lanka, and his [[Test cricket|Test]] debut against [[New Zealand cricket team|New Zealand]] on 23 November 2009. He is a right-handed [[batsman]] and a [[spin bowling|part-time spinner]]. Like his two brothers, [[Adnan Akmal|Adnan]] and [[Kamran Akmal|Kamran]], Umar has kept wicket for the national team in many ODIs.

Domestically, he played for [[Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Limited]] for eleven years, before signing with [[United Bank Limited cricket team|United Bank Limited]] in August 2017.<ref name="UBL">{{Cite web|url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/pakistan/content/story/1115097.html |title=Umar Akmal signs up with United Bank |access-date=4 August 2017 |work=ESPN Cricinfo}}</ref> He has also played in many franchise [[Twenty20|Twenty20 teams]] around the world.

In February 2020, he was suspended by the [[Pakistan Cricket Board]] (PCB), after he had breached their Anti-Corruption code.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.icc-cricket.com/news/1616108 |title=PCB suspends Umar Akmal under Anti-Corruption Code |work=International Cricket Council |access-date=20 February 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/28741135/umar-akmal-suspended-pcb-anti-corruption-code |title=Umar Akmal suspended under PCB's anti-corruption code |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=20 February 2020}}</ref> In April 2020, the PCB banned him from cricket for three years, after he pled guilty to failing to report corrupt approaches.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/29103103/pcb-hands-umar-akmal-three-year-ban-all-cricket |title=PCB hands Umar Akmal three-year ban from all cricket |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=27 April 2020}}</ref> The following month, he lodged an appeal against his ban.<ref name=":5">{{cite web|title=Umar Akmal files appeal against three-year ban|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/29194658/umar-akmal-files-appeal-three-year-ban|last=Farooq|first=Umar|date=19 May 2020|work=ESPN Cricinfo|access-date=19 May 2020}}</ref> In July 2020, Akmal's ban was reduced to one-and-a-half years, with his suspension running from February 2020 to August 2021.<ref name="ban_reduce">{{cite web|last=Farooq|first=Umar|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/29556619/umar-akmal-ban-halved-three-years-1.5-years |title=Umar Akmal's ban halved from three years to 1.5 years |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=29 July 2020}}</ref> In August 2020, the PCB appealed the ban reduction to the [[Court of Arbitration for Sport]] (CAS) and Akmal appealed to the CAS to have his ban overturned.<ref name=":6">{{Cite web|last=Farooq|first=Umar|date=10 August 2020|title=PCB to challenge Umar Akmal's ban reduction in Swiss court|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/29632609/pcb-challenge-umar-akmal-ban-reduction-swiss-court|access-date=10 August 2020|website=ESPN Cricinfo|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":7">{{Cite web|last=Farooq|first=Umar|date=20 August 2020|title=Umar Akmal files appeal to overturn 18-month ban|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/29702414/umar-akmal-files-appeal-overturn-18-month-ban|access-date=20 August 2020|website=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref> In February 2021, the CAS reduced the ban to 12 months and imposed a [[Pakistani rupee|PKR]] 4.25 million (27,000 [[United States dollar|USD]]) fine on Akmal.<ref name=":8">{{Cite web|last=Farooq|first=Umar|date=26 February 2020|title=Umar Akmal eligible to return to cricket after CAS reduces his ban by six months|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/umar-akmal-eligible-to-return-to-cricket-after-cas-reduces-his-ban-by-six-months-1253096|access-date=26 February 2020|website=ESPNCricinfo}}</ref>

In July 2021, Akmal apologised for not reporting corrupt approaches last year, which led to him being banned for 12 months.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Umar Akmal apologises for not reporting corrupt approaches|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/umar-akmal-apologises-for-not-reporting-corrupt-approaches-1268892|access-date=2021-07-08|website=ESPNcricinfo|language=en}}</ref> He then left Pakistan to sign a short-term contract with the Northern California Cricket Association in the United States.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/umar-akmal-leaves-pakistan-for-league-cricket-in-california-1281465 |title=Umar Akmal leaves Pakistan for league cricket in California |work=ESPN Cricinfo |access-date=4 October 2021}}</ref>

==Early and personal life==
He was born to Mohammad Akmal Siddique, "a very senior administrator in Pakistan cricket", in a family of eight children, with seven sons who all played cricket at some point but many went to business, and one daughter.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Wilson|first=Andy|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2012/jan/21/adnan-akmal-pakistan-england|title=Adnan Akmal keeps family flame burning for Pakistan against England|date=21 January 2012|website=[[The Guardian]]|access-date=9 August 2018}}</ref> He is the youngest brother of [[Adnan Akmal]] and [[Kamran Akmal]] who are also cricketers, both [[wicket-keeper]]s. He is also the cousin of Pakistani batsman [[Babar Azam]].

In 2014 he married Noor Amna, the daughter of Pakistan leg-spinner [[Abdul Qadir (cricketer)|Abdul Qadir]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.thenationalnews.com/sport/umar-akmal-in-trouble-over-wedding-celebrations-1.452506|title=Umar Akmal in trouble over wedding celebrations|date=16 April 2014|website=The National|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref>

==Early career and domestic career==

Akmal represented [[Pakistan]] in the [[2008 U/19 Cricket World Cup]] in [[Malaysia]]. After his success at the U-19 level he earned himself a first-class contract and played the 2007–08 season of the [[Quaid-i-Azam Trophy|Quaid-e-Azam Trophy]], representing the [[Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Limited cricket team|Sui Northern Gas]] team.<ref>{{cite web |title=First-class matches played by Umar Akmal (117) |url=https://cricketarchive.com/Archive/Players/83/83229/First-Class_Matches.html |website=CricketArchive |access-date=17 June 2024 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

He is an aggressive style cricketer. In only his sixth first-class match he scored 248 off just 225 deliveries, including four sixes.<ref>{{cite web|title=Full Scorecard of Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Limited vs Karachi Blues Group B 2007 - Score Report|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/8840/scorecard/313931/karachi-blues-vs-sui-northern-gas-pipelines-limited-group-b-quaid-e-azam-trophy-2007-08|website=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref> He followed that up with an unbeaten 186 in his 8th first-class match, off just 170 balls. He fared less well in his second season of first-class cricket, with a string of low scores batting at number 3.{{Citation needed|date= July 2022}}

He found form in the final few matches of the 2008/09 season and then in the RBS T20 tournament which led to him getting selected to play for Pakistan A side on their tour to Australia A.

Akmal came to prominence during the Australia A tour in June/July 2009. In the two unofficial Test matches he recorded scores of 54, 100*, 130, 0. In the unofficial ODI series that followed, Akmal continued his fine form with a century in the opening ODI encounter off just 68 deliveries. These performances made him gather considerable praise from the media who were there to witness him and calls began to grow about his inclusion in the ODI series for the main Pakistan side against Sri Lanka. Later that year, Akmal made his Test, ODI, and T20I debut.

He played for Sui Northern Gas in the Quaid-e-Azam trophy until 2016–17, during which time Sui Northern Gas won three times ([[2007–08 Quaid-e-Azam Trophy|2007-08]], [[2014–15 Quaid-e-Azam Trophy|2014-15]], [[2015–16 Quaid-e-Azam Trophy|2015-16]]). However, he was briefly dropped from the first-class side for the [[2012 Patron's Trophy|2012 President's Trophy]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Umar Akmal dropped by his domestic side|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/22128901/umar-akmal-dropped-domestic-side|last=Farooq|first=Umar|date=14 November 2012|website=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref> Akmal played for United Bank Limited in 2017–18, and for [[Habib Bank Limited cricket team|Habib Bank Limited]] in 2018-19 and won the [[2018–19 Quaid-e-Azam Trophy]] with Habib Bank Limited.

Akmal played for the [[Lahore Lions]] in the [[National T20 Cup]] until 2015–16, during which time Lahore Lions won the tournament three times ([[2010–11 Faysal Bank T20 Cup|2010-11]], [[2012–13 Faysal Bank T20 Cup|2012-13]], [[2013–14 Faysal Bank T20 Cup|2013-14]]).

Akmal played for [[Balochistan cricket team|Balochistan]] in the [[2016 Pakistan Cup]]. He captained [[Punjab cricket team (Pakistan)|Punjab]] in the [[2017 Pakistan Cup]], with Punjab finishing 4th out of 5th.

In April 2018, he was named in [[Khyber Pakhtunkhwa cricket team|Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]]'s squad for the [[2018 Pakistan Cup]].<ref name="squads1">{{cite web|url=https://www.geo.tv/latest/191967-pakistan-cup-one-day-tournament-to-begin-in-faisalabad|title=Pakistan Cup one-day tournament to begin in Faisalabad next week|work=Geo TV|access-date=21 April 2018}}</ref><ref name="squads2">{{cite web|url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/print/306831-pakistan-cup-cricket-from-25th|title=Pakistan Cup Cricket from 25th|work=The News International|access-date=21 April 2018}}</ref> He was the leading run-scorer for [[Habib Bank Limited cricket team|Habib Bank Limited]] in the [[2018–19 Quaid-e-Azam One Day Cup]], with 410 runs in ten matches.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/averages/batting_bowling_by_team.html?id=12569;team=2798;type=tournament|title=Quaid-e-Azam One Day Cup, 2018/19 - Habib Bank Limited : Batting and bowling averages|work=ESPN Cricinfo|access-date=4 November 2018}}</ref> In March 2019, he was named in [[Baluchistan cricket team|Baluchistan]]'s squad for the [[2019 Pakistan Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pcb.com.pk/press-release-detail/federal-areas-aim-to-complete-hat-trick-of-pakistan-cup-titles.html|title=Federal Areas aim to complete hat-trick of Pakistan Cup titles|work=Pakistan Cricket Board|access-date=25 March 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/print/447913-pakistan-cup-one-day-cricket-from-april-2|title=Pakistan Cup one-day cricket from April 2|work=The International News|access-date=25 March 2019}}</ref> In the opening match of the tournament, he scored 136 [[not out]], his highest total in [[List A cricket]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pcb.com.pk/news-detail/ton-up-umar-akmal-gives-balochistan-winning-start-in-pakistan-cup.html|title=Ton-up Umar Akmal gives Balochistan winning start in Pakistan Cup 2019|work=Pakistan Cricket Board|access-date=3 April 2019|archive-date=3 April 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190403080031/https://www.pcb.com.pk/news-detail/ton-up-umar-akmal-gives-balochistan-winning-start-in-pakistan-cup.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was the leading run-scorer in the tournament, with 342 runs in five matches.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/batting/most_runs_career.html?id=12939;type=tournament|title=Pakistan Cup, 2019: Most runs|work=ESPN Cricinfo|access-date=12 April 2019}}</ref>

In September 2019, he was named in [[Central Punjab cricket team|Central Punjab]]'s squad for the [[2019–20 Quaid-e-Azam Trophy]] tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pcb.com.pk/press-release-detail/pcb-announces-squads-for-2019-20-domestic-season.html|title=PCB announces squads for 2019-20 domestic season|work=Pakistan Cricket Board|access-date=4 September 2019|archive-date=3 September 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190903183721/https://www.pcb.com.pk/press-release-detail/pcb-announces-squads-for-2019-20-domestic-season.html|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/27527401/sarfaraz-ahmed-babar-azam-take-charge-pakistan-domestic-sides|title=Sarfaraz Ahmed and Babar Azam to take charge of Pakistan domestic sides|work=ESPN Cricinfo|access-date=4 September 2019}}</ref> Central Punjab won the tournament and Akmal was named man of the match in the final.<ref>{{cite web |title=Northern vs Central PNJB, Final, Karachi, December 27 - 30, 2019 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/quaid-e-azam-trophy-2019-20-1199386/central-punjab-pakistan-vs-northern-pakistan-final-1199425/full-scorecard |website=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=17 June 2024}}</ref>

==Test career==

[[File:Umar Akmal, Dunedin, NZ, 2009.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Umar Akmal at the [[University Oval, Dunedin]], in 2009.]]
Akmal made his [[Test cricket|Test]] debut against [[New Zealand cricket team|New Zealand]] at [[Dunedin]] on 23 November 2009. On the third day of his debut Test, Akmal hit 129 runs from 160 balls becoming only the second Pakistani to score a hundred on debut away from home after [[Fawad Alam]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Statsguru – Tests – Pakistan centuries on debut |url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/stats/index.html?class=1;debut_or_last=1;filter=advanced;orderby=start;runsmin1=100;runsval1=runs;team=7;template=results;type=batting;view=innings |website=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=17 June 2024}}</ref>

This feat also made him the first Pakistani batsman to score both his maiden Test and ODI century away from home, following his ODI century against Sri Lanka. The innings was noted as special due to Pakistan's tough position in the match and the hundred partnership which Akmal was involved in alongside his elder brother Kamran. He followed up the century in the first innings with a fifty in the second innings.<ref>{{cite web |title=New Zealand vs Pakistan, 1st Test, Dunedin, November 24–28, 2009 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/pakistan-tour-of-new-zealand-2009-10-423768/new-zealand-vs-pakistan-1st-test-423778/full-scorecard |website=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=17 June 2024}}</ref>

In only his second Test match he was moved up the order to the crucial spot of number 3, where he struggled initially but managed to counter-attack making 46 runs before he was undone by an inswinger by [[Daryl Tuffey]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Black Caps take ascendancy |url=https://www.nation.com.pk/04-Dec-2009/black-caps-take-ascendancy |access-date=17 June 2024 |work=The Nation |date=4 December 2009}}</ref> In the second innings he was moved down the order to his usual batting spot of number 5 as captain [[Mohammad Yousuf (cricketer)|Mohammed Yousuf]] chose to bat at number 3 himself, and Akmal looked his usual aggressive self throughout his innings of 52 runs which came off only 33 balls.<ref>{{cite web |title=New Zealand vs Pakistan, 2nd Test, Wellington, December 03 - 06, 2009 |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/pakistan-tour-of-new-zealand-2009-10-423768/new-zealand-vs-pakistan-2nd-test-423779/full-scorecard |website=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=17 June 2024}}</ref>

He had his first failure in the first innings of the third Test at Napier where he was caught in the gully for a duck but scored a rearguard 77 in the second, promoting him to the leading run scorer of the series. Akmal finished the tour with 379 runs at an average of 63.16.<ref>{{cite web |title=Pakistan in New Zealand Test Series, 2009/10 Records - Most runs |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/records/series/batting-most-runs-career/pakistan-in-new-zealand-test-series-2009-10-5462 |website=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=17 June 2024}}</ref>

Akmal played his last Test match in the [[Pakistani cricket team in Zimbabwe in 2011|one-off test against Zimbabwe]] in 2011. Akmal scored only 15 in that match and was dropped from the Test team thereafter and has yet to be recalled.<ref>{{cite web |title=Player Profile: Umar Akmal |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/cricketers/umar-akmal-317273 |website=ESPNcricinfo |access-date=17 June 2024}}</ref>

== ODI and Twenty20 career ==
In an interview, Akmal said "My own dream is to one day play for Pakistan alongside [[Kamran Akmal|Kamran Bhai]] (Akmal's brother) and I'm working hard to try and achieve that goal".<ref>{{Cite web|title=Exclusive Interview|url=http://www.pakpassion.net/articles/umar_akmal|website=Pakpassion.net|access-date=30 April 2020|archive-date=12 August 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090812092425/http://www.pakpassion.net/articles/umar_akmal|url-status=dead}}</ref> Akmal was selected in Pakistan's squad for the One Day International Series against Sri Lanka in July–August 2009.

After not playing in the first ODI, Akmal made his debut in the second match of the series replacing [[Mohammad Yousuf (cricketer, born 1974)|Mohammad Yousuf]] in the middle order. In only his second career ODI, Akmal scored his maiden ODI fifty. He followed up his maiden fifty by scoring a  century in the very next match. For this match winning effort he was awarded his career's first [[Man of the Match]] award.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Umar and Iftikhar script crushing win|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/13605/report/403373/sri-lanka-vs-pakistan-4th-odi-pakistan-tour-of-sri-lanka-2009|last=Alter|first=Jamie|date=7 August 2009|website=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref> His exploits in [[Sri Lanka]] earned him a place in the Pakistan squad for the [[2009 ICC Champions Trophy]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=2009-08-25 |title=ICC Champions Trophy 2009 squads |language=en-GB |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/cricket/8164322.stm |access-date=2022-05-10}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Pakistan Squad - Pakistan Squad - ICC Champions Trophy, 2009 Squad |url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/icc-champions-trophy-2009-10-374074/pakistan-squad-420936/series-squads |access-date=2022-05-10 |website=ESPNcricinfo}}</ref>

His 41 not out against West Indies was a match winning knock and landed him his second career [[Man of the Match]] award.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Young guns impress Alam|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/22769870/young-guns-impress-alam|last=Samiuddin|first=Osman|date=24 September 2009|website=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref> His next big innings came in the semi-final against New Zealand, where he scored a brisk 55 in a losing effort, before he was wrongly given out by umpire [[Simon Taufel]], who later apologized.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Simon Taufel apologizes to Umar Akmal|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/champions-trophy-2009/top-stories/Simon-Taufel-apologizes-to-Umar-Akmal/articleshow/5090173.cms?|date=5 October 2009|website=The Times of India|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref>

Despite the fact that Akmal is not a wicket-keeper he kept wicket for Pakistan temporarily in the third ODI against England in 2010 from the 27th over onwards because his elder brother Kamran was being diagnosed for an injury to his finger. Umar Akmal scored 71 runs from 52 balls in his debut [[Cricket World Cup|World Cup]] match and was named Man of the Match.<ref>{{cite web|title=Full Scorecard of Pakistan vs Kenya 6th Match, Group A 2011 - Score Report|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/8039/scorecard/433563/kenya-vs-pakistan-6th-match-group-a-icc-cricket-world-cup-2010-11|date=23 February 2020|website=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=18 February 2012}}</ref>

In February 2012, Pakistan faced England in [[Pakistani cricket team vs England in the UAE in 2011–12|four ODIs]]. Pakistan's brittle batting meant the team management chose to play Akmal as a wicket-keeper based on his batting, though his brother Adnan was considered the better 'keeper'. The result of choosing the less accomplished glovesman was that in the first two matches Umar Akmal missed opportunities to dismiss [[Ravi Bopara]] and [[Alastair Cook]] early in their innings, and they respectively went on to score a half-century and a century.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.espncricinfo.com/pakistan-v-england-2012/content/story/554091.html |title=Misbah troubled by wicketkeeper issue |publisher=Cricinfo |first=George |last=Dobell |date=17 February 2012 |access-date=18 February 2012}}</ref>

Akmal was included in Pakistan's squad for the [[2012 ICC World Twenty20|2012 World Twenty20]]. Pakistan made it to the semifinal where they lost to Sri Lanka.

Akmal was dropped from ODI series against Sri Lanka in 2015, but called up for the [[Pakistani cricket team in Sri Lanka in 2015#1st T20I|T20I series]]. He proved his value to the team, by scoring 24-ball 46 runs in the first T20I match.

Akmal was initially suspended from [[English cricket team against Pakistan in the UAE in 2015–16|Pakistan's T20I series against England]] for attending a party without PCB permission, but was subsequently cleared of wrongdoing and allowed to go on tour.<ref name=":3" /> Akmal scored only 26 runs across 3 innings in that series.<ref>{{Cite web|title=RECORDS / PAKISTAN V ENGLAND T20I SERIES, 2015/16 - PAKISTAN / BATTING AND BOWLING AVERAGES|url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/averages/batting_bowling_by_team.html?id=10307;team=7;type=series|website=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref>

Akmal was initially suspended from [[Pakistani cricket team in New Zealand in 2015–16|Pakistan's first T20I against New Zealand]] due to an incident in the final of the recently concluded Quaid-e-Azam trophy. However, the suspension was lifted on appeal.<ref name=":2" /> Akmal was the highest run scorer of the T20 series for the Pakistanis with 85 runs across three innings with one fifty.<ref>{{Cite web|title=RECORDS / PAKISTAN IN NEW ZEALAND T20I SERIES, 2015/16 - PAKISTAN / BATTING AND BOWLING AVERAGES|url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/averages/batting_bowling_by_team.html?id=10459;team=7;type=series|website=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref>

Akmal played in the [[2016 ICC World Twenty20|2016 World Twenty20]]. Akmal was dropped from the T20 side afterwards. He was also dropped from a training camp afterwards for disciplinary issues.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Shehzad, Akmal left out of Pakistan training camp|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/26174283/shehzad,-akmal-left-pakistan-training-camp|last=Farooq|first=Umar|date=2 May 2016|website=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref>

Akmal was recalled to the T20 side for the [[West Indian cricket team against Pakistan in the UAE in 2016–17|series against West Indies]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Akmal returns to Pakistan's T20 squad|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/17501751/umar-akmal-returns-pakistan-t20-squad-face-west-indies-uae-september-23|date=9 September 2016|website=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref> He played one game with a high score of 1*.<ref>{{Cite web|title=RECORDS / PAKISTAN V WEST INDIES T20I SERIES, 2016/17 - PAKISTAN / BATTING AND BOWLING AVERAGES|url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/averages/batting_bowling_by_team.html?id=11485;team=7;type=series|website=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref>

Akmal was dropped from the ODI side for the [[Pakistani cricket team in the West Indies in 2016–17|series against West Indies]] due to fitness issues. He was later recalled and included in the ODI squad for the [[2017 ICC Champions Trophy]] only to fail a fitness test shortly before the tournament. Akmal was subsequently sent back and was replaced by [[Haris Sohail]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/19430965/umar-akmal-fails-fitness-tests,-called-back-england|title=Umar Akmal fails fitness tests, called back from England|last=Farooq|first=Umar|date=21 May 2017|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref>

Akmal was dropped from PCB's list of centrally contracted players on 12 July 2017 due to persistent fitness issues.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/19969251/umar-akmal-not-given-central-contract-|title=Umar Akmal not given central contract|last=Farooq|first=Umar|date=12 July 2017|website=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref>

In March 2019, Akmal was recalled to the ODI squad for their [[Australian cricket team against Pakistan in the UAE in 2018–19|series against Australia in the UAE]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/26184713/shoaib-malik-lead-umar-akmal,-junaid-khan-recalled|title=Shoaib Malik to lead as Umar Akmal, Junaid recalled|last=Farooq|first=Umar|date=8 March 2019|website=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref> He scored 150 runs across 5 innings at an average of 30 and failed to cross 50 in the entire series.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Australia v Pakistan ODI Series, 2018/19 - Pakistan Cricket Team Records & Stats|url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/averages/batting_bowling_by_team.html?id=12883;team=7;type=series|date=31 March 2019|website=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref> In addition, he was fined 20% of his match fee for breaking team curfew ahead of the 5th ODI.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Umar Akmal fined for breaking team curfew|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/26416207/umar-akmal-fined-breaking-team-curfew|date=1 April 2019|website=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref>

Akmal was not picked for the [[2019 Cricket World Cup]] squad.

In October 2019, Umar Akmal was recalled to the T20 side for Pakistan's [[Sri Lankan cricket team in Pakistan in 2019–20|home series against Sri Lanka]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Umar Akmal, Ahmed Shehzad return to Pakistan T20I squad|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/27748740/umar-akmal-ahmed-shehzad-return-pakistan-t20i-squad|date=2 October 2019|website=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref> However, he scored two [[Duck (cricket)|golden ducks]] in the first two games of the series and was subsequently dropped.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Full Scorecard of Sri Lanka vs Pakistan 1st T20I 2019 - Score Report|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/19504/scorecard/1198489/pakistan-vs-sri-lanka-1st-t20i-sri-lanka-in-pakistan-2019-20|date=5 October 2019|website=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Full Scorecard of Sri Lanka vs Pakistan 2nd T20I 2019 - Score Report|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/19504/scorecard/1198490/pakistan-vs-sri-lanka-2nd-t20i-sri-lanka-in-pakistan-2019-20|date=7 October 2019|website=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref> As a result, he equalled [[Tillekaratne Dilshan]]'s unwanted record for scoring the most ducks in T20Is with 10.<ref>{{cite web|title=Records {{!}} Twenty20 Internationals {{!}} Batting Records {{!}} Most Ducks in a Career|url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/records/284058.html|website=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref> Umar Akmal has the record for scoring the second most ducks in Twenty 20 cricket history (27) just behind [[Dwayne Smith]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/content/records/305198.html|title=Most ducks in career|website=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=9 January 2018}}</ref>

==T20 franchise career==
===Pakistan Super League===
Akmal was bought by [[Lahore Qalandars]] for US$140,000 in [[2016 Pakistan Super League|2016 season]]. He performed well and ended up as the highest runs-scorer in [[PSL 2016]] scoring 335 runs in seven innings with four half-centuries.<ref>{{cite web|title=PAKISTAN SUPER LEAGUE, 2015/16 / RECORDS / MOST RUNS|url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/pakistan-super-league-2015-16/engine/records/batting/most_runs_career.html?id=10555;type=tournament|website=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref> His team didn't qualify for play-offs and finished last in the group stage. He was retained by Lahore Qalandars for [[2017 Pakistan Super League|2nd season]]. He finished the season with 164 runs from 8 matches with only one fifty.<ref>{{cite web|title=PAKISTAN SUPER LEAGUE, 2016/17 / RECORDS / MOST RUNS|url=http://stats.espncricinfo.com/pakistan-super-league-2016-17/engine/records/batting/most_runs_career.html?id=11673;type=tournament|website=ESPNcricinfo|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref> He was again retained by Qalandars for [[2018 Pakistan Super League|3rd season]]. He was eventually dropped by Lahore Qalandars for later part of the tournament for his below par performance and disciplinary issues.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/22788839/axed-umar-akmal-lahore-qalandars-future-doubt|title=Axed Akmal's Lahore Qalandars future in doubt|last=Farooq|first=Umar|date=16 March 2018|website=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref>

Akmal joined [[Quetta Gladiators]] for [[2019 Pakistan Super League|4th season]] as a result of a trade. He scored 277 runs in 12 matches in the tournament.

Umar was originally part of the Quetta Gladiators squad for the [[2020 Pakistan Super League|2020 season]], but was removed a day before the tournament after he was suspended by PCB with immediate effect under Article 4.7.1 of its anti-corruption code, disallowing him from taking part in any cricket-related activity under the board's purview, "pending the investigation being carried out by PCB's Anti-Corruption Unit". He was replaced by [[Anwar Ali (cricketer)|Anwar Ali]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pakistantoday.com.pk/2020/02/20/pcb-suspends-umar-akmal-from-all-cricket-activities-under-anti-corruption-code/|title=PCB suspends Umar Akmal from all cricket activities under anti-corruption code|date=20 February 2020|website=Pakistan Today|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref>

=== Caribbean Premier League ===
Akmal played for three seasons. He played for the [[Barbados Tridents]] in [[2013 Caribbean Premier League|2013]], [[Guyana Amazon Warriors]] in [[2015 Caribbean Premier League|2015]], and the [[Trinbago Knight Riders]] in [[2016 Caribbean Premier League|2016]].

While he was  playing for the [[Barbados Tridents]], in the [[Caribbean Premier League]], he had to spend a night in [[hospital]] after he suffered mild seizures. Following this, the [[Pakistan Cricket Board|PCB]] called him back for a complete medical checkup and also dropped him from the upcoming [[Zimbabwe]] tour. On 6 September 2013, he was cleared by a neurologist, saying that the seizure was possibly due to a lack of sleep.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://cricbuzz.com/cricket-news/58228/umar-akmal-receives-clean-bill-of-health|title=Umar Akmal receives "clean bill of health"|date=10 September 2013|work=Cricbuzz}}</ref>

===Other leagues===
Akmal played for [[Wayamba United]] in the [[2012 Sri Lanka Premier League|2012]] season of the [[Sri Lanka Premier League|Sri Lankan Premier League]] (SLPL). Akmal played two games and scored 13 runs.<ref>{{Cite web|title=SRI LANKA PREMIER LEAGUE, 2012 - WAYAMBA UNITED / RECORDS / MOST RUNS|url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/sri-lanka-premier-league-2012/engine/records/batting/most_runs_career.html?id=7327;team=4908;type=tournament|website=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref> However, Akmal would not play another season as the SLPL folded that year.

Akmal was picked for the [[Sydney Sixers]] for the [[2012–13 Big Bash League season|2012-13 Big Bash]] but did not play a game.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Umar Akmal joins Sydney Sixers|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/22131203/umar-akmal-joins-sydney-sixers|date=6 November 2012|website=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref>

Akmal spent two seasons in the [[Bangladesh Premier League]]. He played for [[Chittagong Vikings]] in the [[2015–16 Bangladesh Premier League|2015-16 season]]. The Chittagong Vikings finished bottom of the group that season. Akmal played for the [[Rajshahi Kings]] in the [[2016-17 Bangladesh Premier League|2016-17 season]]. He played nine games and scored 106 runs at an average of 13.25.<ref>{{Cite web|title=BANGLADESH PREMIER LEAGUE, 2016/17 / RECORDS / BATTING AVERAGES|url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/bangladesh-premier-league-2016-17/engine/records/averages/batting.html?id=11593;type=tournament|website=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref>

Akmal spent two seasons ([[2015 t20 Blast|2015]] and [[2016 t20 Blast|2016]]) in the [[T20 Blast]]. He played for the [[Leicestershire Foxes]] in both seasons. In 2015, he played 4 games and scored 133 runs at an average of 133 with two fifties and a high score of 76*.<ref>{{Cite web|title=NATWEST T20 BLAST, 2015 / RECORDS / BATTING AVERAGES|url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/natwest-t20-blast-2015/engine/records/averages/batting.html?id=9757;type=tournament|website=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref> However, he fared worse in 2016. He played 6 games and scored 134 runs at an average of 33.5 with one 50.<ref>{{Cite web|title=RECORDS / NATWEST T20 BLAST, 2016 / BATTING AVERAGES|url=https://stats.espncricinfo.com/ci/engine/records/averages/batting.html?id=10775;type=tournament|website=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref>

In June 2019, he was selected to play for the Winnipeg Hawks franchise team in the [[2019 Global T20 Canada]] tournament.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Global T20 draft streamed live|url=http://www.canadacricket.com/?p=12755|website=Canada Cricket Online|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref>

== Ban for corruption ==
On 20 February 2020, Akmal was provisionally suspended by PCB with immediate effect under Article 4.7.1 of its anti-corruption code, disallowing him from taking part in any cricket-related activity under the board's purview, "pending the investigation being carried out by PCB's Anti-Corruption Unit". This prevented Akmal from playing in that season's Pakistan Super League.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Umar Akmal suspended under PCB's anti-corruption code|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/28741135/umar-akmal-suspended-pcb-anti-corruption-code|date=20 February 2020|website=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=28 February 2020}}</ref> On 20 March, the PCB formally charged Akmal with two breaches of its anti-corruption code for two unrelated incidents. The charges were laid under article 2.4.4 of PCB's anti-corruption code which deals with "Failing to disclose to the PCB Vigilance and Security Department (without unnecessary delay) full details of any approaches or invitations received by the participant to engage in corrupt conduct under this Anti-Corruption Code". Akmal decided not to contest the charge, forgoing his right to a hearing in front of the PCB's Anti-corruption Tribunal, and instead his case went directly to the disciplinary committee, chaired by Retired Justice Fazal-e-Miran Chauhan.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Umar Akmal won't contest PCB's corruption charges|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/29016564/umar-akmal-contest-pcb-corruption-charges|date=9 April 2020|website=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref> At the disciplinary hearing held on 27 April, Akmal appeared without a lawyer and did not plead guilty. Akmal admitted to being approached by two different men on separate occasions but tried to justify why he did not report these approaches to the PCB. At the end of the hearing, the PCB banned Akmal from all representative cricket for 3 years, with the ban to last until 19 February 2023.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|title=PCB hands Umar Akmal three-year ban from all cricket|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/29103103/pcb-hands-umar-akmal-three-year-ban-all-cricket|last=Farooq|first=Umar|date=27 April 2020|website=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Umar Akmal 'not prepared to show remorse and seek apology' - PCB panel chairman|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/29149659/umar-akmal-not-prepared-show-remorse-seek-apology-pcb-panel-chairman|last=Farooq|first=Umar|date=8 May 2020|website=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=9 May 2020}}</ref> It was thought that his 3-year ban, which was longer than his fellow countryman [[Mohammad Irfan]] (12 month ban with 6 months suspended) for a similar offense, was due to a lack of remorse on Akmal's part.<ref name=":4" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=Umar Akmal given harsh penalty because of lack of remorse|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/29105207/umar-akmal-given-harsh-penalty-lack-remorse|last=Farooq|first=Umar|date=27 April 2020|website=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref> The following month, he lodged an appeal against his ban.<ref name=":5" /> In July 2020, Akmal's ban was reduced to one-and-a-half years, with his suspension running from February 2020 to August 2021.<ref name="ban_reduce" /> In August 2020, the PCB appealed the ban reduction to the [[Court of Arbitration for Sport]] (CAS) and Akmal appealed to the CAS to have his ban overturned.<ref name=":6" /><ref name=":7" /> On 26 February, the CAS reduced Akmal's ban to 12 months, meaning that Akmal can immediately return to playing cricket, subject to first completing a rehabilitation program under the PCB's anti-corruption code. In addition, the CAS imposed a fine of [[Pakistani rupee|PKR]] 4.25 million (27,000 [[United States dollar|USD]]).<ref name=":8" />

== Controversies ==
In addition to ban for corruption, Akmal has been involved in several on and off field incidents throughout his international and professional career.

In the final Test match of [[Pakistani cricket team in Australia in 2009–10|Pakistan's 2009–10 tour of Australia]], Akmal allegedly feigned an injury to protest the dropping of older brother Kamran. Umar denied such rumors and played in the final match without his brother. Pakistan went on to lose that match by 231 runs and lost the three match series 3–0, with Akmal registering scores of only 8 and 15 in the match.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/series/13400/scorecard/406201/australia-vs-pakistan-3rd-test-pakistan-tour-of-australia-2009-10|title=Full Scorecard of Australia vs Pakistan 3rd Test 2010 - Score Report|date=18 January 2010|website=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref> He was later fined 2 million [[Pakistani rupee]]s and put on probation by the PCB for breaching his contract and speaking to the media without approval.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Top Pakistan players face fines, bans|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/22636059/top-pakistan-players-face-fines,-bans|last=Samiuddin|first=Osman|date=8 March 2010|website=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/22582107/akmal-brothers-appeal-fines|title=Akmal brothers appeal against fines|date=7 April 2010|website=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref>

Akmal's name initially popped up in investigations surrounding the [[Pakistan cricket spot-fixing scandal]]. His name was mentioned by bookmaker [[Mazhar Majeed]] as someone who he was working with.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Pakistan agent claims four other players worked with him|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/22378206/spot-fixing-controversy-pakistan-agent-mazhar-majeed-claims-four-other-players-worked-him|last=Samiuddin|first=Osman|date=30 November 2010|website=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref> However, no evidence was unearthed that Akmal had accepted any money in exchange for spot-fixing.{{citation needed|date=April 2022}}

In Pakistan's semifinal loss against Sri Lanka in the 2012 ICC World Twenty20, Akmal was fined 50% of his match fee. In the 17th over of the second innings and with Akmal at the non-striker's end, Akmal called for a change of gloves despite instructions from umpires [[Simon Taufel]] and [[Rod Tucker]] to the contrary. Akmal ignored the umpires and changed his gloves regardless. After the match, Akmal pled guilty and match referee [[Jeff Crowe]] handed a level 2 charge and a fine of 50% of match fees, with Crowe noting "Umar showed blatant disregard to both the umpires' requests, which was offensive and unacceptable from an international cricketer and contrary to our unique spirit".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/22200647/umar-akmal-fined-ignoring-umpires|title=Akmal fined for ignoring umpires|date=5 October 2012|website=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref>

On 1 February 2014, Akmal was arrested by Gulberg Police in [[Lahore]] for allegedly not stopping at a traffic signal and subsequently getting into a physical altercation with the traffic warden which resulted in the warden's uniform being torn. Akmal was booked under Section 186, 279 and 353 of the [[Pakistan Penal Code]] and a [[First information report|First Information Report]] (FIR) for "obstructing public servant in discharge of public functions, rash driving or riding on a public way and assault or criminal force to deter public servant from discharge of his duty". Akmal denied the claims and implied that he was physically attacked by the warden. Akmal was released on bail after 12 hours of police detention.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/21564387/umar-akmal-charged-run-police|title=Umar Akmal charged for run-in with police|date=1 February 2014|website=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref>

On 16 April 2014, four people were arrested at a party that celebrated Akmal's marriage to Noor Amma, the daughter of Pakistan leg-spinner [[Abdul Qadir (cricketer)|Abdul Qadir]], for violating local by-laws that were in place to curb excessively lavish wedding parties.<ref name=":0" />

On 12 November 2015, Akmal was dropped from Pakistan's T20 side for their series against England for "bringing the PCB and Pakistan Cricket into disrepute." It was reported that Akmal had attended a party while playing for Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Limited in their Quaid-e-Azam Trophy match against [[Hyderabad cricket team (Pakistan)|Hyderabad]] without the PCB's permission.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/20483745/akmal-omitted-t20-squad-rafatullah-earns-call|title=Akmal omitted from T20 squad; Rafatullah earns call|date=12 November 2015|website=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref> Local newspaper ''Daily Kawish Sindhi'' had reported that some cricketers allegedly were engaging in "immoral activity" at the party. In Akmal's place, [[Rafatullah Mohmand]] was called up. Akmal was later reinstated after an investigation by the PCB into the activities at the party.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/20452193/pcb-clears-umar-akmal-england-t20s|title=PCB clears Umar Akmal for England T20s|last=Farooq|first=Umar|date=20 November 2015|website=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref>

During the final of the [[2015–16 Quaid-e-Azam Trophy]] on 3–6 January 2016, Akmal reportedly wore a uniform that sported a different logo to that of his teammates. This constituted a charge of committing "abuse of cricket equipment or clothing, ground equipment or fixtures and fittings during a match" which is a Level 1 charge of the PCB's code of conduct. As this was Akmal's third such offense, the PCB banned Akmal for one match, which ruled Akmal out of [[Pakistani cricket team in New Zealand in 2015–16|Pakistan's first T20 during their tour of New Zealand]]. However, Akmal was allowed to play after the ban was lifted on appeal.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/15871293/umar-akmal-banned-first-nz-t20-due-misconduct|title=Umar Akmal banned from first NZ T20 due to misconduct|last=Farooq|first=Umar|date=9 January 2016|website=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref>

On 26 April 2016, it was reported that Akmal was involved in a brawl at a local theater in [[Faisalabad]]. Allegedly Akmal had requested that a song be replayed, but the theater administration denied the request at which point Akmal got into an argument and was ushered outside.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/sports/cricket/story/umar-akmal-in-trouble-again-after-alleged-theatre-brawl-320036-2016-04-26|title=Umar Akmal in trouble again after alleged theatre brawl|date=26 April 2016|website=India Today|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref> Akmal was cleared by the PCB the next day.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cricwizz.com/blog/2016/04/27/umar-akmal-cleared-brawl-theater-case/|title=Umar Akmal cleared of brawl in theater case|date=27 April 2016|website=Cricwizz|access-date=28 April 2020}}{{Dead link|date=September 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>

On 17 May 2017, the PCB fined Akmal and teammate [[Junaid Khan (cricketer)|Junaid Khan]] 50% of match fees as well as being put on one month probation in relation to an incident that occurred during a Pakistan Cup match against Sindh on 27 April 2017. Akmal, who was captaining Punjab at the time, made comments at the coin toss explaining Junaid Khan's absence from that game, implying that Khan had simply decided not to show up. Later in the day, Khan rebutted the comments in the form of a video shot from his hotel room in which he stated that he was "saddened to hear the remarks Akmal made on television, saying 'I ran away from the team'... I am dealing with a case of food poisoning and the team management is aware of that... Umar Akmal knew of this..."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/19403391/umar-akmal,-junaid-fined-pakistan-cup-spat|title=Umar Akmal, Junaid fined for Pakistan Cup spat|last=Farooq|first=Umar|date=17 May 2017|website=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref>

On 16 August 2017, about one month after losing his central contract due to persistent fitness issues, Akmal held an impromptu press conference in which he criticized then Pakistan national team coach [[Mickey Arthur]]. It was reported that Akmal had tried to enter the National Cricket Academy (NCA) to work on his fitness, but none of the coaches wanted to work with Akmal since NCA coaches only work with PCB's centrally contracted players. Akmal then took up this issue with the chief selector at the time [[Inzamam-ul-Haq]] who then redirected Akmal to Mickey Arthur. It was at this point that Akmal claimed that Arthur used "abusive language" towards Akmal. In a separate statement to the media, Arthur confirmed that an exchange occurred between himself and Akmal but denied using abusive language, instead saying that "he had to earn the right to use our support staff because he is not a contracted cricketer. He can't just walk in here and demand what he wants."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/20360463/umar-akmal-furious-arthur-snub|title=Umar Akmal furious at being denied NCA facilities|last=Farooq|first=Umar|date=16 August 2017|website=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref> The PCB issued a show-cause notice to Umar Akmal and formed a committee to investigate the situation. On 28 September, the PCB fined Akmal 1 million rupees, banned Akmal for 3 matches, and revoked Akmal's No-Objection Certificates (NOC) for the next two months. The revocation of Akmal's NOCs meant that Akmal was ruled out of all but the last two weeks of the [[2017–18 Bangladesh Premier League|Bangladesh Premier League]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/20849480/umar-akmal-picks-three-match-ban-mickey-arthur-outburst|title=Umar Akmal picks up three-match ban for Arthur outburst|last=Rasool|first=Danyal|date=28 September 2017|website=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref>

On 24 June 2018, Akmal gave an interview with [[Samaa TV]] in which he revealed offers to spot-fix during the [[2015 Cricket World Cup|2015 World Cup]]. Akmal reported that he was offered US$200,000 to "leave two balls alone" but Akmal denied accepting the offer. The PCB issued a show-cause notice and asked Akmal to come before anti-corruption unit on 27 June to explain his comments. The [[International Cricket Council]] (ICC) also began conducting its own investigations into the matter.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/23896693/pcb-serves-umar-akmal-notice-spot-fixing-claims|title=PCB serves Umar Akmal notice over spot-fixing claims|last=Farooq|first=Umar|date=24 June 2018|website=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref>

On 1 April 2019, Akmal was fined 20% of his match fee for breaking team curfew ahead of the 5th and final ODI of [[Australian cricket team against Pakistan in the UAE in 2018–19|Pakistan's ODI series against Australia]]. Akmal headed out to watch an [[Akon]] concert on the night of 29 March without getting permission from team management.<ref name=":1" />

On 2 February 2020, it was reported that Umar Akmal exposed himself to a staff member of the NCA while undergoing a fitness test. While undergoing a skin-fold test to measure body fat, Akmal undressed completely in front of the staff member and asked, "Where is the fat?"<ref>{{Cite web|title=Umar Akmal facing punishment after misbehaving at fitness test|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/28618362/umar-akmal-facing-punishment-misbehaving-fitness-test-|last=Farooq|first=Umar|date=2 February 2020|website=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref> In response to this incident, the PCB initiated an inquiry that lasted two days. At the end of the inquiry, the PCB decided against handing any punishment, and instead "reminded him of his responsibilities as a senior cricketer".<ref>{{Cite web|title=Umar Akmal's misbehaviour 'due to a misunderstanding' - PCB|url=https://www.espncricinfo.com/story/_/id/28684559/umar-akmal-misbehaviour-due-misunderstanding-pcb|date=12 February 2020|website=ESPNCricinfo|access-date=28 April 2020}}</ref>
